title: If Commanders lose, NFC East will be first division with zero wins in back-to-back weeks since merger
summary: Thanks to another rough Sunday around the NFC East, the Commanders could make some history on Monday night.
full_text: Thanks to another rough Sunday around the NFC East, the Commanders could make some history on Monday night. Josh Dubow of the Associated Press points out that a Commanders loss to the 49ers at Levi's Stadium would make the NFC East the first division since the merger to win zero games over back-to-back weeks despite having all of its teams in action. The Eagles and Cowboys are both 0-2 over the last two weeks while the Giants followed up their Week Five tie with the Commanders by losing to the Saints on Sunday. The 49ers are favored by more than a touchdown on Monday night, so oddsmakers believe that the NFC East will end the two-week stretch with an 0-6-2 record. Week Seven will bring a bye for the Commanders and a trip to Houston for the Giants while the Eagles and Cowboys play each other, so chances are that the division should find its ninth win of the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mike Vrabel: We were lucky to win on Sunday
summary: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel opened his postgame press conference on Sunday by saying that his team was "lucky to win" against the Jets.
full_text: ' Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel opened his postgame press conference on Sunday by saying that his team was "lucky to win" against the Jets. The Patriots took a 17-3 lead into halftime and wound up winning 26-19 to extend their winning streak to three games, but Vrabel expanded on his earlier comment to make it clear that he doesn't think they had the right formula on the field. "We just didn't play very well," Vrabel said, via a transcript from the team. "We tried to beat ourselves, but we made enough plays in critical situations to help us get through here today." A.J. Brown's dropped passes were one obvious way the team hurt itself and they also lost a pair of fumbles, which moves them to 13 turnovers on the season. Vrabel focused on the latter issue during an appearance on WEEI on Monday morning. "We turn the ball over at a historic rate , and it's ridiculous," Vrabel said, via Mike Reiss of ESPN. "It's an embarrassment." If there's a bright side to the turnovers, it is that Drake Maye has contributed none of them over the last two weeks after having nine in the first four weeks of the season. His stability has helped fuel the team's winning streak and Vrabel will have to find a way to have it carry over to the rest of the team.
author: Josh Alper

title: Panthers TE Tommy Tremble: I taunted Cooper DeJean because of his "egregious" hit on teammate
summary: Panthers tight end Tommy Tremble punctuated his second touchdown of Sunday's 25-14 win over the Eagles by turning toward and pointing at defensive back Cooper DeJean.
full_text: ' Panthers tight end Tommy Tremble punctuated his second touchdown of Sunday's 25-14 win over the Eagles by turning toward and pointing at defensive back Cooper DeJean. Tremble's move drew a flag for taunting and it came a play after DeJean picked up a personal foul of his own. DeJean and Tremble's fellow tight end Mitchell Evans got into it after a Chuba Hubbard run and DeJean was penalized for picking Evans up and slamming him to the ground. After the game, Tremble explained that he was trying to stand up for his teammate. "I just thought that earlier personal foul was just kind of egregious, and so it was uncalled for, something that didn't need to happen," Tremble said, via the team's website. "I shouldn't have retaliated. That wasn't cool for me to do." The ensuing extra point was no good, so the 15 yards hurt the Panthers and they would have hurt a lot more had it been a closer game. Tremble will likely feel a little more pain via a fine from the league, but Sunday was a net positive for him and the team.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jameis Winston: I'd love to put myself in a better position to execute
summary: Giants quarterback Jameis Winston spent the fourth quarter of Sunday's game watching J.J.
full_text: '' Giants quarterback Jameis Winston spent the fourth quarter of Sunday's game watching J.J. McCarthy try to pull off an improbable comeback and the day ended without any certainty that he'd be back on the field in Week 7. Head coach John Harbaugh said the immediate aftermath of a 34-27 loss to the Saints was not the time to make an announcement about a starter moving forward. Winston threw a touchdown as the Giants moved to a 10-0 lead in the first quarter, but he was pulled after 34 straight Saints points and a pair of second-half interceptions. McCarthy led the Giants to 17 points and had a shot to tie the game on the final drive, which made his argument for getting the start next week pretty straightforward. Winston was asked what he'd say to Harbaugh about his case. "That's him. You know, that's the decision that he'll have to make," Winston said, via a transcript from the team. "What I would love is to just put myself in a better position to execute. And that just starts with me. Things that I can control, going out there every single play, doing my very best." McCarthy has only been with the Giants for a few weeks, but they traded for him so that they had an option other than Winston as they played out the season in the wake of Jaxson Dart's knee injury. That option looked like a viable one on Sunday and his time as a starter is likely coming even if he isn't on the field for the first snap in Houston next Sunday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Kyren Williams: Offensive inconsistency "probably because I'm not out there"
summary: Sunday's 18-16 home loss to the Cardinals dropped the Rams to 2-4 and continued a start that has many people scratching their heads given how high the hopes were for the team heading into the season.
full_text: '' Sunday's 18-16 home loss to the Cardinals dropped the Rams to 2-4 and continued a start that has many people scratching their heads given how high the hopes were for the team heading into the season. Everyone associated with the team is fielding questions about why things have gone so poorly, including running back Kyren Williams. Williams was asked about why he thinks the offense has been inconsistent from drive to drive over the first six weeks and he pointed to his role in his answer. “I can’t tell you, bro,” Williams said, via Adam Grosbard of the Orange County Register . “Probably because I’m not out there .” Williams played 70 percent of the snaps in the first five games and he outsnapped Blake Corum 42-16 on Sunday while fielding 13 touches to 11 for Corum. Williams' workload is in line with last season, but down from its peak in 2024 and he's seeing fewer carries than at any point since he became a starter. He was asked if he'd like to see that change in the coming weeks. “I can’t really call that. It’s not on me,” Williams said. “But I just think no matter what, we gotta continue to have the energy. You gotta continue to, when plays are made, be excited, be happy so we uplift not only the offense but the defense and the special teams and just being able to have that camaraderie to where we’re playing off of each other and I think that’s what is going to allow us to be where we want to be.” Musing about playing time and soul-searching about how to get into a groove weren't the kinds of things people expected from the Rams this season, but that's what happens when losses start to pile up and the Rams need to get right in a hurry if they want to avoid those things becoming the most consistent part of their season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Last time the Chargers were 0-6, their QBs were Ryan Leaf, Moses Moreno and Jim Harbaugh
summary: The Chargers are 0-6 for the first time since 2000.
full_text: '' The Chargers are 0-6 for the first time since 2000. Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh remembers that well. That's because Harbaugh was one of the quarterbacks on the terrible 2000 Chargers, who were 0-6 through six weeks like this year's Chargers. That 2000 Chargers team ended the season 1-15. The Chargers began the 2000 season with Ryan Leaf as their starting quarterback. Leaf had been the No. 2 overall pick in 1998, was awful as a rookie and missed all of his second season with a shoulder injury. The 2000 season was Leaf's last chance in San Diego, and it did not go well. Through the first two weeks, the Chargers were 0-2 and Leaf had one touchdown pass and five interceptions, so they benched him for Moses Moreno in Week 3. Unfortunately, Moreno was also terrible, and he suffered a shoulder injury in that Week 3 game, so Leaf started again in Week 4. But after Leaf again struggled in Week 4, he was benched again, this time for Harbaugh. Harbaugh started Week 5, and he completely transformed the Chargers' offense: Through the first five games, Moreno and Leaf had combined to average 131 passing yards, and totaled one touchdown pass and seven interceptions. In Week 5, Harbaugh threw for 348 yards, with two touchdowns and one interception, against the defending Super Bowl champion Rams. Unfortunately for the Chargers, their defense couldn't stop the Greatest Show on Turf, and the Rams won 57-31. Harbaugh kept the starting job for four more games, but he didn't play as well, and by the time the Chargers were 0-10 they went back to Leaf to close out the season. Leaf won one game as the starter, but the Chargers' 1-15 record was the worst in franchise history. At least, the worst so far. Harbaugh's 2026 Chargers have a chance to break the 2000 team's franchise record for the most losses in a season.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Brian Schottenheimer: Cowboys' effort and fight is right, but mistakes are killing us
summary: The Cowboys fell to 2-4 with Sunday night's loss to the Packers.
full_text: ' Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer defended his team's effort but not the results after Sunday night's loss to the Packers. On a night when Dak Prescott threw two interceptions, Schottenheimer pointed the finger at turnovers. "The effort is right, the fight is right, but mistakes are killing us," Schottenheimer said. "We've got to protect the football." At 2-4, the Cowboys are not a good team right now, but there are no good teams in the NFC East and the Cowboys are actually the betting favorites to win the division. Schottenheimer thinks there's still a future for his team. "We're in a hole. We've put ourselves there. There's one way out of it. I told our guys we've got to work, we've got to find solutions, we can't repeat mistakes. And they understand that," Schottenheimer said. Although Schottenheimer defended Prescott's effort, he made clear that he wasn't happy about the interceptions. "The ball matters more than anything in the National Football League," Schottenheimer said. "It's the ball. Second, it's the line of scrimmage. And we haven't been very good in the last two games, so that's what we're responsible and accountable for, and I stand up here and accept that."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Sunday Night Football: Packers move to 4-2 with 23-13 victory over Cowboys
summary: Green Bay has won three games in a row after a strong defensive performance against Dallas on Sunday night.
full_text: The Packers have stabilized their offensive front, and their defense is taking significant strides. Now the team is on a bona fide winning streak. Green Bay controlled the ball and the clock on Sunday night, defeating Dallas, 23-13. The game didn’t feel as close as the final score, as Green Bay took a 17-0 lead into halftime and allowed just one Dallas scoring drive until late in the fourth quarter. While a second-half possession got aided by penalty and moved the Cowboys all the way down to the Green Bay 14, eventually the Packers still managed to get a turnover on downs when Dak Prescott’s pass went high and incomplete out of the end zone. Prescott ended up throwing 54 times, finishing the night with 258 yards on 34 completions. He a touchdown and two interceptions, both of which led to points in the first half — a field goal and a 1-yard touchdown run by Jordan Love at the end of the second quarter. He would’ve had at least one more had it not been negated by a roughing the passer penalty. Prescott was under siege throughout much of the night, as he was officially hit seven times. The Packers registered one sack. On the other side, Love was 23-of-41 for 276 yards with a touchdown and an interception. While the Packers’ run game didn’t get going, Matthew Golden led the team with six catches for 104 yards with a TD. Christian Watson also had 64 yards on three receptions. Trey Smack connected on three field goals of 25, 44, and 29 yards. With the win, the Packers are now 4-2 and have won each of their last three games. They will be in Detroit for a big divisional matchup against the Lions next week. The 2-4 Cowboys will again be on the road next week to face the fellow 2-4 Eagles on Monday night.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Tristan Wirfs can't blame Bucs fans for not showing up vs. Steelers
summary: Steelers fans overwhelmed Raymond James Stadium on Sunday, boosting the road team's effort to overcome a 13-0 halftime deficit and a 16-3 fourth-quarter deficit.
full_text: '' Steelers fans overwhelmed Raymond James Stadium on Sunday, boosting the road team's effort to overcome a 13-0 halftime deficit and a 16-3 fourth-quarter deficit. Tackle Tristan Wirfs isn't upset with Buccaneers fans for the lack of in-person support. “ Can you blame them? ” Wirfs said, via JoeBucsFan.com. “You know, we’re 1-4 and haven’t really given them much to cheer about. "So, yeah, it sucks. It sucks when you’re going damn near silent count at home. But you've got to give [fans] something to cheer for.” The Bucs are now 1-5. And the fans didn't have much to cheer for on Sunday, as the double-digit margin melted into a loss. Wirfs was asked whether the failure to close out games is physical or mental. “You know, I don’t really know, to be honest,” Wirfs said. “We’re up by 13 and, I don’t know. I don’t have anything. I’m not going to say anything right now. I don’t know what it is. It’s insanely frustrating. You know, to be up 13 at home. We haven’t won a fucking home game yet. And to not be able to finish out the game is really frustrating.” The Bucs were on the brink of extending their winning streak to two before it all fell apart. Now, they're all alone at the bottom of the NFC South with a 1-5 record, looking up at the 3-2 Panthers, the 2-4 Falcons, and the 2-4 Saints. Next up, the Bucs face the Panthers in Carolina before the Falcons come to town. After that, it's a Sunday night game in Chicago against the Bears. If Tampa Bay is ever going to turn it around this season, the time is now. After starting the 2025 season at 6-2, the Bucs are 3-12.
author: Mike Florio

title: Todd Monken wants to enjoy the win over the Ravens while he can
summary: In Week 1, the Browns were embarrassed by the Jaguars.
full_text: '' In Week 1, the Browns were embarrassed by the Jaguars. Former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin, quoting JuJu Smith-Schuster, declared on NBC, "The Browns is the Browns." Since then, the Browns is 4-1. The biggest win of the season came on Sunday, when the new Browns beat the old Browns to create a three-way tie atop the AFC North. Because the Browns have beaten both the Ravens and the Steelers, both of whom are 4-2, Cleveland is in first place. And first-year head coach Todd Monken intends to relish it. Until tomorrow. "I’m going to enjoy tonight," Monken told reporters after the 13-10 win. "And that’s what you have to do in the NFL. These are the nights that you don’t ever want to end, because tomorrow it’s on to the next game. And so, I sit there, I know it sounds really goofy, but you sit there in bed and you don’t want the night to end. It’s 10:30 and you’re tired as hell and you want to be up another 15, 20, 30 minutes to enjoy it, because, shit, tomorrow I’ve got to look at the offensive tape and then you’ve got to move on to the next game." The next game could push the Browns to 5-2; they head to Tennessee to play the Titans. And the Browns are road favorites. The best news is that the Browns are relevant. They'll likely be jockeying for a playoff berth after Thanksgiving. In a league littered with teams that claim they want to win the Super Bowl, the truth is that they hope to still be in the mix after the fourth Thursday in November. Because that's when the NFL season truly starts. This year, the Browns will likely be one of the teams that is hoping to finish strong enough to earn a spot in the AFC playoff field, and to win as many games as they can once the single-elimination phase commences.
author: Mike Florio

title: Javonte Williams scores 1-yard TD, Packers still lead Cowboys 17-7
summary: The Cowboys are on the board.
full_text: The Cowboys are on the board. Needing a stop and a score, Dallas got exactly that and now trails Green Bay 17-7. The Packers received the second-half kickoff, but their drive was quickly derailed by an offensive holding penalty on the first play of the possession. After the three-and-out, Dallas used a seven-play, 46-yard drive to get in the end zone with Javonte Williams' 1-yard touchdown. Dallas converted fourth-and-2 with a pass to CeeDee Lamb to keep the chains moving. Additionally, Tucker Kraft has returned to the game after suffering an apparent leg injury late in the second quarter.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Rams K Blake Grupe left SoFi Stadium with crutches and a brace on his leg
summary: The Rams signed kicker Blake Grupe after Week 5.
full_text: The Rams signed kicker Blake Grupe after Week 5. They'll be signing another kicker after Week 6. Via Arash Markazi of The Sporting Tribune , Grupe left SoFi Stadium with his leg in a brace and on crutches . It was a result of Grupe's effort to make a tackle on a kickoff return. The attempt took courage, especially since he's listed at 5-7 and 156 pounds. (Which could mean he's actually shorter and lighter than that.) Either way, the hit will apparently end Grupe's time with the Rams. The next question is whether they'll bring back Harrison Mevis or look elsewhere for help. And that's far from the biggest of the problems the Rams have. They're 2-4 after six games, and they're getting closer and closer to having too many losses to qualify for the postseason. Can they heat up? Yes. Will they? We'll find out, one game at a time.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sunday Night Football: Jordan Love TD gives Packers 17-0 halftime lead
summary: Jordan Love threw for a touchdown and rushed for one in the first half of Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
full_text: ' The Packers have taken advantage of Cowboys mistakes throughout the first 30 minutes of Sunday’s matchup, building a 17-0 lead at halftime. Dak Prescott has thrown two interceptions while a couple of defensive pass interference penalties helped the Packers score a touchdown on a Jordan Love QB sneak toward the end of the second quarter. Green Bay started the game 7-of-7 on third down and finished the first half 9-of-10 in the category. Green Bay has 225 total yards, 15 first downs, and is averaging 5.8 yards per play. Love is 14-of-22 for 190 yards with a touchdown and an interception, plus two carries for 14 yards with a TD. Matthew Golden caught the first touchdown pass from Love, capping a 14-play, 90-yard opening drive for the Packers in the first quarter. Trey Smack added a 25-yard field goal midway through the second period. Golden leads with 71 yards on four catches while Christian Watson has two catches for 55 yards. Prescott is 11-of-15 for 86 yards with two picks — both of which came in Green Bay territory. On the first, safety Evan Williams stepped in front of a pass intended for CeeDee Lamb at the 3-yard line. On the second, Lamb slipped on the turf, which allowed the ball to go Brandon Cisse. Cowboys linebacker Dee Winters is questionable to return with an ankle injury. He had an interception in the first half. Returner KaVonte Turpin has been downgraded to out with a rib injury. Green Bay tight end Tucker Kraft also suffered an apparent leg injury late in the second quarter. The Packers will have a chance to double up, as they’ll receive the second-half kickoff.
author: Myles Simmons

title: C.J. Gardner-Johnson: "I've got to control my emotions"
summary: During Sunday's game against the Raiders in Las Vegas, Bills safety C.J.
full_text: '' During Sunday's game against the Raiders in Las Vegas, Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected for spitting on an opponent. He addressed the situation after the game victory, without denying any of it. " I’ve got to be a better player , I've got to be a better vet," Gardner-Johnson said. "I let my emotions get above me, and I hurt my team. They brought me here to play in big games like this. So I've got to do better and control my emotions, nothing crazy." Asked specifically whether he spit on an opponent, Gardner-Johnson glossed over the question. "I've got to control my emotions," Gardner-Johnson said. "It was nothing towards competitive. We just — like I said, heat of the moment. Everybody saw what was going on. It wasn't nothing egregious against nobody. Like I said, we was just competing in the game. A call was made, a flag was made. We went to chirping. And I guess, you know, just being competitive, like I say, nothing towards [Raiders tight end] Brock [Bowers] and nothing towards the team. Like I said, we was chirping, going back and forth. I've got to be better and keep pushing." How did he process being required to leave before halftime? "You've got to take it on the chin like a grown man, and understand that you can't be doing shit like that in a game," Gardner-Johnson said. "No matter how passionate I am, I just can't be doing shit like that in the game. I cost my team. A player to go down, which is me, as a vet. I'll be better. I'll take my consequence as it is. A fine, whatever it may be." Gardner-Johnson also said he spoke to coach Joe Brady and apologized to the team. He also acknowledged that his "gesture isn't warranted." For his part, Brady said, "The discipline of our football team has to improve. And that sure as hell can’t happen . The team is bigger than that. The situation is bigger than that. Everything is bigger. And it can't happen. And it definitely has to be addressed." Again, Gardner-Johnson didn't specifically admit to doing it. Given the context, combined with his comments and his failure to deny doing it, it's clear that he knows he did it. The next question is whether he'll get a suspension to go along with an ejection that resulted in Gardner-Johnson missing half of Sunday's game.
author: Mike Florio

title: Shane Steichen on Daniel Jones' job: He's our starting quarterback
summary: The Colts signed Daniel Jones to a two-year, $88 million extension in the offseason, even though he was returning from a torn right Achilles.
full_text: '' The Colts signed Daniel Jones to a two-year, $88 million extension in the offseason, even though he was returning from a torn right Achilles. It does not currently look like a good decision, but coach Shane Steichen is not wavering on Jones as his starter. " I love Daniel , but we have to clean up the turnovers," Steichen said after the 26-20 loss to the Titans, via Stephen Holder of ESPN. Jones has multiple turnovers in three games this season and nine total turnovers after throwing two interceptions against the Titans. "I don't think it's been consistent enough. I think, certainly, today wasn't consistent enough," Jones said. The Colts have 2023 first-round pick Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard behind Jones. Steichen, though, said the Colts are not making a change. "He's our starting quarterback," Steichen said of Jones.
author: Charean Williams

title: Referee Shawn Smith: Umpire Tra Blake witnessed C.J. Gardner-Johnson spitting on an opponent
summary: Bills safety C.J.
full_text: ' Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the first half of Sunday's game against the Raiders. It appeared that Gardner-Johnson was ejected for spitting. After the game, referee Shawn Smith explained the decision to pool reporter Case Keefer. "We had two players jawing back and forth and then our umpire witnessed him spitting on the opponent ," Smith said. The umpire on Smith's crew is Tra Blake. The video seems to show Gardner-Johnson spitting in the direction of Raiders tight end Brock Bowers, with the spit either striking Raiders center Tyler Linderbaum's hand or Bowers's leg. Either way, Blake was right there to see it. "He saw him spit on the opponent," Smith said, regarding Blake's account of the situation. "So, we don't go into the judgment of where he is spitting and this, that, or the other. He spit on an opponent." The situation looked a lot like the incident between Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott and Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter from Week 1 of the 2025 season. After Prescott spit on the ground before the first play from scrimmage, Carter spit on Prescott.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jim Harbaugh on Mike McDaniel: We'll look at everything, offense needs to be addressed
summary: McDaniel could be dismissed as offensive coordinator after an 0-6 start.
full_text: '' The Chargers failed to score a touchdown in Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs and they head into their bye week under increased speculation about whether offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will still be on the staff when they return in Week 8. PFT reported " growing buzz " on Sunday that the Chargers will be parting ways with McDaniel after the team fell to 0-6 since putting him in charge of the offense. The Chargers have scored just 84 points in those six losses, which is a far cry from what many expected when McDaniel was hired to work with quarterback Justin Herbert in the offseason. Herbert threw his eighth interception on Sunday and has thrown at least one in each of the futile offensive performances. After Sunday's loss, head coach Jim Harbaugh was asked if McDaniel will be calling the plays when the team returns against the Rams in two weeks. "We're going to look at everything . . . . I feel bad for our players, our team, our coaches, our fans. And (the offense) needs to be addressed," Harbaugh said, via Noah Furtado of TheAthletic.com. If the Chargers do make a move with McDaniel, former Jets head coach and current pass game specialist Adam Gase is expected to take over the offensive reins.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jordan Love touchdown pass gives Packers 7-0 lead over Cowboys
summary: Dallas’ defense still looks porous to start Sunday night’s game against Green Bay.
full_text: ' Dallas’ defense still looks porous to start Sunday night’s game against Green Bay. Packers quarterback Jordan Love connected with receiver Matthew Golden for a 9-yard touchdown, giving the club a 7-0 lead. The 14-play, 90-yard drive took 6:30 off the clock. Though the Packers didn’t really get anything going on the ground, Jordan Love moved it just fine through the air. He was 6-of-8 for 109 yards with a TD to open the contest. Two penalties moved Green Bay back, allowing for that yardage on what was technically a 90-yard possession. Golden caught the touchdown and had a big 37-yard catch to move the chains — though he was flagged for taunting. Christian Watson also had a 27-yard reception on the possession. Green Bay was 4-of-4 on third down. The Cowboys had to punt to end their first possession after gaining one first down. Dallas returner KaVontae Turpin has a rib injury and is questionable to return. He was hurt on the opening kickoff. Tyler Goodson has come in to replace Turpin as a kickoff returner.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Caleb Williams "just let it rip" in his return from hamstring tear
summary: Caleb Williams had one question for the media as he made his way into the tunnel toward the visiting locker room.
full_text: '' Caleb Williams had one question for the media as he made his way into the tunnel toward the visiting locker room. " Y’all like that ?" Williams asked rhetorically, smiling, via Courtney Cronin of ESPN. The Bears quarterback returned after missing three games with a torn hamstring. He completed his first 12 passes and finished 30-of-36 for 305 yards and a touchdown. "I felt confident from the jump," Williams said. "When I get out there, I'm going to feel confident in my leg, in myself and in my guys and the O-line. So I just let it rip, let these guys go make plays for us, get first downs and score touchdowns." The Bears now have a quick turnaround, with a Thursday night game against the Patriots looming. Despite four sacks, Williams said he is no worse for wear in his first game back. "Felt great to get hit after three weeks of just rehabbing," Williams said. "So [I] feel strong, feel good. Obviously got to go and take care of it this week. It's going to be a weekly thing, just taking care of it, staying up to date on it and taking care of my body."
author: Charean Williams

title: Former Broncos G.M. John Beake dies at 87
summary: Former Broncos G.M.
full_text: ' Former Broncos G.M. John Beake recently died. He was 87. Beake, pictured with former Broncos coach Dan Reeves, spent 22 years with the Denver organization. He served as the General Manager until 2000. "The Broncos are saddened by the passing of longtime executive John Beake, who made an enduring impact on our organization during more than two decades with the team," the Broncos said in a statement. "John helped guide the Broncos to five Super Bowl appearances, including back-to-back World Championships , and was a respected leader throughout one of the most successful eras in franchise history. Following his time in Denver, he remained an influential figure through his work with the NFL and on the Broncos Ring of Fame Committee. Our deepest condolences are with his wife, Marcia, his sons, Chip and Chris, and the entire Beake family." Before joining the Broncos in 1979, he worked as an assistant coach with the Chiefs from 1968 to 1974 and the Saints from 1976 through 1977. Beake was on Hank Stram's coaching staff when Kansas City won Super Bowl IV. After leaving the Broncos, Beake worked for the league office.
author: Mike Florio

title: A.J. Brown: I'm much better than what I put on display
summary: The Patriots were excited to get wide receiver A.J.
full_text: ' The Patriots were excited to get wide receiver A.J. Brown back in the lineup on Sunday, but Brown showed a lot of rust after missing the last four games with an ankle injury. Brown was targeted 10 times by quarterback Drake Maye, but finished with three catches and three drops. He also muffed an onside kick after the Jets drew within seven points late in the fourth quarter and was bailed out when tight end Eli Raridon corralled the loose ball to secure a 26-19 win. "I didn't play good. I don't know, like, my timing was off," Brown said after the game. "I'm much better than what I put on display today. There's no excuses. I'll be better." Brown called himself "more than capable" of making the plays he failed to make on Sunday and said nothing related to the injury factored into the rough day. Brown will get a chance to shake off the rocky return quickly because the Patriots face the Bears on Thursday night. The team's need for him to return to form will be even greater if Romeo Doubs is not able to play after hurting his shoulder while catching a touchdown early in Sunday's win.
author: Josh Alper

title: Chargers have a decision to make about offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel
summary: With no wins in six games and an average of 15.0 points per game, a change could be coming.
full_text: '' The Chargers enter their bye with an 0-6 record. On Sunday, their offense scored only two field goals in a 22-6 loss to the Chiefs. And the next move very well could be a separation from employment of first-year offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. There's a growing buzz that the Chargers will be making that move, soon. Pass game specialist Adam Gase, a former head coach of the Jets and Dolphins, is expected to take over, if McDaniel is fired. McDaniel spent four years as head coach of the Dolphins, after five years as an assistant with the 49ers. The Chargers have scored 90 points in six games, an average of 15.0 points per game. It's not done yet, but it's the move that many are expecting to see. Especially with the Chargers limping into their annual week off — which will be followed by a "road" game in their home stadium, against the 2-4 Rams.
author: Mike Florio

title: Andy Dalton tells Eagles "no thanks," will sign with another team soon
summary: With starting quarterback Jalen Hurts out indefinitely, the Eagles have had to scramble to fill out the depth chart.
full_text: ' With starting quarterback Jalen Hurts out indefinitely, the Eagles have had to scramble to fill out the depth chart. Tanner McKee started on Sunday against the Panthers. They also have rookie Cole Payton, and they added Joe Milton from the Cowboys' practice squad. They had 16-year veteran Andy Dalton, but the Eagles cut him nine days ago. They wanted to bring him back, but Dalton has politely declined, we're told. Dalton, who has played for the Bengals, Cowboys, Bears, Saints, Panthers, and Eagles, will be signing with a team other than the Eagles as soon as tomorrow. And his arrival in a new city likely will trigger a current member of the quarterback room making his exit. Which would then, frankly, make that player a potential option for the Eagles.
author: Mike Florio

title: Chiefs stay unbeaten, Chargers stay winless
summary: The Chiefs scored nine points on their first two possessions of Sunday's home game against the Chargers and that would be all they'd need to move their record to 5-0 on the season.
full_text: The Chiefs scored nine points on their first two possessions of Sunday's home game against the Chargers and that would be all they'd need to move their record to 5-0 on the season. Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert threw his eighth interception of the season, wide receiver KeAndre Lambert-Smith lost a fumble and the Chiefs broke a three-game sackless streak by dropping Herbert four times in a 22-6 win. The loss drops the Chargers to 0-6 on the season and sends them into their bye week without any signs that things are getting better. While there was plenty to like about the defensive effort on Sunday, the Chiefs probably won't be thrilled with the way the rest of the team performed in the second half of the game. They failed on a fourth down on their first possession of the third quarter and then saw punt returner Nikko Remigio lose a fumble to give the Chargers another chance. They forced another punt, but punted the ball back and then missed a field goal to allow the Chargers to hang around even as they did their best to give the game away. Kenneth Walker ran for a pair of scores to help stake the team to a 19-3 halftime lead and is now up to eight in his first five games with the Chiefs. He finished the day with 128 yards on 19 carries while Patrick Mahomes was 23-of-30 for 272 yards. Those numbers would point to more scoring, but the missed kick and a Mahomes interception in the end zone in the first half contributed to the relatively modest output. Mahomes completed passes to eight different receivers with Rashee Rice out of the game, which is a positive for the overall offensive depth in Kansas City moving forward. They did lose right tackle Jaylon Moore to a concussion during the game, which could be an issue when they head to Seattle for one of Week 7's marquee matchups. The Chargers will not have to leave Los Angeles for their return to the field in Week 8, although they'll be the road team in their game against the Rams. Both teams have wildly underperformed expectations to this point in the season — the Cardinals have more wins at SoFi Stadium than the two tenants combined — and it will be interesting to see what kinds of changes the Chargers make during their bye week in an attempt to salvage something of what's already a lost season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bills hold off Raiders 33-30 to move to 5-1
summary: Bills quarterbcak Josh Allen was 23-of-33 for 255 yards and two touchdowns.
full_text: The Raiders hung with the Bills. The game was tied 13-13 at halftime and 23-23 in the fourth quarter. It never felt like the Bills were in danger of losing, though the Raiders never went away. Josh Allen led Buffalo to a 33-30 win in Las Vegas as the Bills moved to 5-1. The Raiders fell to 3-3. The Bills gained 345 yards, with 169 coming in the second half when they scored 20 points. Allen was 23-of-33 for 255 yards and two touchdowns, including a Houdini-esque 12-yard touchdown pass to Keon Coleman on third-and-8 in the fourth quarter. James Cook's 3-yard touchdown run with 4:43 left was the go-ahead score, with Tyler Bass adding a 38-yard field goal with 1:56 remaining. Bass also made kicks from 44, 28 and 47. Coleman caught four passes for 59 yards and a touchdown, and Cook had 22 carries for 95 yards and a touchdown. The Raiders made it interesting on Kirk Cousins' 44-yard touchdown throw to Tre Tucker with 1:32 left. The Raiders, though, didn't have a prayer of recovering the onside kick, something they haven't done since 2017 against the Chiefs. Matt Gay kicked a drop kick too far, and Khalil Shakir caught it in the air. Cousins finished 23-of-41 for 313 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. Tucker had five catches for 97 yards and two touchdowns, and Michael Mayer added seven receptions for 95 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Joey Porter Jr. is active for the Cowboys on Sunday night
summary: The Cowboys will have cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in the lineup against the Packers on Sunday night.
full_text: ' The Cowboys will have cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in the lineup against the Packers on Sunday night. Porter played in Week 4 after being acquired in a trade with the Steelers, but he sat out last week's loss to the Buccaneers with an illness. The Cowboys listed him as questionable to play this week due to a foot injury, but he is ready to make his second appearance with the team. The Cowboys ruled cornerback Cobie Durant and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown out over the last couple of days. Safety Alijah Clark, running back Emari Demercado, linebacker James Houston, offensive lineman Drew Shelton, and wide receiver Camden Brown are also inactive. Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse will play after being listed as questionable with a hip injury. Cornerback Benjamin St-Juste, offensive lineman Jager Burton, offensive lineman Aaron Banks, and offensive lineman Donovan Jennings are their inactive players.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cardinals stun Rams, defeat Los Angeles 18-16
summary: A Super Bowl favorite to begin the season, the Rams have now fallen to 2-4 in 2026.
full_text: Maybe the Cardinals should only play at SoFi Stadium. Arizona got its second win of the season on Sunday, stunning the Rams 18-16 for the club’s second victory of the season. The first came Week 1 at the same venue over the Chargers. Entering the week at No. 26 in yards allowed and No. 32 in points allowed, Arizona stifled Los Angeles’ offense throughout the contest. The Rams barely had 100 yards at halftime with three three-and-outs. It didn’t help that the team lost its new kicker, Blake Grupe, to a knee injury early in the game when he made a tackle on a kickoff. But the Cardinals were able to control the ball and the clock throughout the afternoon, winning time of possession 34:52 to 25:08. And while the club never reached the end zone, Chad Ryland was automatic in Rams territory with his six field goals — including his 43-yard make as time expired to give Arizona the win. Los Angeles got to the end zone twice — once with Blake Corum’s 15-yard touchdown reception in the second quarter. It then took them until there were 47 seconds left on the clock for Matthew Stafford to find Colby Parkinson for a 6-yard touchdown. With Grupe out, punter Ethan Evans put the Rams ahead with a successful extra point. But that lead did not hold, as Jacoby Brissett connected with Jalen Brooks for a 21-yard completion to open the ensuing Cardinals possession. An unnecessary roughness penalty tacked on 15 yards, putting Arizona in clear field goal range. A few plays later, Ryland sent his sixth kick through the uprights for the win. Brissett ended the day 24-of-35 passing for 218 yards with an interception. Trey McBride led with seven catches for 53 yards. On the other side, Stafford finished 25-of-33 for 222 yards with two touchdowns. Puka Nacua had six receptions for 80 yards. Davante Adams — who hopped off the field late in the fourth quarter with an apparent leg injury — had three catches for 39 yards. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this season — two — than the Rams and Chargers, who have a combined one. At 2-4, Arizona will be at home to host the Broncos in Week 7. The 2-4 Rams are reeling and will be in Las Vegas next weekend to play the Raiders.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Kirk Cousins' TD pass has Raiders tied with Bills 23-23
summary: The Bills were in control until they weren't.
full_text: The Bills were in control until they weren't. The Raiders have scored 10 points in the fourth quarter to tie the Bills 23-23 with 8:07 remaining in the fourth quarter. Las Vegas reached the Buffalo 4 before settling for a 23-yard Matt Gay field goal, a 15-play, 70-yard drive. After forcing a Buffalo punt, Kirk Cousins hit Tre Tucker for an 11-yard touchdown. The touchdown came on third-and-8. The Raiders now have 334 yards, with Cousins going 22-of-36 for 269 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Michael Mayer has seven catches for 95 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Alvin Kamara reaches 5,000 career receiving yards, puts Saints up 17-10
summary: Saints running back Alvin Kamara reached a career milestone while putting his team in the lead for the first time on Sunday.
full_text: '' Saints running back Alvin Kamara reached a career milestone while putting his team in the lead for the first time on Sunday. Kamara took a short pass from Tyler Shough and carved through the Giants defense for a 31-yard touchdown. The score capped the first possession of the second half and put the Saints up 17-10 with 12:21 to play in the third quarter. The catch was Kamara's first of the day and it moved him over 5,000 receiving yards for his career. Per the Fox broadcast, he's the sixth player in NFL history with 5,000-plus rushing yards as well as 5,000-plus receiving yards. The Giants had a 10-0 lead in the first half, but they'll now have to play catchup to avoid falling to 3-2-1 on the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Panthers lead Eagles 10-7 at halftime
summary: The Panthers led 10-0 before the Eagles made things interesting.
full_text: ' The Panthers led 10-0 before the Eagles made things interesting. Tanner McKee, starting for Jalen Hurts, led Philadelphia on a 10-play, 78-yard drive with Dameon Pierce scoring on a 2-yard run with 2:42 remaining in the first half. Carolina leads 10-7 at halftime. On their touchdown drive, the Eagles benefited with a 22-yard defensive pass interference penalty on rookie Will Lee, who pulled down Dallas Goedert's pants. It was Lee's second DPI, and set up Pierce's touchdown run. The Panthers have outgained the Eagles 178 to 110, with Bryce Young going 12-of-21 for 162 yards and a touchdown. Tetairoa McMillan has five catches for 79 yards. McKee is 13-of-23 for 94 yards, with Goedert catching four passes for 38 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: 49ers vs. Commanders how to watch: 'Monday Night Football' time, channel, odds and prediction
summary: San Francisco can improve to 6-0 and strengthen its NFC West lead, while Washington enters Levi's Stadium looking to pull off a sizable road upset
full_text:
In the Week 6 edition of "Monday Night Football," the San Francisco 49ers play host to the Washington Commanders .
San Francisco is riding high atop the NFC West with a 5-0 record, having defeated the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in a barnburner last week. The Niners have battled injuries on both sides of the ball all season, yet have remained unbeaten. They can create a three-game lead in the division with a victory on Monday night.
Washington is coming off an absolute debacle last Sunday against the New York Giants , wherein the Commanders had a chance to kick a field goal to win the game at the end of overtime, but bungled the clock management as badly as any team you'll ever see. The Commies are just 1-3-1 entering this game, and they're looking to avoid falling further into the basement in the NFC East.
Will the Niners continue to roll, or will the Commanders pull off the upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Jayden Daniels looked no worse for wear last week in his return from another dislocated elbow. He completed 17 of 25 passes for 199 yards, while also rushing nine times for 103 yards and two touchdowns. Had he and the entire offense not totally brain-farted at the end of overtime, it would have been a wildly encouraging performance for Washington's rest-of-season outlook.
While Daniels has been excellent when taking off to run in his three starts, Washington's running backs have been extremely inefficient on the ground. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (who was ruled out for this game after not practicing all week), Rachaad White , Austin Ekeler and the recently-released Kaytron Allen have combined to average just 3.7 yards per carry. The offensive line has created little push up front, with the backs collectively gaining just 0.95 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, and the backs themselves have broken tackles at the second-lowest rate in all of football.
The 49ers, meanwhile, have allowed just 3.7 yards per rush to enemy running backs, with great tackling being the primary method of limiting yardage. Backs have gained 1.47 yards per carry before contact (an above-average mark), but only 2.22 yards after contact thanks to the lowest broken-tackle rate in the league. As a result, San Francisco has allowed only two explosive runs all season, per Tru Media, the fewest in the NFL .
San Francisco has also been mostly strong against the pass, checking in 10th in opponents' EPA per dropback and 5th in opponents' success rate. The 49ers have allowed quarterbacks to complete only 64.4% of their passes at an average of 6.1 yards per attempt, with just five touchdowns and three interceptions in five games.
It's tough to know what to make of Washington's passing game because it hasn't been at full strength for most of the season. Daniels missed two-and-a-half games. Chig Okonwko missed two. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs each missed one and saw their snaps limited in another. The Daniels-McLaurin-Diggs trio has shared the field for only 57 plays so far this season, according to Tru Media. Daniels is just 15 of 30 for 129 yards on those plays, but he has thrown for three scores and scrambled for 62 yards.
Daniels should, in theory, see at least some clean pockets with the 49ers again playing without Nick Bosa , but Washington's offensive line has yielded pressure on over 38% of dropbacks so far this season, so the Niners could have a chance to get into Daniels' lap and force him into tough throws and mistakes. With the generally sticky coverage the San Francisco corners have played so far this season, it could be tough sledding for Washington in the passing game on Monday night.
San Francisco has been the league's fourth-most efficient offense by EPA per play, according to Tru Media, ranking second with the pass and 14th with the run. Brock Purdy is playing at as high a level as any quarterback in football, completing 69% of his passes at an average of 8.4 yards per attempt with a league-high 13 touchdown passes and just two interceptions. Purdy also has a 57.9% passing success rate, which ranks as the best in the league.
Purdy has done that despite hemorrhaging wide receivers throughout the season. Ricky Pearsall was lost for the year in training camp. Christian Kirk (listed as questionable for this week) has yet to make his 49er debut. De'Zhaun Stribling was injured in Week 1. Demarcus Robinson went down in Week 2. Deebo Samuel and Jacob Cowing were knocked out of last week's win over the Seahawks. Mike Evans has been playing through a painful rib injury. (He's also questionable for Monday night.) George Kittle spent the first two weeks ramping up to a full workload after last season's Achilles tear. And yet, here the 49ers are.
Washington, meanwhile, has been one of the league's friendliest pass defenses. Every team the Commanders have faced has thrown for at least 257 net yards. Four of the five teams have gone more than 300 and two of them exceeded 400. The Commanders have allowed opponents to complete 65.2% of passes at an average of 7.1 yards per attempt, with 14 touchdowns and just three interceptions. The 103.9 passer rating against the Commanders to date is the sixth-worst mark in the league. It's very easy to see San Francisco finding success through the air so long as Evans suits up for the game.
Christian McCaffrey is sharing the workload in the run game far more this season than in years past, with 61 carries for 286 yards againt Kaelon Black's 37 carries for 136 yards. McCaffrey's 4.7 yards-per-carry average is far better than what he posted over the last two years (4.0 and 3.9), and his rushing success rate of 45.9% is seventh-best out of 48 qualifying running backs. That figure is the second-best mark of his career, behind only the 2023 season, during which he led the NFL in rushing yards.
The Commanders have actually been stingy against the run this year, allowing only 3.9 yards per carry, with opposing backs limited to 0.69 yards per attempt before contact by the defensive front. Washington having similar success stopping the run here is important because it could make the 49ers one-dimensional, but the Commanders' pass-funnel defense also plays right into San Francisco's hands because of how efficient the 49ers' passing game has been so far this year. Purdy and Co. should eat, even if McCaffrey doesn't.
I picked against the 49ers last week and regretted it almost immediately after seeing how their offense struggled against the stingy Seattle defense. Needless to say, Washington's defense is not of the same quality. I know the 49ers are still hemorrhaging wide receivers, but as long as Brock Purdy, Mike Evans, George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey are healthy and Kyle Shanahan is calling the plays, they are going to move the ball efficiently. And I don't trust the Commanders to do quite enough to keep up with their explosive offense.
Pick: 49ers 27, Commanders 16
author: Jared Dubin

title: Giants have a QB controversy: J.J. McCarthy makes case to replace Jameis Winston
summary: The Giants must decide whether to ride McCarthy's momentum immediately or give him the Week 8 bye to prepare for a potential change
full_text:
The New York Giants have a quarterback question to address. Jameis Winston is 2-1-1 in his four starts under center in place of the injured Jaxson Dart , but the team also traded for J.J. McCarthy last month, who received his first extensive action as a Giant during Sunday's 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints .
After Winston threw his second interception of the game and set up the Saints with an opportunity to extend their lead to 24 points, John Harbaugh made the decision to replace him with McCarthy. The former No. 10 overall pick of the Minnesota Vikings came in and led three straight scoring drives, and had the Giants in position to send the game to overtime. McCarthy completed 11 of 21 passes for 243 yards, one touchdown and one interception, and may have stolen the starting job from Winston.
The Giants sit atop the NFC East with a 3-2-1 record. With the Dallas Cowboys ' tragic defense and Jalen Hurts sidelined indefinitely with a blood clot, New York has an inside track to a playoff berth. This is not just a lost season because Dart went down in Week 2. So, should Harbaugh start McCarthy in Week 7 when the Giants travel to Houston to take on the Texans ? Or, should he stick with Winston? Let's take a look at some pros and cons of promoting McCarthy to starter.
If you watched the Giants game on Sunday, you know how frustrating it was. New York jumped out to a 10-0 lead -- only to allow the Saints to score 34 unanswered points. With the game tied at halftime, the Saints scored 17 points in the third quarter, while the Giants went three-and-out and then turned the ball over. After another three-and-out followed by another interception, Harbaugh knew something had to be done. That's when McCarthy went in.
McCarthy threw an interception on his fourth passing attempt, but then led a six-play, 52-yard drive that was capped by a Tyrone Tracy Jr. touchdown and a successful Isaiah Likely two-point conversion to trim the deficit to 16 points. Following a Saints three-and-out, McCarthy took the Giants offense 73 yards down the field on just three plays, and hit Likely for a 24-yard touchdown to make it a 10-point game.
McCarthy was given the opportunity to lead a game-tying drive with 57 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter with zero timeouts. It came down to a fourth-and-1 from the Saints' 14-yard line, where McCarthy couldn't connect with Likely in the end zone.
McCarthy's 243 passing yards were the most in a game in the last 35 years by a quarterback with zero passing yards through three quarters, per CBS Sports Research. He came in and turned a 34-10 game into a 34-27 game. That's tough to ignore.
This game has already established that there is a quarterback controversy. Why not ride the hot hand?
JJ McCarthy SHINED in his Giants debut: - 243 Passing Yards - 26 Rushing Yards - 1 TD, 1 INT All in just one quarter. pic.twitter.com/QGjADfd7eI
It's understood why the Vikings moved on from McCarthy. He completed 57.6% of his passes for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions last season, and was holding back a team that boasted a top-three defense and a talented supporting cast headlined by Justin Jefferson . McCarthy became the only first-round pick at quarterback since 1970 to finish last in completion percentage and TD-INT ratio in their debut season.
McCarthy is a 23-year-old kid who just got to the Giants three weeks ago. I want to know how he's coming along in learning Matt Nagy's offense. Does he have enough of a handle on it to start, run the operation effectively and handle whatever wrinkles Nagy may want to throw in? McCarthy looked pretty good on Sunday, but that situation was entirely different. The Giants were down double digits in the fourth quarter of a game. McCarthy came in with zero pressure and just tried to make plays downfield. Playground football. It's not like you can claim McCarthy came in and "ran the offense." I'm curious how comfortable he is with this brand-new playbook, and how much Nagy would have to change the game plan if Harbaugh made the call to change quarterbacks.
This may be the best argument for starting McCarthy right now. He entered the game in the fourth quarter and ended up leading the Giants in rushing yards. On the first play of what could have been the game-tying drive, McCarthy scrambled up the middle for 28 yards -- getting the ball from the Giants' 29-yard line into enemy territory quickly. Winston can't do that.
McCarthy isn't Lamar Jackson by any means, but he will tuck and run if you give him that opportunity. He's more capable of moving the chains with his legs and keeping defenses honest than Winston.
The Texans may be 2-4, but they are certainly finding their rhythm. Houston has strung together two straight victories after DeMeco Ryans took back play-calling duties on defense, including a 34-31 upset of the Jacksonville Jaguars across the pond. The Texans no longer statistically have one of the league's top defenses, but this is still an aggressive unit capable of pressuring the quarterback.
Danielle Hunter and Will Anderson Jr . make up the best pass-rushing duo in the NFL , and the Giants could potentially be down their top two tackles. Right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor missed this week with a calf injury, while left tackle Andrew Thomas left Sunday's game early to be evaluated for a concussion. A road matchup against a surging Texans team is not exactly a conducive situation for a young quarterback learning a new offense to make his first start.
The Giants have a Week 7 date with the Texans in Houston, and then will enjoy their bye in Week 8. Week 9 against a Jalen Hurts-less Philadelphia Eagles team could be the ideal time to promote McCarthy. You give him the bye and a full week of practice before he takes over your team. That makes sense, and gives Winston one more chance to save his job.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: NFL Week 6 grades for every team that played so far: Browns, Steelers earn high marks, Colts get 'F'
summary: We're handing out grades for every Week 6 game, and we don't hold back
full_text:
Welcome to the Week 6 grades!
You know the NFL season has been turned upside down when the Cleveland Browns are in first place, and that's exactly what we have after their wild comeback win over the Raven s. It was a wild week in the AFC North, which is suddenly looking like the best division in the NFL.
How rough is the AFC North? The Bengals (3-2) were tied for second place going into their Week 6 bye, and after everything that happened on Sunday, they're now in last place.
Let's get to the Week 6 grades, starting with Cleveland's win over Baltimore.
author: John Breech

title: NFL Week 6 overreactions: Time for Colts to clean house? A.J. Brown trade a mistake for Patriots?
summary: Indianapolis blew a 13-0 lead in a loss to the previously winless Titans
full_text:
The battle between two of the NFL's most woebegone franchises lived up to its lack of hype Sunday. In fact, in terms of excitement, it more than lived up to it. But the on-field product was a special sort of fun-bad.
Titans 26, Colts 20. It's the first win of the year for Tennessee, and a stunning one at that. The Titans trailed 13-0 at halftime and looked completely lifeless. Bench Cam Ward ? Throw in the towel? It seemed on the brink.
And then the Colts, being the generous team they are, quite literally gave it away over the next four possessions:
From up 13-0 to down 20-13 in about 18 minutes of game time. Horrifying stuff. The Colts actually tied the game on a Taylor touchdown, only for the defense to commit an awful pass interference to set up a Titans field goal. Tennessee tacked on another field goal late.
A collapse in all three stages? Against a winless team? For an organization already skating on thin ice? Check, check, check. Which leads me to say ...
Overreaction or reality: Reality
Since 2020, there have been 16 in-season coaching changes. Shane Steichen will either be the next or, at the very least, join that list.
This was an unacceptable collapse. The Titans are completely inept offensively. The only way they could do anything was if the Colts blew it, and the Colts blew it over and over again. I've generally been a proponent of Steichen as a good offensive mind, but as a head coach, you have to be more than that. You are responsible for everything, and in that matter, Indianapolis isn't close to good enough.
Steichen can't play the game, though, so we turn to the players ... and the person who chose them. Chris Ballard is in his 10th season as Colts GM. The team has one playoff win over that span, and it was back in 2018, his second year. He has been completely unable to find a quarterback, and his latest attempt is turning out as bad as the others.
Remember, at the start of Ballard's tenure, he had Andrew Luck. Andrew Luck retired ahead of the 2019 season. It's been that long. Inexcusable. He has tried half-measures with veterans. He tried drafting one ( Anthony Richardson ). He has failed in every measure. The defense remains iffy at best, even after the blockbuster ( and, in retrospect, misjudged ) Sauce Gardner trade.
But really, it all comes back to Jones: He was 22-for-42 for 269 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions. He took six sacks. He's tied for the NFL lead in turnovers. Sunday, he simply did not put an NFL-caliber product on the field.
INT by Flott‼️ 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/XuoBtoPyIe
Remember, the Colts signed him to a two-year, $88 million deal over the offseason, even though they were bidding with ... no one. There is an out after this year that would carry $35 million in dead cap, but continuing with him would be even more punitive for a franchise long overdue for a reset.
Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon is known for standing on the sideline and keeping notes. Her only notes needed from Sunday? It's time to clean house.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
This is simply a non-playoff team right now. Here are the stunning numbers from the Rams ' stunning 18-16 loss to the Cardinals :
Sean McVay summed it up aptly: "There's nothing positive that I can say about today."
The offense has very little juice, outside an occasional excellent play by Puka Nacua or Davante Adams . It just feels really stagnant; Stafford used play action on 37% of his dropbacks last year and averaged 8.4 yards per pass on those throws. This year, it's down to 25% and 7.2, respectively. And when a team doesn't have juice, it has little room for error. But the Rams keep making errors: penalties, turnovers, missed assignments, etc.
Meanwhile, the defense just isn't causing much havoc. And the special teams issues remain. New kicker Blake Grupe got hurt in the first quarter, forcing the Rams to adjust on the fly.
Even if the Rams had won, it's not close to good enough. Sean McVay said as much. If they lose in Week 7, it's officially panic time.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
JOSH ALLEN DOING JOSH ALLEN THINGS!!!! 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/F0GGilwmd6
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
Well, well, well, if it isn't a three-way tie atop the AFC North through six weeks?! The Browns , Steelers and Ravens are all 4-2, and the Bengals (on bye this weekend) aren't far behind at 3-2.
Cleveland technically leads the division thanks to Sunday's 13-10 win over Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore, and Pittsburgh is second because it has a better in-division record.
Sorry, Browns and Steelers fans, but neither one of you is winning the division. Cleveland's largest win this season is by four points. It lost to the Jets just last week. Deshaun Watson looked awful Sunday. The Steelers looked similarly awful, needing a late comeback to force overtime against the Baker Mayfield-less Buccaneers . As it turns out, playing against backup quarterbacks is very helpful.
Both teams rank in the bottom half of most major offensive stats. The quarterback play simply isn't good enough and won't be good enough, especially when put up against Lamar Jackson and Joe Burrow rather than Tyler Huntley and Jalon Daniels .
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
A.J. Brown's grand return from IR was ... not so grand. Three catches for 27 yards on 10 targets. Officially, he's been charged with two drops. Unofficially, given his high standards, it was probably more. He even bobbled away a Jets onside kick, but lucky for him, a teammate recovered to clinch the Patriots ' 26-19 win.
It's worth being concerned about the debut, but to say the trade is a bust or a mistake would be a drastic overreaction. Yes, it's been a tough start with the injury and the underwhelming return. But let's not write it off. He won on the routes New England brought him in to win: quick in-breakers and deep balls. Drake Maye missed him on one of each, and Brown failed to finish other opportunities he did have. It sounds like a silly thing to say, but if you cut the tape right before the ball arrives, Brown's film would look encouraging.
Of course, he has to make the plays that are there. Getting open doesn't gain yards, score points or win games. Brown will bounce back, and he can still be a huge boost. He came back from his high ankle sprain earlier than expected. Let's give him a week's worth of grace.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
Another week, another outstanding performance for C.J. Stroud . The fourth-year pro threw for 312 yards, three touchdowns and an interception and led the game-winning drive in the Texans ' 34-31 win over the Jaguars .
The numbers are one thing, but the film is just as good, if not better. This is one of the best throws you will see all season.
WHAT A THROW FROM CJ STROUD. HOUvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Z8LUxZceAl
Foster had to double it! 📺: @nflnetwork pic.twitter.com/srjLPbSesF
This is Stroud at his best: laser-accurate, huge arm, can access every part of the field. It's been missed the past few years, and the Texans should be very glad it's back. Not only that, but he is improving at mitigating negative plays. His interception Sunday was really bad, but it was his first all year. He's also taking fewer devastating sacks than he did last season. And he's doing it all while still not having much of a run game.
The Texans and Stroud didn't reach an extension in the offseason. He had been awful in the playoffs, and while both sides said the right things, no agreement happened.
He is very much on the way to earning that massive extension this offseason, though. This offseason is setting up to be a huge one for quarterback deals — Caleb Williams , Jayden Daniels , Drake Maye and Bo Nix from the 2024 class, Bryce Young from Stroud's 2023 class and Lamar Jackson are all looking for a new deal. Stroud's deal will put him among the top five highest-paid quarterbacks, and it will be well-deserved.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
The Panthers topped the…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Meltdown in LA: What went wrong for Rams as Cardinals earn largest upset of the season
summary: The Rams fall to 2-4 and have a whole host of issues
full_text:
As Chad Ryland 's 43-yard field goal went through the uprights as time expired, the Cardinals capped a wild finish and opened up a whole new set of questions for Los Angeles. The kick, which gave the Cardinals an 18-16 win over the Rams , marked the largest upset of the season. Arizona, which entered as 13.5-point underdogs, also tied for the largest upset of any game in the past five years. It was the largest upset loss of Matthew Stafford's career thus far.
The Cardinals, who did not score a single touchdown, led 15-12 with under three minutes left. Stafford led a quick touchdown drive, fueled by big completions to Puka Nacua and capped by a 5-yard touchdown pass to Colby Parkinson with 47 seconds left. Punter Ethan Evans made the extra point after new kicker Blake Grupe got hurt making a tackle earlier in the game .
The Rams then kicked off into the end zone — sending the ball to the Cardinals' 35-yard line — and Jacoby Brissett found Jalen Brooks for a 21-yard play on the first play of the drive. Add in a 15-yard unnecessary roughness penalty on Josh Wallace , and that was all it took to set up Ryland's game-winner.
BRISSETT TO BROOKS PAST MIDFIELD AZvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YcxBytI37I
Give tons of credit to the Cardinals, who earned their first win since the season opener. The maligned defense had a major bounce back after allowing 45 points last week to the Lions , and the offense rolled up 338 yards and scored on six of its 10 drives. Yes, all the scores were field goals, but Arizona's ability to stay on track — Brissett didn't take a single sack and didn't turn it over after the first possession — was key. Arizona had nearly 10 minutes more of possession time than Los Angeles did.
But this is really on the Rams, who are 2-4 after entering the season as the Super Bowl favorite. In fact, it's the same record as the Cardinals.
The offense was disjointed, the defense failed to make the big plays, and special teams issues loomed large again.
Before the madness at the end of the game, it looked like this would be the defining play of the game: fourth-and-8, and the Rams do this.
Pass is incomplete and the Cardinals force a turnover on downs 👀 AZvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/u0bfxJgdFJ
A running back screen — and a failed one at that — in that situation sums up the Rams offense's woeful day. Stafford finished 25-for-33 for 222 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions, but before that, it was an absolute slog: 18-for-26 for just 137 yards. Add in three sacks, and Stafford had a putrid 4.2 yards per attempt.
Stafford was getting rid of the ball in 2.50 seconds. He had thrown two deep passes. He was averaging 4.6 yards downfield per throw; for reference, Bo Nix is at 4.9 yards, and that's the lowest number through six games in the past 20 years.
In other words, basically nothing in the explosive department. The Rams had only two plays of 20+ yards, and both came on the last drive. Keep in mind this is a defense that allowed five plays of 20+ yards in three quarters against the Lions in Week 5.
There were a few opportunities for big plays — Stafford missed an open Nacua on one notable one — but largely, the quick-passing game appeared planned, and the Cardinals dominated it.
If big plays aren't on the menu, there's no margin for error elsewhere. The Rams had plenty of mistakes, though. Arguably, the biggest was a Tyler Higbee fumble.
SIMON + BURKE ON THE FUMBLE AND RECOVERY 😮‍💨 #AZvsLAR | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/QyCLr3X7wZ
The play before that, Stafford stumbled and fumbled — untouched — when trying to wheel out of the pocket. He recovered the ball, but it set the Rams way behind the sticks on another unforced error. And in another key moment, Los Angeles failed on a fourth-and-1 on a run by backup tight end Davis Allen , a curious play call at best.
The Rams also committed four penalties, three crucial:
The Rams are tied for the 12th-most offensive penalties and tied for the fourth-most defensive penalties this season.
After a Brissett interception on the first drive, the Rams did not have another takeaway. They also recorded zero sacks against a quarterback who's among the more statuesque in the game and an offense down its top offensive lineman ( Paris Johnson Jr. ) and its top running back ( Jeremiyah Love ).
The Rams have eight sacks all year. Entering "Sunday Night Football" that is tied for the third-fewest in the NFL . And four of those eight came in one game, against the offensively hapless Eagles . Myles Garrett's absence is a major issue, but several other talented pass rushers aren't getting it done.
Grupe nailed his first field goal attempt, a 44-yarder, in the first quarter. Good news! But the Rams gave up a 40-yard return to Devin Duvernay on the ensuing kickoff, and Grupe hurt his knee making the tackle.
New Rams kicker Blake Grupe is doubtful to return after making this tackle pic.twitter.com/EgxKFTFSsq
The Rams have now lost games by two, three and four points, and special teams problems have featured heavily in all three. The Grupe injury is out of their control, but it came after they allowed yet another huge kickoff return.
Simply put, the Rams have huge problems in all three phases, a truly stunning sentence to type. A team all-in on a Super Bowl just lost to a team that's been counted out for months. Sean McVay's nightmare start continues to get worse.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: NFL Week 6 winners and losers: Giants face QB, RB turmoil while Browns take control of AFC North
summary: Jameis Winston and Cam Skattebo spent time on the bench in a disappointing home loss for New York, but the story in Cleveland is much happier
full_text:
A little over a month ago, Jameis Winston watching a New York Giants game from the sideline would have been a non-story. In Week 6, it was a defining reality of the team's disheartening 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints . That is how far the Giants have fallen since their exciting season-opening win. Everything is still in front of them, and they might just have found their starting quarterback for the rest of the year in J.J. McCarthy , but there is no other way to define Sunday's defeat as a step backward.
Meanwhile, another team that has spent the majority of this decade at the bottom of its division is on the rise. The Cleveland Browns won their fourth game of the year this week and now hold tiebreakers over two of their rivals as they stand atop the AFC North. Preseason expectations? Forget about them. Deshaun Watson has the Browns cooking.
The dichotomy between winners and losers is always stark in the NFL , and Week 6 in particular displayed just how wide the chasm can be. Below are those who came out on top and those who were not nearly as fortunate during Sunday's action.
The situation in the Meadowlands is not a complete disaster, given that the Giants still lead the NFC East, but Sunday's loss hurts. There is no such thing as a "must-win" game in Week 6, but what the Giants just experienced was a defeat in a contest that held a lot of hope for New York. The opportunity to pull further ahead in a downtrodden division while playing a Saints team on a three-game losing streak escaped them. That result could haunt them down the line.
Not only had New Orleans gone a month between victories, but it also trotted out a quarterback in Tyler Shough who has broken bones in his non-throwing hand . The New York defense watched the injured signal-caller throw for three touchdowns and rack up 34 points. And on the other side of the ball, perhaps John Harbaugh should not have relegated Cam Skattebo to the sideline, because giving him only six snaps and holding him without a touch did not help the Giants' offense. He struggled with fumbles in Weeks 1-5, yes, but he remains one of the team's top weapons and was noticeably absent while the unit around him floundered.
It was a pleasant surprise to see McCarthy enter the game for the Giants and amass 243 passing yards and a touchdown in the fourth quarter alone, but now New York faces questions about whether to trust McCarthy as a starter moving forward or whether to continue with the "Jameis Winston experience." In other words, Harbaugh is stuck between a rock and a hard place.
The last time the Browns held at least a share of first place in the AFC North this deep into a season was more than a decade ago in 2014. A team that entered the year projected to be in the mix for the No. 1 overall draft pick leads its division a month and a half into the campaign. First-year coach Todd Monken deserves heaps of credit for orchestrating a 4-2 start and putting his squad at the forefront of the most competitive divisional race in the NFL.
Cleveland has the same record as the Steelers and Ravens, but it now holds the tiebreaker over both rivals thanks to the Week 6 triumph over Baltimore. Its defense was excellent from the second quarter onward, holding the Ravens off the board after a 10-point first period and opening the door for its offense to squeak out a win. Watson's shockingly clutch performances just keep on coming, and this time, he set up a game-winning 37-yard field goal off the foot of Andre Szmyt as time expired.
The Los Angeles Rams , by way of tiebreakers, are the last-place team in the NFC West through Week 6. That is a sentence so difficult to fathom, considering their offseason successes, that it almost does not feel real. Anyone who has watched them play over the season's first month and a half understands why they hold a 2-4 record: They have looked nothing like the superstar-laden squad they are on paper. But that does not make it any easier to digest just how stunning a failure these first six weeks have been.
The bewildering 18-16 loss the Rams sustained at home against the Arizona Cardinals was the biggest upset of the season to date. Cardinals kicker Chad Ryland walked it off with a 43-yard field goal to push the NFL's most disappointing team to the bottom of their division.
Maybe Myles Garrett will fix this team when he recovers from his knee surgery, but the Rams feel more than one player away. Matthew Stafford has not been anywhere near as sharp as he was in his MVP season last year. Puka Nacua's absence hurt the offense in the first two games, the defense continues to allow far more points than anticipated and three different players have attempted a field goal or extra point in the last two games. This is a mess.
Tom Brady has company in the history books — there is now a tie for the fastest quarterback to reach 100 career wins. It took Patrick Mahomes only 131 games to cross the century mark, which matches the volume of contests Brady required to reach that threshold. Joe Montana was the third-fastest at 139 games.
Mahomes secured win No. 100 against the Los Angeles Chargers and did so in convincing fashion. His defense did the heavy lifting as the Kansas City Chiefs stifled Justin Herbert and the opposing offense in a 22-6 smothering, but he held up his end of the bargain, too, with an efficient effort through the air: 23-for-30 for 272 yards. Kenneth Walker III aided Mahomes with another remarkable performance in the ground game with 128 rushing yards and a pair of touchdowns.
It might be tanking season in Philadelphia. Jalen Hurts is on injured reserve as he recovers from a blood clot in his leg. The offensive line is in shambles. The running back unit is a shell of its former self due to a plethora of injuries. Nolan Smith suffered a concussion on Sunday . The Eagles slipped to 2-4 on the year with a 25-14 loss to the Carolina Panthers . There is hardly anything for fans to cling to as a source of optimism that this season will turn around.
The Panthers sacked Tanner McKee on the first play from scrimmage, and that set the tone for a game that was always just out of the Eagles' reach. McKee was serviceable in his third career start, but hardly anything more than that. He will need to be more efficient if Philadelphia is to stay above water during Hurts' absence, but that might not be the point anymore. The arguments for this franchise to tear everything down and look to the future are as strong as ever.
A couple of things went poorly for the Texans during their trip to London, but neither cost them the game. They overcame an untimely C.J. Stroud interception and another head-scratchingly porous showing from their defense to notch a 34-31 win over the Jaguars in Jacksonville's home away from home. Ka'imi Fairbairn booted a game-sealing field goal at the horn to give Houston its second-consecutive win and move the squad one step closer to becoming just the second team in NFL history to reach the playoffs on the heels of an 0-4 start.
Stroud was fantastic outside of that fourth-quarter turnover. He continues to show immense growth after falling under the microscope for a disappointing 2025 season, and he completed 24 of 34 passes for 312 yards and a season-high three touchdowns on the Jaguars. The interception was only his first of the year, and he did not take a sack. This is as comfortable as Stroud has looked running the Houston offense since he won the NFC Offensive Rookie of the Year award three seasons ago.
The biggest winner on the Texans' side in Week 6, however, might have been Marvin Harrison Jr .
