It would have been understandable if he was silent less than a week after being traded from the Arizona Cardinals , because learning a playbook on such short notice and doing so while traveling overseas is a significant task. Instead, he caught three passes on four targets for his best game of the campaign. The numbers were still modest, but this is a solid starting point for him…

title: Aaron Rodgers calls for NFL to examine Buccaneers' field over player-safety concerns
summary: Rodgers threw the game-winning touchdown in overtime before calling attention to a field on which he had previously suffered two injuries
full_text:
After throwing darts during the final stages of the Steelers ' come-from-behind win over the Buccaneers , Aaron Rodgers took a shot at Raymond James Stadium's playing surface. Rodgers didn't hold back when asked about the playing surface during his postgame press conference.
"It's got to be one of the worst playing surfaces in the league. When we're talking about player safety, that's a real concern," Rodgers said . "I'm thankful I didn't get hurt today, but I've been injured twice on this field before, and in my opinion, the turf was a factor both times. I know USF plays here, but that surface just doesn't feel very safe. From my perspective, it's a field that needs to be looked at because player safety should always come first."
Rodgers' first injury in Tampa occurred in 2008, his first season as the Packers ' starting quarterback. He injured his right (throwing) shoulder during a 30-21 loss. The injury did not lead to any missed time for Rodgers, who started in each of Green Bay's 16 games that season.
In Week 16 of the 2014 season, Rodgers injured a calf muscle during a 20-3 win over the Buccaneers. Like in 2008, the injury did not sideline Rodgers, who won his second of four league MVPs that season.
Last year, Rodgers called the Steelers' home field "borderline unplayable" following a win over the Browns in which kicker Chris Boswell lost his footing on an attempted field goal. The Steelers replaced the playing surface before their next game (which had been planned before Rodgers' comments).
Raymond James Stadium uses natural grass and shares its field with a local college team.
NFLPA president JC Tretter has lobbied for playing surfaces since 2020. In 2022, he called for an immediate ban on specific slit-film turf surfaces. Several teams opted to remove that turf from their stadiums in subsequent fields.
Rodgers, who threw the game-winning touchdown pass in Sunday's overtime win, is in the middle of his 22nd and final NFL season. Rodgers and the Steelers will now begin preparations for next Sunday's international game in Paris against the Saints .
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: LOOK: Josh Allen channels Brett Favre with unbelievable backhanded touchdown pass
summary: Allen avoided a potential sack and improvised an extraordinary touchdown pass that immediately drew comparisons to a legendary Brett Favre play
full_text:
It may only be Week 6, but Josh Allen made what could end up the NFL's play of the year during the Bills' win over the Raiders . Allen extended Buffalo's lead in the second half after making one of the most jaw-dropping touchdown passes in recent memory. On the play, Allen stepped up in the pocket and evaded a possible sack before stepping up and flipping a backhanded pass to wideout Keon Coleman .
The play had historical significance as Allen tied Hall of Famer Jim Kelly for the most touchdown passes in franchise history.
How did Josh Allen make this TD pass to Keon Coleman? BUFvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CNLw6KW2tC
Allen's play immediately conjured memories of a similar play made 30 years earlier by another great quarterback, Brett Favre (that play appears at the 5:23 mark in the video below).
The arm strength. The creativity. The energy. On his 50th birthday… @BrettFavre 's 50 most INCREDIBLE plays! 🧀🎉 (via @nflthrowback) pic.twitter.com/VkOSsl8hsR
Favre's incredible play against the Rams came during the second of his three consecutive MVP seasons. That was also the season where Favre helped lead the Packers to the franchise's first title in 29 years.
Allen would undoubtedly love to have a similar outcome this season for himself and for his team.
The league's MVP in 2024, Allen is the current front-runner to win the award again this year. Through the season's first five games, Allen scored 15 touchdowns that included a whopping eight touchdowns on the ground. In Buffalo's Week 5 win over the Rams, Allen moved into 16th on the all-time rushing touchdown list. Allen's 87 career touchdown runs are 12 more than the next-closest quarterback, Cam Newton .
While his play on Sunday was reminiscent of Favre's, Allen would undoubtedly love to mimic another Hall of Fame quarterback by season's end. If he can win a Super Bowl this season, the 30-year-old Allen would do so 20 years after Peyton Manning captured his first title during his age-30 season.

title: Rams kicker Blake Grupe ruled out after suffering knee injury minutes into L.A. debut
summary: Grupe suffered the injury while making a tackle on a kickoff
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams ' kicking conundrum continues into Week 6, but not in the way you'd expect. After cutting former placekicker Harrison Mevis after Week 5, L.A. seemingly found its solution after signing Blake Grupe to assume the kicking duties. The former Notre Dame kicker made his Rams debut on Sunday and quickly endeared himself to his new squad by netting a 44-yard field goal in the first quarter.
However, things went downhill after that. After initially being listed as doubtful to return, Grupe has been downgraded to out and will not return to Sunday's contest due to a knee injury, the team announced . Grupe suffered the injury while making a tackle on the kickoff following his made field goal. He was seen lowering his shoulder to hit returner Devin Duvernay and came down awkwardly.
New Rams kicker Blake Grupe is doubtful to return after making this tackle pic.twitter.com/EgxKFTFSsq
With Grupe sidelined, the entire kicking operation is reshuffled. Punter Ethan Evans will serve as the kicker, while receiver Jordan Whittington could be the holder, as ESPN notes he was working on holds along the sideline.
So far, however, the Rams have not called Evans' number to kick. After Matthew Stafford connected with Blake Corum for a 15-yard touchdown in the second quarter, they kept the offense on the field for a two-point attempt, which failed. Then, when they were at the Arizona 27-yard line and faced with a fourth-and-1, Los Angeles went for it, but turned the ball over on downs.
Grupe entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2023, initially signing with the Saints . He played for New Orleans until midway through the 2025 season, when he was released. After that, he made stops with the Colts and Jets before finding his way to the Rams. Coming into this game, Grupe had converted 81.9% of his career field goals (86-of-105) and 98% of his extra points (96-of-98).
The kicking game has been an issue throughout the first half of the season for the Rams, and it came to a head during Monday's overtime loss to the Bills . Mevis failed to convert on either of his field goal attempts, including what would've been a game-winner, which was blocked. That forced Los Angeles' hand to make a change in favor of Grupe, but this latest injury keeps them in a kicking nightmare.

title: Bills' C.J. Gardner-Johnson ejected vs. Raiders after spitting at Brock Bowers
summary: It's Gardner-Johnson's second career ejection
full_text:
Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson got ejected in the second quarter of Buffalo's game against the Raiders after spitting at Brock Bowers .
C.J. Gardner-Johnson spits in the direction of Brock Bowers, leading to disqualification pic.twitter.com/8zW4OYIP7o
Spitting is an automatic ejection. Last year, Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter got ejected six seconds into the first game of the season for spitting on Dak Prescott , and later in the season, Ja'Marr Chase got suspended one game for spitting on Jalen Ramsey (who got ejected for punching Chase after the alleged spitting incident). Initially, the refereeing crew did not see Chase spit, which is why only Ramsey was ejected, but the NFL determined after the game that Chase indeed spat on Ramsey, resulting in the suspension.
It's the second ejection of Gardner-Johnson's NFL career; the other came in 2024, when he accrued two personal foul penalties in the same game. He then gave middle fingers to the Commanders ' crowd on the way out.
Gardner-Johnson is in his first season in Buffalo — his sixth different team and fourth in the past three years. title: Jameis Winston benched: J.J. McCarthy's thrilling, historic comeback bid comes up short vs. Saints
summary: McCarthy helped New York score 17 unanswered points before ultimately coming up just short
full_text:
It could be the beginning of a new era in New York, as the Giants benched quarterback Jameis Winston for J.J. McCarthy in the fourth quarter of their eventual 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints . While McCarthy threw an interception on his third passing attempt, he rebounded to spark the Giants and made his case to be John Harbaugh's new starter.
In all, McCarthy completed 11 of 21 passes for 243 yards, one touchdown and one interception in his first extensive action with his new team. In 11 minutes of action, he would throw for 243 yards, which made NFL history for the most passing yards in an 11-minute span. He also led the Giants in rushing with 26 yards. Following his interception, McCarthy led a six-play, 52-yard drive that was capped by a Tyrone Tracy Jr . touchdown and a successful Isaiah Likely two-point conversion to trim the deficit to 16 points. After a Saints three-and-out, McCarthy took the Giants offense 73 yards down the field on just three plays, and hit Likely for a 24-yard touchdown to make it a 10-point game.
J.J. finds Isaiah Likely 🙌 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/0fLSL9TMTV
McCarthy was given the opportunity to lead a game-tying or game-winning drive with 57 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter with zero timeouts. On first down, he scrambled up the middle for 28 yards to get the Giants into enemy territory, and then hit Likely for 20 yards to get New York to the Saints' 23-yard line.
The Giants eventually faced a fourth-and-1 14 yards from the end zone with 12 seconds remaining, and McCarthy could not connect with Likely in the end zone. The Giants wanted a flag on this play, but the officials held onto their yellow handkerchiefs.
Saints defense comes up big on 4th and 1 to prevent the TD! NOvsNYG on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/mG6S1WoaSs
This was a performance good enough for McCarthy to unseat Winston permanently. Last month, the Giants traded a fifth-round pick to the Minnesota Vikings for McCarthy. The former No. 10 overall pick went 6-4 as the starter for the Vikings in 2025, completing 57.6% of his passes for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions. He became the only first-round pick at quarterback since 1970 to finish last in completion percentage and TD-INT ratio in their debut season.
JJ McCarthy with an absolutely ridiculous throw to Malik Nabers. The Vikings gave up on him too quickly. pic.twitter.com/WiDBhBEbCB
Harbaugh said after the game he can't answer who his starting quarterback will be moving forward, and that those are not issues decided 10 minutes after a game.
John Harbaugh says Giants QB J.J. McCarthy did a “heck of a job” in end of game.  Notes situation was “different” than managing a whole game. Also has “no problem with Jameis.” Harbaugh declined to name starter for next game, emphatic he won’t decide 10 minutes after a game. pic.twitter.com/o1kAyEOJeS
It's called the "Jameis Winston experience" for a reason. Last week in the tie vs. the Washington Commanders , he completed 33 of 54 passes for 326 yards and three touchdowns. Winston actually became the first Giants quarterback to throw three touchdowns in back-to-back games since Eli Manning in 2016. However, his performance on Sunday opened the door for Harbaugh to consider his other quarterback. Winston completed 14 of 26 passes for 152 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions before his benching.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Cam Skattebo demotion: Giants RB logs zero touches, responds to apparent benching
summary: After a slew of fumbling mistakes, Skattebo has lost his starting job to Najee Harris
full_text:
In the wake of an array of fumbles this season, Cam Skattebo was completely phased out of the New York Giants offense in Week 6.
Coming into Sunday's action, a report from ESPN noted there would be a change in the New York backfield rotation. Najee Harris was likely to see a large role, while Skattebo was downgraded. The assumption was that even amid a demotion, Skattebo would be in the mix of the Giants' rushing attack. However, that never came to fruition during the club's 34-27 loss to New Orleans.
Skattebo did not log a single carry or a single target on Sunday. This marked the first time in his career that Skattebo was active for a game but did not see any touches. In all, Skattebo played six snaps.
"I didn't expect to have zero," Skattebo said after the game, via The Athletic. "I was expecting to not play as much just like I did. The message was to keep your head down and keep going. They understand the type of player I am, and I just got to continue doing my job and do it to the best of my ability.
Postgame, head coach John Harbaugh said Skattebo's lack of action "wasn't by design" and that he was not benched.
"It was not by design for him not to carry the ball," he said, via Yahoo Sports . "When he was in there, we didn't call any runs. You're not thinking about which back is in the game and how many runs they're getting."
With Skattebo on the outside looking in on the rushing attack, the Giants finished the day with 20 carries for 84 yards (4.2 yards per carry average) and one touchdown. Specifically, Giants backs rushed 14 times for 34 yards and a touchdown. Tyrone Tracy Jr . led the way with six carries, followed by Devin Singletary and Najee Harris, who each finished with four attempts.
On top of the carries, Tracy saw three targets (two catches), while Singletary was targeted once (one catch).
Skattebo's demotion stems from fumbling issues. So far this season, he's fumbled four times, including a back-breaking fumble last week in the overtime tie to the Washington Commanders . That turnover at the Washington 24-yard line eliminated an opportunity for a game-winning kick and instead led to the Giants nearly losing the contest had it not been for Jayden Daniels and the Commanders' offense mismanaging the clock en route to the tie.
"I got punished for what I did (last week)," Skattebo said. "I understand it, so I gotta be ready when coach calls my name, and that wasn't today."
He later added: "It's hard, but I've made mistakes, and I got to own up to them. If that is what they want to do -- keep me on the sidelines because of that -- I totally understand."
New York will be in Houston next Sunday for a Week 7 matchup against the Texans before entering the bye in Week 8.

title: Pittsburgh coach Mike McCarthy suffers injury during Steelers' game vs. Buccaneers
summary: McCarthy spent halftime in the blue medical tent
full_text:
Instead of spending halftime in the locker room, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy spent it in the medical tent after he sustained an ankle injury at the conclusion of the first half.
McCarthy was starting to make his way to the locker room when he started limping and had trouble walking. He was then assisted off the field and into the blue medical tent. He did not speak to the Steelers at halftime.
After the game, he revealed he had been stepped on, and that's why he had to go into the blue tent. However, he said he is feeling better. He told the media he delegated much of the halftime head coach responsibilities to assistant coach Joe Whitt Jr.
Despite the injury, McCarthy returned to the sideline for the start of the second half. He has also resumed his duties as the team's offensive playcaller. According to the CBS Sports broadcast team, McCarthy twisted his ankle, but it's unclear exactly when or what caused it.
Mike McCarthy (ankle) QUESTIONABLE #Steelers #NFL pic.twitter.com/EijrUvY7R8
McCarthy's injury capped off what was a lousy first half for the Steelers, who trailed 13-3 at the intermission. Pittsburgh committed several mental errors in the first half, including Darnell Washington's juggling of an Aaron Rodgers pass, which was ultimately picked off by A'Shawn Robinson . The pick set up the game's first score, a 43-yard field goal by Chase McLaughlin .
The Steelers' offense gained just 102 yards in the first half. They were just 1-of-6 on third down and 0-of-1 on fourth down.
Jalon Daniels , the Buccaneers ' undrafted rookie quarterback, dominated the Steelers in the first 30 minutes. Daniels completed nine consecutive passes at one point and recorded the game's first touchdown on a short touchdown pass to Emeka Egbuka .
The Steelers went on to beat the Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Keenan Allen passes Terrell Owens, Anquan Boldin on NFL career receptions leaderboard: How high will he climb?
summary: The Colts receiver climbed to ninth in NFL history with 1,081 career receptions, and another productive season could carry him even higher
full_text:
There is a new member in the heralded club of the NFL's top 10 career receiving leaders. Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen made eight catches in Sunday's 26-20 loss to the Tennessee Titans to bring his career total to 1,081. That is good for the ninth most in league history.
Allen entered Week 6 at No. 11 on the leaderboard. Cracking the top 10 was not enough for the 34-year-old wideout as he jumped two spots and leaped in front of both Anquan Boldin and Terrell Owens. He now stands a mere 13 receptions behind Tim Brown for eighth place and is on pace to climb even higher than that this season.
The vast majority of Allen's career receptions came with the Chargers . His first four years in the NFL were the last four of the franchise's San Diego era, and he moved with them to Los Angeles, where he earned six Pro Bowl selections in seven years. Allen made 70 catches in 2024 with the Chicago Bears before returning to the Chargers last year and adding 81 to his tally.
Allen has now accumulated 26 receptions in his first five games as a Colt, which is good for second-most on the team.
The rise up the ladder saw Allen surpass one Hall of Famer, and nearly everyone else in front of him already has or will one day earn a gold jacket. Tight ends Jason Witten and Travis Kelce are the only non-Hall of Famers standing between Allen and the all-time receptions record.
The Colts will eventually get their No. 1 receiver, Alec Pierce , back from injured reserve. That will diminish Allen's target share, but he should still retain a sizable role in the passing scheme, considering his skill set as a premier route-runner differs from Pierce's threat as a big-play, downfield weapon. At his current pace, Pierce is on track for 83 catches by season's end. That would place him sixth on the leaderboard, presuming Kelce (the only active player ahead of him) does not slip from his own pace.
At that point, the question becomes whether Allen will suit up in 2027 and beyond or hang up his cleats for a much-deserved retirement. If he plays one more year, produces at the same pace as he has from 2025-26 (the only stretch of his career in which he was not an every-week starter), and Kelce retires at the end of this season, then he would likely move into the top five.
At that pace, it would take five seasons beyond this year to unseat Jerry Rice as the all-time receptions leader.
The company Allen keeps makes it fair to wonder whether he will end up enshrined in Canton, Ohio. The only wide receivers ahead of him on the catches leaderboard are Hall of Famers, and both Witten and Kelce are expected to join the fraternity in due time.
There are a couple of other key factors working in Allen's favor. His route-running acumen and ability to move the chains on third down are some of the greatest of his era. And the longevity element works in his favor, too, considering he remains productive into his mid-30s and strung together five consecutive Pro Bowl seasons and another in 2023. Allen was also the Comeback Player of the Year in 2017 when he led the NFL in first downs one season after tearing his ACL in Week 1.
A couple of knocks against Allen's resume are critical, though, and could eventually make him the only top-10 career receiver to be absent from the Hall of Fame. The fact that he is a wide receiver presents a challenge, given the extensive backlog at that position on the ballot. Allen does not have a single All-Pro selection; he never led the league in anything besides first downs, and his postseason experience is extremely limited, with just six playoff games played and no Super Bowl appearances.
Allen's position on the receiving leaderboard would have to do a lot of heavy lifting for him to separate himself from the other deserving pass-catchers who have been waiting years to get into the Hall.

title: Has the Travis Hunter breakout arrived? Jacksonville CB/WR showcases long-term, two-way potential vs. Texans
summary: Hunter is hitting his stride with his utilization in 2026, making history with an interception and a receiving touchdown in Week 6
full_text:
Second-year CB/WR Travis Hunter showcased the tantalizing two-way production on Sunday that the Jacksonville Jaguars dreamed about when they traded up to select the 2024 Heisman Trophy winner second overall in the 2025 NFL Draft .
Jacksonville traded the 2025 fifth overall pick, a 2025 second-round pick (No. 36), a 2025 fourth-round pick (No. 126) and a 2026 first-round pick to the Cleveland Browns to move up three spots to the second overall pick while also picking up a 2025 fourth-round pick (No. 104) and a 2025 sixth-round pick (No. 200). That was a heavy investment of draft capital for Hunter, and the Jaguars weren't able to fully capitalize on his skillset his rookie year with it being cut short at the end of October by a torn LCL.
The Jaguars fell 34-31 after a buzzer-beating field goal from the Houston Texans in London. But the game represented the start of the game-changing, two-way impact they envisioned for Hunter. He started at cornerback while catching all four of his targets at wide receiver for 59 yards and a touchdown, a seven-yarder that cut the Texans' lead to 31-28 with 11:26 left in the game. On the next Texans' drive after his touchdown, Hunter picked off Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud in the end zone for a crucial stop, marking Stroud's first interception of the entire 2026 season. That allowed the Jaguars to tie the game at 31 with 1:55 left to play.
Hunter is now the first player with a receiving touchdown and an interception in the same game since Pro Football Hall of Famer Brian Dawkins did so back in 2022, also against the Texans. Hunter's performance on Sunday is now just the fourth time a player has produced a receiving touchdown and an interception in the same game (including the playoffs) since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger.
NYJ Keyshawn Johnson (1998)*
* Occurred in the playoffs
It's interesting to see the shift in how the Jaguars are deploying Hunter this season compared to his rookie year in 2025. Last season, Hunter profiled as a full-time wide receiver moonlighting at cornerback. Of his 459 total snaps from scrimmage, around two-thirds of them were on offense (66.4%, 305 of 459) and a third of them were on defense (33.6%, 154 of 459) in seven games played. He racked up 298 yards receiving and a touchdown with 28 catches on 45 targets while totaling three passes defended and a fumble with 15 total tackles in seven games in 2025.
So far in 2026, Hunter has transitioned to full-time cornerback while playing wide receiver as a side hustle. Of his 322 snaps from scrimmage this season, just over 90% of them (90.7%, 292 of 322) are on defense, and just under 10% of them (9.3%, 30 of 322) are on offense. Hunter has caught all six of his targets this season for 76 yards receiving and a touchdown, with the bulk of that coming on Sunday. He's also totaled two interceptions, three passes defended, and 22 tackles in six games. Deploying Hunter as cornerback first was a great call: His 49.7 passer rating allowed in coverage this season is the lowest in the entire NFL, minimum 30 passes attempts against.
Travis Hunter, dual threat. HOUvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/lCIpPmb9hJ
What a game for @TravisHunterJr . HOUvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XOlzBq18zl
It seems like head coach Liam Coen and defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile have found a winning formula for Hunter's usage with the team out to a 4-2 start and first place in the AFC South through six weeks. More often than not, Hunter making a splash on both sides of the ball will yield winning outcomes for the Jaguars, exactly what Jacksonville hoped for when trading up to select him second overall just two drafts ago.

title: NFL, Saints address plans for Paris game during Week 6 as protests escalate in France
summary: The league says its continuing with its original plans and monitoring the situation
full_text:
Protests escalated in France over the weekend over living costs and education, raising concerns over the NFL game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints scheduled to take place in Paris next week. The unrest stems in part from citizens demanding better school conditions, teacher shortages and public services, but it has since grown as violent groups have rioted, clashed with police, and set fire to public buildings. At least 1,800 across the country, according to CBS News .
Hundreds of thousands have taken to the streets across the nation to demand change from the government, as both protesters and law enforcement have turned to violent methods. Concern over player, personnel, and fan safety has become the main topic surrounding next week's international game, the first-ever regular-season matchup to take place in France.
The league released a statement last week saying they still plan to conduct the game as scheduled on Oct. 25 and provided a similar update on Sunday after news of the social unrest spread.
"Preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France next Sunday," the NFL said . "We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We are also providing the two clubs with regular updates. There's been no disruption or impact at league sites."
Saints executive Greg Bensel backed the league's statement and offered some insight into the league's safety precautions.
"We concur with the NFL's statement and are planning to play the game. In addition to working closely with the NFL, we have also maintained daily security updates with our security partners in France," Bensel said . "Members of our football operations staff and internal security team have been on the ground in France for the past few days and there has been no disruption or impact at any of our team sites."
Last week, the league's statement said, "We're excited for the first-ever regular season game in Paris, and preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France on October 25. As we do for every NFL game, including our international games, we work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We look forward to welcoming fans to Paris later this month."
The game is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET, 2:30 p.m. local time. The Saints are scheduled to leave Sunday night and spend the week practicing in France.
The league has changed games in the past due to various factors, including weather and field conditions, so it is not entirely out of the realm of possibility that the game could be moved. The Saints are considered the home team, so if they did move it, which they clearly do not plan to do right now, New Orleans would be the obvious new location.
While protests have taken over Paris, it's not the only place in France affected. Here's more from CBS News:
"Authorities said masked groups on Saturday set fires and attacked public buildings, including city halls, in several cities.
"In Limoges, a city in central France, flames engulfed the 19th-century City Hall, causing its roof to collapse. Haute-Vienne prefect Maurice Barate told LCI television that the fire was deliberately set and nearly destroyed the building. The fire was under control Sunday."
"Around Paris' Place de la République on Sunday morning, dislodged cobblestones, shattered storefronts and broken glass marked the aftermath of the events. Looting and damage were reported around the square and in some other tourist and shopping areas in the city center.
"Paris police said Sunday that 855 people were arrested in the French capital region alone. The Paris prosecutors' office said that 557 of them were kept in police custody."

title: NFL addresses safety concerns for Steelers-Saints game in France as protests in Paris continue
summary: The league says it is still planning to play the game as originally scheduled
full_text:
With protests on their third week in Paris and an NFL game scheduled to take place in the city in just a week, growing concern over fan and player safety has left some wondering if the league will alter any of its plans. But the NFL said on Wednesday that the game will go on as scheduled, with the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints meeting on Oct. 25 at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis, located just north of Paris.
"We're excited for the first-ever regular season game in Paris, and preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France on October 25," the NFL said in a statement earlier this week, via ESPN . "As we do for every NFL game, including our international games, we work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We look forward to welcoming fans to Paris later this month."
As protests continue, the league released another statement emphasizing that they plan to play the game in Paris.
"Preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France next Sunday," the NFL said . "We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We are also providing the two clubs with regular updates. There's been no disruption or impact at league sites."
The social unrest stems from demands for the government to change multiple aspects of the education system. Protestors are asking the government to address under-resourced schools, poor conditions and teacher shortages. Students say the schools are falling apart and rats are in the buildings.
The protests have sparked violence, with authorities using tear gas, stun grenades and various other means to attempt to stop the crowds. Protestors have reportedly set fires and caused damage. Police detained over 5,000 people in connection with protests, according to CBS News .
Local officials say they are investigating both the protests and the police response.
The French government is currently in a "political deadlock" as they approach the presidential elections in the spring. They have not responded to protestors with any plans or solutions for their complaints and demands.
If the situation in Paris escalates, the NFL could reconsider its stance, but right now, it is sticking with its original plan. The NFL has changed game locations in the past due to extreme weather or field conditions.
The Saints are considered the home team for the game, and their only listed event for the day in New Orleans is a private event where youth and amateur sports teams have the chance to play inside the stadium. It is scheduled for 8:30 a.m. local time, so if needed, the game could seemingly be played at Caesar's Superdome. But that seems unlikely at the moment.
If the game does go on as planned, it will mark the first-ever NFL game played in France.
This will be the second straight year the Steelers play a game outside the United States, having played in Dublin last season against the Minnesota Vikings . The Saints last played an international game in 2022, visiting London to face the Vikings.

title: Beaks & Geeks: Cardinals, Rams Winners & Losers: Arizona kicker Ryland goes 6-6 in field goals, including the game winner
summary: The Arizona Cardinals were in a pickle going into Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. The season is only 17 games in, and with a 1-4-0 record entering the divisional matchup against the Rams, a loss would shove Arizona further down the rabbit hole. Could the season be lost with a loss? RELATED: RAMS […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Chad Ryland #38 of the Arizona Cardinals kicks a game winning field goal against the Los Angeles Rams in the fourth quarter of a game at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals were in a pickle going into Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. The season is only 17 games in, and with a 1-4-0 record entering the divisional matchup against the Rams, a loss would shove Arizona further down the rabbit hole. Could the season be lost with a loss? RELATED: RAMS VS. CARDINALS DISCUSSION What was needed was a Cardinals win. Then the team could gather itself and at least think, for the moment, that the year is not completely gone and maybe start a run. It does happen. Because the schedule going forward for the next few games is pretty brutal. Arizona had plenty of opportunities for the offense to score, but ended up with field goals instead. Good teams finish drives by getting into the end zone; so, that’s that. In the end, the Cardinals came back with just 47 seconds on the clock to get into field goal range as Ryland nailed his sixth FG of the day to defeat their division rivals on the final play, 18-16. Get after it. #AZvsLAR | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/I9jh96WPA0 — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 18, 2026 Congrats to Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur, who won his first-ever NFL contest and now defeated his former team in their first-ever divisional battle. Both of these aspects are rare in the coaching industry. So, who played well for the Cardinals? Who didn’t? ——————————————————————————– BEAKS another FG on the day for 3️⃣8️⃣ #AZvsLAR | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/Sv0rjqrqVt — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 18, 2026 K Chad Ryland – Ryland is having a very good year, and thank goodness. The Arizona offense had plenty of long drives that just stalled, and trotted out Ryland to get something out of it. He converted kicks of 34, 30, and 22 in the first half alone, as the half ended in a 9-9 tie. He nailed the game winner of 43 yards for the road win. LB Cody Simon – Rams TE Tyler Higbee had caught the ball, then cradled it as he was attempting to gain another yard or two. LB Simon reached down and was able to rip the ball from Higbee’s grasp as CB Denzel Burke wrestled the loose ball away from Rams receiver Puka Nacua at Arizona’s 30-yard line. The strip and recovery took away points from LA. Offensive line – Gave QB Jacoby Brissett time to find receivers on most passing downs. Brissett was not sacked a single time all day. This is still a work in progress, but the progress is showing. Great lead block on the pull by C Hjalte Froholdt on Bam Knight’s big gain and a second-level block by rookie LT Jayden Williams. Field goal team – On every field goal attempt, it is nine blockers against 11 defenders. Yet, the Cardinals took care of business on six successful field goal attempts. Long snapper Casey Kreiter was a great signing during the offseason and sends his pass quickly and accurately. The holder, punter Blake Gillikin, has a difficult job. He has to catch the pass with both hands, lay it down while spinning the ball so that the laces face forward, and place it at the correct angle that the kicker wants. Too much forward or backwards will alter the trajectory of the kick. When all of your team’s points come from field goals, this group works well as a special teams unit. . @MackWilson coming 🆙 BIG on 4th down 😳 pic.twitter.com/kFDAO0Apqg — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 18, 2026 LB Mack Wilson – This dude was everywhere all game long. Made tackles on three consecutive plays in the second quarter. In Quarter 3, LA began at its own 27, and a 14-yard run plus a 16-yard pass put the Rams at Arizona’s 36. A one-yard run made it second-and-nine. An incompletion, then an eight-yard dash by WR Konata Mumpfield produced a fourth-and-one at the Cardinals’ 27-yard line. LA already had a field goal in their back pocket, but decided to go for it. It was Wilson who stuffed TE Davis Allen on the short-yardage play, and a turnover on downs. He hit him first, and LB Jack Gibbens finished him off. Wilson led all Cardinals defenders with nine total tackles. WR Jalen Brooks – No completion was bigger than Brooks snaring the 21-yard pass completion on that final drive. This, plus an unnecessary roughness penalty, got the ball down to the Rams’ 29-yard line and ensured at least a field goal attempt. Game ball here. Had only two catches for 30 yards, and that’s okay. This was a hero catch with great focus. ——————————————————————————— GEEKS RB Tyler Allgeier – The talented back was supposed to be a sensation this year in the desert, but then the team drafted Jeremiyah Love. And now that Love isn’t playing, Allgeier is being relegated to spot duty and staying in the pocket to block. What happened? He had almost the same number of carries as Bam Knight, yet gained half as much. No explosiveness, no second-level speed. 18 carries for 38 yards is not what this offense had in mind. AD WITH THE TACKLE FOR LOSS! 😤 📺 @NFLonFox | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/46dBtCRvYc — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) October 18, 2026 Offense not finishing – At the beginning of the season, a lot of media outlets had penciled in the Rams in the NFC Championship Game. Now that they have stumbled out of the gate and look more human, their defense is very suspect. The Cardinals marched up and down the field all game long, and had drives of eight plays, 10 plays, 12, 15 plays, and 14 plays. These drives ended at LA’s 16-yard line, 12, three-yard line, 19, and 9-yard line. Getting three instead of six was the difference in the game. Think about it: If the offense had scored TDs on those drives instead of field goals, on the Rams’ final drive it would have been 35-9 instead of 15-9. Defense final Rams drive – Arizona was holding onto a slim 15-9 lead that was built on the leg of Ryland. Los Angeles got the ball back with just 2:48 left in the game. Several short passes and a run, plus a Rams penalty, gave them a crucial first-and-15 with 2:01 left. Who is one of the best receivers in the game? We all know it is #12, Nacua, who was open for 16 yards with coverage by S Budda Baker. Two plays later, LA scored to make it 16-15. ———————————————————————————– Bird Seed – When life gives you lemons, just add vodka Q LAKE WITH THE INT. 😤 📺: @NFLonFOX | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/3fzMZAlh5l — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) October 18, 2026 QB Jacoby Brissett – Nothing spectacular, but a good game manager. He will fling it quite a bit in games, but he isn’t finding his best pass catchers as much. Avoided the pass rush and wasn’t sacked at all. The interception on the first drive was unfortunate, but TE Trey McBride wasn’t even open. Went 24 for 35 for 218 yards, zero TDs, one interception, a 6.2 yards-per-completion average, with a QB rating of 73.3. mama there goes, Bam💥 31-yard pickup for 20 #AZvsLAR | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/boe9ENrdGz — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 18, 2026 RB Bam Knight – Knight showed he could become the bellcow if needed. His 31-yard scamper was a great run and got the offense into Rams territory as the first quarter was winding down. Led all runners with 15 carries for 80 yards and a 5.3 yards-per-carry average. Not getting the defensive two-point conversion – The Rams went for the two-point conversion after the TD pass from QB Matt Stafford to RB Blake Corum in the second quarter. Now up 9-6, LA opted for two. DE Josh Sweat nailed Stafford, who then fumbled. The loose ball was picked up by DT L.J. Collier, who took off. When Collier was at Arizona’s 40-yard line, he had four teammates surrounding him, with two more trailing. Three Rams were in the mix. Sweaty J says NO on 2-pt conversion 🚫 #AZvsLAR | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/rT1mTRFan1 — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 18, 2026 At the 50-yard line, CB Kei’Trel Clark was to his outer right…

title: Arizona Cardinals defense and Chad Ryland dominate in close win over Rams
summary: The Arizona Cardinals needed every one of those six field goals after maybe the best defensive performance of the Nick Rallis era. They also needed an egregious call to go their way for once. And they got all of that to pull out an 18-16 win over the Los Angeles Rams. The story of the […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Chad Ryland #38 and Josh Sweat #10 of the Arizona Cardinals celebrate after Ryland's game winning field goal in their team's 18-16 win against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals needed every one of those six field goals after maybe the best defensive performance of the Nick Rallis era. They also needed an egregious call to go their way for once. And they got all of that to pull out an 18-16 win over the Los Angeles Rams. The story of the day was the Arizona Cardinals incredible defense, who held the Rams offense coming off four consecutive games of 300-plus yard passing games to less than 300 yards of total offense while forcing a big turnover late. It was almost all for nothing though, as the Arizona Cardinals offense was stuck in mud inside the redzone once again. Luckily, an aggressive and opportunistic defense, and a potent running game did all the heavy lifting today. The Arizona Cardinals move to 2-4 on the season, and they find themselves out of the NFC cellar. Now, can they stack games and get a little complimentary football going?

This is why it seemed like at the time for some of us, that moving on from Jonathan Gannon and not moving on from Monti Ossenfort did not make sense. Because now, you have this playing out. The Cardinals are the biggest underdogs of the 2026 season at 12.5-points ahead of today’s matchup with the Los Angeles Rams according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Can the Cardinals afford a one and done head coach? Can they saddle a new GM with LaFleur? These are all questions that we would not have to ask if they just won some darn football games.

title: Week 6 Snap Reactions: Too little, too late
summary: The Atlanta Falcons made a late push, but ultimately couldn’t overcome their early game errors and fell to 2-4 against the Chicago Bears. Here are the Week 6 Snap Reactions. Too Many Injuries to Overcome The Falcons laundry list of injuries has brought down Jeff Ulbrich’s house of cards. Fair to say he hasn’t been […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Michael Penix Jr. #9 of the Atlanta Falcons is pressured by Clark Phillips III #20 of the Chicago Bears during the first quarter of the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons made a late push, but ultimately couldn’t overcome their early game errors and fell to 2-4 against the Chicago Bears. Here are the Week 6 Snap Reactions. Too Many Injuries to Overcome The Falcons laundry list of injuries has brought down Jeff Ulbrich’s house of cards. Fair to say he hasn’t been on his A game, but you try to get your game off with Josh Woods, Mike Ford, Jared Ivey, etc. The hits keep coming; Kendal Daniels left after a frightening impact to the head and neck area. Divine Deablo continues to stack injuries and left with an arm injury, and Avieon Terrell and Billy Bowman were banged up late. The defense needed the offense to carry them in this one, but their effort came too late. Poorly Coached Special Teams Look, I’ll fall on the sword after pounding the table for more Branch (even though I meant as a WR), but both returners attempted to field punts inside the 10; one couldn’t read the ball well enough and muffed it, and the other forgot to fair catch. Almost like there’s a reason most coaches don’t let their guys attempt those at all. The mental mistakes are too numerous to blame solely on the players; they aren’t getting good enough coaching. Bears recover the muffed punt! CHIvsATL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Bp13sT3Yo5 — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 This roster is packed with special teams talent, but it’s not making a difference, and it’s hard to ignore that the team hired two of the worst special teams coaches from 2025. Offense Played 1 Quarter of Football The late surge was great, but everything before it was embarrassing. Rees got in his own head in the first half and let the Bears dictate his run game. There’s zero excuse for giving Bijan the ball 4 times in a half. His screen game needs to be trashed. After having no answers against pressure versus the Ravens, it took till the 4th quarter to get any against the Bears. Penix deserves a fair share of the blame when it comes to responding to pressure. He keeps locking in on his first read, and he has a bad habit of taking sacks and being careless with the football. Kyle Pitts continues to have his talents wasted. He’s one of the team’s best answers against pressure and makes things happen when he gets the ball, but even after the team prioritized him this offseason, he’s still an afterthought. Kyle Pitts what a play! CHIvsATL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1K7vEntXHI — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 A Volatile Product The Falcons have two 2-game losing streaks and one 2-game winning streak–they’re streaky. After praising Stefanski and Co. for resetting the team after a Cooper Rush-led start, they’ve since failed to wash away concerns about this team’s ability to play competent football week to week and quarter to quarter. The Bears aren’t a cakewalk, but their defense isn’t an immovable object; the Falcons late surge proved that. Even when the Falcons were spotted over 100 penalty yards, they looked inept for most of the game. Mental mistakes showed up in every phase of the game, and the staff failed to give the players a viable game plan. The Atlanta Falcons are now two games below .500 as they enter the rough patch of their schedule. There’s plenty of blame to go around, and the team better get itself sorted quickly because the 49ers are up next, and Kyle Shanahan and Raheem Morris are licking their chops.

title: Kendal Daniels injury: Falcons rookie LB carted off with apparent head/neck injury vs. Bears
summary: UPDATE: 6:06 p.m ET Kendal Daniels has apparently been released from Grady Memorial Hospital and returned to the Falcons’ locker room postgame. According to Will McFadden of AtlantaFalcons.com, Daniels was walking on his own, which is a relief considering how dangerous the injury looked. UPDATE: 3:53 p.m. ET The Falcons released a statement on Daniels. […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - AUGUST 14: Atlanta linebacker Kendal Daniels (53) reacts during the NFL pre-season game between the Denver Broncos and the Atlanta Falcons on August 14th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images UPDATE: 6:06 p.m ET Kendal Daniels has apparently been released from Grady Memorial Hospital and returned to the Falcons’ locker room postgame. According to Will McFadden of AtlantaFalcons.com, Daniels was walking on his own, which is a relief considering how dangerous the injury looked. While we were wrapping up with Bijan Robinson in the locker room after the game, rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels came in with a couple of trainers. He was walking on his own, which is obviously a good sign after the scary scene today. — Will McFadden (@willmcfadden) October 18, 2026 UPDATE: 3:53 p.m. ET The Falcons released a statement on Daniels. Atlanta Falcons linebacker Kendal Daniels is alert and has movement in all his extremities. He was taken to Grady Memorial Hospital for further evaluation. Falcons linebacker Kendal Daniels was carted off the field in the third quarter of the Falcons’ Week 6 matchup against the Bears. The top of his head collided with another player during a tackle on Bears TE Colston Loveland, and he immediately reacted like he was in intense pain. Daniels’ injury comes after fellow linebacker Divine Deablo left the game with an arm injury. Deablo has been ruled out for the remainder of the matchup. Losing both of these players is a blow for sure, but I have to think it’s especially to focus after seeing a player who’s been so central to what this defense does well go down with such a scary injury. Prior to leaving the field, Daniels was secured to a backboard. Prior to the medical staff getting involved, right after the hit, Daniels did appear to be moving his arms and hands, so hopefully that’s a good sign. Daniels has been a fantastic fit for Jeff Ulbrich’s defense, and he’s very quickly developed as a leader on the field. When Deablo went down with the arm injury, it was the rookie Daniels who took over the green dot. Josh Woods swapped out his helmet while the medical team was attending to Daniels to take over the green dot, according to The Athletic’s Josh Kendall . The Falcons defense has been hit hard with injuries of late. In addition to Daniels and Deablo, cornerback AJ Terrell is on injured reserve, and his counterpart CJ Henderson is out Sunday with a groin injury. We will update this post as more information becomes available, and we’re wishing Daniels all the best.

full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears scrambles to throw a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter of the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Falcons had a chance to bounce back from a last minute overtime loss to the Baltimore Ravens. Instead, they hit the pavement and stayed there. This was a catastrophic effort. They lost Divine Deablo, lost Kendal Daniels to a very scary injury, and looked discombobulated and sloppy all game despite the Bears piling up penalties. Caleb Williams was unstoppable, the Bears ground game rolled, and Atlanta’s ground game was limited by circumstance and weird play calling, putting pressure on a passing game that couldn’t deliver. Two special teams fumbles—one a muffed punt return by Zachariah Branch, the other a fumbled kick return also by Branch—just made the problem worse. When the game was over, the Falcons had lost at home, where they remain winless in 2026. It is difficult to overstate how discouraging this loss was. The Falcons looked completely overmatched from the very beginning of the game, going into a hole immediately and staying there until five minutes into the fourth quarter, when they put together an admirable, furious rally to pull within eight points. That comeback ultimately fell short—the odds were against it succeeding—but it was very nice to see real life from the offense before things ended. But of course, that’s a pyrrhic victory. The Falcons have shown signs of life in three of their four losses this year and have still fallen short, and now sit at 2-4 on the season having lost both starting linebackers to injuries, looking sloppy and godawful on special teams in particular, and set to go into a rough matchup with the 49ers next. Anything can happen, but this appears to be another lost season in Kevin Stefanski’s first year at the helm. Perhaps they’ll make me eat those words. I would like that. Here’s a drive-by-drive rundown of the game you just watched. 1st Quarter The Falcons deferred and kicked it off to Chicago, who took it to about the 33 before DeMarcco Hellams tripped him up. Caleb Williams drifted away from pressure and hit Colston Loveland for 16 yards on first down. D’Andre Swift took it up the middle for four yards. On play action, Williams got Swift for a first down pass. The Bears then got hit with a false start. A quick pass to Loveland got five yards and erased the penalty. Williams was nearly sacked, then launched one up where it was nearly picked off by Xavier Watts. A holding call backed the Bears up, and then Williams found Luther Burden III for nine yards. A catch from Rome Odunze that was lateraled to Roschon Johnson went for a first down. Johnson then picked up seven yards on the ground. Johnson found more running room up the middle for a first down. Swift got a couple of yards on first down. A delay of game after the Bears failed to get the snap off backed them up five yards. Williams then got away from pressure and hit Loveland for a touchdown in between two defenders. 7-0 Bears. Zachariah Branch got crushed shy of the 20 yard line on the return. Bijan Robinson took the opening carry for six yards after cutting back to the middle. On play action, Penix walked back and tried a screen to Bijan that was dead before the ball left Michael Penix Jr.’s hand. Penix evaded a sack, ran around a bit, and then sort of threw one away toward a receiver. Punt. The Bears returned the punt to the 40 yard line. After a one yard run, Williams just didn’t catch the snap, but managed to fall on it for an eight yard loss. Williams then hit a leaping Odunze over the middle for a first down. Williams then hit Burden on the sideline for another first down. A quick screen to Swift went for nine yards. Swift cut back inside and got a first down. Williams then hit Kmet on a rollout for about six yards. Swift was stopped cold after a yard by Gervon Dexter and company. Swift then plunged up the middle and scored to make it 14-0 Bears. Branch’s return was stopped just shy of the 25 yard line. Penix hit a sharp sideline ball to Drake London for about five yards. Another screen to Robinson went nowhere again. 2nd Quarter Penix tried one low to Olamide Zaccheaus, but OZ simply didn’t get the diving catch. Punt, it was brought back past the 30. Williams managed to loft one over a free rusher to Swift, who picked up about eight yards. Kalif Raymond caught one working against Divine Deablo and spun out of contact for a first down and more. Swift was swiftly upended on the next play by Jessie Bates. A quick pass to Swift was then stopped cold by Kendal Daniels. Williams then threw it away against the blitz. Punt, and a touchback. Bijan picked up nine yards on first down. He then took the next carry across midfield. Penix on play action just missed a streaking, open London downfield. Penix then hit Pitts across the middle for about six yards. Brian Robinson Jr. was crushed trying to carry it up the middle for no gain. Penix’s fourth down pass was knocked down. Williams couldn’t find an open man and just threw it downfield out of bounds, but a roughing the passer call gave the Bears plenty of yardage. A screen to Raymond went for a mile, but a holding call backed Chicago up. Williams moved around long enough to find Johnson for about 14 yards. Johnson’s run lost a yard. Williams was hit by Gervon Dexter as he threw and threw it away. Cairos Santos then missed the long kick attempt. Penix then lofted one to a wide open London, who left a defender in the dust and ran all the way to about the 15 yard line. BRJ got about three yards. Penix then threw one to Dotson over the middle, but he took a hit that threw him off his route and didn’t get the ball. Then Penix went right back to Dotson, who was smothered but pulled in the touchdown grab. 14-7 Bears. Swift took the opening handoff of the drive for six yards. Williams slipped away from a near sack to hit Swift for a first down. The toss to Swift picked up 11 yards, but it was brought back by penalties. Roschon Johnson was then hit by Jared Ivey right over the middle of the field. Two yards followed, and then Williams hit Odunze for a big first down before another hold backed the Bears up. Then Williams got Loveland over the middle, who dove and came up a little short of a first down. Punt. And it was a catastrophic punt, as it clanked off Zachariah Branch’s hands and was picked up by the Bears on the 10 yard line. Loveland then took it eight yards. Loveland then dropped the would-be touchdown pass. Swift then plunged in for a touchdown again. 21-7 Bears. Branch brought the kick to the 28 yard line. Penix tried for Zaccheaus downfield and didn’t get him. He then overthrew it a bit to Bijan, but a defensive holding call gave the Falcons five yards and a first down. Penix threw it low for Pitts, who couldn’t quite scoop it out of the dirt. Penix then was sacked on third down and fumbled, but on review it was ruled not a fumble, but it was still 3rd and 20. Bijan then took it close to 15 yards. Punt, and a holding call backed the Bears up. A quick pass to Kmet went for a yard. On the next play, the Falcons finally got home, with Brandon Dorlus hitting Williams and Dexter finishing the sack. Swift somehow got loose for 15 yards. 3rd Quarter After a return to about the 25, Penix tried it deep to London and he was interfered with, giving the Falcons a big pickup. A quick throw over the middle to Austin Hooper went for six yards. Bijan then got away from defenders and picked up a couple of yards. The Falcons ran a play action pass on third down and Penix was sacked. Punt, but the Bears roughed Jake Bailey and the Falcons got 15 yards and the ball back. Bijan took it up the middle for a couple of yards. Penix was then sacked again on second down as the pocket immediately collapsed. A screen to London got the Falcons within…

title: Intriguing players to watch in Falcons vs. Bears
summary: The Atlanta Falcons look to reset against the Chicago Bears in a Week 6 battle that could have playoff implications down the line because of tie-breakers. The Falcons also look to reset their lack of home-field advantage, as they’re winless in the supposed friendly confines of Mercedes-Benz Stadium so far in 2026. If the team […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Jahan Dotson #4 of the Atlanta Falcons celebrates after a catch against the Baltimore Ravens in the second quarter of a game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons look to reset against the Chicago Bears in a Week 6 battle that could have playoff implications down the line because of tie-breakers. The Falcons also look to reset their lack of home-field advantage, as they’re winless in the supposed friendly confines of Mercedes-Benz Stadium so far in 2026. If the team wants a renewed outlook, here are five players who can spark it. Bijan Robinson After a relatively quiet Week 5 against the Baltimore Ravens , running back Bijan Robinson is poised for another big performance against the Bears. While the Bears’ run defense ranks ninth-best in the NFL in yards allowed, that stat is a bit misleading. They’ve benefited from facing teams that lack a commitment to running the ball (see Green Bay Packers ) or teams that wanted to run the ball but couldn’t because they were playing from behind (see Carolina Panthers and Philadelphia Eagles ). If the Falcons don’t fall behind early and have to abandon the run, they should be able to lean heavily on Robinson to carry the offense, as they did against the Packers and New Orleans Saints . Jahan Dotson Wide receiver Jahan Dotson could be instrumental in exploiting a glaring weakness on the Bears’ defense. According to Next Gen Stats , the Bears have given up the most yards per game on deep passes this year. Dotson has been Atlanta’s most effective deep threat so far this year, hooking up with Michael Penix for explosive plays in each of the last two games. He can go for the hat trick against a vulnerable Bears secondary. Avieon Terrell Falcons rookie cornerback Avieon Terrell is set to make his starting debut this weekend as an injury replacement for C.J. Henderson . This could be an audition for the permanent starting gig if things go well. With A.J. Terrell potentially returning from injured reserve next week, the Falcons could sideline struggling starting cornerback Mike Hughes moving forward. So if Avieon’s starting debut goes well, Hughes’ demotion could come sooner rather than later. Maason Smith & Samson Ebukam Pressuring Bears quarterback Caleb Williams will fall on the entire Falcons front, but Maason Smith and Samson Ebukam are likely to have the most favorable matchups to spearhead that effort. Williams has been extremely effective when kept clean this year, with the 5th best EPA per dropback when he’s not pressured, according to Next Gen Stats . So the Falcons must pressure him to slow the Bears’ offense. Smith will face undersized center Garrett Bradbury and can use his size and power to bully him, while Ebukam should get a favorable matchup at left tackle. Ozzy Trapilo may return to the lineup this weekend , but he hasn’t stepped on a field since he suffered a knee injury last January . Ebukam can provide a not-so-warm welcome back come Sunday. Can Atlanta bounce back under the bright lights of Mercedes-Benz Stadium and capture that elusive first home win of 2026? Can you name other Falcons players who intrigue you in this battle?

title: Falcons vs. Bears: What will Week 6’s win or loss mean for Atlanta?
summary: It kind of feels like the Falcons are at an early crossroads as to what their season might yet become. Following the digging of an 0-2 hole behind the theatrics of a Cooper Rush-led offense, Atlanta bounced back emphatically with back-to-back primetime blowout victories before dropping the ball and blowing a fourth quarter lead in […]
full_text: Photo by Quinn Harris/Getty Images It kind of feels like the Falcons are at an early crossroads as to what their season might yet become. Following the digging of an 0-2 hole behind the theatrics of a Cooper Rush-led offense, Atlanta bounced back emphatically with back-to-back primetime blowout victories before dropping the ball and blowing a fourth quarter lead in a very winnable game against a Lamar Jackson-less Ravens team. Sitting at 2-3, the Falcons welcome a Chicago Bears team that on paper looks like a true NFC contender but in reality is more than just a little bit banged up. As of this writing, we still are unsure if quarterback Caleb Williams will make his return from a hamstring injury. Now in their “difficult stretch” of the season, the chance to steal a game or two as a traditional underdog feels like it could be the difference between actually competing for the division and another season falling by the wayside. Here is the scenario the Falcons face if they beat the Chicago Bears in Week 6, as well as if they lose. If the Falcons win They will get the season back on track and pull themselves back to .500, which is likely what many fans would have signed up for at this point in the campaign before it started. Fans certainly would have taken it following the 0-2 start. Looking at the early division race, Atlanta would have a chance at claiming sole possession of first place with a Panthers defeat in Philadelphia against a reeling Eagles squad. The Saints and Buccaneers could also be left by the wayside with their own defeats as well. The aforementioned schedule at the top of this article will continue to get more and more difficult with games against the 49ers, Bengals and Chiefs along with a road divisional clash in Tampa coming before the bye week. Even in a weak NFC South it kind of feels like the Birds need to have at least four wins minimum by that bye week to have a chance. This game against a banged-up Bears represents one of their best opportunities at getting one of those wins and keeping themselves on track. Speaking of games against the Bears, Atlanta would pull within one game of the all time head to head record in this series with a win (they are currently historically 14-16). If the Falcons lose Then they will have completely fumbled a golden opportunity to secure wins against two shorthanded teams back to back. Losing that game against Baltimore may come back to bite them later on; losing to the Bears in addition to it would all but guarantee deep regret at a later point in the season. Carolina could widen the gap of their currently slender division lead to 1.5 games with a victory, and either the Saints or Bucs could pull to within a tie for second place. Sitting at 2-4 with the (as of this writing) undefeated San Francisco 49ers coming to town is a very tough position the Falcons will have put themselves in. The game against Tampa the week after the next feels like it will be a must-win, and they’ll need to find another victory somewhere else down the line that they’re currently not expected to achieve to make up for this slow start.
