title: Chicago Bears Ground the Atlanta Falcons in Caleb Williams’ Return
summary: Hello Chicago Bears fans! Well, I think we were all nervous coming into this week as we tried to forget that terrible afternoon in Lambeau and get our Bears back on track. While that Guy (Kyle Monngai) would be out for the game again, we got back the captain, the Iceman, Caleb Williams, to lead […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Michael Penix Jr. #9 of the Atlanta Falcons congratulates Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears after the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello Chicago Bears fans! Well, I think we were all nervous coming into this week as we tried to forget that terrible afternoon in Lambeau and get our Bears back on track. While that Guy (Kyle Monngai) would be out for the game again, we got back the captain, the Iceman, Caleb Williams, to lead the Bears on the field. And while the Bears had a number of starters, particularly on defense, out for the game, hope blossomed in Georgia. The Chicago Bears controlled this one for three-plus quarters with efficient offense and decisive special-teams play, but then watched the Falcons mount a spirited late rally against backups. The final score landed at 31-23 in favor of the Bears once the clock hit zero. Let’s talk about what happened. First Quarter: Bears Open the Gates Chicago came out sharp. After a methodical 10-play, 67-yard drive, Caleb Williams hit Colston Loveland for a 14-yard touchdown (Cairo Santos kick) to go up 7-0. The Bears then answered their own three-and-out defense with another sustained drive, capped by D’Andre Swift ’s 4-yard plunge. This officiating crew is known for a lot of yellow on the field, and they didn’t disappoint – well, at least if you’re a Falcons fan. More on that topic on this week’s Upon Further Review. Gooch Observation: Williams was surgical early (perfect on the opening series in some accounts), and the red-zone issues that plagued Chicago recently were nowhere to be found. Two trips, two touchdowns. The Bears didn’t just take the lead—they treated Atlanta’s end zone like an open house with free punch (non-alcoholic, of course). Gooch Aside : Hey, Sam. Yes, you, Sam Roush. Could you, I don’t know, NOT mess up horribly in every game you play in? That would be great, thanks. Second Quarter: The Muff That Mattered Atlanta finally got on the board when Michael Penix Jr. found Jahan Dotson for a 13-yard score after a chunk play to Drake London, cutting it to 14-7. Despite the fact that the Bears had dominated on the field (even though the Stripes were throwing flag after flag), this touchdown brought a certain parity to the game belied by the actual play. But, that momentum was brief. The Falcons muffed a punt (Zachariah Branch), and Josh Blackwell (yes, that JOSH BLACKWELL) recovered, and three plays later Swift punched in his second score from 2 yards out. Halftime score: 21-7 Bears . Key moment of the half: The muffed punt. It flipped field position and momentum in one bounce and handed Chicago a short field that became a touchdown. Special teams remain the great equalizer. One clean recovery turned a one-score game back into a comfortable lead. Nothing says “welcome back to reality” like turning a fair-catch attempt into a Bears touchdown. Halftime Observations The striped ones were enforcing the Bears Tax hard in the first half. In particular, missing an obvious leg whip on Swift that was at the point of attack and got the tackle – should have been a 15 yard penalty. Caleb was calm and efficient – destroying every narrative about his play in a half where he decidedly did not use his legs at all. Remember when being a Bears fan meant that 3rd and long was just a down away from the punt? How nice is it not to be chained to that reality anymore? I have to note that my prediction that this game would feature a Colston Loveland breakout game came true – and he almost hit my prop with two touchdowns! I’ll take the one. This Ben Johnson offense with Caleb behind it was dynamic and surprising. Looking back now on the parade of the backups – it is clear BJ stuck with a vanilla approach to protect those QBs and their limitations. With Caleb – we get the full flowering of the Ben Johnson offensive attack – and it flustered the Atlanta Falcons. Allen had the defense rocking. This game was a tour-de-force of the training camp heroes, as Street, Noah Sewell, Lynch, and D’Marco Jackson all made big plays for the Bears on defense. For those wondering if the Bears defense was an illusion after the Pack attack last week, Allen had a resounding response to the contrary. Last note for the half – how much better is it to have Kalif Raymond as a Bear than it is Olamide Zacchaeus. Oz again featured in a number of key drops, and Raymond was dynamic in the return and passing game. Third Quarter: Business as Usual Chicago kept the pedal down. A 7-play, 52-yard drive ended with Roschon Johnson ’s 4-yard touchdown run, pushing the lead to 28-7. The Bears owned the clock and the line of scrimmage. It was as dominant a performance as the Bears had produced against the Eagles and the Jets. This despite a major flag/yardage disparity between what the Stripes called on the Bears and what they called on the Falcons. GOOCH Observation: The running game (Swift + Johnson) was the closer in the red zone, while Williams continued to distribute efficiently. Atlanta’s offense stayed quiet. At this point, the Falcons’ offense looked like it was still looking for the parking lot. The Bears, perhaps looking forward to their short week and the Thursday Night game, began to sub in subs for a defense that had already suffered a number of “outs” for the game, and on offense, Jonah Jackson went out with a hip injury. But it looked like the Bears had the game in the bag – so why not? Well… Fourth Quarter: Santos, Then the Late Spark Cairo Santos drilled a 50-yard field goal early in the quarter to make it 31-7. We’re a clear winner right? Well, the fact is there was still quite a bit of time on the clock. Despite this, Chicago rotated in defensive backups. Penix and the Falcons took advantage: Kyle Pitts caught a 10-yard touchdown (successful 2-point conversion to Branch) to make it 31-15, then a 5-yard throw for another successful 2-point conversion to Drake London – to pull within 31-23. I was sweating. You were sweating. We were all sweating. But a late Penix fumble on a sack (forced by Kyler Gordon, and then recovered by the Bears) helped snuff out any real threat. Kyler Gordon had three sacks – the most sacks by a defensive back since Todd Bell (sidenote: I drafted Todd Bell onto my historical Chicago Bears team that we drafted at WCG this summer). Key moments: Santos’ 50-yarder provided the cushion. The two successful two-point conversions showed Atlanta’s fight, but they came against a second-team defense after the Bears had already built a 24-point lead. Gordon’s sack/fumble was a timely reminder that the starters, and how GREAT is it to have Gordon back as a starter, could still close the door. GOOCH Observation: Williams finished 30-of-36 for 305 yards and a TD (no interceptions). Swift had two short-yardage scores, Loveland contributed the early receiving TD, and Luther Burden led the receivers with 95 yards. Penix threw for three scores but spent most of the day chasing the game. Time of possession heavily favored Chicago until the final stretch. And Kyler, let me just say, for all Chicago Bears fans, ALL IS FORGIVEN AND WELCOME BACK. Final Thoughts The Bears built the lead like a team that wanted to go home early and rest up for the Thursday night tilt against the Patriots, but then they politely held the door open while the Falcons scored a couple of late ones against the understudies and made it a game again. But then the Bears reasserted themselves and again showed what had won them the game in the first place, an efficient, physical, and ultimately comfortable performance on both sides of the ball. As for the striped ones, tune in this week for “Upon Further Review” as I take those dudes to the woodshed. But what did you think about the Bears, now 4-2, and their decisive win against the Falcons? Tell us in the comments below!

title: Bengals vs. Ravens odds: Opening lines for Week 7 may hint at Lamar Jackson’s status
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are coming off their bye week with a 3-2 record and are hopefully healthy, rested, and have all their kinks ironed out. They’re 0-1 in the AFC North, having lost to the Steelers in Week 3, but will get a chance to even their division record out in Week 7 when they […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are coming off their bye week with a 3-2 record and are hopefully healthy, rested, and have all their kinks ironed out. They’re 0-1 in the AFC North, having lost to the Steelers in Week 3, but will get a chance to even their division record out in Week 7 when they travel to Baltimore to face the 4-2 Ravens. The Ravens are coming off a division loss of their own, dropping an ugly 13-10 loss to the Browns in Cleveland, but they’ve been without two-time NFL MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson, who suffered a rare medial sprain of his left ankle in Week 4. Jackson missed the entire week of practice before the Ravens’ Week 6 game and was ruled out prior to the game. It’s unclear as to whether or not he’ll be available against the Bengals, but his projected return is Week 7 or Week 8. As of right now, the Bengals are going into their Week 7 game as three-point underdogs in Baltimore, according to the FanDuel Sportsbook . This makes sense if Lamar plays, considering the ups and downs we’ve seen from both the Bengals’ offense and defense so far this season. But if Tyler Huntley were to start, the Bengals would likely be favored. If nothing else, the game would be closer to a pick ‘em, so it seems like the oddsmakers expect Lamar to suit up. Hopefully, the bye week gave Cincinnati time to figure things out. Stay tuned throughout the week for updates on both the Bengals and Ravens before their Week 7 matchup on Sunday in Baltimore. title: Bengals Bye Week Awards: Team MVP
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals hit the bye at 3-2, and if you squint, you can see how this team could’ve been 5-0 or 1-4. A three-point loss in Pittsburgh. A five-point loss to Jacksonville after Ja’Marr Chase left with a concussion in the first 18 minutes. Then a 31-24 win in Miami to stop the bleeding. […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals hit the bye at 3-2, and if you squint, you can see how this team could’ve been 5-0 or 1-4. A three-point loss in Pittsburgh. A five-point loss to Jacksonville after Ja’Marr Chase left with a concussion in the first 18 minutes. Then a 31-24 win in Miami to stop the bleeding. So who’s been the one player this team can’t do without? Here are the nominees. Joe Burrow, QB : 135-of-189 (71.4%), 1,361 yards, 11 touchdowns, three interceptions, and a 104.4 passer rating. That completion percentage leads the NFL. He’s done it while losing Colbie Young on the first play in Pittsburgh, Chase early against Jacksonville, and Tee Higgins late in that same game. Four touchdowns in Miami went to Mike Gesicki, Samaje Perine, Tanner Hudson and Chase. That’s an MVP spreading the wealth. Tee Higgins, WR : 27 catches for a team-high 423 yards (15.7 per catch). When Chase was out or limited, Higgins was the guy keeping defenses honest down the field. Ja’Marr Chase, WR: While Chase had a quiet debut and battled a concussion against the Jaguars, he has had his share of splash plays. He has four receiving touchdowns through five games, and continues to be a key to the Bengals’ success. Boye Mafe, DE : The biggest free-agent deal of the offseason, and he’s earned it: three sacks, five tackles for loss, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. He’s been among the league leaders in pressures, and he tipped the pass that became Battle’s first interception in Miami. Dexter Lawrence II, DT: The biggest free agent acquisition (figuratively and literally) by the Bengals has had a big impact on the previously maligned defense. Through five games, Lawrence has three sacks, nine tackles (five for loss), and eats up space for other defenders. Is it fair that a quarterback almost always wins this? If Burrow weren’t eligible, who’s your MVP? Sound off on the comments!
author: Anthony Cosenza

title: Bengals Bye Week Awards: Defensive MVP
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals spent the offseason loading up on defense, and five games in, you can see it. They have 17 sacks as a team, have allowed just five passing touchdowns (third-fewest in the league), and rank third in red-zone defense. The run defense is another story: 5.0 yards per carry allowed, and Miami ran […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals spent the offseason loading up on defense, and five games in, you can see it. They have 17 sacks as a team, have allowed just five passing touchdowns (third-fewest in the league), and rank third in red-zone defense. The run defense is another story: 5.0 yards per carry allowed, and Miami ran for 217 on Sunday. But this group has playmakers, and that makes this award a real debate. Boye Mafe, DE : Three sacks, five tackles for loss, four quarterback hits, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. The pressure numbers have been even better than the sack total. Dexter Lawrence, DT : Three sacks, five tackles for loss (tied with Mafe for the team lead) and six quarterback hits from the interior. Opposing offenses have to account for him on every snap, and that’s freed up everyone else up front. Jonathan Allen, DT : Three sacks, four tackles for loss, six QB hits, a forced fumble, a fumble recovery, and a pass defensed. He had a sack and a forced fumble in Miami alone. Barrett Carter, LB : 41 tackles, 1.5 sacks, four tackles for loss, a forced fumble and two passes defensed. He’s been everywhere. Entering Week 6, his 16 stops were the 15th most among all NFL linebackers and lead the Bengals. Let’s talk: Three defensive linemen with three sacks each. Which one has actually been the most disruptive when you watch the tape? And what’s the fix for a run defense giving up 5.0 yards a carry? Sound off in the comments on your pick!
author: Anthony Cosenza

title: Bengals Bye Week Awards: Offensive MVP
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals rank 10th in the league in points per game (25.6) through five weeks, and they’ve done it with almost no running game: 3.6 yards per carry as a team, with a Zac Taylor-era low of 23 rushing yards against Jacksonville. That means the passing game has carried this offense. Here’s who’s done […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals rank 10th in the league in points per game (25.6) through five weeks, and they’ve done it with almost no running game: 3.6 yards per carry as a team, with a Zac Taylor-era low of 23 rushing yards against Jacksonville. That means the passing game has carried this offense. Here’s who’s done the carrying. Joe Burrow, QB : 1,361 yards, 11 touchdowns, three interceptions, and an NFL-best 71.4% completion rate. He’s also taken nine sacks behind a line that’s still figuring things out. Through three games, his numbers almost exactly matched his 2024 pace, the year he led the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns. Tee Higgins, WR : 27 catches, 423 yards, one touchdown. He leads the team in yards by more than 130 and has been the reliable downfield option, including 90 yards and a touchdown in Pittsburgh. Ja’Marr Chase, WR : 27 catches, 289 yards and four touchdowns, despite missing most of the Jacksonville game with a concussion. He came back six days later and made a one-armed, 45-yard touchdown catch in Miami while getting mugged by the corner. Mike Gesicki, TE : Only 12 catches, but they’ve gone for 159 yards and four touchdowns. One in every three Gesicki catches has ended in the end zone. That’s red-zone efficiency in a 31-year-old tight end. Amarius Mims, OT: The mammoth right tackle has been outstanding this year. Some outlets credit him with zero pressures or sacks allowed, while PFF has him as the 6th-best pass-blocking tackle in the league right now. Higgins has more yards, but Chase has more touchdowns. Which number matters more to you? And should a quarterback be eligible for both Team MVP and Offensive MVP? Sound off in the comments on your winner!
author: Anthony Cosenza

title: Bengals Bye Week Awards: Comeback Player of the Year
summary: Last season went sideways fast. The Bengals finished 6-11, and they went 1-8 in the stretch Joe Burrow missed with a Grade 3 toe sprain that required surgery. So it’s fitting that this year’s comeback race starts with the quarterback, but he’s not the only one with a story. Joe Burrow, QB: From toe surgery […]
full_text: Last season went sideways fast. The Bengals finished 6-11, and they went 1-8 in the stretch Joe Burrow missed with a Grade 3 toe sprain that required surgery. So it’s fitting that this year’s comeback race starts with the quarterback, but he’s not the only one with a story. Joe Burrow, QB : From toe surgery to an NFL-best 71.4% completion rate, 1,361 yards, 11 touchdowns, and a 104.4 rating through five games. He posted a 123.9 rating in Pittsburgh, the best of his career against the Steelers. Anyone worried about whether he’d be the same player after that injury has their answer. Erick All Jr., TE : All tore his ACL in November 2024, had a setback in his recovery, and missed the entire 2025 season. It was his second tear of that knee, after one in his final season at Iowa. Now he’s played in all five games. The box score is modest (five catches, 30 yards), but just being out there as the versatile tight end this offense was built around in 2024 is a win. Demetrius Knight Jr., LB: This is more of a comeback story from how poorly Knight played last year. While Knight currently sits around the middle of the pack, in terms of linebacker PFF scores, it’s still a big improvement from last year. He also has a 71.9 PFF score against the run (top-20), while posting 19 total tackles and 4.5 stuffed run plays. Mike Gesicki, TE : Gesicki was limited to 13 games last season due to injury, and even when he did play, he rarely made a major impact, catching just 28 passes for 307 yards and two scores. This year, he’s already up to four touchdown grabs in five games. That’s the most scores he’s had in a season since 2022. At this pace, he’ll easily surpass his previous single-season high of six scores in 2020. Let’s talk: Should All be getting more targets than five catches through five games? What does this offense look like when he’s fully unleashed?
author: Anthony Cosenza

title: Fines handed out to Bengals after win vs. Dolphins
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are officially in their bye week after a 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins last weekend. The Bengals are now 3-2 on the young season and will have the extra week after the Dolphins win to prepare for the Baltimore Ravens. Although Cincinnati picked up the win in Miami, a few players […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are officially in their bye week after a 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins last weekend. The Bengals are now 3-2 on the young season and will have the extra week after the Dolphins win to prepare for the Baltimore Ravens. Although Cincinnati picked up the win in Miami, a few players were hit with fines on a few plays against the Dolphins. Backup tight end Erick All Jr. was fined $7,073 for an unnecessary roughness penalty against the Dolphins, while safety Jordan Battle was fined $21,623 for an illegal-use-of-the-helmet penalty. Both were important pieces in the win over a scrappy team desperate for a victory. Battle finished the day with two interceptions thrown by Malik Willis, and All finished the day with 3 catches for 25 yards. All was the second-leading receiver for the Bengals behind Ja’Marr Chase, who finished the day with 77 yards and another ridiculous touchdown. The team will need to cut down on the self-inflicted wounds before heading to Baltimore next weekend.

title: Bengals News: Early look at Cincinnati’s 2027 free agents
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals don’t play today because of their bye week, so it is a perfect time to kind of zoom out and look at things on a more macro level beyond just this season. Recently, John Sheeren from A to Z Sports put together a list of upcoming players who will have their contracts […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals don’t play today because of their bye week, so it is a perfect time to kind of zoom out and look at things on a more macro level beyond just this season. Recently, John Sheeren from A to Z Sports put together a list of upcoming players who will have their contracts expiring following the season. It may seem long at first, but in reality most teams have a laundry list of players who are set to become free agents following the end of the season, but they aren’t all filled with the same quality of talent. Here we are going to focus simply on the 2023 draft class as it seems to be the most prominent: Jordan Battle, Chase Brown, Andrei Iosivas, Myles Murphy, and DJ Turner II are all former draftees from the Bengals’ 2023 draft class set to hit free agency next offseason. That’s five starters who’ve all been together since the beginning of their careers. It is safe to say that Turner is probably viewed as the most “you have to re-sign this guy” on the entire list. If he were to hit free agency, he would easily be one of the top free agents. The odds of that are low, as the franchise tag would probably be used, but him being unsigned is likely a sign of a bigger problem Cincinnati has had, which is catching up with giving their players more guaranteed money or even guaranteed money beyond the first year. Neither side dragged this out in the media, but given how common of a theme it has been, that is likely. The problem after that is you kind of have to start looking at who is worth re-signing or maybe investing in elsewhere. We have seen this team successfully do this a few times. They opted to let pass rusher Carl Lawson and cornerback William Jackson walk in free agency after both had been fairly productive during their rookie contracts. Instead, they reinvested that money into players like Trey Hendrickson, Chidobe Awuzie, and Mike Hilton. It effectively helped lay a nice bedrock for that defense that helped them during the height of their Super Bowl window in 2021 and 2022. Are players like Chase Brown, Myles Murphy, Andrei Iosivas, and Jordan Battle replaceable for the right price in free agency or with moderate to low draft capital? I would say absolutely. Brown has had a rough patch, but even if he were playing at a high level, at some point you have to look at all the money you are spending on offense when you know you have an Amarius Mims contract coming up. Murphy might have a case depending on the price, but he likely wouldn’t sign for less than what he was set to make if they had exercised his fifth-year option without at least hitting the open market first. The front office’s biggest win was not extending Battle this offseason, like there were rumblings about. He has flashes of being a playmaker, but his tackling has been downright unacceptable for a guy who is going to be in so many open-field situations. He is 100 percent replaceable with a veteran signing. The team already has several players in place to take Iosivas’ spot at WR3. Honestly, he had been splitting time there with Mike Gesicki already, and the team could stand to add someone with a bit more speed to open things up and take advantage of the constant 1-on-1s they see because of Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. It is set to be an offseason where we may see another big turnover. The 2023 draft class has been mediocre at best, and some of the better hits are at positions that are easily replaceable. Chat live with fans during the game Browse with fewer ads Jump easily between communities and conversations Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Bengals News 3 Potential Trades the Bengals Could Make Prior to 2026 Deadline Pro Football Focus currently has Barton graded as the 27th-best linebacker in the league. The cap hit for the 30-year-old linebacker is over $4 million for the 2026 season. If it’s an all-in situation, Barton would fit the bill. The Bengals made an unnecessary cote of confidence in Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight at linebacker by not bringing in any competition at the position. Now we are seeing some consistent struggles pop back up. This team has to find a way to fix that issue and fast. We have seen the Bengals make an in-season trade in each of the last two seasons (running back Khalil Herbert 2024 and Joe Flacco last season), so it wouldn’t be that out of the realm for this front office to do something like this. Bengals banking on Al Golden, Jack Kiser Notre Dame reunion What is fortunate here is that Kiser isn’t Cincinnati’s answer to their linebacker problem. He is hopefully the answer to a special teams issue. Even though he is replacing one of their better pieces in linebacker Swayze Bozeman. This unit — especially on field goal blocking and punt return — could not be much worse. You have to consider had the Bengals not rushed anyone on field goal blocks or had anyone move on punt return that they probably have at least one more win. It is unacceptable. Bengals Could Reshape Backfield With Star SEC Running Back in 2027 NFL Draft Pro Football Focus had the Bengals landing Florida running back Jadan Baugh. Even if it isn’t Baugh, this could be the year that taking a dynamic running back makes sense to get this offense to that next level of ridiculousness. You already have Burrow, Chase and Higgins, you just need someone who can make that first man miss to really do some damage. NFL News NFL Network: Bears QB Caleb Williams (hamstring) expected to start Sunday vs. Falcons This is a big return for the Chicago Bears who are coming towards a fork in the road on their season similar in a way to how Cincinnati sits at 3-2 going into the bye week. The Bears have fared alright in his absence, but they are coming off a rough loss to the Green Bay Packers and need a jolt of energy. Eagles place Jalen Hurts on IR, as he deals with superficial blood clot This is a pretty sizable blow to an Eagles team that is already dealing with a ton of injuries. The exact severity here is still the main concern, obviously. We all want Hurts to be okay. From a football perspective the NFC East is looking more wide-open than ever. After knocking out KC Concepcion, Jets safety gets fine from NFL Minkah Fitzpatrick has — and will always be — a dirty player. What he did in this Browns game is truly unacceptable and he honestly deserves a suspension for how consistent he has been with these actions that endanger offensive players. The NFL was going to fine Chase and Higgins more for their celebration than head hunting a rookie wide receiver.

title: Browns Week 6 win in review: 4 downs lead us to shifting narratives
summary: The Cleveland Browns are 4-2. Yes, you read that right. After trailing by double digits in the first half against a Baltimore Ravens team that was missing star quarterback Lamar Jackson, the Browns scored 13 unanswered points to improve to 4-2 on the season. It wasn’t pretty (in any way), but like before, the team […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns are 4-2. Yes, you read that right. After trailing by double digits in the first half against a Baltimore Ravens team that was missing star quarterback Lamar Jackson, the Browns scored 13 unanswered points to improve to 4-2 on the season . It wasn’t pretty (in any way), but like before, the team found a way to win when it mattered the most . 1st Down: Another uneven offensive performance It’s going to be a persistent topic, but Cleveland’s offense struggled once again. Granted, the team wasn’t playing in a monsoon like last week, but the same issues that have been persistent all season were prevalent today. The run game has been nonexistent, and the passing game has been inconsistent, at best. Head coach Todd Monken didn’t do his offense any favors in the first half with his play-calling. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter pretty much bottled up the passing game by playing primarily zone, and the Baltimore defense did a great job dropping and getting to their spots. The Browns receivers struggled to get open, and Watson was hesitant to pull the trigger. Watson needs to just let it rip and be okay with making mistakes. Watson isn’t costing the team with his play, and he’s doing enough when they need him. Is it sustainable? No, but the consistency has to appear at some point. Overall, the offense was ineffective for most of the game but found a way to get something going late in the fourth quarter, again . 2nd Down: Let’s talk about the QB more In terms of the quarterback performance, Watson didn’t play well at all. However, when the team needed him, he found a way to get the job done. On paper, the stats are fine and not the worst. The film tells a different story. The flashes are brief, but his flaws are more noticeable. However, the team is finding a way to win despite that. Watson’s level of play isn’t necessarily sustainable, as I’ve mentioned before, but I do believe the Browns will be hesitant to pull the trigger on a quarterback change unless the team starts to lose. Everyone knows that the future quarterback isn’t on this team, but for years fans complained about not having competent quarterback play, which is what Watson is giving you. It’s not pretty, and it’s not flashy, but it’s better than what the team had previously, including from Watson. I am not saying that Watson has played well throughout the entire season, but he’s not playing at a level that screams “he needs to be benched.” Can the play be better? Yes. But I don’t believe that the team needs to bench him right now and winning games will certainly keep him in place. 3rd Down: This defense might be really good How about this defense? Going into the offseason, I said that going from Jim Schwartz to Mike Rutenberg was going to be an upgrade. Six weeks in, the take seems to be aging well. Scheme-wise, it’s a major improvement from last season. One of the many complaints I had about Schwartz’s defense was how the scheme was predictable. Rutenberg’s scheme is anything but that. It’s more unpredictable, with much more chaos, and the players are thriving in it. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger had a fantastic game, and defensive tackle Maliek Collins continues to be a force in the interior. The Ravens running game was nonexistent today, and the passing defense did enough to contain wide receiver Zay Flowers. Granted, the Ravens didn’t have quarterback Lamar Jackson, but this was another strong performance by a legit defense. Is it better than last year’s? 4th Down- 4-2 is 4-2. The Cleveland Browns being 4-2 right now is a surprise, and we don’t have to lie to ourselves about it. The win wasn’t pretty, but the Browns are 4-2. With that being said, no one knows how good this Cleveland Browns team is right now. I don’t. You don’t. Are they a playoff team? As of now, they have the fourth seed, but on the field they are not playing playoff-level football. The offense still has issues, but the defense is playing at an elite level. It’s a question whether or not this team can find consistency on the offensive side of the ball or will the offense just stay at this level for the entire season. Being 4-2 is a lot better than being 1-5. Or 0-6. It’s a week-to-week league, and Cleveland is finding ways to win. Can’t complain about that. Extra points Wide receiver Jerry Jeudy is giving valid reasons why the Browns shouldn’t trade him. He’s well respected in the wide receiver room, and the team probably loses if he doesn’t have the game he had on Sunday Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion both struggled today, but it happens for young players. Jared Verse played well in the run game; need the pressures to convert to sacks soon. Might as well stop talking about the running game; it was already broken before the season, and it might be a while before it actually gets fixed. Whenever Cleveland sports teams play on the same day, it feels like a guarantee both teams will not win. Wish that had been different on Sunday. A day later, what are you thinking about the Browns, their Week 6 win, and the changing narratives around the team? Join the conversation! full_text: Victory Monday , no matter how it comes, is oh so sweet for Cleveland Browns fans. A little extra sugar is added to that treat when the win is over an AFC North rival , maybe even especially over the Baltimore Ravens . Unlike many years in the past, the Week 6 win over the Ravens wasn’t just a fun thing. Instead, it established the Browns in first place in the AFC North and gave them two wins in the division, a huge tiebreaker in division and playoff standings. What does the win mean when it came from a game where most fans assumed a loss was coming and the play on the field was less than amazing? You can tell us in DBN’s Feed: What it also means is that Cleveland sits in one of the top four spots in the AFC playoff picture, just a game behind the two-seed in the division. With Monday Night Football being between two NFC squads, the Browns have the fourth seed in the AFC playoff race locked in place going into Week 7: AFC Playoff Picture after Week 6 Kansas City Chiefs: 5-0 Buffalo Bills: 5-1 Jacksonville Jaguars: 4-2 Cleveland Browns: 4-2 New England Patriots: 4-2 Denver Broncos: 4-2 Pittsburgh Steelers: 4-2 Baltimore Ravens: 4-2 Cincinnati Bengals: 3-2 Las Vegas Raiders: 3-3 New York Jets: 2-4 Indianapolis Colts: 2-4 Houston Texans: 2-4 Tennessee Titans: 1-5 Miami Dolphins: 0-5 Los Angeles Chargers: 0-6 The Jaguars own the tiebreaker over the Browns for the third seed, while Cleveland owns tiebreakers over both Baltimore and Pittsburgh for the AFC North lead. title: Cleveland Browns news: Hello, first place! We’ve missed you
summary: The Cleveland Browns are in first place in the AFC North Division! That is not a typo or a hallucination, so let’s take a moment to let that sink in. This is the first time the Browns have been in first place this late in the season, and the fact that it is only Week […]
full_text: (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns are in first place in the AFC North Division! That is not a typo or a hallucination, so let’s take a moment to let that sink in. This is the first time the Browns have been in first place this late in the season, and the fact that it is only Week 6 makes it even crazier, since Week 10 of the 2014 season. Cleveland finds itself atop the division after Sunday’s 13-10 victory over the Baltimore Ravens that followed a script that has become familiar in all four of their wins: The defense looks completely out of sorts on the first drive of the game. In this case, it was an 11-play, 66-yard touchdown drive by Baltimore. From there, the defense goes into lockdown mode. Today, it allowed just three points, a fumble recovery, and 169 yards of total offense after the first drive. The offense takes it to the extreme by bumbling around for the first three quarters. Against the Ravens, that meant three points and 107 yards of offense heading into the fourth quarter. Somehow, the offense does just enough in the fourth quarter to pull out the win. Today, that was a two-yard touchdown run from Audric Estime, and Deshaun Watson driving the Browns 62 yards to set up Andre Szymt for a game-winning 37-yard field goal. It is doubtful that the coaches and the players know how they are pulling this off, but they have done it enough to sit atop the division. title: Browns vs. Ravens Week 6: Winners and losers in a key victory
summary: The Cleveland Browns against the Baltimore Ravens is a pivotal game. So far, Cleveland hasn’t played a good team. Which means each of their wins has been against weak to mediocre teams. So, here is a good team in the Ravens. Can the Browns probably beat the division’s best team? A Cleveland win would prove […]
full_text: (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cleveland Browns against the Baltimore Ravens is a pivotal game. So far, Cleveland hasn’t played a good team. Which means each of their wins has been against weak to mediocre teams. So, here is a good team in the Ravens. Can the Browns probably beat the division’s best team? A Cleveland win would prove they can stay with talented clubs and perhaps get a playoff seed this year. But it starts with Baltimore. The Browns came into the game with a 3-2 record while the Ravens were 4-1. Prior to kickoff, both rosters had plenty of players listed on their injured list, so new players would dot both sides of the ball for each team. In the end, Cleveland was dominated by Baltimore for most of the contest, but came back and won the game on a 37-yard Andre Szmyt field goal to make it a 13-10 Browns win. The victory put Cleveland in a first-place tie for the lead in the AFC North Division, although the Browns hold the tie breaker over both the Ravens and the Pittsburgh Steelers. So, who played well for the Browns? Who didn’t? Week 6 winners – Brownies: Persistence – The Ravens dominated the game, yet in the fourth quarter, Cleveland was still just one score down. That is because Baltimore scored all of their points in the first quarter and then their offense was shut down. The Browns were able to score the game-tying touchdown off of a rare Derrick Henry fumble, and then got into field goal range to win the game late. Back in the 1980s, the Browns parlayed similar games and were crowned the “Kardiac Kids.” With four wins that were all come-from-behind victories this year, we now call this group the “Myocardial Vascular Adolescents.” Plays that won the game – Baltimore kicker Tyler Loop missed a 49-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter. Ravens running back Henry fumbled on their next possession. The fourth-and-two delay-of-game penalty against Baltimore with 2:08 remaining that became a punt instead. The third-and-five miscommunication between safeties Jaylinn Hawkins and Malachi Starks about who was supposed to pick up the crossing route of Browns wide Jerry Jeudy with 42 ticks left in the game, which became a 33-yard gain into field goal range. What do all of these things have in common? They are all Baltimore mistakes. 33 YARDS down the field! #BALvsCLE on Fox pic.twitter.com/OToiJ0J6fZ — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 18, 2026 WR Jerry Jeudy – All week, Browns media and fans alike debated whether to trade Jeudy before next month’s trade deadline. Back and forth the subject went. Jeudy not only balled out against Baltimore, but he also bailed out the Browns. In the second quarter, on a second-and-four with 8:32 left before the half, quarterback Deshaun Watson hit Jeudy for a 14-yard gain when the Browns offense wasn’t moving at all. With 4:36 left in the game, Watson again found Jeudy for 13 yards to convert a third-and-six into Baltimore territory. Then came the clincher on the final drive. Jeudy led all receivers with 69 yards on four catches, and caught all four of hit targets. Nice work. LB Carson Schwesinger – The kid was everywhere. He was a bit slack on coverage of the tight ends, but his tackling skills were on full display. Early in the first quarter, he collided with Henry for a three-yard gain that shook the stadium. Rhino against Ram. As the opening quarter was winding down, Baltimore quarterback Tyler Huntley found Henry for an outlet pass, but Schwesinger nailed the talented back for just a two-yard gain. In the second quarter, Henry was bottled up inside and took to the corner, only to have Schwesinger take him down for no gain. On the first play of the fourth quarter, Huntley was facing a third-and-22 and found tight end Josh Cuevas as Schwesinger tackled him for an 11-yard gain instead of moving the sticks. The Henry fumble was caused by Schwesinger, which proved to be a pivotal play in the contest. Then, with 2:57 remaining, Huntley was flushed out of the pocket and took off needing eight yards, but instead found Schwesinger after gaining six. Baltimore then was going for it on a fourth-and-two, but a delay-of-game penalty set them back and forced a punt. Schwesinger finished with a game-high 13 total tackles. Defense – Baltimore appeared to be a runaway train early in this one. They built a 10-0 lead during their first two possessions. But as the second quarter began, and Cleveland’s offense was struggling, the defense put a brisket on to cook and was smoking for the duration of the game. As outlined, Schwesinger played a terrific game, but so did his partner in crime, linebacker Quincy Williams, who had six tackles, a second-quarter sack, and two quarterback hits. Defensive tackle Sam Kamara nailed Henry for a two-yard loss in the second quarter and minus one late in the third quarter. Cornerback Denzel Ward broke up a pass to wide receiver Zay Flowers early in the second quarter. Defensive tackle Maliek Collins dropped Henry for a one-yard loss before halftime, then had a second-quarter sack. Defensive end Adin Huntington had back-to-back pass rushes that forced Huntley to throw early as the half was winding down, which became incompletions. Defensive end Jared Verse caught Henry for a one-yard gain early in the third quarter. Defensive end Isaiah McGuire had a sack with 57 seconds left on the clock in the third quarter. Then, lastly, the Browns needed a defensive stop when Baltimore got the ball back with 3:40 left, an eternity in the NFL. Williams tackled Cuevas for just two yards; safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren stuck it to Flowers for an incompletion, but dropped a sure interception late in the fourth stanza. As time was getting sparse, Huntley scrambled and was forced out of bounds by Schwesinger, needing eight yards and gaining only six. A Baltimore penalty forced a punt, and the Browns offense trotted on the field one more time. . @denzelward : the best of the best 🙂‍↕️ #BALvsCLE on Fox pic.twitter.com/6LFsQlUcEb — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 18, 2026 The defense came to play. After Baltimore’s offense built a 10-point cushion, the Browns’ defense shut them down. On their third possession and until the end of the game, the Ravens: punt, punt, punt, punt, punt, missed FG, lost fumble, punt, punt. Week 6 Losers – Frownies: CB Myles Harden – Too many times, Harden was getting juked and faked out. Then, how many balls could he have batted away or even intercepted if he had just turned his head around and found the ball in flight? Had two batted balls and could have had double digits. Three tackles. Third-down efficiency – Any time an offense struggles to convert third downs, it becomes more of a punt team. The defense needs the offense to stay on the field longer. Five of 16 is absolutely atrocious. Use of tight ends – This was a game that was tailor-made for the talents of tight end Harold Fannin, yet he had just three targets all game, with one reception for nine yards. Figure that out. Then tight end Blake Whiteheart had only one target and grabbed it for eight yards. That was it. Wasn’t this offense supposed to be 12 and 13 personnel heavy? TREY HENDRICKSON SACK!!! Tune in on FOX. pic.twitter.com/g1kdly9oo9 — Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) October 18, 2026 Offensive line – These sacks and penalties are killing any momentum the offense generates. Name a time/quarter when Watson was not flushed from the pocket on passing downs. The Ravens defense just came in rain sheets for the majority of the game, except in the final quarter for whatever reason. Rookie right guard Austin Barber is outmatched on most passing downs. Most of the pressure was coming up the gut, but both left tackle Spencer Fano and right tackle Tytus Howard had issues with blitzing linebackers. Stunts were the giant killers in this game. Several times, the Browns O-Line was blocking three men on two defenders, with a guy looping around with a free shot at…

title: Browns vs. Ravens: Quick takeaways from Week 6’s amazing win
summary: The Cleveland Browns and Baltimore Ravens locked up in an AFC North “battle” in Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season. The home team’s offense was atrocious for most of the game, while the visitors made big plays when they needed them, especially on third downs, but points were at a premium heading into the […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns and Baltimore Ravens locked up in an AFC North “battle” in Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season. The home team’s offense was atrocious for most of the game, while the visitors made big plays when they needed them, especially on third downs, but points were at a premium heading into the fourth quarter. A somewhat wild, somewhat boring game between two teams struggling with injuries ended with the Browns beating the Ravens 13-10 and taking first place in the AFC North. Neither team played well; injuries showed up in the overall performance Sometimes, a 10-10 game in the 4th quarter is all about great defenses. Sometimes, it is just two teams struggling on offense. Week 6 was the latter, mostly, in a game where it was obvious how much talent was missing from the field. Deshaun Watson isn’t quick enough Whether it is quick decision-making on throws, quick cuts, quickly pulling the ball down to run, or quickly giving up on a play, Watson seems to be slow in everything he does. Even his running has seemed to slow down as the season has gone on. While the announcers said receivers weren’t getting open, it is also on Watson to throw players open, and he seems uncomfortable attempting to do that. The offense’s problems were not all on him, but the quarterback lacking any anticipation and gumption to throw the ball takes everyone out of rhythm. Watson hitting his back foot and delivering, as he did to KC Concepcion in the 4th quarter, is what the team needs from him. Line, backs, or system? Run game issues remain With Quinshon Judkins, Raheim Sanders , and Dylan Sampson all out for the game, it is a bit hard to pinpoint the primary issue for Cleveland’s run game, but it continues to be a problem. The shotgun formation is a setup where the back can’t get any momentum and is limited to only a few run routes. The defense can then tee off on those routes. The line is getting pushed around a bit, and there is only so much you can expect from two running backs who were signed off the street and practice squads this season. Give Jaleel McLaughlin, Audric Estime credit, however While the run game was lacking, McLaughlin and Estime made some important plays, including some key blocks in pass protection. In the 4th quarter, both new to the Browns backs had important rushes, including Estime’s game-tying run. McLaughlin runs hard every play, fighting every tackler and pushing ahead with everything he has. Predictably unpredictable on defense, especially on 3rd downs The biggest difference between Mike Rutenberg’s defense and the one run by Jim Schwartz is his blitzing. The former defensive coordinator rarely did; the new one does in very creative ways. And, seemingly, on most third downs, which Baltimore knew were coming and took advantage of, especially on long third downs. If the offense knows it is coming, even if where it is coming from is unpredictable, plays can be schemed up to protect the quarterback and/or have him on the move. Jerry Jeudy redeeming himself and raising trade value Just three catches for 36 yards before the 33-yard gain on 3rd and 5 late in the game, Jeudy made some big plays, including great hands on a throw behind him on a key play earlier in the 4th quarter. Jeudy also didn’t have a drop in the game. While none of that is eye-popping, Jeudy’s willingness to push through weeks of getting only a few targets but still coming up with big plays was huge for the team. If GM Andrew Berry decides to trade the veteran receiver, as rumored, Week 6 was helpful for his value. Cannot compete when you can’t convert third downs Heading into the 4th quarter, this was true: The Browns are 1-10 on third down — Zac Jackson (@AkronJackson) October 18, 2026 Teams cannot win if they cannot sustain drives. The drive in the middle of the fourth quarter, the Browns converted a few key third downs, including a big play to Concepcion and a pass interference call. Lack of consistency is not surprising for a young team, all-new HC/OC/DC Why does Cleveland’s offense come alive in the fourth quarter? Why does the Browns defense look lost, then like one of the best in the NFL? It is as simple as the young roster and having a first-time head coach, offensive coordinator, and defensive coordinator. Young isn’t a bad thing, but the lack of experience at most of the important positions leads to the up-and-down swings we’ve seen this season. Kickers are mostly inconsistent; it just depends on when and how often With 3:40 left, Andre Szymt missed a 48-yard field goal that would have given Cleveland the lead. While kickers are making longer and longer kicks in the NFL, they remain “when,” not “if,” they could fail your team. Sometimes it happens multiple times during a season; other times a kicker will fall off a cliff and not be heard from again. Hopefully, Szymt’s miss was just a miss, but most fans should not assume their kicker is going to make every kick. There are a couple of kickers each year that do, but the clock is sometimes just ticking before they miss as well. Szymt got a chance to redeem himself and end the game from 37 yards out and came through.
author: Jared Mueller

title: Baltimore Ravens vs. Cleveland Browns recap: Back in first place of AFC North with late rally
summary: It was a frustrating opening quarter for the Browns, who went down 10-0 immediately. The defense pitched a shutout the rest of the game, though, and forcing a fumble in the fourth quarter led to Cleveland’s first touchdown of the game to tie things up at 10-10. They drained some clock and tried a field […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 18: Tyler Huntley #5 of the Baltimore Ravens throws a pass against Adin Huntington #98 of the Cleveland Browns during the second quarter of the game at Huntington Bank Field on October 18, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was a frustrating opening quarter for the Browns, who went down 10-0 immediately. The defense pitched a shutout the rest of the game, though, and forcing a fumble in the fourth quarter led to Cleveland’s first touchdown of the game to tie things up at 10-10. They drained some clock and tried a field goal, but it was no good from 48 yards out. The defense forced a punt, and Cleveland got a shot to lead a two-minute drive. They executed with a big catch by WR Jerry Jeudy , and this time, Szmyt hit the game-winner for the 13-10 win and first place in the AFC North! Let’s get to the full game recap. 1st Quarter – Ravens vs. Browns The Ravens received the opening kickoff, and just like we’ve seen this season, opposing teams took their first drive right down the field on the Browns’ defense. RB Derrick Henry had runs of 11 and 17 yards, and QB Tyler Huntley completed a couple passes. Then, facing a 3rd-and-6 at the Browns’ 17 yard line, Huntley completed an 8-yard pass to WR Ja’Kobi Lane to set up a goal-to-go situation at the 9 yard line. Huntley used his legs to improvise and run for 7 yards, but Henry was bottled up on second down to set up 3rd-and-goal at the 1 yard line. Huntley gave it to Henry, but S Emmanuel McNeil-Warren chopped him down for a loss of 1 yard. Baltimore went for it on fourth down, and off of the playaction fake, Huntley found backup TE Josh Cuevas open in the back of the end zone for a touchdown to put the Ravens up 7-0. TOUCHDOWN RAVENS!!! FIRST CAREER TOUCHDOWN FOR @JCuev_80 !! Tune in on FOX!! pic.twitter.com/Lb9kKMqtLw — Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) October 18, 2026 Unfortunately, Cleveland’s opening drive didn’t last long: a first down incompletion, and then after a 5-yard run by RB Jaleel McLaughlin (starting for the injured Quinshon Judkins ), Watson was sacked on third down by DE Calais Campbell after the defense dropped zone coverage into the Browns’ route patterns. After the punt by P Corey Bojorquez , Baltimore took over at their own 39 yard line. Cuevas lined up at guard, but off the line, on the next play, and Huntley found him wide open on a catch-and—run crosser for 30 yards, plus 15 yards tacked on due to a roughing the passer penalty on DT Maliek Collins . Two runs by Henry only netted 1 yard, setting up 3rd-and-9 in the red zone. Huntley’s throw for WR Rashod Bateman was off the mark, so K Tyler Loop came on and hit a 34-yard field goal to put the Ravens up 10-0. On the Browns’ second drive, they got a first down after a quick pass for 9 yards to WR Jerry Jeudy , but nothing was going after that. A run and Watson combined for no gain on the first two downs, and on third down, a free rusher came on a twist, forcing Watson to throw the ball in the dirt. Bojorquez’ punt went out of bounds at the 22 yard line. Also of note: S Grant Delpit was officially ruled out for the rest of the game with a concussion. The Ravens had two penalties (one declined) to close out the first quarter on offense. 2nd Quarter – Ravens vs. Browns Baltimore couldn’t get going and punted. The Ravens’ gunner made a terrific diving save to prevent the ball from going in the end zone, batting it back to the 4 yard line. RB Audric Estime picked up 7 yards for some breathing room, and then on second down, another run made it 3rd-and-1. Watson kept it on the sneak on third down to move the chains. The drive went no where after that: a screen to TE Harold Fannin was doubled and thrown in the dirt, then Watson had no where open on second down, so led McLaughlin to having his head taken off by S Kyle Hamilton for just a yard, and then his scramble on third down didn’t get to the line to gain. KYLE. HAMILTON. 😱 😱 Tune in on FOX. pic.twitter.com/2I1tSNGi52 — Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) October 18, 2026 Bojorquez boomed a 62-yard punt to get the ball to the 17 yard line. title: Cowboys news: Dallas drops second-straight game behind a flat offensive performance
summary: In a complete reversal compared to the rest of the season, the defense gave the Cowboys multiple opportunities to get back into this game. However, despite the Green Bay defense continually bailing the Cowboys offense out with penalties, Dallas was completely unable to get anything going. Dak Prescott looked shaky in the pocket, the offensive […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images | Getty Images In a complete reversal compared to the rest of the season, the defense gave the Cowboys multiple opportunities to get back into this game. However, despite the Green Bay defense continually bailing the Cowboys offense out with penalties, Dallas was completely unable to get anything going. Dak Prescott looked shaky in the pocket, the offensive line gave Prescott no time, the receivers dropped balls, and the running game was nonexistent. Uncomplimentary Cowboys on full display in 23-13 loss to Packers on SNF- Shane Taylor, Inside The Star Somehow, the 13 points are misleading; the offense was actually worse than that. Six of those points came in garbage time where Dallas had next to no chance to win. A 10-0 lead felt like game over for Dallas, and it clearly was. The Cowboys had a pick-6 taken off and CeeDee Lamb fell down, leading to an interception. It could be 14-10 Dallas, but it was 17-0 Green Bay at the half. Why? Because it is the Cowboys. This team cannot get out of their own way, and we see it every single week. The offense stinks, the defense stinks, the head coach stinks and the list goes on and on. Game Recap: Cowboys lose to Packers, 23-13- Kurt Daniels, DallasCowboys.com The disappointing part of this game was it felt all too familiar. Green Bay had a successful first drive, and then from then on out, Dallas was fighting an uphill battle. The game certainly didn’t get off to the start the Cowboys wanted. After the team punted on its first offensive possession, Green Bay took over and promptly went on what has become an all-too-familiar lengthy march that took 6:30 off the clock. Dallas simply couldn’t get off the field on the 90-yard drive as the Packers converted four third-down attempts, including twice moving the chains despite facing third-and-13. Even the touchdown was a third-and-6 toss from Love to Golden for the early 7-0 lead. Download the SB Nation app today! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . 7 instant reactions as Cowboys get embarrassed again in ugly loss to Packers- Jerry Trotta, The Landry Hat This may be an overreaction, but this game may be the end of the Cowboys’ season. Even a win next week against the Eagles would mean the Cowboys have a long uphill battle if they want to win the division. The Cowboys got one first down on the game’s first drive, but did not pick up another. To put it kindly, Schottenheimer’s play-calling was questionable. Why would you throw short of the sticks on third down if you don’t plan on going for it on fourth down? Does that make sense? No targets for CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens. After 10 days of preparation following last week’s loss? That’s a really, really bad look. Eagles Lose Fourth Straight, Giants Face a Choice at QB | Around the NFC East- Phillip Hughes, Sports Illustrated Once again, the only consolation from the weekend was that the rest of the NFC East again fell flat. The Eagles and the Giants both lost, and the Commanders are 7.5 point underdogs tomorrow against the 49ers. With approximately seven minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, the Giants also lost offensive lineman Andrew Thomas for concussion evaluation. Thomas had been questionable heading into Week 6 due to a groin injury, but was active for the start of the game. 3 things we learned about the Cowboys versus Packers- Dyllan Rivers, Blogging The Boys The season has been incredibly frustrating so far. Dallas can’t seem to do anything right, there is no balance to the offense and defense, and the self sabotage has gotten out of control. Everything is difficult for the Cowboys Nothing has come easy for this team in the last two weeks. There is little-to-no room for error, and the Cowboys simply cannot stop making mistakes. Whether it’s dropped balls, missed blocks, or just plain slipping – Dallas cannot get out their own way.

title: Cowboys vs. Packers: 2 winners and 4 losers from the game
summary: The Dallas Cowboys arrived at Lambeau Field needing a response after an ugly loss to Tampa Bay, but another slow offensive performance and unprepared defense left Dallas chasing the game all evening.  Dallas went into halftime down 17-0, with turnovers and penalties repeatedly wasting opportunities leading to Dallas falling to Green Bay 23-13. Here are […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys arrived at Lambeau Field needing a response after an ugly loss to Tampa Bay, but another slow offensive performance and unprepared defense left Dallas chasing the game all evening. Dallas went into halftime down 17-0, with turnovers and penalties repeatedly wasting opportunities leading to Dallas falling to Green Bay 23-13. Here are this week’s winners and losers from the game. Winner: Dee Winters Dallas has waited a long time for an interception, and Dee Winters finally delivered one. Winters read Jordan Love perfectly late in the first quarter, stepped in front of the pass and appeared to return it for a touchdown before replay ruled him down at the Green Bay 42-yard line. Even without the score, it was exactly the type of momentum-changing defensive play Dallas has desperately needed. The frustrating part was that the offense immediately wasted the opportunity with an interception of its own. That shouldn’t take anything away from Winters. On a defense that was searching for takeaways and impact plays, Winters provided one. Winner: Quinnen Williams The Cowboys needed considerably more from their defensive front after weeks of inconsistent pressure, and Quinnen Williams made his presence felt early. Williams got to Jordan Love for a sack and helped Dallas produce a much more disruptive start up front. Green Bay found success through the air, but its conventional rushing attack has been much less effective. Williams’ sack was one of the Cowboys’ biggest early defensive plays and it was needed to try an inject some optimism in a defense that’s struggled this season. This is the type of performance Dallas expected when it paid the price to bring Williams into the middle of the defense. The Cowboys need him affecting games rather than simply occupying blockers, the sack showed exactly that. Loser: Brian Schottenheimer For the second straight week, the Cowboys looked completely unprepared offensively for long stretches, and it’s the second straight week Schottenheimer finds his way on the loser list. Dallas getting shut out at halftime trailing 17-0, producing no points despite the defense creating a turnover and giving the offense opportunities is a huge disappointment. The Cowboys turned it over twice, struggled to establish any rhythm and again waited until the second half before finally showing signs of life. That is especially disappointing against a Green Bay defense missing major pieces, including Micah Parsons, Javon Hargrave and Edgerrin Cooper. Dallas spent the week admitting it was still searching for an offensive identity, with establishing Javonte Williams and the running game identified as part of the solution. Yet the same problems returned at Lambeau Field. Williams had only 11 carries, Dallas had just 48 total rush yards. Schottenheimer is the head coach, and at some point these repeated slow starts become his responsibility. Dallas cannot keep needing halftime adjustments before its offense looks ready to play. Loser: Cowboys third-down defense This isn’t just a problem tonight, it’s becoming one of the defining weaknesses of the Cowboys defense. Dallas entered Week 6 allowing opponents to convert 30 of 57 third downs with a 52% conversion rate. That means opponents were moving the chains on more than half of their third-down opportunities before Jordan Love even stepped onto the field. There were moments Sunday night when Dallas produced excellent first- and second-down defense, only to allow Green Bay to stay on the field when it mattered most. That’s particularly damaging because it wears down the defense, keeps Prescott and the offense on the sideline and allows the Packers to control the pace of the game. The Cowboys did force an important three-and-out to begin the second half, which helped set up a touchdown drive. But one successful series doesn’t erase the larger problem. Getting teams into third down is supposed to be the hard part, Dallas kept doing that and then failing to finish the job. Green Bay had 18 third downs and converted on 11, that’s a success rate of 61% and that makes controlling a game impossible. Until this changes, even good defensive possessions are going to keep turning into long drives and the time-of-possession war is never going to look good Dallas. Loser: Dak Prescott Dak Prescott needed a major bounce-back performance after struggling against Tampa Bay, instead, the turnovers continued. Prescott threw two interceptions before the end of the third quarter, including one in Green Bay territory immediately after Winters had given Dallas excellent field position. That erased what should have been a major opportunity for Dallas to answer Green Bay’s opening touchdown. The second interception came after CeeDee Lamb slipped, so that one carries no blame for Prescott. But Dallas entered halftime scoreless with its quarterback having two interceptions beside his name and the pressure was clearly getting to him. The Cowboys needed Prescott to settle the offense after last week’s problems and he didn’t do enough of that. Dak was clearly rattled and facing a Packers defense that was allowing 22 points per game. What we saw was a quarterback having back-to-back games where he panicked, felt pressure, and failed to throw a touchdown until late in the fourth quarter, ending the game with a passer rating of just 65.2. Loser: Caleb Downs Caleb Downs had a difficult night trying to limit Matthew Golden and Green Bay’s passing game. Golden produced six catches for 104 yards and a touchdown, including gains of 37 and 21 yards. Dallas has moved Downs around the defense, but whether playing deeper or closer to the line, the rookie wasn’t been able to help take away one of Jordan Love’s favorite targets. Golden consistently found space and produced explosive plays when Green Bay has needed them and the majority of the time he was lined up opposite Downs. There will always be growing pains for a rookie safety, especially against an offense capable of moving receivers around to create favourable matchups. But Dallas drafted Downs to become exactly the type of defender who can erase explosive plays and help control dangerous receivers. Tonight, Golden won that battle.
author: Mike Poland

title: 3 things we learned about the Cowboys versus Packers
summary: The Dallas Cowboys slipped to 2-4 on the season, as they look less and less like the team most envisioned coming into the season. After their loss to the Green Bay Packers, we learned some things. Everything is difficult for the Cowboys Nothing has come easy for this team in the last two weeks. There […]
full_text: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys slipped to 2-4 on the season, as they look less and less like the team most envisioned coming into the season. After their loss to the Green Bay Packers, we learned some things. Everything is difficult for the Cowboys Nothing has come easy for this team in the last two weeks. There is little-to-no room for error, and the Cowboys simply cannot stop making mistakes. Whether it’s dropped balls, missed blocks, or just plain slipping – Dallas cannot get out their own way. In the first half, the defense performed extremely well on first and second down. They could not get off the field on third, however, regardless of the distance. It didn’t matter if the defense sent the heat on a blitz or if they dropped their guys back in coverage – the Packers and Jordan Love had their number. In a way that wasn’t supposed to happen this season, the offense mirrored the defense’s inadequacies throughout the first half. Zero points scored paired with two turnovers on the plus side of the field is not the ideal situation. Put it all together and you end the first half down by 17 points. The defense did clamp down after half time, allowing just six points after the break. The offense never truly found their way, scoring just two touchdowns on the night. The offense remains lost Zero points in the first half, with 13 points on the board at the final whistle is not good enough, and will never be good enough with the way this Cowboys team is constructed. The team will win zero games if that’s the offensive result each week. This is a unit featuring some of the best playmakers in the NFL, yet for the second week in a row, they cannot adjust to the blitzing onslaught from their opponent. Dak Prescott was under assault the entire game, taking hit after hit, sometimes even resulting in personal fouls. Everything is out of rhythm and very little is working. They need to figure out how to beat the blitz if they’re going to have a chance on offense. This is a blueprint other teams will attempt to duplicate until Dallas can figure out how to stop it. Where’s the rushing attack? This team still refuses to run the ball, even when it’s working. Balance does not seem to be something that Brian Schottenheimer is too interested in through six weeks, and especially the last two. Regardless of what the head coach says to the media, sticking with the run is clearly not in the forefront of the mind of the head coach and play caller. Ten carries on the night for Javonte Williams until nearly two minutes left in the fourth quarter is inexcusable considering the game was well within reach for the entire second half. Dallas ran the ball five-out-of-nine plays on their opening drive of the second half, resulting in a touchdown. After that, there was not another run play called until nearly two minutes left in the fourth quarter. The play-caller felt the pressure to put up points. It’s possible he didn’t trust his defense to get stops in the second half, which is reasonable. But the rushing attack was working, and it was completely abandoned when it wasn’t necessary to do so. This offense needs balance if it’s going to survive. Dak Prescott cannot throw the ball 50 plus times each week, or this could be the result.

title: Cowboys lose to Packers in humiliating and humbling fashion
summary: Death, taxes, and the Dallas Cowboys being no match for the Green Bay Packers in the 21st century. Much was made about how it had been 10 years (Thursday was the official anniversary) since the Cowboys tasted victory against their longtime rivals. Sunday night offered the next opportunity, and we are all going to have […]
full_text: Oct 18, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) talks with Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer talk during the first quarter against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Death, taxes, and the Dallas Cowboys being no match for the Green Bay Packers in the 21st century. Much was made about how it had been 10 years (Thursday was the official anniversary) since the Cowboys tasted victory against their longtime rivals. Sunday night offered the next opportunity, and we are all going to have to keep on waiting. The Cowboys were never really in the game against Green Bay and seemed to be fighting themselves as much as they were the Packers. It is hard to believe that they had the mini bye to prepare for this as they looked as without preparation as a Cowboys team has looked in some time. Dallas is officially 2-4 after their latest outing and while they have the “benefit” of playing in a down NFC East… they in no way look like a team that you can trust right now. In fact, they looked like that last week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and only corroborated that notion at Lambeau Field. This is a really tough moment for a Cowboys franchise that has experienced several of them within the last 1,000 days (and well beyond that, but you know what I mean). What happens next? Anything? Should something? Only time will tell. Below you will find our recap of how this mess unfolded. Welcome to another long week. First Quarter The Cowboys won the toss and chose to receive, interestingly. It seems that they wanted to set a tone. Unfortunately that was not the case. While Dallas picked up a first down, they ultimately punted right after. Their opening drive lasted just six plays before putting the defense on the field. Gulp. It turns out fear was appropriate. The Packers put together a masterclass drive that featured two different 3rd and 13 conversions. While the Cowboys were showing some aggression early on in it they quickly were put on their back foot. Green Bay ultimately cashed in with a Jordan Love to Matthew Golden touchdown which game them a 7-0 lead. The Cowboys responded by going three and out on offense which had things feeling rather tense. It seemed like Green Bay was destined to march down and make it 14-0. Dee Winters said no, though! For real! He intercepted Jordan Love and replay eventually showed he was down before getting up and returning it for a touchdown. Still, it helped. INT!!! pic.twitter.com/ou9mlZY1Fv — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) October 19, 2026 As this was happening KaVontae Turpin was being ruled out with a rib injury, hopefully he is alright long-term. The quarter ended after CeeDee Lamb had a big gain. Second Quarter That was the first interception of the season for the Cowboys defense so capitalizing on it would have been ideal. Unfortunately that was not the case. Dak Prescott took a huge shot on second down as the team was inside the 20 and then one play later didn’t see a Packers defender and was picked off. Those are the types of things this team cannot afford. EVAN. WILLIAMS. 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/H2dBumCPkg — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 19, 2026 Green Bay marched almost all the way down the field, but thankfully was held out of the endzone as they could smell it. The Packers faced a fourth and goal from the Dallas 2-yard line, lined up to go for it, the Cowboys called a timeout to get set, and the Packers made it seem like they were going to go for it before taking a delay of game. They ultimately kicked the field goal to make things 10-0 with about six minutes left before halftime. While the Cowboys were “only” down by 10, this felt like a must-score drive for the Cowboys, especially with the Packers set to receive the kickoff after halftime. Dallas was really moving and grooving, and it seemed like they felt that urgency. As the two-minute warning hit they were well within field goal range, and unfortunately on the first play out… CeeDee Lamb slipped on a slant route and Dak’s pass had nothing between him and Green Bay’s Brandon Cisse. Brandon Cisse's first NFL INT! DALvsGB on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/9wXk2Vevi2 — NFL (@NFL) October 19, 2026 Somehow… it all got worse. The Packers masterfully moved all the way down the field, partly thanks to Brian Schottenheimer inexplicably calling a timeout and stopping the clock for them, and scored another touchdown with under a minute to go. The home team took a 17-0 lead into halftime and prepared to come out and get the ball again. Third Quarter The quarter began with Green Bay’s offense on the field and more points felt inevitable given the way the game had gone to that point. Miraculously, the Cowboys forced a punt. A tried and true punt. It was hard to believe. What’s more is the offense turned it into legitimate points, the most possible as a matter of fact. On a drive where Brevyn Spann-Ford got the lion’s share of work at tight end the Cowboys finally capped things off with Javonte Williams and drew blood for the first time in the game. Javonte Williams gets the @DallasCowboys on the board! DALvsGB on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LCSq1izwak — NFL (@NFL) October 19, 2026 It would have been foolish to assume the Cowboys could force another Packers punt. That assertion wound up accurate, but they did force the next-best thing in a field goal. This extended Green Bay’s lead to 20-7. Dallas took over and the pressure was seriously mounting what with a quarter and some time left. Unfortunately they could not get much going themselves and had to punt the ball away. No bueno. Green Bay’s next possession began close to their goal line, and it ended even closer. Kenny Clark sacked Jordan Love on third down and forced yet another punt. The Cowboys took over on offense and the quarter came to a close shortly after. Fourth Quarter Things began with Dallas driving and down by 13. They soon reached a fourth and short near midfield. They went for it… and did not get it. That felt very much like the ballgame. Green Bay turned their possession into another field goal to make things 23-7 which left the Cowboys with very faint, but literal hope. It turned out to be faint at the absolute best. Needing touchdowns and two-point conversions the Cowboys were forced to go for another fourth down well on Green Bay’s side of the field and turned it over on downs. Ballgame. Although technically not. The Cowboys scored a touchdown inside of the final minute, failed the two-point attempt, and then failed the onside kick attempt. That was officially ballgame. The Packers beat the Cowboys yet again, this time by a final score of 23-13.
