title: Chargers-Chiefs Game Recap: Groundhog Day again as Bolts stay winless
summary: The Chargers fell to the Chiefs 22-6 on Sunday afternoon on the road in Arrowhead Stadium. Los Angeles six points on the day, by far their worst scoring output of the season. Against a stout Chiefs defense, Herbert was chased around the field as he’s become accustomed to in recent years. Despite Kansas City failing […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 18: Chris Jones #95 of the Kansas City Chiefs tackles Omarion Hampton #8 of the Los Angeles Chargers in the second quarter of a game at Arrowhead Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers fell to the Chiefs 22-6 on Sunday afternoon on the road in Arrowhead Stadium. Los Angeles six points on the day, by far their worst scoring output of the season. Against a stout Chiefs defense, Herbert was chased around the field as he’s become accustomed to in recent years. Despite Kansas City failing to sack any quarterback since Week One, they managed to bring down Herbert four times. Herbert was also picked off for the eighth time this season on a play where he was hit from behind as he threw. The ball sailed nowhere near his intended target and right into the waiting arms of linebacker Jack Cochrane. Herbert finished with 204 passing yards on 22-of-37 passing with one pick and no touchdowns. It was his sixth consecutive game this season in which he turned the ball over more times than touchdown scored. He also rushed for a team-high 26 yards on five scrambles. It was another game in which Herbert had to do everything because…well…this is what the Chargers have built around him. Four rookies started once again on the offensive line in front of him. A silver-lining heading into today’s matchup was the return of receivers Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston, Brenen Thompson, and KeAndre Lambert-Smith. However, McConkey left the game with a head injury early in the first half and Thompson did not play despite being active. Johnston ended the game with one catch for 57 yards (a bomb from Herbert in which QJ looked like he caught it on accident) while KLS caught a team-high five passes on nine targets for only 32 yards. There wasn’t much help coming from the ground game, either. Kansas City came in ranked seventh against the run (92.8) and the Bolts managed just 73 yards on 22 carries (3.3). Kimani Vidal led the backs with 21 yards on seven carries while Hampton took seven totes for 18. Defensively, O’Leary’s unit had to face a Chiefs offense averaging nearly 30.0 points per game and they once again stood tall in moments where most other groups would have faltered. At one point, they stopped the Chiefs and running back Kenneth Walker (19-128-2) at the one-yard line to force a turnover on downs. In all, the Chargers turned the ball over three times (Herbert INT, downs, KLS fumble) and the defense held Kansas City to just one successful field goal, one missed field goal, and an interception of Patrick Mahomes by cornerback Cam Hart. But what did that do for the offense’s momentum? Absolutely nothing. Six points is what the Chargers got. Following three turnovers by the Chiefs, the Los Angeles offense turned it into a pair of punts and a turnover of their own. The Chargers are now 0-6. They haven’t been 0-6 since the 2000 season when they finished 1-15. There will be no postseason. The potential wins left on the schedule look few and far between. As of Sunday night, the Chargers hold the number one pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. The Dolphins, who are also 0-6, sit behind them. Jim Harbaugh and his team could go into full-on tank mode. If this season truly is a fluke, then the idea of adding a premium player at the top of the draft to a group that won 22 games from 2024-2025 doesn’t sound too bad. But I think there’s some reality in that scenario that needs to be addressed. The first overall pick is not going to fix what we’ve seen from this offense. It’s not going to fix Justin Herbert’s eight picks or the league-leading 16 giveaways that Mike McDaniel’s unit has coughed up through six games. Everything is about to be evaluated over the next seven-plus days. Everything should be up in the air at this point. If there’s one thing ownership does not like, it’s a tidal wave of negative criticism. At 0-6, that’s all the Chargers are going to receive this week. Prepare accordingly for that first domino to fall. Continue on below for a complete recap of today’s game. First Quarter The Chiefs offense was up first and they came out of the gate throwing. On their first play from scrimmage, Mahomes found receiver Xavier Worthy for a gain of 33 yards, but it was called back due to an illegal block in the back by tight end Travis Kelce. That still gave the Chiefs only a first-and-five which was quickly converted on another pass to Worthy for 15 yards. That was then followed by a 13-yard carry by Kenneth Walker on his first touch of the game. A holding call on Chiefs left guard Trey Smith brought Kansas City back to a second-and-18. Mahomes only found tight end Noah Gray for 16 yards on third-and-18, so Harrison Butker came on to convert from 44 yards out and give the Chiefs an early 3-0 lead. The Chargers’ first drive of the game was a quick three-and-out that definitely did not look the way they drew it up. On first down, Herbert threw a designed swing to Omarion Hampton into the right flat but the play was snuffed out immediately for a loss of one. On second down, Herbert booted to his left after a handoff but Chiefs edge rusher George Karlaftis was in his face immediately and Herbert’s pass attempt to Keaton Mitchell in the flat was deflected. Herbert then tried to check the ball down to running back Kimani Vidal on an angle route but the pass went straight into the helmet of left tackle Travis Burke which led to an incompletion. The Chiefs only needed six plays to find the end zone for the first time. On third-and-one from the Chargers’ 33, Walker broke through a pile of bodies up the middle and outraced cornerback Tarheeb Still into the end zone. Butker missed the extra point so Kansas City led 9-0 about halfway through the quarter. On the Chargers second drive of the game, the offense found some life. Herbert got it started with a 17-yard pass to wideout Ladd McConkey. A pair of Vidal runs and a Derius Davis jet sweep combined to move the chains a second time for the Chargers. After a pair of six-yard scrambles by Herbert, the Bolts had first-and-10 from the Chiefs 11-yard line. They managed just six yards from there which led to a Cameron Dicker field goal from 23 yards out. That made it a one-score game at 9-3. Second Quarter The Chargers defense stepped up to begin the second quarter by forcing a punt from the Chiefs after a DPI call on cornerback Deane Leonard. After the flag brought Kansas City to midfield, they allowed just eight yards and got the stop on third down. On second-and-three at the Chiefs 42-yard line, Herbert threw his eighth interception after trying to whip a ball to receiver KeAndre Lambert-Smith while being sacked. The ball did not have enough power behind it and it floated short of KLS into the arms of linebacker Jack Cochrane who returned it 48 yards the other direction. There was a flag on the play, but it ended up being an illegal formation penalty on the Chargers which was declined. A fate would have it, the Chargers defense stole it right back. On the fifth play following the LAC turnover, Mahomes threw a desperate attempt to the back of the end zone but cornerback Cam Hart dropped off his assignment to undercut the pass for his second interception of the season. A four-yard Hampton run was followed by a one-yard trot by Mitchell to begin the next LA drive. On third-and-five, Herbert found wideout Theo Wease for seven yards with a toe-tapping grab on the right sideline. After initially being called incomplete, the Chargers challenged the call and won. On the ensuing third-and-nine, Herbert scrambled for seven yards after being stopped in his tracks by linebacker Nick Bolton which forced another punt. The Chiefs got back into the end zone via another run from Walker. This time, from the two-yard line, Walker received the handoff and reversed field aided by a Mahomes block on Tuli Tuipulotu before prancing in for the score. After forcing another…

summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are getting ready for their Week 6 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. While most of the players are getting ready, a few members of the team will be on the inactive list. S Derwin James (hamstring), WR Tre’ Harris (hamstring), CB Rodney Shelley (hamstring), CB Donte Jackson […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - SEPTEMBER 20: Los Angeles Chargers offensive tackle Joe Alt (76) stands by during a timeout during an NFL game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the Los Angeles Chargers on September 20, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA.(Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Los Angeles Chargers are getting ready for their Week 6 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. While most of the players are getting ready, a few members of the team will be on the inactive list. S Derwin James (hamstring), WR Tre’ Harris (hamstring), CB Rodney Shelley (hamstring), CB Donte Jackson (hamstring), OLB Bud Dupree (neck), LG Kayode Awosika (fibula) and RT Joe Alt (neck) are all out for the Chargers against the Chiefs. It’s a lot of key players who are out for the Chargers. Alt’s injury woes are bleeding into 2026 after he was on the sidelines for most of 2025. James is also missing the game, which marks three straight absences for the former All-Pro defensive back. LB Daiyan Henley (knee), DT Dalvin Tomlinson (hamstring), WR Brenen Thompson (quad) and DT Jamaree Caldwell (knee) were all on the injury report, but are all active. Meanwhile, the inactives for the Chiefs are WR Rashee Rice, TE Jared Wiley, QB Garrett Nussmeier, DB Jadon Canady, DE Jack Pyburn, OT Diego Pounds and OT Josh Simmons. Rice is the most notable of the Chiefs inactives, but his absence isn’t much of a surprise. He hasn’t played since Week 3 against the Miami Dolphins. Kickoff between the Chargers and Chiefs is set for 1:25 p.m. PT inside Arrowhead Stadium. Fans can watch the game on CBS or stream it on the Paramount Plus app.

title: Kicker wishlist: Rams likely need to replace Blake Grupe
summary: Blake Grupe’s debut with the Los Angeles Rams last only a single kick. He injured his knee defending an early return and was quickly ruled out for the game. Grupe was seen on crutches following the game, suggesting that he won’t be available for some time. Following last week’s kicker struggles, I posted a shortlist […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Blake Grupe #19 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on before a game against the Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Blake Grupe’s debut with the Los Angeles Rams last only a single kick. He injured his knee defending an early return and was quickly ruled out for the game. Grupe was seen on crutches following the game , suggesting that he won’t be available for some time. Following last week’s kicker struggles, I posted a shortlist of kickers the Rams should target if they indeed moved on from Harrison Mevis. They did, and signed Grupe in replacement. But now it’s time to dust that list off again . It’ll be shorter and includes less quality options this time around. The Rams have done it to themselves. Priority #1: Tanner Brown, Free agent Maybe the Rams did not initially sign Brown because the team has history with the player. Brown signed with the Rams after going undrafted in 2023. After competing with another undrafted rookie in training camp, LA effectively concluded neither were good enough and opted for veteran Brett Maher instead. But Brown’s career has progressed nicely away from the Rams. He’s perhaps the best kicker in the United Football League (UFL) for the Louisville Kings. Brown made all three of his attempts from beyond sixty yards last season, which is a four-point play in the UFL. Overall he converted 25 of 28 opportunities. It was debatable whether the Rams should have went with Brown or Grupe to start. They made their decision. Now it’s time to go for option B. Priority #2: Charlie Smyth, Saints Poaching a player off another team’s practice squad is not a risk-free endeavor. NFL rules require that player stays on the 53-man roster for at least three games. Grupe will likely be placed on injured reserve to create a spot, depending on the severity of his injury. The downside is more performance based, because the Rams would effectively need to roster two kickers if the first guy isn’t good enough. And Smyth is a risk by himself. He has played in only six regular season games and made 12 of 16 field goal attempts with a long of 57. Smyth converted all 13 extra point tries. It’s worth nothing that the Saints can keep Smyth on their practice squad with an extra roster spot as part of the league’s International Player Pathway (IPP) program. As a former soccer player from Northern Ireland, Smyth is one of the developing international players that can be retained without counting against traditional practice squad slots. Priority #3: Jake Moody, Free agent Moody has failed in prior NFL stints with the San Francisco 49ers and Washington Commanders. He most recently spent time with the Baltimore Ravens but was released from their practice squad in mid-September. Moody made 10 of 11 field goals and 10 of 11 extra points in six games with Washington last year. No one has seen enough to keep Moody around. This feels like a desperate option for the Rams. Priority #4: Younghoe Koo, Free agent The lowest ceiling of any of the aforementioned options. Koo has bounced around the NFL in recent years. He seems on his way out. Priority #5: Harrison Mevis, Free agent We broke up with you, but it was a mistake. Take us back. We can debate whether Mevis should have been blamed for the missed overtime field goal against the Buffalo Bills. It’s speculation whether his kick would have missed, even though it looked off the ideal trajectory before it hit a defender and straightened out. Mevis isn’t the long-term option for the Rams. His lack of range is paradoxical to the modern prowess of kickers. Even with that in mind, he’s at least a known commodity.
author: JB Scott

title: It’s time to start Ty Simpson
summary: The Los Angeles Rams invited a quarterback controversy. The time of reckoning is now. If LA would have ignored the backup quarterback position as they had done in recent years, there would be no conversation. Instead, this year is different. They drafted Ty Simpson thirteenth overall. With the Rams currently holding a 2-4 record and […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 27: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Ty Simpson (15) runs the ball for a gain during the NFL preseason game between the Los Angeles Chargers and the Los Angeles Rams on August 27, 2026 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams invited a quarterback controversy . The time of reckoning is now. If LA would have ignored the backup quarterback position as they had done in recent years, there would be no conversation. Instead, this year is different. They drafted Ty Simpson thirteenth overall. With the Rams currently holding a 2-4 record and tied for last place in the NFC West with the lowly Arizona Cardinals, the playoffs are far out of reach barring a dramatic reversal in overall team performance. This is a losing team. At some point you must accept who you are and decide who should be part of the turnaround next year. Matthew Stafford won’t be back in 2027. He looks like a shell of his MVP form from a year ago. Stafford can’t mitigate pressure, be consistently accurate, take care of the football, or complete a deep pass to save his life . Tiptoeing around Stafford’s mulled retirement in order to avoid rocking the boat does not help the team. Learning what Simpson is capable of and whether he is a viable long term option is of the upmost importance. Simpson is the future. Stafford was at his best a decade ago. It’s time for change. The whole idea was that Simpson was supposed to sit behind Stafford for a year and learn from one of the game’s best. What is Stafford teaching him now? How to lose to a 1-4 team? That you can turn the ball over every single week and keep your job? Simpson proved in the preseason—despite its low stakes—that he is ready. He avoided pressure in the pocket, displayed his mobility, demonstrated his decision making and processing upside, and looked poised even in the face of adversity. Stafford is currently somewhere around the 14-17th best quarterback in football. Are we sure Simpson couldn’t be better, even if rookie mistakes are expected? It’s a low bar to clear, and Simpson’s running ability brings a high floor to the table. Stafford’s struggles seem different this time. He has made mistakes in the past but played well enough to overcome them. That’s not happening this time around. It’s mostly all downside with little to make up for it. We know what Stafford is capable of. It’s obvious he’s not putting his best on display. At his age, it’s unlikely he can regain form. 2026 is becoming a lost season. Finding the franchise quarterback of the future would give this year purpose. That’s why it’s time to start Ty Simpson.

title: Blake Grupe on crutches, Rams likely need new kicker for Week 7
summary: The Los Angeles Rams may need another kicker ahead of Week 7 after Blake Grupe was spotted on crutches, raising questions about his availability for the upcoming matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. Spotted on his way out of the locker room was recently signed kicker, Blake Grupe, who suffered a knee injury in the 2nd […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Blake Grupe #19 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on before a game against the Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams may need another kicker ahead of Week 7 after Blake Grupe was spotted on crutches, raising questions about his availability for the upcoming matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. Spotted on his way out of the locker room was recently signed kicker, Blake Grupe, who suffered a knee injury in the 2nd quarter on an attempted tackle during kickoff coverage. Rams kicker Blake Grupe is on crutches and his leg is in a brace. He’s saying goodbye to his teammates on the way out of the locker room. — Arash Markazi (@ArashMarkazi) October 18, 2026 With the Rams already struggling to find consistency on special teams, the injury at the place kicker position creates more unwanted complication for Sean McVay’s team. Los Angeles must find stability at the position. Grupe’s status will be worth monitoring as the Rams prepare for their next game but considering he was seen saying goodbye to his teammates in the locker room, it seems likely that the kicker will be placed on IR or waived altogether. Being on crutches does not automatically rule him out, but it raises legitimate concerns about his short term and long term availability. If he cannot go, Los Angeles will likely need to bring in another kicker to what has already been a nightmare of a season to start. Instability at the position has cost the Rams far too long. Harrison Mevis was released after struggling through five games, forcing the team to look for an alternative option. Losing Grupe before Week 7 would mean another change at a position where consistency is critical for a team aspiring to be playing in January and February.

title: Rams-Cardinals takeaways: Playoffs odds take hit…
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have plenty to address after a disappointing Week 6 performance against the Arizona Cardinals. What should have been an opportunity to get back on track instead turned into another frustrating afternoon, as the Rams fell 18-16 and continued to raise questions about their consistency in 2026. Los Angeles entered the matchup […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Blake Corum #24 of the Los Angeles Rams hurdles Garrett Williams #21 of the Arizona Cardinals in the second quarter of a game at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams have plenty to address after a disappointing Week 6 performance against the Arizona Cardinals. What should have been an opportunity to get back on track instead turned into another frustrating afternoon, as the Rams fell 18-16 and continued to raise questions about their consistency in 2026. Los Angeles entered the matchup needing a strong response, but the offense struggled to deliver enough points while the team failed to capitalize on opportunities that could have changed the outcome. In a division where the San Francisco 49ers continue to build momentum, every loss makes the Rams’ path toward the postseason increasingly difficult. With the season threatening to slip away, there are several lessons Los Angeles must take from this defeat. From execution on both sides of the football to the decisions that shaped the final result, Week 6 exposed concerns the Rams cannot afford to ignore moving forward. 1st Down: Rams playoff odds are not good… Currently, the Rams have a 43% chance to make the playoffs. That might actually surprise you. Regardless, the Rams are going to need help now as they navigate to secure a wild card spot in the NFC. Playoff chances for the NFC West, per @NextGenStats : 1. 49ers (5-0): 96% 2. Seahawks (3-3): 58% 3. Cardinals (2-4): 4% 4. Rams (2-4): 43% Are the Rams' chances … too high?! pic.twitter.com/f5L0qbNSQJ — Henry McKenna (@henrycmckenna) October 18, 2026 2nd Down: Rams aren’t a great football team (right now at least)… Great football teams do not commit silly penalties in crucial moments. It happened with the Warren McClendon false start that killed a drive and resulted in a turnover on downs. And then on the Cardinals final drive, the Rams were flagged twice on the big play. The Rams were offsides AND Josh Wallace was flagged for an unnecessary roughness penalty. While the latter was bogus to say the least, it still does not excuse the offsides penalty; giving the Cardinals a free play. In addition, the Rams also have limped across this season with its special teams. You need all three phases to be a great team in the NFL. 3rd Down: Tackling Issues Bam Knight might as well have looked like Bijan Robinson in the 2nd and 3rd quarters. The Rams defense was on the field far too long because they could not stop the run. The Cardinals offense was able to run 70 offensive plays, far too many against a defense that did not allow a touchdown all day… The Rams' tackling on this drive has left a lot to be desired — Adam Grosbard (@AdamGrosbard) October 18, 2026 4th Down: Alaric Jackson’s Week 5 postgame actions had a huge effect Alaric Jackson’s selfish decision to throw a punch at Bradley Chubb had huge ramifications. With David Quessenberry plugged in at left tackle, the Cardinals decided to blitz the Rams early and often. While Quessenberry wasn’t glaringly bad, the Rams line wasn’t as smooth with its protection of Stafford, surrendering three sacks. It forced the Rams offense to work even harder to try and climb back into the game. Los Angeles is fortunate the suspension was reduced from a 2 game suspension to 1 game.
author: Steven Ridings

title: Winners & Losers: Rams fall to Cardinals, 2-4, and hit rock bottom
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are inventing new ways to lose. Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals sure feels like rock bottom. LA dropped to 2-4 following a 16-18 loss to Arizona. Flatly put, the Cardinals entered this game with a 1-4 record. The Rams should have trounced them. Instead, the offense looked anemic yet again despite […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Blake Corum #24 of the Los Angeles Rams reacts after scoring a receiving touchdown against the Arizona Cardinals in the second quarter of a game at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are inventing new ways to lose. Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals sure feels like rock bottom. LA dropped to 2-4 following a 16-18 loss to Arizona . Flatly put, the Cardinals entered this game with a 1-4 record. The Rams should have trounced them. Instead, the offense looked anemic yet again despite a favorable matchup. They failed to muster more than nine points until the game’s final moments. The defense kept the Cardinals out of the end zone; however, special teams and offensive failures continued to put them in disadvantage field position leading to six field goals. It’s all bad right now. The damage that has already been done may be insurmountable. So who put the Rams in the losing column again Sunday? Let’s be honest about the individual contributions. Winners Puka Nacua, WR This wasn’t Nacua’s most electric performance and he didn’t fill up the box score. Even still, Nacua accounted for 79 of LA’s 223 gross passing yards (35%) with six receptions. No other individual receiver surpassed 39 yards. The passing game started flat, showed signs of life late, and couldn’t do enough to finish with a win. Stop me if you’ve heard that before. And even on the offense’s final two drives, outside of Colby Parkinson stretching for a touchdown, Nacua was doing all the work. He caught a short pass from Stafford and broke tackles to put his team in scoring position. He later added another long pass. The Rams cannot ask Nacua to be their entire passing attack. It’s not a sustainable approach. Puka ‘big plays’ Nacua pic.twitter.com/UN3tRrNtf9 — 11ª jarda (@11ajarda) October 18, 2026 Aaron Donald, DE Donald was most disruptive in the run game where often made first contact at or behind the line of scrimmage. The Cardinals’ passing game is not efficient and they heavily relied on screens. These run stops often put Jacoby Brissett behind the chains and helped the defense get off the field. Aaron Donald doing GOAT things, slipping behind blockers, going back door for a TFL this is time capsule AD pic.twitter.com/5xSQmjUMcc — Jim Youngblood 53 (@53_jim70721) October 18, 2026 Josh Wallace, CB We should have an honest conversation of whether Josh Wallace should take over for Jaylen Watson opposite Trent McDuffie moving forward. Wallace has been the better corner the last two weeks. Wallace was targeted very often in this game—often on screen plays. He was stingy in terms of space allowed and was forceful making tackles and deflecting passes. While his initial 2026 debut was rough, he’s earned the right to be on the field over the two most recent games. Quentin Lake, DB Lake struggled mightily last week after fighting through an injury just to be active on gameday. The ailment must be in the rearview mirror because Lake looked like his normal self today. The veteran safety picked off Brissett in the first quarter setting up LA’s first score. Lake made seven solo tackles and assisted three times. It was an active afternoon. Quentin Lake INT! AZvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SI43YVW2NQ — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 Losers Matthew Stafford, QB With the two defenses the Rams have faced over the last two weeks , we should feel much better about where Matthew Stafford and the passing game are. Instead, Stafford continues to put the ball in harm’s way—even if not reflected as turnovers in the box score—and is leading an offense that continues to underperform. Stafford gets absolutely smoked from his blind side and fumbles the ball! The big man scoops it up and rumbles downfield for a huge return for the Cardinals!💥 pic.twitter.com/N4O5Q8M2f0 — J💥S Sports (@JordanOnSports1) October 18, 2026 LA’s red zone struggles were heightened today with their kicker getting injured early. These tough circumstances also highlight how the Rams are playing offense with one hand tied behind their back because their quarterback is immobile. Running ability with lower the degree of difficulty in short yardage situations. Even more concerning is the fact that Sean McVay called plays scared for the offense. With the ball less than a minute before halftime, the Rams ran out the clock. On third and fourth down with a chance to take the lead, McVay called two consecutive screen plays. That doesn’t suggest he trusts his quarterback. Stafford has done nothing of late to change his mind. And something we must reconcile with over the coming weeks is whether it’s time to pull Stafford. The Rams are 2-4. There is no talking about playoffs until performance dramatically improves. 2026 is fast becoming a lost season. The team may be better served long term to collect information on Ty Simpson. Goals change for losing teams. Stafford should know as he’s been a part of many of them. PUKA NACUA CATCH OF THE YEAR pic.twitter.com/0NAkUvk6Rz — seahawksmemes (@seahawksmemes_) October 18, 2026 Tyler Higbee, TE The Rams would be in a tough spot following recent injuries to Terrance Ferguson and Colby Parkinson if Tyler Higbee didn’t step up over the last three weeks. On the other hand, you cannot have a veteran player and locker room leader fumble the ball when driving for the lead in the fourth quarter. While this play didn’t directly cost LA the game, it certainly was still costly. Resetting at kicker… again Blake Grupe made a 48-yard first quarter field goal to quell concerns at the kicker position. It was possible that the Rams moved on from Harrison Mevis and found their guy. Instead, Grupe injured his knee defending on a kickoff and was quickly ruled out for the remainder of the game. The search for continuity at kicker likely continues.

title: 5 key plays from Rams embarrassing loss to Cardinals
summary: The Los Angeles Rams suffered a frustrating 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals, dropping a divisional matchup that could have significant implications for their season. Looking back at the matchup, five key plays stand out as defining moments in the Rams’ narrow defeat. The Rams had opportunities to come away with a victory, but close […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Bam Knight #20 of the Arizona Cardinals runs the ball against the Los Angeles Rams in the first quarter of a game at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams suffered a frustrating 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals , dropping a divisional matchup that could have significant implications for their season. Looking back at the matchup, five key plays stand out as defining moments in the Rams’ narrow defeat. The Rams had opportunities to come away with a victory, but close games often hinge on a handful of critical moments. Against Arizona, those moments proved costly as Los Angeles struggled to do enough to finish the job. With the final score separated by just two points, even a single missed opportunity or pivotal play can change the entire story of a game. From crucial situations on offense to the defensive stops and special-teams contributions that shaped the contest, these sequences help explain how Los Angeles let a winnable game slip away. Here’s a closer look at the five key plays that determined the outcome of the Rams’ 18-16 loss to the Cardinals. 1. Rams fail to convert 2 pt conversion After Blake Grupe was knocked out of the game because of … lower body? injury, the Rams tried for a 2 point conversion after Blake Corum’s touchdown. Stafford tried to connect with Davante Adams on a fade but held onto the ball way to long; allowing for an Arizona defender to hit him from the blindside. The Cardinals nearly scored themselves on the play as LJ Collier tried to scoop the ball and return it the distance. The final score was 18-16 and the Rams would surely wish they could have converted on that play. title: Rams-Cardinals final score: L.A. loss puts playoffs in jeopardy
summary: The Los Angeles Rams need to win against the teams they should beat. They didn’t do that on Sunday as Sean McVay lost to his former protege Mike LaFleur and the Arizona Cardinals, 18-16. The Rams lost on a walk-off field goal by Chad Ryland at the final second, one minute after taking a late […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams need to win against the teams they should beat. They didn’t do that on Sunday as Sean McVay lost to his former protege Mike LaFleur and the Arizona Cardinals, 18-16. The Rams lost on a walk-off field goal by Chad Ryland at the final second, one minute after taking a late one-point lead thanks to hero punter Ethan Evans. It was another heartbreaking loss for the 2-4 Rams, as their season is about as close to life support as it can get, falling to last place in the NFC West. Behind the Cardinals. McVay and defensive coordinator Chris Shula were out-coached by LaFleur, and the Rams need to look at themselves for this loss. Penalties, turnovers, and a lack of urgency was L.A.’s identity on Sunday, and it led to a fitting defeat. McVay told the media after the game, “We beat ourselves”. We'll never win a game if we don't figure out how to stop beating ourselves. -Sean McVay on with us postgame — J.B. Long (@JB_Long) October 18, 2026 An Offensive Embarrassment A week after giving up 45 points to the Detroit Lions, the Cardinals held the Rams to 16 points as their offense was inefficient against one of the worst rated defenses through five weeks. Matthew Stafford went 25-of-33 for 222 yards, 2 touchdowns, and no interceptions. But that stat line wouldn’t paint a picture of how inept L.A.‘s offense was for the duration of the game. It took a late touchdown pass to Colby Parkinson just to get to 16 points, with kicker Blake Grupe injured early in the first quarter . The Rams were unable to kick field goals after that, going for two points on their initial touchdown, leading to a sack-fumble of Stafford. Josh Sweat LEVELS Stafford on the 2 point attempt. The Cardinals defense nearly houses it but gets caught. pic.twitter.com/Aggeb9J4Gx — The Goal Line Grind (@theGLgrind) October 18, 2026 There’s a growing trend that this Rams offense can’t seem to get going except when trailing or later in the game, and that happened again in Week 6 as the Rams failed to get much going on offense until the fourth quarter. 16 points is rarely enough to win in the NFL and it wasn’t enough to win on Sunday. This is an exciting victory for Arizona and an embarrassing loss for the Rams. The Rams should be concerned as McVay looks to be regressing as a playcaller. The offensive mastermind used to attack defenses on third and long. Now, the coach calls screens that have a higher chance to lose yards than gain the needed first down. This game was expected to be a “get right” style game for L.A. Instead, the Rams looked flat throughout the day. Defense Was OKAY, Not good enough L.A.’s defense was without Trent McDuffie and Myles Garrett, and they were still the stronger unit than the Rams’ offense. The defense kept the Rams in the game, a reoccurring theme this year, by holding the Cardinals to six field goals and no touchdowns. However, the defense still allowed SIX scoring drives to the Cardinals. Including not being able to get a stop on Arizona’s game-winning drive for an easy 43-yard field goal by Ryland. CHAD RYLAND WINS IT FOR THE CARDINALS pic.twitter.com/QfTHlvwVcr — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 The bend don’t break defense would have been effective for the Rams, but they needed their offense to score touchdowns for that style of defense to work, and the offense left much to be desired as Stafford didn’t break 100 passing yards until the fourth quarter. Arizona came into the game with the idea of keeping L.A.’s offense off the field, and they did that. Arizona lined up with bigger personnel to run the ball, and the Rams relied on their smaller defensive backs while the Cardinals played more physical than L.A. and controlled the clock. The silver lining for the Rams is that they kept the Cardinals out of the end zone, but they didn’t give their offense much of a chance to get in rhythm or expose the Cardinals questionable defense. A lost season? The Rams fall to 2-4 and have more questions than answers. The question L.A. has answered is they look more like a bad team than a good one, and if this keeps up, people will lose their jobs. The Rams entered 2026 looking at the Super Bowl. Through six weeks, the Rams sit well outside the playoff picture as they aren’t looking at the Super Bowl, they are looking at a lost season. Should heads roll? That’s not something you would think after a loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia, but through this season the Rams have continued to look like worse. Not better.

title: Rams lose new kicker moments into his L.A. debut
summary: The Rams signed Blake Grupe last week to replace Harrison Mevis as the team’s new kicker, but that stint may be over before it even started. Grupe injured his knee while attempting to make a tackle in the first quarter of L.A.‘s Week 6 game against the Cardinals and is doubtful to return. Grupe made […]
full_text: The Rams signed Blake Grupe last week to replace Harrison Mevis as the team’s new kicker, but that stint may be over before it even started. Grupe injured his knee while attempting to make a tackle in the first quarter of L.A.‘s Week 6 game against the Cardinals and is doubtful to return. Grupe made a 44-yard field goal just before the injury. If necessary, it appears that punter Ethan Evans will kick field goals for the Rams. Evans has never attempted a field goal in the NFL. Evans went 10-of-18 on field goals as a college kicker/punter at Wingate. Unbelievably, new #Rams K Blake Grupe, who just replaced Harrison Mevis, is doubtful to return with knee injury. — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 18, 2026 The Rams can’t seem to avoid special teams problems, even when they try, which isn’t always. The Rams have consistently gone through multiple kickers per season and now it appears that L.A. could already be on their third kicker next week, assuming that Grupe’s injury is bad enough to keep him out. Given how quickly he was ruled as doubtful, that could be the case.

For Arizona, they just had a deflating loss to the Detroit Lions and have lost 4 games in a row after starting their season 1-0. Meanwhile, the Rams have lost two out of their last three, and may still be stunned form their narrow primetime loss to the Buffalo Bills. The Rams have had some success over the Cardinals since Sean McVay became L.A.’s head coach. The new head coach in Arizona, Mike LaFleur, would love to change that narrative and lead his team to a big win in L.A. The Rams are up against it a bit here as a loss could end their shot at the division and the playoffs. A win still doesn’t assure L.A. anything but it would give them some breathing room. title: Raiders-Bills: 17 things we learned
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders went back to playing competitive football Sunday in Week 6 after an embarrassing blowout defeat in Week 5. However, the Raiders are still not playing enough winning football and they has turned a promising 3-0 start to the season to a sobering 3-3 record after a 33-30 home defeat to the […]
full_text: . (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders went back to playing competitive football Sunday in Week 6 after an embarrassing blowout defeat in Week 5. However, the Raiders are still not playing enough winning football and they has turned a promising 3-0 start to the season to a sobering 3-3 record after a 33-30 home defeat to the 5-1 Buffalo Bills on Sunday. This game was similar to Week 4 when the Raiders lost at home 30-27 to the Kansas City Chiefs. Like the Chiefs, the Bills made more plays and were leading late but the Raiders were valiant, but ultimately couldn’t catch up. As Raiders’ head coach Lint Kubiak said Sunday, though, there are no moral victories. A clearly frustrated Kubiak said the team has to close teams out. But really they have to stop falling behind and playing catch up. They have to go back to playing winning football. The Raiders have forced one turnover in the past three games after forcing nine takeaways when they went 3-0. Las Vegas has to learn to win against good competition. Their next opponent is the Los Angles Rams, who were a a preseason Super Bowl favorite, but they now sit at 2-4. The three teams the Raiders have beaten are a combined 2-15. The Raiders must beat the Rams or they will have a losing record. Three weeks ago, Las Vegas was tied for the best record in football. Now they trail the 6-0 Chiefs by three games in the AFC West. Eight teams in the AFC have more wins than the Raiders. Here are some key aspects of this game: Defense sags: Rob Leonard’s defense continues to get gutted. They have allowed 135 points in the past four games and have allowed 30 or more points for three straight games for the first time since 2019. Bills’ quarterback Josh Allen and running back James Cook toyed with the Raiders’ defense for most of the game. This is the play of the year so far. Josh Allen. WOW. pic.twitter.com/qy8XrhsbDs — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 18, 2026 Mayer cooks, Bowers comes on late: The Bills were focused on containing Brock Bowers, so Michael Mayer did work. He had 95 yards on seven catches. Bowers did get targeted until late in the third quarter. He did find a way to contribute as he finished with four catches for 70 yards. Tucker delivers: Wide receiver Tre Tucker had his second strong game of the season as he had 97 yards and two scores on five grabs. Run game still uneven: The Raiders’ ground game had some success in the second half, but it also struggled at times. Starter Ashton Jeanty had just 22 yards on 10 carries. Rookie Mike Washington got involved after not being a big part of the plan last week and he responded with two 10-plus yard run. He finished with 43 yards on nine carries. Yet, the Raiders are still looking for consistency in this area. Red-zone offense is off: The Raiders were 2 for 5 in the red zone, which pissed off Kubiak. You’re not going to beat Allen that way. The Bills were 3 for 5 in the red zone. That was the difference. No reported new injuries: The Raiders didn’t report any injuries Sunday. They are relatively healthy at this point of the season and should get defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway, the only starter not to play Sunday, back in Week 7. JPJ benched: Kubiak suggested last week that their would be competition during the practice week in an attempt kickstart the offense line. Most of the speculation surrounded on left guard Spencer Burford, who has struggled in pass protection. Yet, the change Sunday was 2025 third-round pick Caleb Rogers replacing 2024 second-round pick Jackson Powers-Johnson at right guard. This could be a fluid situation because Kubiak has stated he believes in both Powers-Johnson and Rogers. Rough start for Bills’ offense: Buffalo had two call two timeouts on their first offensive drive of the game. Ouch. Key Buffalo defender bounced: Buffalo cornerback CJ Gardner-Johnson was disqualified for the first of the game late in the second quarter after an incident with Brock Bowers. Gardner-Johnson appeared to spit at the Raiders’ direction. It was a huge advantage for Las Vegas. Porter is starter again: In an expected move, 2025 third-round pick Darien Porter started at an outside cornerback spot ahead of fifth-round pick, rookie Zeke Masses. Porter got the majority of snaps last week after Masses stole Porter’s starting job earlier in the season. But Masses had struggled after a hot start. Masses did take over in the second quarter. They continued to rotate in the second and and that will likely continue moving forward. Big special teams penalties: Raiders’ special teamer Segun Olubi was called for holding on a Raiders; kick return late in the game and then when that series ended with a punt. He was called for a face mark. Brutal. Third-quarter woes continue: The Bills outscored the Raiders 10-0 in the third quarter. Las Vegas has been outscored by 26 points in the third quarter this season. It’s the worst deficit in the NFL. Kubiak said he is very “upset” about the Raiders are starting the second half. Issues with tush push: The Raiders’ tush-push attack with fullback Cam Heyward snapping t he ball has not been great this year. It bit them on fourth and short late in the second quarter when were called for a false start. They had to settle for a field goal to make it a 13-10 game. It was the third penalty on new Raiders’ center Tyler Linderbaum has three penalties on tush-push plays this season. Kubiak said these penalties are “killing” the Raiders. Fatukasi starts: Foley Fatukasi got the starter’s snaps at defensive tackle with Hemingway out with a concussion. Another fan takeover: We knew the Bills’ Mafia would be loud and it was. It was estimated that about 65 percent of the Allegiant Stadium stands were occupied by Bills’ fans. This was Buffalo’s first game in Las Vegas with fans allowed in the stadium. Bills Mafia travels well. Allen heard “MVP” chants and he said it felt like a Bills’ home game. It’s a point of frustration for the Raiders. Two key Bills’ player didn’t suit up: Buffalo key starters, wide receiver DJ Moore and defensive lineman Ed Oliver, were inactive Sunday. They were listed as questionable on the the injury report. Rookie inactive: The Raiders elevated rookie defensive end Cian Slone from the practice squad on Saturday. Yet, they made him inactive for the game. Slone can only be in elevated twice more this season from the practice squad.

title: Las Vegas Raiders lose to Buffalo Bills for 3rd straight defeat
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are playing are hosting the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. Here is everything to need to know about the contest: First quarter The Raiders won the coin toss and deferred to the third quarter. The Bills went down the field to kick a short field goal to take a 3-0 lead on […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are playing are hosting the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. Here is everything to need to know about the contest: First quarter The Raiders won the coin toss and deferred to the third quarter. The Bills went down the field to kick a short field goal to take a 3-0 lead on the first drive of the game. The Raiders came back and scored a touchdown to take a 7-3 lead with 4:27 go in the quarter on a 1-yard touchdown run in which the Raiders had a good push on. It was Jeanty’s first rushing score in 14 games. Second quarter: . The Bills cruised down the field, but, in the end, had to settle for a field goal to cut the score 7-6 with 14:45 to go in the quarter. The Raiders will win this game if the can continue to stay tough on third down on defense. The Raiders were forced to punt on their second drive of the game. The Bills easily went down the field on the fuel of some big chunk plays to take a 13-7 lead with 7:13 to go. Buffalo already has 183 yards of defense. The Raiders answered with a field goal to cut the score to 13-10 with 2:23 to go after a nice drive stalled. Kwity Paye, who had been very quiet since Week 1, had a big sack to force the Buffalos to punt late in the half. That was a huge stop by the Raiders’ defense. The Raiders got down into field-goal range and Mat Gay tied it at 13-13 at the half. It was a good half for the Raiders and they get the ball to start the second half. Third quarter: The Raiders’ blew an opportunity by going 3-and-out to start the second half. The Bills responded with a touchdown, but a penalty wiped it out. Buffalo did convert a field goal to make it 16-13 with 9:45 to go. A bad interception thrown by Kirk Cousins. Bills’ ball at Raiders’ 32. The Bills’ cash in with a touchdown pass from Josh Allen to Keon Coleman as Buffalo took a 23-13 lead with 6:22 to go. Fourth quarter: The Raiders got the ball inside the Bills’ 5-yard line, but two straight run calls lost yardage. They had to settle for a 23-yard Matt Gay field goal. The Bills lead 23-16 with 13:32 to go. The Raiders’ force a huge three and out. The Raiders answer. Cousins to Tre Tucker for the tying score. 23-23 with 8:07 to go. The Bills marched down the field to take a 30-23 lead with 4:43 to go. Raiders must answer again. Score and go for two? Nope, punt. The Bulls hit a field goal to make it a 33-23 game with 1:55 to go. Cousins hits Tucker for a deep TD. 33-30. It’s not over. Bills’ get the inside kick. It’s over. Final score: Bills 33, Raiders 30 Now that the game is over, let’s take a look at the key aspects: Team records: The Las Vegas Raiders are 3-3. The Buffalo Bills are 4-1. What the loss means for the Raiders: The Raiders are now 3-3 on the season after starting 3-0. They trail the 6-0 Kansas City Chiefs by three games in the AFC West. Turning point of the game: There were a lot of twists and turns, but the Raiders were playing catch up most of the game. Injury report: The Raiders didn’t report any injuries. What’s next for the Raiders: The Raiders are hosting at the 2-4 Los Angeles Rams next Sunday. Kickoff is at 1:25 p.m. PT.

full_text: (Photo by Matt Kelley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders aim to avoid a three-game losing streak in Week 6 against the Buffalo Bills . To preview the game for Raider Nation, Silver and Black Pride reached out to our friends at Buffalo Rumblings, and Matt Byham was kind enough to answer a few questions about the Bills . Q: On paper, it doesn’t seem like Josh Allen has a go-to target this season since no pass-catcher enters Sunday with 20 receptions or 300 yards through five games. However, five players have double-digit catches and triple-digit receiving yards . So, is there a receiver or two who you think will make a big impact in Las Vegas? On a similar note, is there an alpha in the group that Allen will turn to if he needs a big play? A: At the start of the season, the Bills’ passing attack was humming along well with wide receiver DJ Moore and tight end Dalton Kincaid leading the charge. Moore finally brought back the WR1 skill set lacking since Stefon Diggs’ departure. Defenses were forced to account for him whenever and wherever he lined up. Moore’s addition really opened things up for Kincaid, who profiles like a huge and athletic wide receiver. Kincaid became the deep threat, and an efficient one at that. Moore suffered an AC joint sprain (separated shoulder) in Week 2, and that brought things crashing back down to Earth a bit. Moore has missed only one game (Los Angeles Rams, Week 5), playing through the pain rather than landing on in-season Injured Reserve. However, he’s understandably not been the same player since Week 1. Now teams can devote additional resources to take Kincaid away, and that’s all but eliminated the deep passing play. But all isn’t lost, with third-year wide receiver Keon Coleman taking a huge leap toward becoming a go-to target for Allen. Coleman isn’t a prototypical burner at receiver, but he’s someone who can play at any level of the passing attack. Through five games, Coleman has made 15 catches on 18 targets for 224 yards and two touchdowns. That’s a highly efficient stat line, which is made more impressive by his 11 catches for a first down. Coleman has proven to be reliable and an important part of the passing game this season. He also climbs an astonishingly high ladder, making contested catches look like routine grabs. I expect Coleman to play a featured role, regardless of Moore’s status. There’s also wide receiver Khalil Shakir, who may well fit the role of alpha. He often operates as Allen’s go-to in the early stages and in crunch time, and his chemistry with Allen acts as an irreplaceable rhythm setter. He’s a typical modern-day slot receiver, though Brady and Allen have tried to involve him downfield more. Shakir can take it to the house from the backfield if the defense doesn’t respect his speed and elusiveness in space. Then there’s running back Ty Johnson, the team’s third-down specialist. He’s an incredible receiver out of the backfield and the speediest player in the team’s running backs room. Johnson is a legit problem for defenses, and he’s likely to play a big role if Allen struggles to get things going with more traditional receiving options. Q: James Cook is a year removed from winning the NFL rushing title and is averaging 11 more rushing yards per game ( 95.4 to 106.4 ) so far in 2026. What makes him such a dynamic running back, and what’s led to the bump in efficiency this year, since he’s also averaging about a half-yard more per carry? A: James Cook is incredibly talented, and it often looks like he’s on ice skates while everyone around him is stuck in mud. Cook’s agility and center of gravity are nearly unrivaled, able to take it to the house on one cut from any distance in a way that reminds me of Terrell Davis or even Marcus Allen. Regarding the efficiency bump, you can likely point to fresh legs at the start of the season and his lethal one-cut approach. He also has a strong group of offensive linemen who thoroughly enjoy slobber-knocking defenders to clear a path for Cook. To boot, Brady is doing a better job mixing plays up on first down in 2026, where in 2025 he’d often have Cook shoulder the load. Cook could be even better with added opportunity, despite a concerning amount of fumbles. He was discussed as the best dual-threat running back in his class, yet Cook is often an afterthought in the passing game. That and a perceived (and incorrect) notion that he’s a liability blocking on 3rd & Long means Cook comes off the field more than is ideal for a featured back. Briefly returning to the fumbles, it’s one of the biggest issues facing the offense right now. Early comments by Brady suggested that Cook needs to get it under control or risk losing snaps. He walked that back a bit and said that Cook’s too good to sideline for too long (and likely benefits from supportive encouragement rather than the doghouse approach McDermott employed). Defenders are tuned in to Cook’s fumble issue, and he faces a ton of punches on every carry. How he responds to that adversity this weekend could go a long way toward defining his season. Cook seems committed to improving, but it’s going to be an issue for him until he proves it’s fixed. Q: One matchup I’ll be keeping an eye on this Sunday is the Raiders’ edge rushers (Maxx Crosby and Malcolm Koonce) against the Bills’ offensive tackles (Dion Dawkins and Spencer Brown). What would you say Dawkins’ and Brown’s strengths and weaknesses are, especially in pass protection? A: I love this question and wish I were better-equipped to discuss the finer nuances of offensive line play. Dawkins is a force of nature. He’s bigger than life and one of the key engines to the Bills’ offense and a massive ambassador for the Buffalo area. He lost roughly 45 pounds in the offseason, which has allowed him to play with quicker feet and better twitch. Dawkins isn’t perfect and will occasionally surrender pressures to highly athletic, twitchy edge rushers. He’s best as a brick wall, whether backpedaling or bull rushing, but he can be beat if a defender forces him into sloppy technique. Spencer Brown looks like a professional wrestler who’s a better right tackle. A freak of nature in so many respects, Brown is a tsunami as a run blocker, and he’s athletic enough to take almost any defensive end to task headed his way en route to Allen. His height (6’8”) can be a detriment from time to time against edge rushers who like to anchor low pivots toward the pocket. Where Brown struggles most is with injuries. He’s dealt with a back issue in multiple seasons, with a flare-up forcing him out early against the Rams. Brown will play Sunday; it’s just a matter of how well his back holds up. Q: On the other side of the trenches, and in a similar vein, two Buffalo defensive linemen who have really caught fire this season are defensive end Greg Rousseau and defensive tackle Deone Walker. How would you describe their respective skill sets, and what has led to their ascension? A: More massive human beings! Greg Rousseau (Bills Mafia calls him Groot) is a 6’7” nightmare for an offense. It’s fair to say that Rousseau was miscast in prior head coach Sean McDermott’s 4-3 system. Now playing outside linebacker for the first time in his career, Rousseau has more space to operate and cause havoc for linemen trying to engage with him. Rousseau is extremely fast for a defensive end, and his speed is magnified operating away from the trenches a bit. He’s playing a brand of football most had never seen before, combining a relentless motor with a physical profile seen only among the top 1% of his peers. Rousseau is a fun watch, and it’s possible he’s just getting started on a path to true greatness. Then there’s Deone Walker. Why did teams pass him up in the draft? Well, his size was part of the issue. At almost 6’8” and over 330 pounds, many wondered how and where Walker would fit in on the defensive line. Would he be able to hold anchor with a high center of gravity, and could he meet…

title: Miami Dolphins offensive line review: Tracking the guards in Week 5
summary: The freefall continued in Week 5, as the Miami Dolphins were defeated by the Cincinnati Bengals by (only!) a touchdown. The loss dropped the Fins to 0-5 as they continue navigating a significant roster rebuild. While wins and losses matter, much of the focus in 2026 remains on the development of Miami’s young talent. That […]
full_text: The freefall continued in Week 5, as the Miami Dolphins were defeated by the Cincinnati Bengals by (only!) a touchdown. The loss dropped the Fins to 0-5 as they continue navigating a significant roster rebuild. While wins and losses matter, much of the focus in 2026 remains on the development of Miami’s young talent. That is especially true along the offensive line, where rookie left guard Kadyn Proctor and second-year right guard Jonah Savaiinaea are important pieces of the team’s future. How are they performing this season? Each week, we take a closer look at the guards and what is being said about their most recent performance. Kadyn Proctor Game Snap Counts Penalties PFF Overall Grade PFF Run Blocking PFF Pass Protection 9/13, @ Raiders 59 (100%) 1 71.2 79.0 63.4 9/20, @ 49ers 56 (100%) 2 62.0 72.4 39.1 9/27, vs. Chiefs 73 (100%) 0 57.5 51.1 71.3 10/4, @ Vikings 39 (100%) 0 51.2 48.6 64.9 10/11, vs. Bengals 66 (100%) 0 72.7 74.9 52.2 Jonah Savaiinaea Game Snap Counts Penalties PFF Overall Grade PFF Run Blocking PFF Pass Protection 9/13, @ Raiders 59 (100%) 0 47.6 50.9 38.2 9/20, @ 49ers 56 (100%) 0 65.9 68.5 46.1 9/27, vs. Chiefs 73 (100%) 0 56.6 58.4 47.5 10/4, @ Vikings 39 (100%) 0 49.5 44.6 77.5 10/11, vs. Bengals 18 (27%) 0 45.4 44.7 78.4 What We Learned First, we should probably talk about Jonah Savaiinaea’s injury. He left the game in the first half with an ankle injury and did not return. Coach Hafley said Monday Savaiinaea was “doing OK” — given the extra week to recover, the expectation is that he will suit up next week against the Jets. Savaiinaea was replaced by Jarrett Kingston, who recorded really solid PFF grades across the board (78.3 overall, 75.0 run blocking, 76.2 pass blocking) — more on that later. Savaiinaea’s grades don’t jump off the page, but he logged only 18 snaps before his injury, and many of them came against three-time Pro Bowler Dexter Lawrence II. PFF hasn’t been especially high on his season overall, but others, including Coach Eric Smith (see the video link below), have been encouraged by his development. He looks increasingly comfortable at right guard after playing a different position last season. Meanwhile, Kadyn Proctor recorded his highest PFF grade of the season and has now posted a run-blocking grade above 70.0 in three of five games. His pass blocking grades are a work in progress, but for both players, I think it’s so far, so good. It’s interesting that Kingston performed as well as he did. I don’t know if you can be called a “journeyman” when you’re only 26 years old, but the Dolphins are his fourth team since being drafted in the sixth round in 2024 by the San Francisco 49ers. Could the Dolphins have unlocked a new offensive line starter? Should he start opposite Jonah Savaiinaea at guard and have Proctor replace the ineffective Austin Jackson at right tackle?! I’m in the “slow your roll” camp, but I wouldn’t mind finding playing time for Kingston and seeing if he can stack some wins. Finally, it’s time for a mini-rant: Offensive line is another area where the Dolphins may be outperforming expectations for an 0-5 team. According to NFL Lines.com , the Dolphins’ offensive line ranks 12th in the NFL. I’m old enough to remember last August, when ESPN regarded the Fins’ offensive line as among the worst in the league , despite being anchored by emerging stars Patrick Paul and Aaron Brewer. The Dolphins may not be loaded with talent yet, but that ranking looked questionable in August and has aged like milk. Miami’s offensive line has been one of the brighter developments of the young season. The tracker will be updated each week throughout the season. For a more in-depth breakdown of Proctor’s and Savaiinaea’s performance, check out offensive line Coach Eric Smith’s film analysis of the game, which you can find on his YouTube channel, Focused on Fins .

title: Dolphins fans losing faith in Malik Willis, team
summary: The Miami Dolphins are on their bye week, enjoying their lone off-weekend of the year after a 0-5 start. This season was expected to be a down year in South Florida, with the franchise resetting everything from the team’s president, through the general manager and front office, on to the coaching staff, and down to […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins in action at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are on their bye week, enjoying their lone off-weekend of the year after a 0-5 start. This season was expected to be a down year in South Florida, with the franchise resetting everything from the team’s president, through the general manager and front office, on to the coaching staff, and down to the roster. Miami has undergone a massive turnover. Fans have been feeling positive about the team’s direction despite the losses, but where do they stand during the bye week? And with a quarter of the season complete, how are fans feeling about quarterback Malik Willis, who signed as a free agent in the offseason? Can Miami turn around and spark a run coming out of the bye? According to FanDuel Sportsbook odds , the team is still expected to finish with 4.5 wins this season (-750 on the under). Dolphins fan confidence Fans still seem to believe in the Dolphins’ direction as we work through the bye, but there was a significant drop-off between Weeks 5 and 6. Last week, our weekly SB Nation Reacts fan confidence survey reached a season-high, with 87 percent of the fans saying they think the Dolphins are headed in the right direction. This week, that number fell to 71 percent. While the result still shows that more than 7 out of 10 fans believe Miami is on the right track in their rebuild, the drop from nearly 9 out of 10 is significant. The Dolphins did not show the kind of growth from Week 5 to Week 6 that they showed between each of the first five weeks, which is concerning. What adjustments can the coaching staff and players make for Week 7 and beyond? Will fan confidence keep falling after the bye? After the team’s Week 7 game against the New York Jets? Miami Dolphins 2026 Season Fan Confidence Results: Preseason – 80% Week 1 – 79% Week 2 – 63% Week 3 – 65% Week 4 – 79% Week 5 – 87% Week 6 – 71% Dolphins fans: Make your pick in the SB Nation app! Take Reacts surveys, create Dolphins polls, and see how your answers compare with fellow Phinsider readers. Then discuss the results with other diehard Fins fans. Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Malik Willis grade The NFL calendar now includes an 18-week regular season, with 17 games scheduled. There is no easy way to break down the season into quarter reviews, but with the Week 6 bye, it is simple to treat Miami’s first five games as the first quarter. With that in mind, we also asked you to grade Willis’s performance over the first quarter(-ish) of the season. You clearly are not happy with it. There was not a single vote for an “A” grade. A majority of the fans (50.4 percent) rated Willis’ first five games with the Dolphins as a “D”. Add another 22 percent who think Willis has failed thus far, and you get a picture of a fanbase that is not happy with the quarterback. Head coach Jeff Hafley has said he is not considering a change at quarterback, but Willis’ play has to turn around quickly if the fans are going to think he is anything more than a one-year rental for the rebuild. Do you agree with the Dolphins’ fan confidence poll results? How about the D grade for Willis? Let us know in the comments.

title: 2026 NFL Week 7: Indianapolis Colts at Minnesota Vikings
summary: The bye week is over for the Minnesota Vikings, and they’ll be making their return to the field in Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season as they host the Indianapolis Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium. The Vikings are still one of just three undefeated teams in the National Football League as Week 7 opens […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 03: Jordan Addison #3 of the Minnesota Vikings dives to catch a touchdown pass against the Indianapolis Colts in the third quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 03, 2024 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The Vikings defeated the Colts 21-13. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The bye week is over for the Minnesota Vikings, and they’ll be making their return to the field in Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season as they host the Indianapolis Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium. The Vikings are still one of just three undefeated teams in the National Football League as Week 7 opens up, along with the Kansas City Chiefs and the San Francisco 49ers (Monday Night Football results pending). The Vikings have been getting the job done primarily on defense and special teams, as Brian Flores’ group is currently allowing the fewest points/game in the National Football League and Matt Daniels’ special teams units have been the league’s best so far this season. The offense has certainly had its issues, particularly in the passing game, but has managed to do enough to keep the team from losing thus far. The Vikings could see the return of several important pieces in this one, including left tackle Christian Darrisaw, wide receiver Jordan Addison, tight end T.J. Hockenson, and running back Jordan Mason. Mason has been on injured reserve since suffering a thumb injury in the season opener but is eligible to return starting this week. Addison and Darrisaw both missed the Week 5 game against New Orleans with injuries, and Hockenson left the Saints game after the second offensive play with a concussion. We’ll be monitoring all of their statuses throughout the week. The Colts are reeling a bit coming into this one, having lost two straight, including a 26-20 loss at home in Week 6 to the previously winless Tennessee Titans. The Colts turned the ball over three times in the loss, including a pair of interceptions by Daniel Jones, and had a punt blocked and returned for a touchdown. The Indianapolis defense allowed the Titans to put up just 186 total yards of offense and led the game at halftime by a score of 13-0, but wound up stumbling badly in the second half against their AFC South rivals. This is the Colts’ third trip in five years to U.S. Bank Stadium, and their last two trips have not gone well for them. In 2024, the Colts came to town for Sunday Night Football and took a 7-0 lead into halftime after they turned a sack/fumble of Sam Darnold into a touchdown. The Vikings took over in the second half, however, scoring two third-quarter touchdowns to take a 14-7 lead, and Darnold iced it with his third touchdown pass of the night just before the two-minute warning to secure a 21-13 victory for Minnesota. And, of course, there was the 2022 Saturday afternoon game at U.S. Bank Stadium, when the Colts shocked the Vikings by taking a 33-0 lead into halftime. . .only to see the Vikings pull off a bigger shocker by going on a 36-3 run in the second half to force overtime and ultimately win the game on Greg Joseph’s 40-yard field goal at the overtime gun to win 39-36 and secure the biggest comeback in NFL history. Kickoff for this one is set for noon Central Time this Sunday afternoon, and the broadcast will be provided by the CBS family of networks, including WCCO-4 in the Twin Cities. We’ll be putting all of our stories about this week’s game in this stream for you, so keep your eyes right here for the latest. Vikings vs. Colts odds: Opening lines for Week 7 matchup

title: ‘Ridiculous’ turnover rate an embarrassment for Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel
summary: The New England Patriots have won three straight games and at 4-2 overall on the season are once again in a competitive position in the AFC. And yet, their head coach is well aware that there is work to be done in order to sustain the success and again compete for a championship. High up […]
full_text: The New England Patriots have won three straight games and at 4-2 overall on the season are once again in a competitive position in the AFC. And yet, their head coach is well aware that there is work to be done in order to sustain the success and again compete for a championship. High up on the list is turnovers, and Mike Vrabel made this clear on Monday morning. “We turn the ball over at a historic rate, and it’s ridiculous,” Vrabel said on an appearance on WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show . “It’s embarrassing.” The Patriots added two more turnovers to their tally on Sunday against the New York Jets. In the third quarter, running back TreVeyon Henderson lost a fumble on his team’s side of the field; in the fourth, wide receiver DeMario Douglas had the ball punched while trying to gain extra yards on a 39-yard catch-and-run. Both plays not only thwarted potential scoring opportunities for New England, but set up the Jets to add points themselves: they turned both takeaways into field goals, scoring six of their 19 total points after the Patriots gifted them the ball. On the season, Vrabel’s team has now turned the ball over 13 times — second most in the league behind only the Chargers’ 15. Drake Maye has thrown seven interceptions, albeit none of them over the last two games, while the team also lost six of its 11 total fumbles. The Patriots’ turnover rate of 21.2% per drive is the worst in the league, and if maintained throughout the rest of the season would be the highest of any single NFL team since the 2006 Oakland Raiders (25.0%). “It’s tough to win, and there are also things that we have to clean up,” Vrabel said. “We just want to keep improving. We did in some areas, and unfortunately I think we have to continue to understand that each and every week in this league you have to play well to give yourself a chance to win. And if you don’t, it’s hard to win.”
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Patriots’ depth steps up after O-line injuries against Jets
summary: The injuries along the New England Patriots’ offensive line piled up in Sunday’s 26-16 win over the New York Jets. After offensive tackle Morgan Moses suffered an ankle injury in the first quarter, New England went on to lose both starting guards, Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and Ben Brown (knee). Despite having three backups play significant […]
full_text: The injuries along the New England Patriots’ offensive line piled up in Sunday’s 26-16 win over the New York Jets. After offensive tackle Morgan Moses suffered an ankle injury in the first quarter, New England went on to lose both starting guards, Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and Ben Brown (knee). Despite having three backups play significant snaps, quarterback Drake Maye was hit just four times and was not sacked in the victory. “Those guys are doing a heck of a job in there,” Maye said post game. “Coach Doug and Coach Haas, I think they have, they’re coaching them hard. They’re expecting a lot in practice, and those guys are playing through injuries. We got three go down today, so these guys are fighting hard. They’re fighting their butts off, and it goes through them.” With the game still within one score in the fourth quarter, New England leaned on its makeshift offensive line to help close out the win. Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels dialed up nine consecutive run plays on a drive that consumed more than six minutes and extended the Patriots’ lead to 10 points. “That last drive running the football, you all got the best seat in the house. It was beautiful to see,” Maye said. “I think the more we can do that, the more we can just gel together as offense and lean on that.” With Moses sidelined, rookie Caleb Lomu played 60 snaps in relief. The first-round pick did not allow a single pressure. At guard, the Patriots called upon Matt Pryor (46 snaps) and Walter Rouse (14), neither of whom spent training camp with the team. “I think that’s just those guys were ready for their opportunity, and it was great to see,” head coach Mike Vrabel said. “I just, you never know what’s going to happen in this league, and we talk about it all the time, preparing for the journey. When guys get their chance, they go in there and perform. I hate that we don’t have the guys. I hate when guys get injured, but I also understand that on the other side of that, there’s an opportunity.” The Patriots now face a quick turnaround, traveling to Chicago for a Thursday night matchup against the Bears. Vrabel noted the challenge of getting players who did not finish Sunday’s game ready to return on a short week. Moses was seen wearing a walking boot on his right foot in the postgame locker room, while Brown left with a noticeable limp. That will likely lead to another opportunity for New England’s depth lineman. “You never want to see [injuries]. It’s terrible to see. It does happen, unfortunately, in this league,” Lomu said. “Everyone’s got to prepare like a starter for those types of things that happen. We had a lot of guys that stepped up today, which is really good.”
author: Brian Hines
