title: 10 things we learned from Patriots vs. Jets
summary: The New England Patriots hung on against the New York Jets in Foxboro on Sunday. It was a divisional game, so a win is a win, but you would have liked to have seen them play better throughout the contest on both sides of the ball. Still, they are now 4-2 and very much in […]
full_text: The New England Patriots hung on against the New York Jets in Foxboro on Sunday. It was a divisional game, so a win is a win, but you would have liked to have seen them play better throughout the contest on both sides of the ball. Still, they are now 4-2 and very much in striking distance in the AFC East. Let’s get into what we lessons learned from the 26-19 game on Sunday . A.J. Brown hast to knock off the rust The Patriots finally got A.J. Brown back from his four-week stint on injured reserve, and he was not good. Despite being targeted 10 times, he only came down with three catches for 27 yards. It was his drops that were really concerning. There was the deep ball where he pulled his arms in too soon; there was the slant that hit him right in the arms that he dropped; there was the touchdown that Drake Maye placed perfectly on his back shoulder but still went through his hands. To cap things off, he also dropped the onside kick attempt at the end of the game, but luckily Eli Raridon jumped on the ball. Yes, it was his first game back and first game in front of the Patriots home crowd, and he probably was excited to be out there and still has to build a rapport with Maye, but his performance on Sunday was unacceptable. Hopefully, he just has to knock the rust off and will be fine moving forward. The team thinks so , at least. Everyone is hurt The Patriots lost Romeo Doubs, Morgan Moses, Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown for the game. They also saw Dre’Mont Jones go down for a bit, even though he did come back onto the field shortly after. New England had a lot of injury luck last year, which allowed them to make a deep playoff run because their depth wasn’t seriously challenged. However, it’s the complete opposite this year. The fact that New England was able to still move the ball was pretty impressive, but there are still major questions coming out of the game. We will see how much time the injured guys miss, but it’s hard to imagine that all five of them will be ready for Thursday night with such a quick turnaround. The offensive line impresses Given all the injuries along the offensive line, and the talent on the other side, Drake Maye getting sacked all day was pretty impressive. And not just that: at the end of the game, with the Patriots up seven points, they were able to run the ball down the Jets’ throats to kill the majority of the clock. I don’t know how long they can keep this up, but the fact that they were able to do it at all speaks for itself. Caleb Lomu played fantastic I already mentioned the offensive line, but I needed to shine the spotlight on the Patriots’ first-round draft pick. Caleb Lomu played extremely well when he went in to replace the injured Morgan Moses at right tackle, and handled NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year candidate David Bailey. The plan all along was to have him take over at right tackle at some point, and it looks like he could do just that sooner rather than later. Of course, going into this week, we thought we would see him at left tackle with Will Campbell leaving with an injury last week, but Campbell played, and it’s a good thing he did because the Patriots literally ran out of offensive linemen (no seriously, they did: all eight on the game day roster saw extended action). For Lomu this is the second week in a row that he has come on in relief duty for an injured tackle, and he’s looked good in both games. He’s going to have some growing pains at some point — every rookie does — but if the Patriots hit on him, that would be a big boost for their offensive line not only this season, but also into the future. Drake Maye wasn’t perfect, but solid Drake Maye had a few bad throws, but his decision-making continued to be good, and he was patient with the football on Sunday. He did spend a little too much time staring at A.J. Brown for my liking, but overall played a solid game. He now has 13 touchdowns and only one interception in the last three games, and he’s back to his MVP form from last year. If he keeps playing like this, the Patriots are going to be in very good shape going forward. Of course, he and fellow 2024 first-round draft pick Caleb Williams are going to be duking it out on Thursday night, which should be a fun head-to-head. Robert Spillane is critically underrated The Patriots have a lot of great players who are getting attention on the defense, including Christian Gonzalez (effectively erasing Garrett Wilson), Milton Williams (first sack of the season) and Elijah Ponder (now up to 5.5 sacks in six games). They deserve the recognition they are getting, but so does one guy who isn’t regularly mentioned among the star players on this side of the ball: Robert Spillane. The counting stats might not be there for him — he had five tackles and a quarterback hit on Sunday — but he consistently has everyone in the right spot, and is almost never out of position himself. He did get caught mugged-up a few times that ended in pretty big runs for the Jets, but he was very solid all game and goes almost completely unheralded. He was the one who picked the left tackle that got Ponder his sack on Sunday, and he had a massive stop on fourth down when he squared Braelon Allen up in the hole. The Patriots are lucky to have a guy that can do as much as Spillane does, and his presence in the clubhouse is a huge benefit as well. Corey Kiner gives the Patriots some very good production With TreVeyon Henderson struggling, and with the Patriots wanting to give Rhamondre Stevenson a bit of a rest, they turned to Corey Kiner late in the game. The August trade acquisition responded with eight straight carries for 42 yards on what was effectively the game-sealing drive for New England. It was an impressive series, especially considering that the team was down three starting offensive linemen, and when you factor in that the Jets knew they were going to try to run the ball. If the Patriots can get solid play from Kiner, it will give them another back to eat some carries, and one who has some juice as well. Kyle Williams should get more opportunities Kyle Williams only finished the game with one catch for 12 yards, but he was open a few other times where he didn’t get targeted. I think that the Patriots need to give him some more opportunities, especially on some deep routes. If they continue to target him down the field, it could open up the rest of the field for other players, and they could also hit some of those shots as well. That is especially true if Romeo Doubs is going to be out this week, which seems very possible. The Patriots could get a big boost on a short week from Williams on a few big plays. Special teamers are contributing Often overlooked, the Patriots are getting really good contributions from the kicking game, and it’s been firing up the whole team: Cameron Latu, Erick Hunter, and Brenden Schooler all had solid plays that got the sideline going. They have to feel good about the contributions they are getting out of them and others in the game’s third phase, with Hunter playing gunner on the punt team across from Schooler, and Latu consistently around the football on the kickoff team. The best signs of a good football team is how it plays on special teams, and right now the Patriots are playing very well. Short week in Chicago next week The Patriots have a short week this week, and play in Chicago on Thursday night. It’s going to be the second matchup, both in Chicago, between Drake Maye and Caleb Williams in their young careers. You’d have to imagine that Williams will be significantly better in this one than he was in the last one in 2024, though, but I suppose that remains to be seen. The Bears offense has been great with him at the helm, and he came back from injury this week to lead them to 31-23 win in Atlanta. On the plus side, their defense is not good at all, and the Patriots should be able to score, even with a bunch of players injured. It should be an interesting matchup on the whole,…
author: Pat Lane

title: 6 winners and losers from Patriots win over Jets
summary: The New England Patriots stayed in the win column on Sunday with a divisional win over the New York Jets. While head coach Mike Vrabel said his team tried to beat itself, the Patriots celebrated a 26-16 victory to improve to 4-2 on the season. Here is who caught our eye for better or worse […]
full_text: The New England Patriots stayed in the win column on Sunday with a divisional win over the New York Jets. While head coach Mike Vrabel said his team tried to beat itself , the Patriots celebrated a 26-16 victory to improve to 4-2 on the season. Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Week 6 contest from the Gillette Stadium press box. Winners QB Drake Maye: The Jets entered Sunday as one of the most aggressive defenses in football, but they smartly pivoted from that game plan blitzing Maye just nine times. Maye showed patience in clean pockets throughout the game that led to numerous big plays, such as the 42-yard touchdown to Romeo Doubs and a 9-yard touchdown to DeMario Douglas. It was an overall another efficient day in the office for Maye, who added +0.39 EPA per drop back. TE Hunter Henry: The veteran tight end was a steady presence for the Patriots’ offense on Sunday recording four catches for 48 yards and a touchdown. Henry’s score came on a busted coverage on third-down while his three other receptions all moved the chains — including a 3rd-and-13 on the Patriots final offensive drive in which he made a defender miss. After a slower start to the year, Henry has been his usual self in recent weeks. Offensive line: New England lost three starters along the offensive line Sunday but still did not allow a sack of Maye. Rookie Caleb Lomu continued to play well and did not allow a pressure in relief of Morgan Moses, while Will Campbell held up on the opposite end allowing just one pressure. Along the interior, New England was forced to use four different guards as Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse were called upon for the injured Ben Brown and Alijah Vera-Tucker. They were solid in relief, while Jared Wilson continued to be steady in pass protection (one pressure) with all the movement around him. CBs Christian Gonzalez and Charles Woods: In his return, Christian Gonzalez played every defensive snap and matched up with star wide receiver Garrett Wilson for most of the day. On 17 matchups (12 in man coverage) Gonzales allowed just two catches for 20 yards on two targets. Charles Woods then earned a game ball for hauling in a late interception — the first Geno Smith had thrown all season. Losers WR A.J. Brown: There was plenty of rust for wide receiver A.J. Brown in his return from injured reserve. Brown was targeted a game-high 10 times but managed to bring in just three for 27 yards. Maye had two misfires in Brown’s direction while the receiver dropped two passes — including a deep go-ball down the right sideline — and failed to corral the final onside kick. “I didn’t play well. I don’t know – if the timing was off. I’m much better than what I put on display today, there’s no excuses. I’ll be better,” Brown said post game. In a positive department, Brown was creating separation throughout the game and played 52 snaps as his ankle felt healthy. Honorable mentions The Patriots turned the ball over twice on Sunday with TreVeyon Henderson and DeMario Douglas fumbling. Douglas had a strong game elsewhere. Kyle Williams ran a nice route on a third-down that Drake Maye converted with plenty of anticipation. Efton Chism III then played 42 snaps with most of his contributions coming in the run game as a blocker. Romeo Doubs made an impressive 42-yard touchdown which he hurt his shoulder on. Vrabel noted postgame that looking back at it, the touchdown was “one of the huge plays of this football game.” Corey Kiner led the team in rushing as he ran hard late in the fourth quarter with eight straight carries. Elijah Ponder continued his strong start to the season with another sack working a stunt with Robert Spillane. He added three other pressures. Milton Williams and Christian Barmore recorded back-to-back sacks along the interior. DaQuon Jones was also notable early as a run defender and drew a pressure with Gabe Jacas on Woods’ interception. The Patriots kickoff return and coverage units had strong days, with Kiner also recording a 37-yard return. Punter Mitch Wishnowsky recovered from a poor snap to place a 54-yard punt at the three yards line. Andy Borregales missed an extra point, but made both short field goal attempts.
author: Brian Hines

title: Patriots ‘lucky’ to beat Jets, says Mike Vrabel
summary: The New England Patriots extended their win streak to three straight victories on Sunday against the New York Jets, but that doesn’t mean they are fully satisfied either. In fact, for head coach Mike Vrabel, a win was not a foregone conclusion given his team’s performance. He event went so far as to use the […]
full_text: The New England Patriots extended their win streak to three straight victories on Sunday against the New York Jets, but that doesn’t mean they are fully satisfied either. In fact, for head coach Mike Vrabel, a win was not a foregone conclusion given his team’s performance. He event went so far as to use the L-word to describe the game: lucky. “We’re lucky to win, is probably where I’d start,” Vrabel said during his postgame presser. “But we’re happy that we won. We’ll enjoy it for about an hour, and then we’re going to focus on the next task.” What exactly did he mean when talking about being lucky, though? “Fortunate, whatever — we just didn’t play very well,” Vrabel added. “We tried to beat ourselves, but we made enough plays in critical situations to help us get through here today.” The Patriots entered Week 6 coming off their two best games of the season. They defeated a well-rounded Bills team on the road 29-26 to emphatically leave their 1-2 start behind them, and the following week thoroughly dismantled a Raiders team that had won three of its first four games. The arrow was pointing up for New England heading into the Jets game, but in Vrabel’s eyes it didn’t do the same during the eventual 26-19 victory on Sunday afternoon . “You have to be able to continue to improve, and I don’t feel like we did,” he said. “We won, which is the most important thing. We just — I don’t think we improved from what we had shown the previous two weeks, and I have to figure out why. That’s my job. My job’s to get us to win and also to get us to improve.” “There are definitely things we’ve got to clean up for sure,” said cornerback Christian Gonzalez when asked about his head coach’s remarks. “We’ve got to clean up two-minute drives. We’ve got to clean that up. And in the backend, we’ve got to do what we do as a defense. We’ve got to not let them drive down the field, get down there and get points. The offense did an amazing job getting down the field, taking time off. The defense, we didn’t do our part. But we got out with a win and that’s what matters.”
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Patriots express confidence in A.J. Brown after quiet return to lineup
summary: A.J. Brown’s return to action gave the New England Patriots their primary weapon in the passing game for the first time in five weeks; however, Brown played a relatively minor role in Sunday’s win. New England’s gritty 26-19 divisional victory over the New York Jets marked Brown’s first game in a Patriots uniform since suffering […]
full_text: A.J. Brown’s return to action gave the New England Patriots their primary weapon in the passing game for the first time in five weeks; however, Brown played a relatively minor role in Sunday’s win. New England’s gritty 26-19 divisional victory over the New York Jets marked Brown’s first game in a Patriots uniform since suffering a high ankle sprain in the season opener against the Seattle Seahawks that placed him on the team’s injured reserve. It was clear on Sunday that, after the missed time, Brown’s chemistry with his quarterback, Drake Maye, is still a work in progress. The receiver fielded 10 targets on the afternoon, catching just three of those passes for 27 yards and dropping at least two. “I thought [Brown] could have probably made a few more plays,” head coach Mike Vrabel said. “He’s been out for a while. I know that he wanted to do well for his football team, and, unfortunately, it wasn’t his best effort. I know that he knows that, and we have all the confidence in the world in A.J. [to] be able to finish those plays… “A.J. has high expectations for himself, and we have high expectations for him as well. [I’m] confident that he’ll come back, do a lot of things and help us here the rest of the season.” Early in the second quarter, Maye sent a deep pass down the right sideline intended for Brown. The 29-year-old, with a step ahead of the opposing Jets defensive back, reached out to secure the catch, but the ball sailed between his hands as Brown struggled to track it over his shoulder. And with green turf ahead, New England’s headlining trade acquisition over the offseason likely would have scored on a 61-yard touchdown. New York also had a chance to reclaim possession in the final 32 seconds and attempt to tie the game by recovering an onside kick. The Patriots’ coaching staff sent Brown onto the field to help field the kick; however, he dropped it before Corey Kiner and Eli Raridon recovered the loose ball. “No excuses,” Brown said. “I expect myself to make each and every one of those plays. The drop, the other drop on third down, on the slant — I am more than capable of making those catches. I’ll be better, that’s all.” Though Maye also had difficulty finding a rhythm with Brown. Later in the second frame, leading 7-3, the New England offense lined up on a third-and-four play at the Jets’ 14-yard line with an opportunity to take a two-score lead by scoring a touchdown. After the snap, Maye quickly looked Brown’s way on a quick slant but missed the open receiver, who could have secured the first down. The Patriots then settled for a field goal, which they converted. “It was great to see [Brown] back out there,” Maye said. “I’m looking forward to him growing and just building that connection. I think there’s some [on] me and some plays he wishes he had back, but I was just telling him in the locker room that you don’t have to worry about [No. 1]. He’s going to be one of the best players on the field every time he steps on it … “I told him I’m going to keep coming his way … He was open tonight. I thought he looked good. [I’m] just glad to have him back, and I’m looking forward to seeing him down the road. It’ll be fun.” Brown remained a clear priority in offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels’ game plan despite missing time, as McDaniels designed plenty of plays to get him involved and Maye frequently looked his way as the first read. On the offense’s only third-down attempt of the opening drive, Maye targeted Brown on another quick slant, but New York linebacker Demario Davis batted the pass down at the line of scrimmage. “No, I think [Brown] has to make the catches when we throw to him,” Vrabel said about whether the receiver’s return is affecting the flow of the offense. “I think there’ll be times where you want to try to put your best players at the point of attack, and if [the play] is not there, the quarterback has to know, ‘Hey, [the defense] did something that took that away.’” Nonetheless, Brown’s presence on the field influenced the Jets’ defensive decision-making. On the play where Romeo Doubs hauled in his 42-yard touchdown catch from Maye running a deep post, New York safety Minkah Fitzpatrick closed down on Brown’s dig route underneath, leaving Doubs with an opportunity to peel open in the end zone. “[Brown] has been in the league for a long time. He knows how to deal with things,” cornerback Christian Gonzalez said. “He’s been out for four weeks. It’s different when you get out there and [you’re] catching the ball when everybody’s flying around. Everybody on this team, in this locker room and in this building has the utmost confidence in him. Those couple of drops don’t really mean anything. He’s going to get back to himself and do what he does.”
author: Andrew Guindon

title: 6 moments that defined the Patriots’ win over the Jets
summary: The New England Patriots did not play their best football on Sunday against the New York Jets, but they made enough plays to still win with a final score of 26-19. Those plays came in all shapes and sizes, and all three phases of the game. And so, here is our Patriots-centric view at some […]
full_text: The New England Patriots did not play their best football on Sunday against the New York Jets, but they made enough plays to still win with a final score of 26-19 . Those plays came in all shapes and sizes, and all three phases of the game. And so, here is our Patriots-centric view at some of those key moments from the Week 6 contest. Moment No. 1: Complementary football The Patriots started the game slowly on both offense and defense, quickly falling behind 3-0. However, the second drives on both sides of the ball were a lot more successful — and allowed the team to take the lead in complementary fashion. Back-to-back sacks from Milt & Bmore. 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/Osl2sQNRb3 — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 18, 2026 First up was the defense, which gave up a short run before back-to-back sacks by Milton Williams and Christian Barmore. The standout defensive tackles forced the Jets to punt from deep in their own territory, which allowed Marcus Jones to give the offense some good field position: his 10-yard return — plus a 5-yard penalty — set the unit up at the Jets’ 42-yard line. It took Drake Maye two plays to make it count. Drake hits Rome for the score 🎯 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/MCfJL3mIY0 — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 18, 2026 The 42-yard touchdown pass to Romeo Doubs, who suffered a shoulder injury on the play that eventually knocked him out of the game, saw the impact of A.J. Brown. The wide receiver, who made his return after four games on injured reserve, helped pull a safety down to free up Doubs over the top. Moment No. 2: Fourth-down excellence The second quarter turned into one of fourth downs. In what ended as a one-score game, those turned into critical plays and stolen possessions even early on. The Patriots got the better of the Jets in that regard, including on a big Robert Spillane tackle to prevent a conversion on 4th-and-1 early in the period. Spill with a huge stop on 4th down 😤 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/ZvLY45dKIn — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 18, 2026 The Patriots defense later produced another fourth-down stop at its own 39-yard line, whereas the offense managed to move the chains on the subsequent possession. That drive, which saw Rhamondre Stevenson convert a 4th-and-1, ended with a field goal to put New England up 10-3. Moment No. 3: Closing in style Facing a 3rd-and goal from the 9-yard line with just 20 seconds to go in the first half, the Patriots had a chance to solidify their lead going into the locker room and set the tone for the second part of the game. The latter did not quite happen, but New England nonetheless managed to put up the necessary points on a Drake Maye throw to DeMario Douglas. TOUCHDOWN POP‼️ @DrakeMaye2 | @popshotta3 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/44jjc5GRBW — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 18, 2026 Up 17-3 at the half, New England appeared to be in full control. However, the home team let control of the contest slip away in the third period due to some sloppy football on both offense and defense. Moment No. 4: Defensive stand The Patriots defense was in full “bend don’t break” mode on Sunday, as evidenced by the fact that the Jets went 0-for-3 in the red zone. In the third quarter, they found themselves in one of those opportunities and were just 10 yards away from tying the game. However, New England’s most productive pass rusher had different plans: Elijah Ponder took down Geno Smith on a 3rd-and-5 for a huge sack and stop. Elijah Ponder keeps doing his thing 😤 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/HZIisZ7sue — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 18, 2026 Moment No. 5: Much-needed TD The Patriots scored a touchdown (but not the ensuing extra point) early in the fourth quarter to increase their lead from 17-13 to 23-13. Drake Maye finding a wide open Hunter Henry for a 7-yard touchdown capped the series on 3rd-and-3. 10 & 85 connection 🙌 @DrakeMaye2 | @Hunter_Henry84 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/nzPrWWrzyS — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 18, 2026 While that play naturally was a big one, it arguably wasn’t the biggest. That title very well could go to Maye finding Kyle Williams for a 12-yard pickup on 3rd-and-10. If the pair had not managed to keep the series going, the Jets might have had a chance to take a lead into the fourth quarter. That did not happen, with New England instead using the momentum to drive to a touchdown of its own. Moment No. 6: Statement drive The Patriots’ final drive of the day was a tour de force. Taking over possession with 7:20 after the Jets made it a 23-16 ball game, the unit marched 56 yards in 13 plays to kick another field goal and extend the lead to 10 points again. Most importantly, New England burned 6:08 off the clock while doing so, leaving New York only 1:12 to play with. The heavy lifting on that possession was done by third-string running back Corey Kiner, who touched the ball on eight straight plays to move the Patriots from the Jets’ 48-yard line to their 6. The late-August trade acquisition did get a big assist from tight end Hunter Henry, though, who had a massive 15-yard pickup to keep the drive going on a 3rd-and-13 with 6:30 to go. That play opened the floodgates on that particular drive — one that saw Kiner and the ground game take over despite New England being down three starting offensive linemen. A statement drive.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Instant analysis from Patriots’ win over Jets
summary: A total of 45 points separated Mike Vrabel’s sideline from Aaron Glenn’s during the 2025 AFC East sweep. Enough of a gap remained Sunday at Gillette Stadium, where the New England Patriots held on to defeat the New York Jets by a score of 26-19. Here’s a glance back on the 1 p.m. ET kickoff […]
full_text: A total of 45 points separated Mike Vrabel’s sideline from Aaron Glenn’s during the 2025 AFC East sweep. Enough of a gap remained Sunday at Gillette Stadium, where the New England Patriots held on to defeat the New York Jets by a score of 26-19. Here’s a glance back on the 1 p.m. ET kickoff as the head coaches move forward with 4-2 and 2-4 teams. Maye’s October rolls on After accounting for one touchdown and seven turnovers in September, the calendar has done more than flip. Drake Maye completed 18-of-32 passes for 235 yards on Sunday. The Patriots quarterback found three touchdowns and no interceptions against a much-improved Jets defense that had finished 2025 without a pick. He added 24 rushing yards over the course of the afternoon, led by a sprint of 21. Taking the field in “13” personnel, the opening drive brought a batted pass at the line of scrimmage and a three-and-out. Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels’ group needed two plays to find paydirt on the second series, however, thanks to a clean pocket and a diving 42-yard touchdown to wide receiver Romeo Doubs. In only 12 seconds of game clock. Maye did not complete his second pass of the outing until the 6:57 mark in the second quarter, but he went 5-of-7 through the air and endured roughing the passer on the final drive going into halftime. And with a trio of timeouts on hand as well as slot receiver DeMario Douglas, a 17-3 game it became. The recent AFC Offensive Player of the Week had gone 9-of-17 for 130 yards, two touchdowns and a passer rating of 117.3 at the break. Things got out of intermission with a turnover on downs and a pair of turnovers by ground for the Patriots. But a 12-play, 63-yard surge ended in the end zone with tenured tight end Hunter Henry’s second touchdown in as many weeks. New England finished 8-of-15 on third down, 1-of-2 on fourth down and 2-of-4 in the red zone. Maye’s October now spans 10 touchdowns. Brown battles drops as wideout room brings in two touchdowns A.J. Brown had been a limited participant for three consecutive practices after having his 21-day window open. And while No. 1 was questionable to return to face the Jets, the light was left on. His official activation to the 53-man roster followed on the eve of the 1 p.m. ET kickoff. The June arrival in Foxborough was the lone wide receiver in the starting lineup on Sunday. After Brown’s first catch was overturned via challenge, it took until his fourth target to get on the board. He finished with 27 receiving yards on a team-high 10 looks in his return from the high ankle sprain that sent him to injured reserve following the season opener. Three drops, including on fourth-and-5, were in the cards along with a bobbled onside kick on the hands team. A New England wideout depth chart of four had amassed three touchdowns in the final game without its Pro Bowler. A week later, a depth chart of five brought in two scores. The aforementioned Doubs was downgraded to out due to a shoulder injury that surfaces during his latest visit to the end zone. The aforementioned Douglas tied him for the team lead with his third touchdown catch of the fall and finished Sunday with seven receptions for 86 yards. And also with a lost fumble on a 40-yard gain in the fourth quarter. Kiner paces Patriots’ backfield committee A high ankle sprain did not keep TreVeyon Henderson away from practice. The No. 38 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft entered the weekend as questionable . He proceeded to outlast the inactives list , one loud hit from linebacker DeMario Davis and one forced fumble courtesy of defensive end David Bailey to handle 40 scrimmage yards across eight touches. Yet it was a backfield of three for the Patriots. Starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson rushed for 36 yards across 14 carries, including a not-down-yet long of 12. Meanwhile, Corey Kiner broke off a kickoff return of 38 yards and provided more than breather on offense with 11 handoffs for a Patriots-best 57 ground yards. The summer trade acquisition was leaned on late after losing a fumble a Sunday ago. Left tackle returns as trio of starters depart from offensive line The knee injury that took Will Campbell out in the midst of a 45-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders did not take him out one Sunday later. The No. 4 overall pick in last year’s class stayed in for every snap at left tackle despite being a questionable call. Three others were unable to do the same for the Patriots’ starting five. Attrition reached a critical mass. Left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker was ruled out due to a hamstring injury sustained in the second quarter. An ankle injury sustained by in right tackle Morgan Moses preceded it. The 35-year-old captain also did not return . And in the final quarter, right guard Ben Brown needed assistance getting off the field due to a knee injury after he had flipped to the other side of the line. In turn, rookie first-rounder Caleb Lomu went from reporting as an eligible tight end to playing bookend while recent 53-man additions Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse stepped on at the guard spots abutting center Jared Wilson. Extra time was fought for by a patchwork offensive line that conceded zero sacks and zero penalties. Smith’s pick-less streak snaps against secondary welcoming back No. 0 A shoulder injury kept Christian Gonzalez sidelined for six practices and two games . But not Sunday. The All-Pro cornerback went without a game designation as part of the starting nickel secondary and helped limit former NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year Garrett Wilson to 44 receiving yards. Jets quarterback Geno Smith completed 20-of-30 passes for 252 yards during the return of No. 0. It marked the veteran’s seventh career start against the Patriots dating back to his rookie introduction in 2013. And it brought one touchdown as well as his initial interception of the campaign. New York’s opening drive stalled on the doorstep of the red zone after 13 plays, 58 yards and a penalty for offensive pass interference that turned a touchdown into a field goal. The next four possessions resulted in a pair of punts and back-to-back turnovers on downs. By the time halftime hit, the visiting offense had gone 1-of-6 on third down, 0-of-2 on fourth down and 0-of-1 in the red zone while hoarding 19:10 of game clock. But a moon ball behind New England starting safeties Craig Woodson and Kevin Byard III found the hands of rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. for a 48-yard touchdown to make it a 17-10 game in the third quarter. It went from 17-13 game to a 23-13 game to a 23-16 game to a 26-19 game soon after. Along the way, Charles Woods, who started for a corner depth chart still missing Carlton Davis III because of a neck injury, broke the seal with a pick along the sideline. It went in the books as the first career pick for the 2024 undrafted free agent and 2025 waiver claim. It snapped a streak of 165 passes without a pick by New York’s QB, too. Ponder extends tally to 5.5 sacks in six games Three sacks were in the cards for New England. Milton Williams got his first of the fall to set up a third-and-16 in the first quarter. Christian Barmore followed it up on the ensuing snap to put the uprights as New York’s back and the punt unit on. The defensive tackles had company after halftime on Sunday. Elijah Ponder took down the Jets’ QB on third-and-5 to force a field goal and extend his Patriots high to 5.5 sacks on the year. He had four in all as a rookie. The 2025 UDFA out of Cal Poly started off the edge opposite Dre’Mont Jones and now has at least a half sack in five straight games. The outside linebackers were joined in starting front by the the club’s leading tacklers off the ball. Christian Elliss and captain Robert Spillane, who stood up a fourth-and-1 carry from 6-foot-1, 235-pound rusher Braelon Allen, combined for 11 more tackles on Sunday. And another fourth-and-1 halting. The Jets’ running backs managed 94 rushing yards across 24 attempts in the absence of all-purpose…

full_text: Update 10/18/2026: Morgan Moses spotted in walking boot after suffering ankle injury vs. Jets Morgan Moses was unable to finish Sunday’s game against the Jets after suffering an ankle injury in the second quarter. He did briefly return to the sideline in the second half but ultimately disappeared into the Gillette stadium bowels again. The team captain was spotted in the locker room after the contest, though. He was wearing a walking boot on his right foot. Update 10/18/2026: Morgan Moses ruled out of Jets game in second half After initially announcing him as questionable with an ankle injury, the Patriots ruled Morgan Moses out of their game against the Jets at the start of the fourth quarter. Rookie Caleb Lomu will finish the game at right tackle. Original story 10/18/2026: Morgan Moses exits Jets game with ankle injury in first half New England Patriots offensive tackle Morgan Moses is officially questionable to return to Sunday’s game due to an ankle injury. The offensive tackle suffered the injury to his right ankle in the second quarter on an incompletion downfield. Moses stayed down on the turf and needed attention from the training staff before going to the blue medical tent. After a lengthy stay in the medical tent he departed to the locker room. With the 35-year old sidelined, first-round pick Caleb Lomu was inserted at right tackle. Lomu played 47 snaps last week at left tackle in relief of Will Campbell, but has spent the majority of his Patriots tenure working on the right side. The Patriots game day roster features no other primary offensive tackles. Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse, who both have previous tackle experience, are active along the offensive line.

title: 6 winners and 4 losers in from NY Giants’ 34-27 loss to New Orleans Saints
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants mounted a furious fourth-quarter comeback, but lost to the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, 34-27. That was a disappointing result against a team that entered the game 1-4. Let’s get to the ‘Kudos and Wet Willies’. Kudos to … J.J. McCarthy —McCarthy mighyt have won himself the […]
full_text: J.J McCarthy nearly led the Giants to an incredible come-from-behind victory on Sunday. | Getty Images EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants mounted a furious fourth-quarter comeback, but lost to the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, 34-27. That was a disappointing result against a team that entered the game 1-4. Let’s get to the ‘Kudos and Wet Willies’. Kudos to … J.J. McCarthy —McCarthy mighyt have won himself the starting quarterback job with an insane performance over the final 11:31 on Sunday. McCarthy entered with the Giants trailing, 34-10. He quickly threw an interception. After that, though, he led three scoring drives in the final 9:31, with a comeback only falling short when his fourth-and-1 pass from the Saints’ 14-yard line fell incomplete with :06 to play. McCarthy completed 11 of 21 for a crazy 243 yards in 11 minutes of play, with a touchdown and an interception. He ran twice for 26 yards, ending up as the Giants’ leading rusher. After the game, head coach John Harbaugh left the door open for a quarterback change. It’s hard to see how he can avoid making one after what McCarthy did on Sunday. Malik Nabers — Nabers caught 12 passes for 165 yards and a touchdown on 15 targets. The 165 yards was the third-highest total of his career. I have an issue with what I saw as a lack of effort from Nabers to help Winston on a third-quarter interception by Martin Emerson, but his numbers are his numbers. There can’t be much doubt that Nabers is back to dominant form. This was his third straight 100-yard receiving game. Isaiah Likely — The talented tight end had six catches on 11 targets for 99 yards. What a tandem he and Nabers are turning into. Ar’Darius Washington/Jason Pinnock — With starter Tyler Nubin sidelined by a neck injury, the two safeties both made bids to take Nubin’s job. Washington had some nice plays in space in the first half. Pinnock had a forced fumble and was used effectively as a blitzer. Jordan Stout — The Giants’ punter is awesome. Five punts on the day for an average 54.2 yards, with a long of 66 yards. Dominic Zvada — The rookie placekicker bounced back from the first three misses of his career last week against the Washington Commanders to go 2 of 2 with field goals of 34 and 41 yards. Wet Willies to … The McCarthy Package — The Giants used it on one play. McCarthy lost 2 yards. McCarthy may have solved the problem on how to convince the Giants to stop messing around with this package by winning the starting job on Sunday. Giants’ run game — PITIFUL. ABOMINABLE. ATROCIOUS. NON-EXISTENT. Cam Skattebo was handcuffed by the Giants on Sunday as they did not give him the ball a single time after last Sunday’s overtime fumble. That left the door open for the rest of the Giants’ back to earn some trust. None responded. Najee Harris started and had four carries for 2 yards, Tracy had six carries for 18 yards, and Devin Singletary had four carries for 14 yards. J.J. McCarthy led the Giants with two carries for 26 yards, getting all of that on a 28-yard scramble on a desperate final drive by the Giants. The running backs weren’t good, and Harbaugh said as much: "One of those guys needs to step up. Somebody needs to step up and be the Back. None of those guys have done that yet" John Harbaugh fiesty when asked why Cam Skattebo was benched pic.twitter.com/chrEEXSvAR — Giants Nation Show (@GiantsNationPod) October 18, 2026 Maybe the Giants need to look for running back help at the NFL Trade Deadline. There is clearly a reason why they were interested in Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker and No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love during the offseason. They also, though, need to figure out why they can’t run block. If there were any holes for Giants’ backs to run through, I didn’t see them. I don’t know if the Giants have an answer to their woeful run blocking. The Saints entered the game 26th in the league in run defense, and the Giants could not budge the New Orleans front. That was pretty embarrassing. “Skattebo” chants — Skattebo played a handful of snaps, but didn’t touch the ball. Late in the third quarter, a smattering of “Skattebo” chants began. Those, to say the least, annoyed me. Fans here at Big Blue View spent a lot of time last week wondering if or when Harbaugh would hold Skattebo accountable for four fumbles in five weeks, including one last week that cost the Giants a chance to win a game. Harbaugh did hold Skattebo accountable on Sunday. Harris started. Skattebo never touched the ball. At the end of the third quarter there were a handful of “Skattebo” chants. Fans cannot have it both ways. You cannot ask for accountability, then complain about a player being held accountable. The coach did what he believed needed to be done. The Giants ran the ball terribly, but Skattebo and his 3.6 yards per carry averages wasn’t going to make a different with noplace to run. The run-blocking was putrid. Whether Skattebo was getting the ball or not was not going to change the outcome of this game. Kick coverage/return units — There was the Charlie Jones fumble, kickoff returns allowed of 41 and 30 yards, a punt return allowed of 23 yards, and two penalties that negated nice returns by Jones. The Giants have been really good on special teams so far this season. That wasn’t the case for their coverage and return units on Sunday. Kwillies to … Charlie Jones — The kick returner/wide receiver had a massive fumble at the end of the first half. After a Daniel Carlson field goal gave New Orleans its first points of the half, Jones lost the ball at the Giants’ 28-yard line. The Saints, who did nothing for the first 28 minutes of the game, capitalized by scoring a touchdown to tie the game at the half, 10-10. Jones did at least somewhat make amends in the second half. He had two catches for 66 yards, including a 49-yarder from McCarthy during the Giants’ furious comeback. Jones also had a 33-yard punt return wiped out by a penalty. Promising stuff, but the bad outweighed the good. Jameis Winston — Yes, there is likely going to be excitement about McCarthy after his fourth-quarter performance replacing Winston. I do not believe, though, that this loss can be blamed on Winston. The quarterback is not responsible for the embarrassingly bad running game. He isn’t responsible for the Jones’ fumble. He isn’t responsible for the lifeless third quarter, and the not-good-enough run defense. Winston threw two interceptions with the Giants already trailing by double digits. He did not put them in that hole. He simply wasn’t up to the task of digging them out of it. Tyrone Tracy — The third-year running back scored two touchdowns. Tracy had a 17-yard catch-and-run for a first-quarter touchdown, and a 5-yard fourth-quarter touchdown run. His overall numbers, six carries for 18 yards (3.0 yards per carry) and 2 receptions for 27 yards aren’t great. Touchdowns matter, though.

title: 4 things we learned from the Giants’ 34-27 loss to the Saints
summary: It’s an annual tradition. How long do we have to wait for the first MetLife stinker of the year by the New York Giants? In 2023 and 2024, the Giants got that out of the way in their opening game. In 2025, it wasn’t until the Kansas City game in week 3, but that was […]
full_text: Malik Nabers makes a catch on Sunday. | Getty Images It’s an annual tradition. How long do we have to wait for the first MetLife stinker of the year by the New York Giants? In 2023 and 2024, the Giants got that out of the way in their opening game. In 2025, it wasn’t until the Kansas City game in week 3, but that was only because the first two games were on the road; it was still the first home game. This year, things were different for a while at MetLife: A stirring opening win over Dallas, then two squeakers over bad Titans and Cardinals teams but in poor weather conditions. Today, the weather was beautiful at MetLife, and it looked like the Giants might be on their way to another home win. They jumped out to a 10-0 lead against the New Orleans Saints and were controlling the game. Then Daniel Carlson kicked a 58-yard field goal with 1:16 left in the first half. Charlie Jones fumbled on the ensuing kickoff, and it was all downhill from there, to the tune of 34 consecutive points by New Orleans. Yet the score wound up 34-27, and the Giants were within one end zone play of sending the game to overtime. What did we learn from this infuriating loss, the Giants’ fourth in four years to one of the NFC’s bottom feeders? Take my offensive coordinator, please I just do not like the Matt Nagy offense. Up to this point he’s run too often on first down, and usually between the tackles. It’s not getting the offense anywhere. More on that in a minute. But first, the passing game: Zero pass attempts beyond 20 yards for Jameis Winston. Only two pass attempts outside the hash marks at intermediate depths. And this against one of the poorer pass defenses in the NFL. For some perspective, let’s look at the same chart for Winston from last year in the Brian Daboll-Mike Kafka offense: Notice the ball being distributed all over the field. Other than Martin Emerson Jr., a good but not great cornerback, the rest of the Saints’ secondary is ordinary at best. And it’s not just the passing depths. It seems to me that almost every pass attempt is a contested catch opportunity rather than a route that is designed to create conflicts in the defense. I’m seeing a lot of stuff into the flat with no blockers in front of the receiver. I’m not seeing the high-low route combinations, the intermediate crossers, etc. that are the staple of explosive offenses. Finally when J.J. McCarthy came into the game, we saw some passes downfield (other than his first brief appearance, when Nagy had him run another one of those useless RPOs). By then, though, he had no choice and the Saints were playing soft to not give up the big play (which they actually did not do very well). Whether J.J.’s performance has created a quarterback controversy or not, I don’t know. What I do know, though, is that Winston is not being given a fair chance to show what he can do in the ultra-conservative, unimaginative offense he’s been asked to run. Malik Nabers had 165 yards on 12 catches today…but many of those came after the Giants fell behind. Isaiah Likely caught six passes for 99 yards. Between them, Darnell Mooney, and Malachi Fields, it should be possible to run up big passing yards before you get to the fourth quarter. Try it, Matt. I’m sure Cam Skattebo has learned his lesson…has John Harbaugh learned his? I get it. Skattebo has fumbled four times already this season, and his last one cost the Giants a victory in Washington. I’m all for a little discipline to get a point across to a player (and to his teammates). But there’s an old expression about cutting off your nose to spite your face. John Harbaugh cut the nose off the Giants’ offense by effectively benching Cam Skattebo, the Giants’ best running back, for the entire game. Najee Harris (four carries, 2 yards) is not the answer. Tyrone Tracy (six carries, 18 yards, but a TD and also two receptions for 27 yards and a TD) is part of the answer. Devin Singletary (four carries, 14 yards and a 19-yard reception) can be part of it, too. But Cam Skattebo is the Giants’ lead back. You want to teach him a lesson? Let him sit for the first quarter, or even the first half. Point made, point taken. But once the Saints had changed the momentum and the teams went in at halftime tied, it was time to get Skattebo back into the lineup to give the offense a jolt. Skattebo did play six snaps, but he didn’t touch the ball once. Giants’ running backs accounted for a total of 34 yards against one of the NFL’s worst rushing defenses. The Giants’ run blocking is bad, but these Next Gen Stats tell us that the running backs are a big part of the problem: The Giants RBs were expected to earn more yards than actual at the time of the handoff, per NGS tracking data: Singletary: 0 yards over expected (14 -> 14) Harris: -14 (2 -> 16) Tracy: -17 (18 -> 35) Skattebo: 0 carries — Doug Analytics (@Doug_Analytics) October 18, 2026 If only D.J. Reader could play every snap As opposed to the Giants’ anemic running game, the Saints’ running backs racked up 143 rushing yards today. It seemed to me that most of those came either when D.J. Reader was off the field or when they didn’t rush to his side. Every time I saw a Saints’ RB stuffed, It seemed I saw #98. He made 7 tackles overall (5 solo, 2 assists). Shelby Harris, who is usually on the field with him, seemed to play fairly well too ( 1 tackle, 2 assists). The run defense degrades considerably when Reader is off the field. Darius Alexander (1 tackle, 0 assists) at this point is a real liability in run defense. I don’t know what the Giants can do about it, other than get far enough ahead that teams are forced to abandon the run. Until they can, though, this will continue to be a problem. Other than the kicker and punter, the special teams are not special Jordan Stout has been as advertised, and Dominic Zvada seems not to have been shaken too much by his three missed field goals last week in Washington. The Giants return teams, however, have been awful. The game-turning play was obviously Charlie Jones’ fumble on the kickoff late in the first half, which allowed the Saints to tie the score at the half. But that’s not all. It seemed to me that every time the Giants had a kickoff or punt to return it was called back by a penalty. Overall the Giants had 10 penalties for 73 yards to the Saints’ 7 for 52. I’m not sure how many of those were on special teams, but I’m not the only one who thinks it’s a problem: These special teams flags are KILLING the Giants. In general the special teams have just let them down in this one with the fumble and penalties on nearly every return. This last penalty cost them 15 yards and was totally unnecessary. Just not disciplined — Dan Schneier (@DanSchneierNFL) October 18, 2026 For someone who earned his chops as a special teams coordinator before becoming a head coach, Harbaugh has a very undisciplined return unit. The shame of all this is that the Giants now go into Houston to face the resurgent Texans at 3-2-1 rather than the 5-1 they should have been.

title: J.J. McCarthy just created a quarterback controversy for the Giants
summary: The New York Giants are triggering a quarterback controversy following their 34-27 loss against the New Orleans Saints in Week 6 at MetLife Stadium. In the fourth quarter, with the Giants trailing 34-10, head coach John Harbaugh swapped out quarterback Jameis Winston in favor of J.J. McCarthy, who was acquired in a trade with the […]
full_text: J.J. McCarthy vs. the Saints. | Getty Images The New York Giants are triggering a quarterback controversy following their 34-27 loss against the New Orleans Saints in Week 6 at MetLife Stadium. In the fourth quarter, with the Giants trailing 34-10, head coach John Harbaugh swapped out quarterback Jameis Winston in favor of J.J. McCarthy, who was acquired in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings late last month. In McCarthy’s first legitimate action as the Giants’ quarterback, he excelled, completing 11 of 21 passes for 243 yards and a touchdown while also getting 26 yards on the ground. He led New York on a trio of scoring drives to cut the deficit to a single touchdown. McCarthy also had one last chance to tie or win the game on the final drive. He marched the Giants downfield all the way to the red zone, but he was unable to finish the job, resulting in a loss for the Giants. After the game, Giants Harbaugh kept the door open on a possible quarterback change ahead of Week 7 against the Houston Texans. “Did a heck of a job, given the circumstances and the desperation,” Harbaugh said postgame. “It’s different than normal football, but he made some plays, got us back, and gave us a chance at the end to win the game. We were throwing the ball in the end zone at the end, so that was good.” Harbaugh said he “can’t answer” who will start next week and would not make a decision 10 minutes after Sunday’s game. Despite winning his first two starts as QB1, Winston struggled against his former Saints team in Week 6. He completed 14 of 26 passes for 152 yards, a touchdown, and two interceptions, both of which led to quick scoring drives for the Saints. Winston was asked about how he felt about a possible benching ahead of next week. “That’s the decision [Coach John Harbaugh] will have to make. What I would love is to put myself in a better position to execute, and it starts with me: things I can control, going out there every single play, and doing my very best,” Winston said. Regardless of whether he is starting or backing up Winston next week, McCarthy is going to prepare against the Texans the same way. “Just making sure that each and every week, even when I got here when we were playing Arizona, I went into the game with the mindset that I could play the whole game. Just being able to really put myself in that position, Monday through Saturday, is something that helped me out today,” McCarthy said in the locker room. McCarthy was just happy to show he could help the team. “I hope I just showed them that I do my job at a high enough level that they can trust me out there,” McCarthy wasn’t biting on whether or not he deserved to be the starting quarterback. “At the end of the day, we didn’t win the game. We’ve got to do things better, and I’ve got to do better, and figure out ways that we can close this thing out.” Big Blue View community, who do you think should start next week between Winston and McCarthy? Let us know by voting in the poll below.

title: Giants-Saints instant grades: Giants failed to capitalize on big opportunity
summary: The New York Giants were blown out at home against the New Orleans Saints, 34-18. It was an odd game, though; New York dominated much of the first half and seemed in control, up 10-0, but a Charlie Jones fumble allowed the Saints to tie the game heading into halftime.  The Giants surrendered 34 consecutive […]
full_text: The New York Giants were blown out at home against the New Orleans Saints, 34-18. It was an odd game, though; New York dominated much of the first half and seemed in control, up 10-0, but a Charlie Jones fumble allowed the Saints to tie the game heading into halftime. The Giants surrendered 34 consecutive points, Jameis Winston threw two interceptions and was benched for J.J. McCarthy, and the Giants struggled on the ground all game. It was a humbling loss to a 1-4 team, albeit the Giants and J.J. McCarthy made it interesting down the stretch of the game. Here are the immediate positional grades following the loss. Quarterback Jameis Winston and the Giants’ offense were adequate in the first half – other than their run game –, but a second-half collapse led to a J.J. McCarthy finish. Winston threw two interceptions and finished 14/26 for 152 yards with one passing touchdown to Tyrone Tracy Jr. and a pair of interceptions. Winston was sacked four times. McCarthy entered the game and threw an interception. He was targeting Malachi Fields and expected him to sit, but the rookie pivoted outward. McCarthy, however, led a comeback effort and got the score to one possession after being down 34-10 in the fourth quarter. McCarthy was impressive and went 11/21 for 243 yards with a touchdown. New York turned the football over on downs with twelve seconds left at the New Orleans 14-yard line. McCarthy did a good job, but the Giants couldn’t pull off the comeback. We only saw the J.J. package once while Winston was still in the game. Grade: B Running Back The Giants running back conversation was lively all week, and it was Najee Harris who drew the start. New York rotated backs all game, but it was Tyrone Tracy Jr. who made his presence felt early. He caught a pass in the flat and outran Pete Werner for a 17-yard touchdown on third-and-seven. Tracy Jr. had the Giants’ fourth-quarter rushing touchdown too. He also had a couple of key blocks in pass protection, including on the 20-yard drag completion to Malik Nabers on second-and-fifteen. He did, though, take a false start penalty on third-and-eight. Devin Singletary had four rushes for 14 yards, Tracy had six for 18 yards, and Najee Harris had two yards on four rushes. Cam Skattebo did not record a carry in the game. Overall, the Giants’ rushing attack was nonexistent once again. Cam Skattebo didn’t receive a carry in the first half, and none of the backs could get anything going. The blocking is poor, and the rushing attack is unimpressive. Grade: C- Wide Receiver Malik Nabers is a stud — “ hey, Nick…tell me something I don’t know!?“ Nabers made a clutch 46-yard catch off impressive pocket maneuvering by J.J. McCarthy. The Giants, perhaps, should have kicked a field goal after the catch, instead of burning valuable time when they were down by ten, but I digress. Nabers finished with 12 catches on 15 targets for 165 yards. Charlie Jones caught two passes for 66 yards, including an impressive tap and secure 49-yard catch in the Giants’ comeback effort. Malachi Fields caught two passes for 19 yards. Darnell Mooney had a 20-yard rush, and he left the game with an injury. Overall, the Giants received the same from their wide receiver corps — a lot of Nabers with small contributions from the other receivers. Nabers is elite, but the Giants got to get more players involved when the opposing team removes Nabers and Likely with double teams. Grade: B+ Tight End Isaiah Likely caught six of 11 targets for 99 yards with a touchdown in comeback mode. Likely is a major part of the Giants’ offense, and he consistently makes plays in the short and intermediate parts of the field. He also secured an important two-point conversion in comeback mode. He is very good. Thomas Fidone II played for Theo Johnson, who missed the game with a neck injury. He took a penalty and was not targeted. Chris Manhertz is a blocking asset, but, again, was not targeted. Grade: A Offensive Line The Giants offensive line can’t run block. It’s been bad for weeks. The pass protection had its losses too throughout the game. Marcus Mbow received the start for the injured Jermaine Eleumunor. Jon Ruyan struggled with power again. Francis Mauigoa was beaten badly for a sack that was negated by a roughing the passer penalty; Mauigoa also took a holding penalty on third-and-eight that offset an offside penalty. Marcus Mbow was thrown to the turf against Cam Jordan on one rep, and he then took a bad false start when the Giants were in field goal range late in the fourth quarter. Grade: D- Defensive Line D.J. Reader continues to be an absolute stud for the Giants – an excellent free agent addition who has secured the Giants’ run defense on the inside. The Giants defense stifled the Saints offense in the first half. The second-half collapse was not on the defense, per se, but they broke in the second half. Shelby Harris was fine from what I saw, and Darius Alexander made the tackle on Kendre Miller’s third-and-five rush, which allowed the Giants’ offense to have a game-tying opportunity. Grade: B EDGE Abdul Carter is a menace for opposing offensive tackles. He drew an important holding penalty that stalled the Saints’ second drive, and he is so quick to win on high-side rushes. The pass rush was harassing when coupled with the blitz in the first half, albeit Shough was not sacked. Still, the pass rush was negated once the game got out of hand. Kayvon Thibodeaux hit Shough on second down, which resulted in a roughing the passer penalty on the Saints’ first drive of the second half; this extended the momentum that the Saints had after the end of the first half debacle. Thibodeaux continues to do his job, but he struggles to generate pressure. Grade: C+ Linebacker Arvell Reese shocks grown men with his strength. He met a climbing offensive lineman in space and put him on his rear end, which resulted in the lineman knocking the Saints’ ball carrier down. Reese is the real deal, and he is constantly around the football. Reese helped Jason Pinnock force a late fourth-quarter fumble. Tremaine Edmunds led the team with 12 tackles. He is good to have as a Giant. Grade: B+ Cornerback Tae Banks and Greg Newsome II are thriving in this heavy-pressure system. The quick outlets for Tyler Shough were not available for easy completions for much of the first half; quick curls were promptly clamped down on, and throwing windows were tight for the second-year quarterback all game. Banks did, however, take a pass interference that was declined in the third quarter. Newsome II exited the game with a concussion and he was replaced by Nic Jones. Jones took a defensive hands to the face in the second half. Jones was then beat by Chris Olave for a dagger touchdown early in the fourth quarter. Dru Phillips helped to make a big tackle near the sidelines, while being blocked, which resulted in a converted 51-yard field goal by Daniel Carlson. Grade: B Safety Jevon Holland continued to be all around the football; he made plays in coverage and around the line of scrimmage, specifically the designed QB keeper that lost the Saints four yards near the goal line. He added a PBU too. Holland played well but did have a missed tackle on Alvin Kamara’s 31-yard touchdown, as did Jason Pinnock. Pinnock and Ar’Darius Washington were involved on the exotic pressure packages for New York, which was impactful in the first half. Pinnock did, however, help to dislodge a fumble late in the game. Grade: B+ Special Teams Dominic Zvada made a 34-yard field goal and then booted a 41-yarder that made the game one score late. Jordan Stout averaged 54 yards on his five punts – he is a stud. However, the special teams were to blame for the turnaround; Charlie Jones fumbled the football on a kickoff with just over a minute in the first half, which allowed the Saints to tie the game heading into halftime. This came directly after the defense forced a 58-yard field goal. The Giants’ kick coverage allowed the Saints to…

author: Ed Valentine

title: ‘Things I think’ before Giants-Saints kickoff: Giants have an opportunity
summary: The New York Giants are staring at a tremendous opportunity. The 3-1-1 Giants lead a division that is convoluted, to say the least. To start with, the Giants have not won the division since 2011. That is the last time the Giants won the Super Bowl. So, no one is used to seeing New York […]
full_text: Cam Skattebo | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants are staring at a tremendous opportunity. The 3-1-1 Giants lead a division that is convoluted, to say the least. To start with, the Giants have not won the division since 2011. That is the last time the Giants won the Super Bowl. So, no one is used to seeing New York atop the standings. The Philadelphia Eagles, who have won the division the past two seasons and three of the past four and had Super Bowl aspirations, are a mess. They are 2-3, riding a three-game losing streak. Quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for an undetermined length of time with a ‘superficial’ blood clot in his calf. Running back Saquon Barkley and wide receiver DaVonta Smith are out with hamstring injuries. Right tackle Lane Johnson retired midseason. Starting center/guard Cam Jurgens was traded. New offensive coordinator Sean Mannion has yet to prove he is up to the task. The Dallas Cowboys are also 2-3. Considering Philadelphia’s woes and preseason expectations for the Cowboys, the division should be Dallas’s for the taking. But there are huge questions about whether or not Dallas can take it. After overhauling their defense and bringing in new defensive coordinator Christian Parker, the Cowboys have still been awful on that side of the ball. They brought in veteran coach Mike Pettine as a consultant this week. Coach Brian Schottenheimer is under fire after his decision-making helped the Cowboys lose a game to the Baltimore Ravens that they tied with :07 to play. Dallas players held a players-only team meeting this week. It’s anybody’s guess which direction the Cowboys’ season will go in. The Commanders (1-3-1) are in crisis after Sunday’s mismanaged game against the Giants. There are questions about head coach Dan Quinn’s fitness for the job. Quarterback Jayden Daniels is being criticized from every direction, including by Green Bay Packers star outside linebacker Micah Parsons. Washington is 0-3 in the NFC East already. In Week 6, they are on the road to face the 5-0 San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football. Their season might already be over. The Giants? They are just chugging happily along, shrugging off Sunday’s tie. Head coach John Harbaugh has convinced them they have worked hard enough to earn the right to win, and that if they stay on task, they will continue to get better. “We want to be more consistent with doing the things that are required to win a football game,” Harbaugh said. “It’s really hard to win in this league. You’ve got to do a lot of things right against a team that’s trying to do a lot of things right too. I think they have it. I think they have what it takes. I’ve told them that. They have what it takes. And they’re chasing execution every single day. So, I’m really proud of them. I think they’re really diligent. They’re tough-minded. They work really hard, and they’re very talented. Those are all really important traits. “So, let’s see what we can do with this. Let’s see where we can go.” The Giants have an opportunity at home on Sunday against an underachieving 1-4 New Orleans Saints team that has been put on notice by owner Gayle Benson . A win could help the Giants gain more ground and stamp themselves as legitimate threats to win the division. We will see if they can get it done. Backfield changes coming? John Harbaugh is not one to ever discuss who will play or who won’t, and I don’t know that we will ever see him do what Buffalo Bills coach Joe did this week, using the media to warn running back James Cook that his carries will decrease if his fumbling doesn’t. Cook, like Cam Skattebo, has four fumbles in five games. That, though, doesn’t mean Harbaugh is going to simply stand around and watch Skattebo continue to put the ball on the ground. “You can definitely coach it. It’s a major point of emphasis. The league is more of a punch-out league than it’s ever been before, and more players are really good at it than they’ve ever been before,” Harbaugh said. “We better ramp it up, just like with everybody else in the league. It’s been a major point of emphasis from day one, and it’s still not good enough. So, we’ve got to get a lot better in that area. That’s been probably the most important thing with our offense. Really, right now, but really all the time. But the fact that we’ve had a number of fumbles, way more than we should, we’re making a big deal out of it.” The Giants are 3-0 this season and 5-0 over Skattebo’s 13-game career when he carries the ball at least 18 times. Being able to do that has been an indication that the Giants are playing the way they want to play, even if it means the offense is grinding rather than explosive. Harbaugh did admit on Friday that there is a breaking point where carries would have to be redistributed. “Of course. Yes. There is a point,” Harbaugh said. Has he reached it? We’ll see. We’ll find out,“ is all the coach would say. Will the Giants' fumbling issues get to a point where John Harbaugh will need to possibly make adjustments? "Yes, there is a point." Have the Giants reached that point? "We'll see. We'll find out." pic.twitter.com/PeEeCR6HFv — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) October 16, 2026 According to reports on Sunday morning, it appears Harbaugh has reached that point. Najee Harris is expected to start . ‘Damn good’ Dominic Zvada needs to bounce back Rookie placekicker Dominic Zvada went 2 of 5 on field-goal attempts last Sunday against Washington, the first three misses of his career after nine made kicks in the season’s first four weeks. Zvada is now 11 of 14 on field-goal tries. Sunday will be a test for the 22-year-old after the first blip of his professional career. Zvada told me on Thursday that he “never” questions himself Special teams coach Chris Horton said Zvada’s alignment was off slightly as he was getting too close to the ball. “It’s just something that sometimes happens,” Zvada said. “That’s just something we have to be mindful of going forward.” Horton isn’t worried about Zvada’s confidence. “You just got to remind him that he is damn good,” Horton said. “That’s one of the things I think when you believe in your players again, and you remind them that they’re here for a reason and you trust in them. You’ve just got to remind them of those things. From a confidence standpoint, that’s solely on him and him understanding that I can go out there and I can do this. “This kid was nine-for-nine before he came into this game. summary: Welcome to the New York Giants betting angle, Week 6 edition! Each week, I’m giving you my three favorite wagers for that week’s New York Giants game. full_text: Let’s Go! | Getty Images Welcome to the New York Giants betting angle, Week 6 edition! Each week, I’m giving you my three favorite wagers for that week’s New York Giants game. My one rule: I won’t ever give you wagers that are less than -120. No gimmes! For the second straight week, the Giants are underdogs to a team with a worse record. The first-place Giants are 3-1-1 after last week’s miracle tie with the Commanders. Their opponent this week is New Orleans, who sits at 1-4 after dropping three straight home games to the Raiders, Falcons, and Vikings, and allowing 103 points in the process. The game is at MetLife stadium, and the Saints are favored by 1.5 points. Hmm. True, in their two road games the Saints took the Lions to overtime and upset the Ravens, and they’ve beaten the Giants in each of the last three seasons. Still, the line is surprising to me, and you’ll see that in my picks. Are the Giants a good team? The oddsmakers are apparently very skeptical. For the fourth straight week, the Giants are facing a team who, like them, picked in the Top-10 in the 2026 draft last April. Three of those games are at home. This is the easy stretch of the schedule, and Big Blue is taking advantage of that. We’ll see if that continues on Sunday. I’m still on a heater – My picks were 2-1 last week, 8-1 over the past three weeks, and 10-5 on the season. I’ll try to keep giving out winners here in Week 6. Let’s get to this week’s picks. All lines and odds are from Fanduel and are as of Saturday, October 17. Perfect fall weather is expected on Sunday, with moderate winds. The line for the game is Saints -1.5, with a game total of 45.5. Giants moneyline (-104). I’m sorry, but the Saints shouldn’t be favored over New York, and especially on the road. New Orleans shouldn’t be favored over more than a handful of teams. They can’t run the ball, or stop the run, and while they’re certainly capable of putting up points and beating good teams, they’re 1-4 for a reason. If you want to take the points, the juice is (-122), so I think the moneyline is giving a better price. You’re only surrendering two outcomes: The Giants losing by a point, or a second straight tie. Game total OVER 45.5 . Kellen Moore’s offense runs fast. They average 74 plays per game, which trails only the Bears. More plays often translates to a decent number of points. But on the flip side, New Orleans has given up 151 points in five games (30.1 per game), and only Arizona is worse than that. James Winston is settling in, and New York put up 63 points over the last two weeks. All signs point me to the over. Cam Skattebo most rushing yards in game (-120). Skattebo’s untimely fumble in overtime last week should’ve cost Big Blue the game, but Jayden Daniels let them off the hook when he let time expire with his team in field goal range. I expect plenty of Skat on Sunday, rather than a visit to the doghouse for fumbling. The way to beat the Saints is to ram it down their throats. New Orleans brings in the NFL’s 30 th -ranked run defense. They also have the 29 th -ranked rushing offense, and with a committee approach taken I don’t see any of their backs outgaining Skattebo. That leaves New York’s other backs and the quarterbacks. I’ll take my chances there. Those are the picks for Week 6. Good luck with your wagers! And if you play fantasy football, be sure to check out my Week 6 fantasy preview, with start/sit advice and more, right here .

title: Jets vs Patriots: Failure in Foxborough
summary: In the New York Jets’ sixth game of the 2026 season, on a crisp, clear day in Foxborough, Massachusetts, the Jets fell to the New England Patriots, 26 – 19. The game opened with the Jets on offense. They put together a solid opening drive, chewing up half the opening quarter, mixing runs and short […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - OCTOBER 18: Romeo Doubs #87 of the New England Patriots scores a touchdown against the New York Jets during the first quarter at Gillette Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the New York Jets’ sixth game of the 2026 season, on a crisp, clear day in Foxborough, Massachusetts, the Jets fell to the New England Patriots, 26 – 19. The game opened with the Jets on offense. They put together a solid opening drive, chewing up half the opening quarter, mixing runs and short passes to get inside the Patriots 15 yard line before settling for a 42 yard field goal and an early 3 – 0 Jets lead. After the Jets forced a Patriots three and out the Jets offense took over for their second drive. It did not go well. Geno Smith was sacked twice, forcing the Jets back to their own three yard line. Austin McNamara punted out of his own end zone and the Patriots started their second drive with great field position in Jets territory. Two plays later the Patriots were in the end zone on a 42 yard bomb to Romeo Doubs, making the score Patriots 7, Jets 3. The quarter ended with the score still Patriots 7, Jets 3, with the Jets driving inside the Patriots 35 yard line. Unfortunately, the Jets came up empty as they came up short on a 4th down try. From there neither team could put together much on offense until the Jets failed to convert another 4th down attempt and the Patriots took over at their own 39 yard line with less than seven minutes left in the first half. The Patriots took advantage of the good field position as they put together a short drive ending in a field goal and a 10 – 3 Patriots lead with just under two minutes left in the half. As has been tradition for the Jets, they looked like they were entirely unfamiliar with the concept of a two minute drill as they went three and out and punted the ball back to the Patriots with plenty of time left on the clock. The Patriots gladly accepted the Jets’ gift as they marched right down the field for a touchdown with less than 20 seconds left in the half. The half ended with the Jets trailing by two touchdowns at Patriots 17, Jets 3. Despite dominating the clock and looking effective on offense, the Jets’ repeated failures in short yardage situations put them in a deep hole to start the second half. The Jets opened the third quarter on defense. The Patriots advanced into Jets territory before they failed to convert on a 4th and five. The Jets offense took over at their own 40 yard line with good field position and an opportunity to get back in the game. It didn’t take long for the Jets to answer the call. On the Jets’ 3rd play of the drive Geno Smith launched a bomb that Omar Cooper settled under in the end zone. The touchdown brought the Jets within seven points at Patriots 17, Jets 10 early in the third quarter. On the ensuing Patriots drive David Bailey forced a Patriots fumble and the Jets recovered deep in Patriots territory with a chance to even the score. The Jets were unable to fully take advantage. They were forced to settle for a 36 yard field goal. That brought the score to Patriots 17, Jets 13 late in the third quarter. The third quarter ended with the score still 17 – 13 with the Patriots driving deep in Jets territory. A few plays into the fourth quarter Drake Maye hit Hunter Henry in the end zone and the Patriots snuffed out the Jets’ building momentum. The Patriots missed the extra point, bringing the score to Patriots 23, Jets 13 early in the 4th quarter. With a double digit deficit to make up things did not look good for the Jets. On the Jets next possession Geno Smith threw up an ill-advised moon ball that was intercepted by the Patriots. It was the first interception of the season for Smith, and it put the Jets in a hole they were unlikely to recover from. The Jets weren’t done yet. A few plays later the Jets forced a reversal of fortune. Jamien Sherwood forced a fumble, Minkah Fitzpatrick recovered and the Jets were in business near midfield. The Jets moved the ball but were forced to settle for a field goal, bringing the Jets within a touchdown at Patriots 23, Jets 16 midway through the fourth quarter. In a humiliating ending to a hard fought game, the Patriots took over and simply ran the ball down the Jets’ throats behind a makeshift offensive line filled with backups. The Jets were helpless to stop them, the Patriots ran the clock down to close to a minute left to play, then kicked a field goal to seal the Jets’ fate. The Jets tacked on a last gasp field goal, but they were unable to recover the ensuing onsides kick, and the Patriots ran out the remaining few seconds of the game. Final score: Patriots 26, Jets 19. The loss brought the Jets’ record to 2-4. The Jets return home next week to take on a winless Miami Dolphins team, looking to get back on the winning track.
