title: Jets vs Patriots Pre-Game Ball
summary: Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 04: Dane Belton #6 of the New York Jets reacts during the fourth quarter of the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on October 04, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage for the Jets in the upcoming game. Occasionally we might hand out a pre-blame ball. If we think the Jets are going to get slaughtered, we’ll try to identify a prime culprit. One caveat: the quarterback is off limits. Nothing personal against quarterbacks, but they are obviously the most important players on the field. We could give out a pre-game or pre-blame ball to the quarterback virtually every week, but that would be boring, so we’re not going to do it. We’ll try to identify somebody besides the quarterback for the glory or the ignominy. This approach comes with the obvious drawback that predictions are difficult, especially about the future. We’re destined to get many of these wrong. No matter. We’ll have some laughs along the way. Let’s get to it. The Jets pre-game ball for the Jets game against the New England Patriots goes to (drum roll please) – Dane Belton! The Jets have some holes on offense going into this game. They are missing Adonai Mitchell, and Omar Cooper and Kenyon Sadiq are both listed as questionable. Breece Hall and Dylan Parham are also missing this game. Against a Patriots team currently ranked 5th in the NFL in yards allowed, the banged up Jets offense will probably not be winning any shootouts on Sunday. The Jets defense may have to carry the day. The Patriots may be missing A.J. Brown again on Sunday after he missed the last two games with an injury. In Browns’ absence the Patriots have been relying on the running game and their tight ends in the passing game a lot. Enter Dane Belton. He has been a revelation for the Jets. He rarely misses tackles, wraps up well, is a force against the run, and has the speed to take on tight ends against the pass. If Belton and his running partner Minkah Fitzpatrick can neutralize the Patriots’ tight ends and running backs, the rest of the Patriots weapons on offense aren’t top of the NFL talent. Against a Patriots team that has put up a combined 74 points on offense over the last two games, the Jets’ safeties will play a crucial role in slowing down Drake Maye and company. Maybe Belton forces a fumble. Maybe he sacks Maye in a crucial spot. Maybe he snags an interception. Somehow, some way, I’m looking for Belton to be a difference maker on defense on Sunday. If he is, maybe the Jets have a chance at an upset win. Dane Belton, come on down! Your breakout game awaits. You get your opportunity on Sunday. Let’s see you run with it. What about you? Who would you give the pre-game ball to? Let us know in the comments.

summary: With the Philadelphia Eagles looking to add another quarterback in the aftermath of Jalen Hurts’ blood clot situation, the team signed Joe Milton III from the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad last week. Milton III was not their first choice. The team wanted to bring Andy Dalton back to Philly, according to a report from Pro […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Andy Dalton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles makes a pass during the first half of the preseason game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the Philadelphia Eagles looking to add another quarterback in the aftermath of Jalen Hurts’ blood clot situation, the team signed Joe Milton III from the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad last week. Milton III was not their first choice. The team wanted to bring Andy Dalton back to Philly, according to a report from Pro Football Talk . But Dalton “politely declined.” Dalton began the 2026 season as Philly’s No. 2 quarterback behind Hurts. But he was demoted to No. 3 after throwing an interception in his sole pass attempt as a member of the Eagles. The team then released him on the Friday leading up to the Eagles’ Week 5 game. At the time, there was talk that Dalton could return. But now Dalton has reportedly decided to go elsewhere. PFT says he will join a new team “as soon as tomorrow.” It’s kinda sad that the Eagles wanted Dalton but couldn’t get him. Then again, it’s for the best. Dalton, who turns 39 later this month, looked physically diminished as he struggled during offseason practices and preseason games. And with the Eagles potentially in a lost season, there isn’t much value in Dalton playing for this team. He’s not good enough to help them in the short-term and he obviously provides no long-term upside. In Week 6, the Eagles had rookie Cole Payton as their No. 2 and Milton III as their emergency third quarterback. Those guys probably aren’t long-term solutions in Philly. But there’s a non-zero chance that’s the case. Could be interesting to watch them play if they ever get the chance. The same couldn’t be said for seeing Dalton in an Eagles uniform again.

title: Eagles vs. Panthers: The good, the bad, and the ugly
summary: This was over before it started. By the middle of the fourth quarter on Sunday, that reality finally reached the fans by the show of large sections of empty seats at Lincoln Financial Field. Get ready for a lot of that in the coming months, because the rest of the Eagles’ 2026 season will be […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 18: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni reacts in the second half during the game between the Carolina Panthers and Philadelphia Eagles on October 18, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Kyle Ross/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images This was over before it started. By the middle of the fourth quarter on Sunday, that reality finally reached the fans by the show of large sections of empty seats at Lincoln Financial Field. Get ready for a lot of that in the coming months, because the rest of the Eagles’ 2026 season will be devoted to evaluating who to keep and who to discard after the Eagles fell to the Carolina Panthers, 25-14, at the Linc. The Eagles are now 2-4— and through , regardless of how bad the NFC East looks. It was the Eagles’ fourth-straight loss, making it the first time they have lost four-straight games since Doug Peterson’s 4-11-1 season in 2020—and the first four-game losing streak in Nick Sirianni’s tenure. Going to the Linc are still great ways to fill autumn Sunday afternoons, sans winning. But after the greatest four-year stretch in Eagles’ history, with the mounting cracks in the wall the Eagles were bound to collapse. They have. The Eagles may be expecting Tanner McKee to be the next coming of Nick Foles (or Tom Brady, according to Zack Baun). The problem is this fanbase knows Nick Foles. It watched Nick Foles win a Super Bowl. Tanner McKee is no Nick Foles. Tanner McKee is no answer to Jalen Hurts for the fools out there who thought he was. Eagles’ fans, that loyal fanbase, get it. They abandoned the home team well before Panthers’ kicker Ryan Fitzgerald’s missed extra point went spinning right to the background of vast empty seats with 6:33 left to play. No one wanted to sit through the inevitable. The Eagles are falling with nothing available to pick them up. They were down to rookie Keyshawn James-Newby and Arnold Ebitketie as their edge rushers for the majority of the game after Nolan Smith was lost to a concussion in the second quarter. Carolina’s Bryce Young is blossoming into a franchise quarterback. He completed 20 of 39 for 281 yards and two touchdowns, while McKee struggled through major portions of the game, completing 26 of 45 for 215 yards and a touchdown. Against Carolina, the Eagles passed 45 times and ran the ball 13, against one of the NFL’s worst rushing defenses. Right now, Eagles’ offensive coordinator Sean Mannion is making Kevin Patullo look like Sid Gillman, if that’s possible. It was interesting that Hurts was nowhere to be found on the sideline. Philly sports salvation is near. If anyone had not noticed, there is a new “King” in Philly, LeBron James and the 76ers will open their season on Tuesday against the defending NBA champion New York Knicks. Numerous Eagles may be courtside. They should thank the Sixers, because the old king, the Eagles, are losing their glare and fading from the eye of the Philly sports storm. The Eagles’ over-under apathy line is mid-November. By then, the Flyers may even double the Eagles’ victory total. There was a pinch of good, undermined by piles of bad and a mountain of ugly in the Eagles’ 25-14 loss to the Carolina Panthers. The Good The Eagles forcing a three-and-out with 9:46 to play after the DeVonta Smith score brought the Eagles to within 19-14. Smith’s great leaping 19-yard touchdown catch with 10:42 left to play. It was a great pass thrown by McKee, who found Smith over the shoulder of Panthers’ rookie cornerback Will Lee in the right corner of the end zone. It brought the Eagles within a score of the Panthers, 19-14. Earlier, Smith’s 16-yard reception gave the Eagles a first down on a third-and-seven on the Eagles’ sixth possession at the Carolina 40. It was the first positive in what was otherwise a dismal first half for the Eagles. The 18-yard reception to Dallas “Cheeks” Goedert on the Eagles’ second drive of the second half —it was a rare second-half first down for the Eagles, who quickly squandered it with a two-yard run, six-yard McKee sack and a McKee incompletion. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. coming up with a touchdown-saving tackle on Bryce Young’s eight-yard scramble on a third-and-nine from the Eagles’ 11 on the second play of the fourth quarter. Dameon Pierce’s two-yard, second-quarter touchdown run with 2:42 left in the first half, thanks largely to the dubious 22-yard pass interference call on a pass to Goedert, who had his pants pulled down two plays prior. It snapped the 57-minute, 21-second home scoring draught the Eagles had under Sirianni, who last saw his team score at home on a Darius Cooper 10-yard touchdown reception with :03 left in the half on Oct. 4 against the Los Angeles Rams. A pair of Pierce nine-yard runs on the Eagles’ third possession, bringing the ball to the Eagles’ 49, the deepest penetration the Eagles had to that point. Nolan Smith’s eight-yard sack on Carolina’s second drive. It was the first good thing that happened to the hapless Eagles. It may have more to do with Bryce Young holding the ball too long than anything Smith did, but it was a minus positive play for the Eagles when everything was going backwards. Smith was lost in the second quarter due to a concussion. The Bad Receiver Dontayvion Wicks going down with yet another Eagles’ injury after a 17-yard reception on a third-and-five play with 12:47 left and the Eagles down 19-7. The first half. The Eagles got plenty of help from eight Carolina penalties for 105 yards, including the big one when Goedert went quarter moon on a 22-yard interference call, which led to the Eagles’ first score. The Eagles were outgained 178-110 in the half, and averaged 3.3 yards per play and 3.5 yards per pass play to 7 yards for the Panthers. Punter Braden Mann booting a rare bad 23-yard punt midway through the second quarter. The ball landed at the Eagles’ 35, and led to the first touchdown of the game, when Bryce Young hit Tommy Tremble for a 12-yard score with 8:08 left in the first half. With 11 minutes left in the first half, Carolina already had six plays of 10 yards or more to the Eagles’ one. The Panthers came into the game No. 2 in the NFL with 20 plays of 20+ yards (behind Buffalo’s 22 plays) and 67 plays of 10+ yards. The Eagles punted on their first five drives and went three-and-out on three of their first five drives. Tight end Johnny “Who” Mundt getting flagged for a 10-yard holding penalty, negating McKee’s 20-yard completion to Cooper. It set the Eagles back to their 21 and eventually placed them in a third-and-12, which they typically failed to convert. Pierce dropping a pass while wide open on the Eagles’ third drive. False start on Jordan Mailata on the Eagles’ third drive. Not good when the only vested starter on the offensive line gets flagged for a false start. The Eagles giving up 26 yards to Trevor Etienne on the Eagles’ first punt. It gave Carolina great field position to the Panthers’ 39, and eventually led to a 3-0 Panthers’ lead on a Fitzgerald 47-yard field goal with 10:50 left in the first quarter, which banged off the right goal post and went through. The Ugly In the second half of their six games this season, the Eagles have now been outscored 68-30, with just 10 points scored in the second half over their last four games. They scored 10 points and gained 149 yards in the second half against Washington, 10 points and 125 yards against Tennessee, 0 points and 54 yards against Chicago, 0 points and 66 yards against the Los Angeles Rams, 3 points and 84 yards against Jacksonville, and 7 points and 112 yards against Carolina, which averages out to 98.3 yards and an NFL-low 5 points a game in the second half. They have now converted 12 of 45 third downs in the second half. Yeah, it may seem like we’re picking on poor Cooper DeJean here, but again, he failed in two clutch situations. On first-and-10 with the Panthers at the Eagles’ 19, because of a DeJean penalty, he…

title: Eagles-Panthers final score: Philadelphia loses fourth straight game in very boring fashion
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are 2-4 after losing to the Carolina Panthers at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday. Final score: 25 to 14. Well, that game was very boring. It felt like a 2025 redux. The offense, led by Tanner McKee instead of Jalen Hurts, pretty much sucked. The defense kept the Eagles in the game […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 18: Bobby Okereke #58 of the Carolina Panthers sacks Tanner McKee #16 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the first quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on October 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are 2-4 after losing to the Carolina Panthers at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday. Final score: 25 to 14. Well, that game was very boring. It felt like a 2025 redux. The offense, led by Tanner McKee instead of Jalen Hurts, pretty much sucked. The defense kept the Eagles in the game for most of the day … until the dam inevitably broke in the second half. Watching this offense is just so painful. Yes, the Eagles are incredibly injured on that side of the ball. And they had to deal with even more injuries that were sustained during this game. But it’s hard to argue the coaching staff is doing their part to make the most of what they do have. Something needs to change. Next up for the Eagles: a home game against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football in Week 7. Ugh. We have to stay up late to watch this dreck? Read on for a recap and stay tuned for BGN’s postgame coverage. Also, check me out talking about this game on the PHLY Eagles postgame show. FIRST QUARTER The Panthers won the coin toss and elected to defer to put the Eagles on offense first. The Eagles took over at their own 26-yard line. Tanner McKee immediately got sacked from unblocked pressure on what was supposed to be a play-action pass. Then McKee’s first throw was a little wide of Makai Lemon and the ball bounced off his hands and was nearly picked off. Facing 3rd-and-21, McKee checked down to Dameon Pierce to pick up some yards to set up a punt. 3 plays, zero yards, punt. Probably not a great thing that the offense looked out of sorts and confused what to do on the very first snap! The Panthers took over at their own 39-yard line. They quickly moved into field goal range. Facing 3rd-and-3 from the plus 30-yard line, the Panthers went with a run that resulted in no gain. Good job by the defense to hunker down. Carolina settled for a 47-yard field goal make that bounced off the right upright and in. EAGLES 0, PANTHERS 3. The Eagles took over at their own 22-yard line after Britain Covey muffed the kick return. Facing 3rd-and-13 after an incompeltion where McKee was pressured with Jake Majors losing his battle and a completion to Pierce for a loss, Lemon made a diving grab that was ruled incomplete by replay assist. Looked like it might’ve actually been a grab. But it was well short of the sticks anyway. 3 plays, -3 yards, punt. The Panthers began at their own 16-yard line. Andrew Mukuba gave up a first down completion to Tetairoa McMillan and also got called for illegal contact, which was declined. Nolan Smith picked up his third sack of the season with the tight end releasing him and Bryce Young holding onto the ball for too long. Facing 3rd-and-12, Young aired it out deep but underthrew Darren Waller and the ball bounced off Riq Woolen’s helmet for a stop. Now that’s what I call using your head! Takedown for Nolan 💪 pic.twitter.com/N32mWI4ll1 — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) October 18, 2026 The Eagles took over at their own 11-yard line. Jordan Mailata immediately false started to knock the offense back. But then McKee aired out to DeVonta Smith, who couldn’t make an impressive one-handed grab while being held but drew the pass interference flag. Positive yardage and a first down! A miracle! McKee got the ball to Carson Steele, who made a nice catch and broke a tackle on his first touch of the season … and then got hurt going to the ground. Naturally. Facing 3rd-and-6, McKee rolled right and it looked like he had nothing to work with … but Dontayvion Wicks was able to make a toe-tapping sideline grab for a first down. Then Pierce took the Eagles’ first rushing attempt for nine yards. Then another Pierce carry for nine yards. Then Pierce broke a would-be TFL to run for no gain. Then Pierce dropped a pass in the flat after getting his head turned around a little late. Facing 3rd-and-10, McKee had his hand hit as he threw for an incompletion. Facing 4th-and-10 from plus 42-yard line, the Eagles lined up to punt and tried to draw the Panthers offside. To literally no one’s surprise, it didn’t work. The Panthers declined the delay of game penalty and Braden Mann punted 28 yards to the Panthers’ 14-yard line. Why not just go for it on fourth down? Or even try a field goal from 60-plus. What are those 28 yards really doing for this team? The Panthers took over at their own 14-yard line and instantly picked up 19 yards (only nine away from where the Eagles punted). Facing 3rd-and-6 after two runs, Young’s third down pass was knocked down by Jalen Carter. Another big defensive stop. The Eagles brought pressure on the punt and it looked like Keyshawn James-Newby got a piece of the ball but he was instead flagged for running into the kicker. The Panthers did NOT opt to go for it on 4th-and-1, instead punting for a touchback. The Eagles took over at their own 20-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-4 after a Pierce run was stopped for a three-yard loss, McKee hit Dallas Goedert at the marker for a first down to end the first quarter. 17 plays for 37 yards to start the game for the Eagles’ offense. Scintillating stuff. SECOND QUARTER McKee hit Darius Cooper for a nice 19-yard completion! But it was wiped out by a Johnny Mundt holding penalty. A league-leading three holding penalties by a tight end. Dude stinks and the Eagles have been asking too much of him to be TE2. Facing 3rd-and-12, McKee stepped up against a blitz and well overthrew Wicks. Watching this offense is sooooo boring. Zzzzzzzzzzzz. The Panthers took over at their own 27-yard line. The Panthers needed just two plays to move into Eagles territory. The Panthers had a 23-yard gain negated by an ineligible man downfield penalty, fortunate break for the Eagles’ defense. Facing 3rd-and-10, Young’s throw short of the sticks to Waller was wide and incomplete. Another stop by Vic Fangio’s defense. The Eagles took over at their own 8-yard line. Goedert dropped a would-be first down reception. Then McKee way overthrew his target as Markel Bell got called for holding but the penalty was declined. 3 plays, four yards, punt. Braden Mann shanked the punt, which went for just 23 yards. The Panthers took over at the Eagles’ 35-yard line. Carter batted down another Young pass and Cooper DeJean flew in for a TFL. Facing 3rd-and-10, DeJean was called for a tacky illegal contact penalty. Unfortunate. The Eagles’ defense pressured Young into an incompletion that was clearly intentional grounding. The refs originally stated that Young was out of the pocket but clearly never left it. Upon discussing it further, they finally threw the flag (lol). But then Jordan Davis got called for roughing the passer by getting his hands on Young’s helmet to give the Panthers more yardage after a 17-yard completion. Hardly a late hit but the refs are gonna call that one. The Panthers entered the red zone and Young hit Tommy Tremble for a 12-yard touchdown. Feels like an insurmountable lead? EAGLES 0, PANTHERS 10. Sure looks like Jihaad Campbell is lost here (as usual). https://t.co/ycQ3hv95AO — Deniz Selman (@denizselman33) October 18, 2026 The Eagles took over at their own 22-yard line. McKee hit Goedert over the middle for a first down! Feels like a miracle. A Goedert false start knocked the offense back to 2nd-and-9. Facing 3rd-and-7 after Lemon got lit up on a short catch in the flat, McKee hit DeVonta Smith over the middle for a first down into plus territory! Is this allowed? McKee threw a pass to Darius Cooper that was actually incomplete but the offense was able to get a snap off fast before a challenge! And it was a run for a first down! Good job. Goedert drew a pass interference penalty with the Panthers’ defensive back pulling his pants down to pick up 22…

full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 28: Carson Steele #34 of the Philadelphia Eagles walks off of the field during an NFL preseason game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field on August 28, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles running back depth is already thin, to but it lightly, but things appeared to get worse in the first quarter on Sunday against the Panthers. Carson Steele nabbed a short pass by Tanner McKee, was pushed out of bounds, and was injured on the play. After a short evaluation in the medical tent, Steele headed to the locker room, and was later ruled questionable to return due to a shoulder injury. Steele did return to the sideline with his helmet, and later in the second quarter was able to get back on the field with the special teams unit. It didn’t last long, however, and after helping with kickoff duties, he was back in the medical tent and was eventually ruled out. Steele has been downgraded to out. https://t.co/2vB8oKPXuf — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) October 18, 2026 The RB was signed to the active roster just over a week ago, and played in London against the Jaguars, although all of his snaps came on special teams. Steele was getting some offensive opportunities early in Week 6 against the Panthers, and was targeted twice, hauling in one catch for four yards — the play on which he was injured. The Eagles running back room is already without Saquon Barkley due to injury, and both Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley were put on IR, leaving Dameon Pierce as the starting RB, Steele, and then Jaydon Blue, as the only other active rushers.

full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Drew Kendall #66 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the national anthem prior to an NFL preseason football game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced the inactives list for their Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers. The following Eagles players WILL NOT PLAY: Saquon Barkley, Jalyx Hunt, Michael Carter II, A.J. Epenesa, Hollywood Brown, and Joe Milton III. Drew Kendall is notably active after being questionable to play. But pregame warmups indicate that he might be available on an emergency basis after only being limited in practice. Jake Majors could start at center for the second week in a row. Barkley was ruled out on Friday’s final injury report. With Barkley out and both Tank Bigsby/Will Shipley on injured reserve, the Eagles are without their top three running backs. Their active RBs in this game: Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele, and Jaydon Blue. All three of those players began the season on the practice squad. Blue, a former Dallas Cowboys draft pick, is active for the first time in his Eagles career. Pierce figures to get the bulk of carries with Steele behind him as RB2. Blue will likely have a small role, if one at all. Hunt and Epenesa being out means the Eagles have four active edge rushers: Jonathan Greenard, Nolan Smith, Arnold Ebiketie, and Keyshawn James-Newby. KJN is making his NFL regular season debut after being temporarily elevated from the practice squad. title: 5 takeaways from the Steelers’ OT win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers
summary: After a slow first half, the Steelers mounted a comeback on the road to defeat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in overtime. Pittsburgh advances to 4-2 on the season. As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had. 1. Receivers step up in time It was no secret that the Steelers were low on wide […]
full_text: Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images | Getty Images After a slow first half, the Steelers mounted a comeback on the road to defeat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in overtime. Pittsburgh advances to 4-2 on the season. As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had. 1. Receivers step up in time It was no secret that the Steelers were low on wide receivers entering their Week 6 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson are on injured reserve. Ben Skowronek was out. Even DK Metcalf had been dealing with an illness earlier in the week. And early on against Tampa Bay, those wide receiver issues were painfully obvious. The passing offense was anemic, and quarterback Aaron Rodgers did not look confident when scanning his options downfield. Rookie Germie Bernard, now that team’s clear WR2, even moved backwards at one point after converting a fourth-down conversion to unintentionally give the Buccaneers the ball back on a turnover on downs. And beyond Metcalf and Bernard, not a single other Steelers receiver logged a catch — or even a target — in over four quarters of play. Some of that was the game plan, of course, but even that spoke to a lack of confidence in the group’s depth. However, both Metcalf and Bernard rose to the occasion in the second half, with each receiver finishing the game with a whopping 11 catches. Metcalf went for 93 yards while the rookie logged 87 and a score, reaching the ball into the end zone on what would be the game-winning touchdown in overtime. And the play only succeeded because of a blocking effort from Metcalf. Germie Bernard's FIRST career touchdown gives Pittsburgh the lead in overtime 👏 pic.twitter.com/o9aIhjS7ma — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 18, 2026 While he’s still had some young-player mistakes, and the broken tackles haven’t come as easy against pro competition, Bernard has largely looked like the same possession and yards-after-catch receiver that he was in college. Despite Rodgers famously taking a while to warm up to rookie pass catchers, Bernard looked like a safety blanket against the Buccaneers — and although injuries ahead of him certainly played a role in his ascension up the depth chart, Bernard’s ability and highly-touted football IQ surely played a part as well. Meanwhile, Metcalf needed to look like a WR1 on Sunday with so many of his teammates missing the game. It took him a while to get going, but he also provided a steady presence on offense, and despite not connecting with Rodgers deep, Metcalf did record five first downs in a game where they were at a premium for the Pittsburgh offense. Metcalf hasn’t looked like a star this season, but he’s now recorded 90-plus yards in two of the Steelers’ last three games. He may not be a superstar, but he has certainly rebounded from a dismal start to the season. 2. Jamel Dean has a great revenge game The Steelers secondary certainly had its issues on Sunday, with lapses in coverage contributing to the Buccaneers finding nine first downs through the passing game. However, there was one name Pittsburgh never had to worry about in man or zone: cornerback Jamel Dean. Dean was still tested plenty in coverage, but the Steelers’ newly-minted CB1 logged a whopping six passes defensed against Tampa Bay. He also capitalized on a poor throw from Tampa Bay’s Jalon Daniels to set up a much-needed late-game score for the Steelers. #Steelers CB Jamel Dean just did what DaRon Bland couldn't last week vs. the Bucs: pic.twitter.com/8YGUEi3z1a — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 18, 2026 Dean was everywhere on the field on Sunday despite being questionable ahead of the game with an ankle issue. Playing against his former team — Dean spent the first seven years of his career in Tampa Bay — the veteran corner was clearly playing with something to prove. He also had to step up for the Steelers, a team still somewhat shorthanded at defensive back following the Joey Porter Jr. trade. A free agent signing this offseason by Pittsburgh, Dean flew somewhat under the radar due to joining a Pittsburgh secondary with bigger names such as Porter and Jalen Ramsey. But he was widely considered one of, if not the best, corner on the market in 2026, and would’ve been in the running for the CB1 spot on a number of teams. Jamel Dean in coverage in 2025 (DB ranks), per @NextGenStats : ▫️41.7 completion pct allowed (1st) ▫️4.7 yards/target allowed (1st) ▫️41.3 passer rating allowed (1st) ▫️-11.9 comp pct over expected (1st) > Minimum 60 targets https://t.co/1P7e2hglOI — NFL Researcher (@NFL_Researcher) March 9, 2026 If Dean can stay healthy, he’ll have a chance to shine in Pittsburgh this season — and the team certainly needs him to rise to the occasion. 3. The Steelers offense still needs an identity In a win against the Colts last week, there was plenty of talk about the Steelers’ offense finally figuring things out. But against the Tampa Bay defense in Week 6, Pittsburgh showed it still has plenty of work to do. The late-game heroics of Aaron Rodgers and co. deserve plenty of praise. For as disappointing as the game began, it turned into a thrilling overtime battle with some fireworks on offense by the end. But let’s be honest — even though it ultimately worked out, a game that involves the 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers throwing the football 49 times is not ideal, especially when his yards per attempt were a mere 5.2. A symptom of that overreliance on the passing game was Rodgers taking five sacks — a number that could’ve been much higher if the veteran quarterback hadn’t shown off some surprising pocket mobility at a few key moments in the game. Even then, several of the sacks Rodgers took were costly. Meanwhile, despite the run game averaging a healthy four yards per carry, Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle combined for just 21 carries. And the team’s highly-touted tight end duo (although Pat Freiermuth was banged up) combined for just 36 yards and a touchdown on six catches. As I’ve written a few times this year, the 2026 Steelers offense has looked like Pittsburgh’s late-career Ben Roethlisberger offenses at times, with an aging, future Hall of Fame passer intermittently coming alive to will an otherwise dead passing attack to late-game success. It’s fun to watch. In many cases, it results in a win. But Steelers fans should know by this point that similarly unsustainable offensive production rarely results in long-term — or postseason — success. 4. The Steelers won despite themselves There were a lot of positives to take away from the Steelers’ win. But it’s hard to ignore a truly ugly first-half performance even if it all worked out in the end. Tampa Bay wasn’t exactly a formidable opponent, either. Were the Buccaneers better than their 1-4 record entering the game? Probably. But you’d hope that a playoff-hopeful team like the Steelers wouldn’t suffer as many cold spells as they did against the team at the bottom of the NFC South standings, starting an undrafted rookie at quarterback and generally lacking star talent. And even when Pittsburgh’s offense and defense did start clicking, the team’s overall decision-making kept getting in the way. Once again, the team consistently struggled to get offensive plays set up on time, with a lack of timeouts unnecessarily complicating a two-minute drill at the end of the first half. Then, Pittsburgh nearly mismanaged the end of the game, with the Steelers throwing the ball twice while near the goal line in the final two minutes of regulation with the score tied. Both passes were incompletions, letting Tampa Bay hold onto two timeouts with plenty of time left on the clock the ensuing overtime-forcing drive from the Buccaneers. That eventual game-tying field goal from Tampa Bay was also handled poorly, with Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy calling a timeout while the Buccaneers’ special teams unit was rushing onto the field with a running clock, slowing things down for the opposition. And if McCarthy had wanted to…

full_text: (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers overcame a 16-3 fourth-quarter deficit to defeat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and get to 4-2 on the season. They now sit atop the division with the Cleveland Browns and Baltimore Ravens, both of whom are also 4-2 on the year after Cleveland defeated Baltimore. The Steelers wouldn’t have been able to complete their comeback, though, had it not been for the Herculean effort of rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard. The second-round pick hauled in 11 receptions for 87 yards and the game-winning touchdown in overtime, which was the first of his career. His 11 receptions are a Steelers single-game record for rookie receivers. In his last two games combined, Bernard has 17 receptions for 171 yards. Bernard has been exactly what Pittsburgh was hoping he’d be when they traded up to draft him back in April. His 24 receptions are second only to Metcalf on the team, and his target success rate of 53.1 percent leads all Steelers wide receivers, per Sumer Sports . title: Steelers stock report after Week 6 win over Buccaneers
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers moved to 4-2 with a thrilling overtime win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6. After a sluggish start, Pittsburgh came through in crunch time with several timely turnovers and a rookie receiver’s breakout performance. As always, here is my weekly stock report from the Steelers’ first road victory of 2026. […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Morgan Tencza-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Pittsburgh Steelers moved to 4-2 with a thrilling overtime win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6. After a sluggish start, Pittsburgh came through in crunch time with several timely turnovers and a rookie receiver’s breakout performance. As always, here is my weekly stock report from the Steelers’ first road victory of 2026. Stock Up CB Jamel Dean Revenge does not get much sweeter than that. Dean came into the game banged up and left early in the contest for a drive, nursing his injury. The veteran corner ended up making the play of the day with a huge interception late in the first quarter that allowed the Steelers to take the lead late in the fourth quarter. The Steelers secondary looked much better when Dean was on the field compared to last week. WRs DK Metcalf & Germie Bernard Pittsburgh came into this contest with Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson, and Ben Skowronek. Calling their receiver room thin today would be putting it nicely. However, both DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard stepped up hugely for the Steelers. Metcalf posted 11 receptions for 93 yards, coming up with a huge third-down conversion in overtime. Bernard’s first career touchdown came in overtime. It was his eleventh reception of the game. The rookie has emerged as a serious piece of the Steelers’ passing attack over the last few weeks, proving he is capable of handling a large volume of targets. EDGE Nick Herbig The Steelers edge rusher came into the contest with zero sacks through the team’s first five games. Herbig responded in a big way with two huge sacks in the contest. He was the Steelers’ most effective edge rusher in this contest. Anyone questioning the contract extension that Herbig received should be silenced after this performance. DB Jalen Ramsey The defensive back continues to play through a broken wrist. I mention that because you would not know anything is wrong with him based on the way he has been playing. Ramsey recorded two sacks today, as he was flying around the field all game long. The veteran continues to be a key piece of the Steelers’ defense. Stock Down Head coach Mike McCarthy Not only did Mike McCarthy appear to sprain his ankle at the end of the first half, but there was also some curious late-game decision-making by McCarthy in this one. With the ball inside the five and Tampa Bay possessing two timeouts, the Steelers opted to throw the ball twice. This allowed Tampa Bay to keep one of their timeouts. Then, McCarthy opted to call a timeout with Tampa Bay running their field goal unit out onto the field. The timeout allowed Tampa Bay to properly set up their field goal unit and send the game to overtime. The Steelers won this game, so this is small potatoes at the end of the day. But I left with some questions about the way McCarthy elected to play the end of the game out. Offensive Consistency/Play-calling The Steelers’ offense looked sluggish for much of the first three quarters. Rodgers and the offense often passed from empty sets, a bit different from their usual under center and play action based passing offense we had become accustomed to seeing this season. The Steelers offense got it going from under center in the second half, and that small switch ended up being enough to help move Pittsburgh to 4-2 overall. K Chris Boswell’s Consistency Listen, it’s perfectly reasonable to talk about it. Boswell missed his fourth field goal of the season, this one from 48 yards out, in Week 6. There is some discourse online as to whether or not the laces were in the right place when Boswell kicked, but four misses this early in the year is notable. The kicker then got back on track as the game went on, nailing four consecutive field goals that proved to be crucial in seeing the game to overtime and eventually giving the Steelers the win. Boswell is not close to being replaced, but there is a conversation to be had about how much Boswell has missed this early in the season. Special Teams I actually came away from this one feeling pretty good about Kaden Wetjen. The rookie had several nice returns in the first half, both of which were called back for holding penalties. The Steelers special teams issues are becoming more noticeable each game it seems like. You can’t expect Wetjen to get any kind of positive momentum going if his returns are going to be called back because of his teammates. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers overcome 16-3 deficit, defeat Buccaneers in OT
summary: In what is now the franchise’s largest fourth-quarter comeback since 1992, the Pittsburgh Steelers overcame a 16-3 deficit in the final 15 minutes to defeat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime, giving them a 4-2 record and their first win streak of the season. After scoring 30 points in two of their last three […]
full_text: (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images In what is now the franchise’s largest fourth-quarter comeback since 1992, the Pittsburgh Steelers overcame a 16-3 deficit in the final 15 minutes to defeat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime, giving them a 4-2 record and their first win streak of the season. After scoring 30 points in two of their last three contests and showcasing a consistent ability to move the ball, Pittsburgh’s offense was nonexistent through three quarters. Pittsburgh had five three-and-outs and were 5-of-15 on third downs while being limited to just three first half points. However, the offense found life in the fourth quarter. Trailing 16-3, Aaron Rodgers and Germie Bernard led Pittsburgh down the field on an eight-play drive that ended with a Darnell Washington touchdown. Daylen Everette then picked off Jalon Daniels, which led to a Chris Boswell field goal after an eight-play drive that only accumulated 24 yards for Pittsburgh. The Steelers forced a Buccaneers three-and-out which led to a Boswell 58-yard boot to tie the game. Then, Pittsburgh’s defense seemed to potentially seal the game. Jamel Dean picked off Daniels and was shoved out of bounds inside the five yard-line. The Steelers, though, couldn’t punch the ball in the end zone. Rodgers tired to find Washington, but the pass was broken up. A stuffed Jaylen Warren run and an incomplete jump ball to DK Metcalf brought out Boswell for his fourth made field goal of the day. That left over a minute on the clock, though, for the Buccaneers, and Jalon Daniels was able to get enough yards to bring on Chase McLaughlin for his fourth field goal to tie the game at 19 and send it into overtime. The Steelers lost the toss and the Bucs deferred, but Pittsburgh would take full advantage of having the ball first. Rodgers led the offense on a 12-play drive that featured a 3rd-and-13 conversion on a completion to DK Metcalf, who had 11 catches on the day. The drive would culminate with Bernard reaching the end zone for his first career touchdown to put Pittsburgh on top 26-19. After one fourth-down conversion on the Bucs’ ensuing drive, Tampa Bay faced 4th-and-8. Patrick Graham dialed up a Jalen Ramsey nickel blitz, which worked all the way back in the fourth quarter, and it worked again. Ramsey came off the edge untouched and recorded his second sack of the game to seal the win for Pittsburgh. After failing to score a touchdown in the first three quarters, the Steelers scored every time they touched the ball in the fourth quarter and overtime, save for the kneel-down to end regulation. In the process of the comeback, the Steelers may have found their permanent one-two duo at receiver going forward. Both DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard hauled in 11 receptions – the rest of the Steelers’ offense combined for 11 receptions. Rodgers finished the day 33-of-49 for 253 yards and two scores, as well as a first quarter interception. The Steelers will now take their 4-2 record to Paris in Week 7 where they will take on the New Orleans Saints, who recorded their second win of the year by defeating the New York Giants. full_text: (Photo by George Gojkovich/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are dealing with a long list of injuries at the wide receiver position. Michael Pittman and Roman Wilson are both on IR, and Ben Skowronek won’t play in Week 6 due to a leg injury. That leaves Pittsburgh with just three healthy receivers who made the 53-man roster. They called up both Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson from the practice squad for their matchup with the Buccaneers, but the lack of depth could come back to haunt them over the next month. Many believe that the Steelers will be hitting the trade market to try and land another receiver. NFL insider Tom Pelissero reports that Pittsburgh has been calling about potential moves. “I do know the Steelers have been calling around on veteran receivers since the injuries last week and I’d imagine that continues with the two WR now onIR,” Pelissero writes . He also adds that Jalen Tolbert and KaVontae Turpin are the two names with the most connections to Mike McCarthy, as both played under the Steelers’ head coach in Dallas. The Steelers have been one of the most active teams when it comes to wide receiver trades over the last handful of years, trading away/for the likes of Diontae Johnson, Mike Williams, George Pickens, DK Metcalf, and Michael Pittman. title: Steelers vs. Buccaneers: Week 6 game picks
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are hoping to win consecutive games for the first time this season, as they travel down to Tampa to take on the Buccaneers. The Bucs will be starting undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels at quarterback for the third consecutive game, as Baker Mayfield continues recovering from a thumb injury. Will Pittsburgh be able […]
full_text: (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are hoping to win consecutive games for the first time this season, as they travel down to Tampa to take on the Buccaneers. The Bucs will be starting undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels at quarterback for the third consecutive game, as Baker Mayfield continues recovering from a thumb injury. Will Pittsburgh be able to get to 4-2? Our staff weighs in with our picks. Austin Bechtold : This is the most confident I am in a possible Steelers win since Atlanta. Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers have the offense clicking. Jaylen Warren is playing like an Offensive Player of the Year candidate. He also is the only player in football to lead his team in both rushing and receiving. If Baker Mayfield was playing, this would be a much closer game. Jalon Daniels hasn’t thrown for over 200 yards in his two starts and I’m surprised that Emeka Egbuka hasn’t taken the next step yet. The Steelers defense needs Nick Herbig and Keanu Benton to step up for a pass rush that only has 11 sacks. The ingredients are there for the better team and roster to win on a beautiful 80 degree day in Tampa Bay. Steelers 28, Buccaneers 17 . Ryan Parish : On paper: the Buccaneers are good at stopping the run, but run a ton of Cover-3 that is susceptible to the passing concepts Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy like to call. On offense, Tampa Bay is once again turning to UDFA rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels. You know the drill. This is a game the Steelers have no business losing. Cue the Yinzer panic in the bleachers. The Steelers continue to win when I pick them to lose, so like any honorable fan, I will not be abandoning the bit now. Buccaneers 27, Steelers 24. Joey Bray: For as beat up as the Steelers wide receiver room is heading into this game, it certainly seems like the Tampa Bay secondary is just as hurt. Star safety Antoine Winfield Jr. has been ruled out, and young corner Benjamin Morrison is listed as doubtful.The Steelers defense should have little to no troubles with rookie undrafted free agent quarterback Jalon Daniels. Despite his strong performance against Dallas a week ago, the Steelers defense should be able to get home and make things uncomfortable for the young QB.I think the Steelers are clearly the better team than Tampa Bay at this point in the season. I’ll take Pittsburgh to move to 4-2 in resounding fashion on the road. Steelers 28, Buccaneers 10 . Ryland Bickley : The Steelers are banged up heading into this one and Tampa Bay’s roster is stronger than the Bucs’ 1-4 record might lead some to believe. Led by Vita Vea, Tampa’s second-ranked run defense will make it tough for the Steelers to get Jaylen Warren going, and Pittsburgh’s wide receiver injuries mean the passing game might not be able to compensate.Still, Tampa Bay is starting a UDFA quarterback in Jalon Daniels who is still inexperienced, but now has some meaningful tape out for opponents to study. And while the Steelers secondary has been shorthanded this season, the Bucs don’t have a threatening WR1. I think Pittsburgh gets it done in a close game. Steelers 20, Buccaneers 17. Jason Aponte : The receiver injuries are a concern moving forward, but expect the Steelers to lean into heavier personnel packages. Big games for Pat Friermuth and Jaylen Warren. The Steelers defense will make it difficult for Jalon Daniels. Steelers 27, Buccaneers 17. Jarrett Bailey: The Steelers should win, even with their long list of offensive injuries. That said, I don’t expect it to be a blowout of any sort. Tampa’s defense has been very good, ranking fourth in EPA per play. Pittsburgh will win, but it will be closer than anyone would look. Steelers 23, Buccaneers 16. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! title: 49ers News: Mondays aren’t so bad when they’re GAME DAYS
summary: Jayden Daniels doesn’t scare me. Sonny Styles doesn’t scare me. Terry and Stefon don’t scare me. Only the football gods of chaos and variance scare me. There’s too many good matchups to exploit… from putting CMC in the pass game, to spamming Mike Evans against the hapless Commanders secondary, to blasting the Commanders’ shoddy offensive […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - DECEMBER 30: Offensive coordinator Kyle Shanahan of the Washington Redskins looks on prior to the start of their game against the Dallas Cowboys at FedExField on December 30, 2012 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jayden Daniels doesn’t scare me. Sonny Styles doesn’t scare me. Terry and Stefon don’t scare me. Only the football gods of chaos and variance scare me. There’s too many good matchups to exploit… from putting CMC in the pass game, to spamming Mike Evans against the hapless Commanders secondary, to blasting the Commanders’ shoddy offensive line… the 49ers’ biggest opponent is themselves tonight. Let’s get it! Serial spitter? 49ers’ Kyle Juszczyk says C.J. Gardner-Johnson spit on him in 2025 (paywall) “Juszczyk called out Gardner-Johnson presumably because he’s among a group of players who have had enough: Gardner-Johnson was named the league’s most annoying player in the Athletic’s anonymous player poll in 2024. His ejection Sunday was the second of his career. He’s committed seven unnecessary roughness penalties and had three unsportsmanlike conduct infractions.” From Joe Montana to Joe Williams, Peter King had a front-row seat to 49ers history (paywall) “[Joe]Williams had off-the-field issues that Lynch viewed as disqualifying, most notably “retiring” during his final college season before later returning. Lynch thought Williams quit on his team. Shanahan viewed him as an ideal offensive fit. “Kyle loved him,” King recalled. “And he said to John Lynch, ‘I would love to get this guy tomorrow. Would you please just think about this?’” Lynch didn’t just give his blessing. He traded up 22 spots to ensure Shanahan got his guy in the fourth round. [Joe] Williams, of course, was a spectacular bust who never played a regular-season snap in the NFL. Why did King, 69, recently recall this nearly decade-old memory? It had nothing to do with Williams not working out. It was about what King thought the pick said about how Shanahan and Lynch, then both rookies in their roles, would be able to work together after inheriting a 2-14 team. “I left that draft thinking, ‘I don’t know if the guys they picked are going to be any good,’” King said. “But I really liked the chemistry I saw…..” …..Before Walsh announced his retirement, emotionally spent after 10 seasons at the helm, he met at midfield with Cincinnati head coach Sam Wyche, a former assistant, and collapsed into his arms. “I was outside one of the locker rooms watching that moment on TV, and it looked like Sam Wyche was almost carrying Bill Walsh off the field,” King said. “It was like Walsh was totally devoid of energy.” Young was also out of gas, severely dehydrated, after leading the 49ers to their fifth and last title in January 1995 by throwing a Super Bowl-record six touchdown passes in a 49-26 win over the San Diego Chargers. But his response was the opposite of Walsh. Back at Young’s room at the Miami Airport Marriott, where a large group of friends and family members had joined him, King observed as the game MVP was stretched out with IVs in both arms and EMTs standing on each side of his king bed. Despite his condition, Young was almost overcome with joy. “Is this great or what?” Young said. “I mean, I haven’t thrown six touchdown passes in a game in my life. Then I throw six in the Super Bowl!” In his 2024 farewell column, King called this scene his favorite moment from his 40-year career.” 49ers safety Malik Mustapha still playing with chip on his shoulder “Credit to Raheem and my DB coach, Jerry Gray,” Mustapha said. “They actually made a pretty interesting comment because they know how downhill and aggressive I am in the run game. But then being able to shift your mind in the pass game and being able to play with that same tenacity, but being able to read the quarterback and being able to still fly around and make plays on the ball as well.”

The Green Bay Packers enter this game sixth overall in total EPA defensively. But they are 18th overall in success rate. The […]
full_text: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2-3 Dallas Cowboys are taking on the 3-2 Green Bay Packers. Dallas has a +2-point differential, despite the losing record, while the Packers boast a -8 point differential, despite the winning record. The Green Bay Packers enter this game sixth overall in total EPA defensively. But they are 18th overall in success rate. The offenses they’ve faced have been underwhelming: The Vikings, Jets, and the Falcons/Bucs/Bears without their starting quarterback. The Cowboys offense has faced the Giants, Commanders, Ravens, Texans, and Bucs. They are still in the top seven in both EPA and success rate. I think Dak Prescott has a field day and the Cowboys bounce back at Lambeau Field after an embarrassing loss to a rookie quarterback a week ago. Plus, there should be a bit of a comedown from the Packers after taking it out on their rivals last week. Dallas is dreadful defensively. They are by far the worst defense in the league from a total EPA perspective, and have also allowed a league-high 50% success rate. Jordan Love should connect on plenty of his patented fadeaway throws to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Cowboys 38, Packers 34.

title: Buccaneers Week 6 Top Performers vs. Pittsburgh Steelers
summary: Welp, that was something. Carrying a tw0-score lead through three quarters, the Buccaneers imploded in all phases and got outscored by geriatric Aaron Rodgers and his only two functioning receivers to the tune of 23-3 across the fourth quarter and overtime. The result? An embarrassing 26-19 loss to mark yet another failing in one-score affairs. […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 18: Rueben Bain Jr. #3 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers sacks Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welp, that was something. Carrying a tw0-score lead through three quarters, the Buccaneers imploded in all phases and got outscored by geriatric Aaron Rodgers and his only two functioning receivers to the tune of 23-3 across the fourth quarter and overtime. The result? An embarrassing 26-19 loss to mark yet another failing in one-score affairs. Baker Mayfield will be back next week, though at 1-5 it doesn’t really seem like that will matter at all. The defense plays really well until it actually matters, so I guess Todd Bowles can hang his hat on something even as his house slowly goes further up in flames. Time for some shoutouts and then some dinner. Offensive Top Performer: No One You can’t give anyone real credit when the offense not only goes completely dormant in the most important frame of the game but actively works against Tampa’s chances. Jalon Daniels, as previously stated, is a very likable person who plays hard and has shown some good tape. But sadly, he’s still an undrafted rookie playing in a poor offensive system, and that was made readily apparent with all the sacks he took, late decisions he made, and backbreaking interceptions he threw (Jamel Dean, how could you do this to us?). It’s unclear what a recovered Baker Mayfield will do for this team when he comes back next week, but he certainly doesn’t need to worry about his long-term security after Daniels’s performance Sunday. Not much else to really highlight here. Emeka Egbuka looked fine enough but still missed on some major plays when the team needed him. Don’t think his busted coverage TD really makes up for that in the long run. Chris Godwin logged a couple uncharacteristic drops, Bucky Irving couldn’t replicate his dominant Week 5 performance. Zac Robinson continues to show he has an extremely limited feel for creating a consistent, easy-to-operate game plan, and it continues to hurt the team. Defensive Top Performer: EDGE David Walker The defense, and the pass rush in particular, played extremely well through three quarters. They forced 5 Steelers 3-and-outs and held them to 3 points. Then Aaron Rodgers started spamming the quick game and the seams like most modern offenses do to this defense and it went downhill fast. This how Bowles chooses to live and die with his defense, and it’s finally run its course in this league. Even when you get tremendous individual efforts like Sunday, most times it’s not enough. David Walker continued his ascension, logging two high-quality pass-rush wins to notch 2 sacks (as well as 5 tackles) and extend his team lead to 4 sacks overall despite playing a fraction of the snap as other outside linebackers. He feels like the real deal. 4️⃣ sacks on the season for David Walker 👏 📺: #PITvsTB on CBS pic.twitter.com/GC9vGuoxQx — Tampa Bay Buccaneers (@Buccaneers) October 18, 2026 The pass rush overall got to Rodgers 5 times, one of which being rookie Rueben Bain Jr. The highly touted draft pick finally looks healthy after dealing with nagging shoulder and groin ailments, as he flashed on some nice reps last week and produced a high-quality win for his first career sack this week. He also recorded a pass deflection that led to A’shawn Robinson’s second (!!) interception. Keionte Scott, another rookie, continued his proficient pass-rushing start with his first career sack. The opportunities aren’t always going to be there, again because of Bowles chooses to play defense, but it’s clear there is talent in this edge room. First-career sack for @ruebenbainjr 😡 📺: #PITvsTB on CBS pic.twitter.com/Q2Hta1d6FN — Tampa Bay Buccaneers (@Buccaneers) October 18, 2026 Special Teams Top Performer: Chase McLaughlin McLaughlin continued to show why he needs his big-time extension and why it should’ve happened months ago. He remained perfect on the year with four makes, including a 53-yard launch that tied the game and forced overtime. He’s now top 10 in NFL history in 50-plus-yard makes and remains one of the most accurate kickers in NFL history to boot.
author: Mike Kiwak

title: Week 6 Game Recap: Buccaneers blow huge lead and fall in overtime, when is enough enough?
summary: First Quarter: With a new, freshly minted victory under their belts, Tez Johnson touched the ball first for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Run, run, sack, punt— Pittsburgh ball. Run, run, incomplete pass, punt— Bucs’ ball. Fans would see another Bucs’ punt before finally jumping out their seats when Rueben Bain Jr., tipped an Aaron Rodgers […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 18: Jalen Ramsey #5 of the Pittsburgh Steelers sacks Jalon Daniels #10 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images First Quarter: With a new, freshly minted victory under their belts, Tez Johnson touched the ball first for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Run, run, sack, punt— Pittsburgh ball. Run, run, incomplete pass, punt— Bucs’ ball. Fans would see another Bucs’ punt before finally jumping out their seats when Rueben Bain Jr., tipped an Aaron Rodgers pass which bounced into the hands of A’Shawn Robinson for his team-leading second interception of the season. The Bucs’ offense would convert Rueben Bain Jr.’s first impact play as a Buc into points with a Chase McLaughlin field goal. Chase’s kick, blocked at the line, still had enough oomph to scoot across the crossbar for Tampa’s first lead of the game. 3-0, Bucs. Trailing by three, the Steelers’ special team struck a big blow against their former coordinator, a kick return that made it was across midfield and into the lap of Chase McLaughlin before finally being shut down by hustling Tampa defenders. That same special teams unit un-struck their big blow, as the big return was flagged and brought back— Illegal blindside block Cole Holcomb. Aaron Rodgers and co. did earn those surrendered yards back, but their drive would ultimately lead to a Mike McCarthy decision— A fourth down with three yards to go. Despite completing a pass beyond the sticks, the Steelers lost the necessary yardage when Germie Bernard reversed course, try to double back across the field, and got tackled behind the line to gain for a crushing turnover on downs. Second Quarter: Tampa Bay’s ensuing drive featured a first for the 2026 Buccaneers and Jalon Daniels— Up tempo. The Buccaneers not only trusted their rookie passer to call the offense at the line, they trusted him to pass . Daniels, without the consistent aid of a Bucky Irving first down, run took his team down the field with passes to Chris Godwin and Emeka Egbuka— Ted Hurst III even found reps as the rookie collected a chain-moving reception, but it was also a down field pass to Hurst III that drew a pass interference and placed the ball on the Pittsburgh one-yard line. Wasting no time, Daniels dropped back and tossed his first touchdown of the day— Emeka Egbuka’s first since week two. 10-0, Buccaneers. With under five minutes remaining in half, the Jalon Daniels-Emeka Egbuka connection had a chance at their second score of the day— The duo missed. Emeka Egbuka, running wide open was slightly overthrown, forcing an attempt at a one-handed snag. The incomplete pass would lead the Bucs to Chase McLaughlin and three points. 13-0, Tampa Bay. Aaron Rodgers would be introduced to a couple of Bucs’ rookies on the next drive. Up first, Keonte Scott a slot blitz Rodgers never saw and a sack. The third down that would follow would be another introduction and a moment that many Buccaneers’ fans have been waiting for a Rueben Bain Jr. sack, the first of his career. Bain Jr.’s first career sack comes on third down against future Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers. Congratulations To Bain Jr. and the Bucs’ defense for a near flawless performance in the first half of Sunday’s matchup. The lone flaw came in the half’s final drive. Needing points, momentum, or just a sign of life before the intermission, the Pittsburgh were able to drive into field goal range, spike the ball and give Chris Boswell the opportunity to atone for earlier miss— Miss atoned for 13-3, Buccaneers. Third Quarter: In a strange sequence, Mike McCarthy sustained an injury walking off the field and spent halftime in the blue tent so the Pittsburgh Steelers never met with their head coach during the break. Whether that was impactful or not is immeasurable, however, the Steelers looked flat as their offense debuted in the third quarter with a three and out. Their defense wasn’t necessarily around to bail them out— A 9-minute drive deep into Pittsburgh territory before Tampa had to settle for a field goal. 16-3, Buccaneers. The Steelers and Bucs would each trot out their punt teams again on the following drives, before Aaron Rodgers was back under center for the final two minutes of the third quarter. Germie Bernard’s eighth catch of the day moved Pittsburgh to the Tampa Bay 40-yard line. David Walker tried stall the attack with a sack of Aaron Rodgers, but it wasn’t enough— Third down and 16, Aaron Rodgers found DK Metcalf for 16 yards and a first down. Fourth Quarter: That conversion got the wick lit, a roughing passer penalty would follow shortly after and a brief time later the Bucs’ defense would allow their first touchdown of the game. A wide open Darnell Washington brought the Steelers within one score. 16-10, Tampa Bay. Jalon Daniels first drive of the fourth quarter was not what his team needed. Daniels, hoping his receiver could make a play, threw a ball to Emeka Egbuka in heavy coverage— Interception. Sunday’s fourth quarter saw the end of a 10-straight completion streak for Aaron Rodgers. On what was his 16th consecutive pass, Rodgers had his team in field goal position and Tampa’s turnover quickly led to points as Chris Boswell delivered. 16-13, Tampa. Back-to-back Emeka Egbuka drops handed Aaron Rodgers the ball back. DK Metcalf (and a questionable pass interference penalty) gave the Steelers another field goal and another three points. 16-16, tie. The 16-16 tie wouldn’t last long because on Tampa’s next drive Jalon Daniels looked much more like a rookie than what he has so far this season. Daniel’s found Jamel Dean— who was a Buc, but is now a Steeler— for what could and arguably should have lost Tampa Bay the game. Jamel Dean left his offense at the three yard line. Tampa Bay’s defense defended those three yards like their season was on the line. The Steelers opted for just one run play and two incomplete passes, taking no time off the clock and leaving Jalon Daniels with one shot to rally. Jalon Daniels was given an inch and he took a mile. Coming off of his one of his worst throws as a Buccaneer, Daniels responded. The rookie took his team down the field and gave his kicker (The best player on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers roster) a chance to tie. 19-19, welcome to overtime. Overtime: The Buccaneers won the toss and elected to kick. They also elected to revert back to missed tackles as the focal point of their defense. A good performance until the final 15 minutes of regulation turned horrid by end of overtime. Todd Bowles’ defense finished caving on the Steelers’ final drive of the day. Pittsburgh delivered one body shot after another to Bowles’ unit as the Bucs were backed up, backed up, and backed up further until they dam broke— Touchdown Steelers- 26-19, Pittsburgh. Jalon Daniels did give Tampa Bay a small sliver of hope before the Steelers ended Tampa’s day and possibly their season— Bucs drop 1-5.

title: Five Washington Commanders players key to beating San Francisco 49ers
summary: The Commanders have emerged from the New York Giants mess intact. The fallout from the end-of-game blunder that allowed the clock to run out within field-goal range and result in a shocking 27-27 tie was massive on a local and national level.   Washington was the league-wide talking point for all the wrong reasons, as […]
full_text: The Commanders have emerged from the New York Giants mess intact. The fallout from the end-of-game blunder that allowed the clock to run out within field-goal range and result in a shocking 27-27 tie was massive on a local and national level. Washington was the league-wide talking point for all the wrong reasons, as headlines about clock management and Dan Quinn’s job status poured in from every corner. Then came the steady stream of accountability pressers, from Quinn to quarterback Jayden Daniels to offensive coordinator David Blough. Through all that time, the important indicators came from the locker room and Commanders practices. Washington’s roster had not lost faith despite being 1-3-1. Consider the fallout handled well by everyone involved. A triumphant rebound may be another matter. It’s not want-to that’s the problem. It’s the opponent. The Commanders traveled across the country to play the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Monday night. They’re 7.5-point underdogs , and appropriately so. There’s a talent disparity at play here that will be difficult to overcome, but not impossible. Washington needs a signature game from Jayden Daniels and vital, positive contributions from these five Commanders: WR Terry McLaurin This is a game where Washington’s stars must play like them. That’s why you’ll see so many big names in a list normally reserved for role players needing to step up and diamonds in the rough. If Stefon Diggs (questionable – hamstring) plays, the Commanders will have all their top pass catchers in a game for the first time since Week 1. That’s a huge asset to Daniels, who likes to spread the ball around. In big moments, though, he’ll turn to McLaurin. Terry’s got to be clutch and steadily productive in this game, showing doubters he can still p roduce at an elite level and in big moments. That’ll be important as the Commanders trying to match the 49ers and eventually beat them down the stretch. RB Rachaad White The Commanders will play Monday’s game without Bill Croskey-Merritt (groin) and his 57% running-back carry share . That leaves a committee including Austin Ekeler, Jeremy McNichols’ presumptive activation off injured reserve and Rachaad White. The former feature back has split time the past few seasons, but he’s capable of ramping up activity as a rusher on early downs, and the Commanders need efficient from the veteran in those instances. He’s also a capable receiver out of the backfield. Washington must put all of that to bear against San Francisco to get into third-and-managable situations that have largely eluded them to this point. S Nick Cross We’re taking a small leap here assuming that safety Nick Cross is going to play, considering he’s questionable on the Washington injury report. And it’s been previously said he needs medical clearance to play again after a Week 2 injury that required hospitalization . He hasn’t received it before, but that news came with the injury report . It didn’t in this case, and he traveled across the country. We’re placing a (safe) bet he’s available. That would be massive. No exaggeration. Cross is a dynamic playmaker in the box and, at times, playing deep. In my opinion, he allows Daronte Jones’ defense run as it should, bringing the intensity level up with a chess piece capable of moving anywhere on the board. We haven’t seen much of Cross to this point, with him out since Week 2. That glimpse offered a belief that he can be a game changer, and his presence will make this defense way better in all facets and help a secondary that’s (finally) starting to get healthy. EDGE Odafe Oweh K’Lavon Chassion is Washington’s top pass rusher this season by every metric . Odafe Oweh was paid to be that guy. While he’s off to a solid start , we’re at a point where Washington needs him to be special. 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is hard to bring down and San Francisco’s rushing scheme is excellent, but Oweh’s a freak athlete and driven competitor who needs to make plays. While sacks and force-fumbled and tackles for loss aren’t the only measure of a good edge rusher, Washington needs Oweh to stack those stats while fighting uphill battle to beat the 49ers. RT Josh Conerly Jr. Sonny Styles was nearly the selection here, to cap a theme that Washington needs its top talent going strong, especially a coverage eraser like Styles who’s also a thumper in the run game. Josh Conerly’s importance can’t be ignored, however, especially with his play on the ascent. While his pressure rate’s higher than you’d like, he hasn’t allowed a sack to this point. He has also stood out in the run game at times, and that must be galvanized in this game. We know guard Sam Cosmi’s a next-level and having a productive partnership with Conerly provides stability on one side at least, and allows OC David Blough to help Brandon Coleman more on the left. Protection and space in the run game is key. Having Conerly as an assertive piece of that puzzle is vital to consistent offensive success.

Four players are officially listed as out: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), Javontae Jean-Baptiste (pectoral), Marcus Mariota (knee) , and Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle). All four players missed practice all week. Nine additional players are also listed as questionable, including Stefon Diggs, Javon Kinlaw, and three safeties. Of the three safeties, Percy Butler (hamstring) and Tyler Owens (hamstring) missed Thursday’s practice but were upgraded to limited; Nick Cross (illness) was a full participant all three days but is still questionable. All three players missed last week’s game against New York . Quan Martin improved from limited on Thursday to full participation on Friday and Saturday, with no game designation. Stefon Diggs ‘ return is possible; he’s officially listed as questionable. He went from missing Thursday’s practice to limited on both Friday and Saturday. Terry McLaurin has no game designation after being limited Thursday and Saturday and sitting out Friday with a hamstring/rest designation. Treylon Burks was also limited all three days but has no game designation. Getting Diggs back would give Jayden Daniels another option in the passing game after playing without him against the Giants. The Commanders will also be without Croskey-Merritt in the backfield , but they should have options. Austin Ekeler was limited all week with a chest injury, while Rachaad White went from full participation Thursday to limited Friday and Saturday. Washington’s defensive front is another area to watch with Omenihu and Jean-Baptiste both out. Kinlaw fully participated Thursday, missed Friday’s practice, and returned Saturday on a limited basis. He’s questionable with ankle and knee injuries. K’Lavon Chaisson , meanwhile, returned to full participation Saturday after sitting out Friday and has no game designation. There are still a few roster decisions to make before Monday night. Trey Amos (ankle) and Jordan Magee (hamstring) are both questionable and, like McNichols , remain in their 21-day practice windows. The 2027 NFL draft is still months away, but with the 2026 season underway, we're starting to track pick order in Round 1. Which teams are in position to add elite prospects in the top 10 next April? What about the top five ... or even at No. 1?

 What follows is not the current draft order based on records. It is a projection of what ESPN's Football Power Index thinks the order ultimately will be by the end of the season. Each week during the season, the FPI projects the draft order by simulating the remainder of the season 10,000 times. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.
