title: NFL Week 6: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 6.
full_text:
The Sunday slate for Week 6 of the  2026 NFL season  kicked off in London with a thrilling matchup between the Texans and Jaguars. Wide receiver  Marvin Harrison Jr . made his much-anticipated Texans debut, but it was quarterback  C.J. Stroud who was the star as Houston held off Jacksonville.

 Back in the United States, the Ravens struggled in their second full game without QB  Lamar Jackson  this season, allowing the Browns to maintain first place in the AFC North. Elsewhere in that division, the Steelers needed an overtime period to defeat the Bucs. And the Eagles dropped their fourth straight game.

 In the late window Sunday, the Cardinals defeated the Rams on a time-expiring field goal despite not getting in the end zone once. The Chiefs stayed undefeated with a comfortable win over the winless Chargers. And the Bills came out on top of a shootout against the Raiders. The Packers ended the night with a convincing victory over the Cowboys.

 Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

 Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

 
 Jump to: 
 DAL-GB |  BUF-LV | LAC-KC 
 ARI-LAR  |  NO-NYG | PIT-TB 
  NYJ-NE  |  CAR-PHI |  CHI-ATL 
  TEN-IND  |  BAL-CLE |  HOU-JAX 

 Catch up on Thursday's game: 
 SEA-DEN 

 
 

 

 Green Bay 23, Dallas 13 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap  | Instant analysis 

 

 Packers 
 Are the Packers over their third-down struggles? Through five games, the Packers were the worst third-down team in the league, converting only 27.6% of them. All they needed was the Cowboys' shoddy defense to help change that. Dallas came in with the worst third-down defense in the league at 52.6%. On the opening drive, the Packers converted a third-and-5, two third-and-13s and a third-and-6 -- the last one a 9-yard touchdown catch by Matthew Golden . They went on to convert nine of their first 10 third downs to start the game. Their only failed conversion in the first half came on third-and-goal from the Cowboys' 2, forcing the Packers to settle for a field goal.

 Trend to watch: No one has more takeaways in the first half of games this season than the Packers. They ran their total to six thanks to interceptions by Evan Williams and Brandon Cisse . For Williams, it was his second interception of the season, while Cisse -- the Packers' top draft pick this year -- snagged his first career pick after receiver CeeDee Lamb slipped on the Lambeau Field turf. -- Rob Demovsky 

 Next game: vs. Lions (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

 

 
 

 Cowboys 
 Did the Cowboys' defense actually do some good things? Maybe it's too early to call it a trend, but the Cowboys had three sacks. It is the first time this season the Cowboys have recorded at least three sacks in a game and just the second time in their past 11 games. Maybe the mere presence of Micah Parsons on the other sideline inspired the Cowboys? Quinnen Williams had the first sack of Jordan Love , his second of the season. Elijah Garcia had the second, and former Packer Kenny Clark , part of the Parsons trade, recorded the third.

 Key stat to know: Dak Prescott was intercepted twice in the second half of the Cowboys' Week 5 loss to the Buccaneers. He opened the first half Sunday with two more interceptions. It was the first time Prescott had been intercepted twice in a first half since Week 17 of the 2022 season against the Giants. Of Prescott's last four interceptions, three weren't necessarily his fault. The Buccaneers' turnovers came off a teammate's hands and face mask. His second pick Sunday came after Lamb slipped on his cut. -- Todd Archer 

 Next game: vs. Eagles (Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

 
 

 Fantasy football takeaway:  Golden had a season-high 22.4 points Sunday against the Cowboys, catching six of team-high 13 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown. Golden has now scored 20 or more points in three of his last four games, and he looks like the guy I saw on his college tape at Texas. Golden is getting loose at every level of the field. With a positive Week 7 matchup versus the Lions' defense, Golden should be played as a high-end WR2. -- Bowen 

 

 

 Buffalo 33, Las Vegas 30 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap 

 

 Bills 
 Did the Bills' secondary finally make the play that turns things around? Even on a day when the Bills broke up 11 passes, the Raiders never feared throwing into the heart of Buffalo's defensive backfield. For the second straight week, the Bills rendered an opposing offense one-dimensional yet still allowed back-breaking scoring drives in the fourth quarter. But on a key third down late, rookie safety Jalon Kilgore broke up a crosser intended for receiver Tre Tucker , marking the first time the Bills' defense successfully got off the field in the fourth quarter or overtime in their past eight series. Of course, one series later, the Raiders gashed the Bills for a 44-yard touchdown, so maybe one play can't fix everything.

 Trend to watch: The Bills' offense was turnover free for the first time in a month, and running back James Cook III carried more than 20 times without fumbling. Over the past three weeks, the Bills had turned the ball over nine times; Cook alone had put the ball on the ground four times.

 Best quote from the locker room:   "I saw Josh flick the ball like it was NFL Street. What a guy. What a guy, bruh. I went over to Josh and I said 'I've been around you a while, bro, and I don't ever want to be like 'Oh my God Josh Allen you're the best!,' but you are him. You are Himothy.' We're seeing it in real time." -- Offensive tackle Dion Dawkins reacting after Allen's shovel pass TD.  -- Nick Suss 

 Next game: vs. Ravens (Nov. 1, 1 p.m. ET)

 
 

 Raiders 
 What should the Raiders do with RB Ashton Jeanty ? The alarm bells around Jeanty have gotten louder. On Sunday, he had 10 carries for 22 yards and a touchdown. He was held to under 3.0 yards per carry for the fourth time in six games. Granted, the Bills entered the game allowing 1.53 yards per first contact -- second best in the league. Still, Jeanty's rushing numbers this season have been subpar for a player taken inside the top 10 of last year's draft. At this point, the Raiders need to consider increasing Mike Washington Jr .'s workload. Washington had nine carries for 43 yards, including an 18-yard run in the fourth quarter.

 Trend to watch: The Raiders switched up their starting offensive line. On Sunday, second-year lineman Caleb Rogers started at right guard over Jackson Powers-Johnson . It remains to be seen if Rogers maintains the starting role for the remainder of the season. However, the move raises questions about how the staff feels about Powers-Johnson. Last season, he was in frequent competition with Alex Cappa . And Powers-Johnson is still competing for a role, unlike the rest of the offensive line.

 Best quote from the locker room:   Raiders HC Klint Kubiak kept it simple when asked what the team needs to improve on: "Close. Games. Out."  -- Ryan McFadden 

 Next game: vs. Rams (Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET)

 
 

 Fantasy football takeaway: The Raiders' offense is making two tight ends fantasy relevant. Michael Mayer -- second on their positional depth chart -- scored 16.5 fantasy points on nine targets, his third game with at least 12 points in his past four. Coach Klint Kubiak 's offense has coaxed a league-leading 64.6 points from tight ends during that four-week span. -- Cockcroft

title: Panthers take shot at Eagles, lead top trolls from Week 6
summary: The Panthers picked at Philadelphia's roots after their road win, but more teams turned petty following their respective Week 6 wins.
full_text:
As the cooler weather starts to settle in, trolls from respective teams are also adjusting their team jabs accordingly with a cold tone.

 
 
With  Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts  on the injured reserve list and running back Saquon Barkley  among inactive players, the Eagles' struggles continued Sunday with a loss to Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers . Young threw for 281 passing yards and two touchdowns in a 25-14 win. 
 
Carolina went after the Eagles with two Philadelphia-themed trolls: the final game graphic with the caption "No dreams, just nightmares" (an inverse of Philadelphia native rapper Meek Mill's "Dreams and Nightmares") and a post with Young as the iconic Rocky Balboa statue with the message "Yo Adrian, we did it!" 
 
 

 Just because the clock strikes zero doesn't mean that's the last teams will hear from their opponents.

 Here are more of the best trolls from Week 6 in the NFL.

 

 Baltimore Ravens 10, Cleveland Browns 13 

 Cleveland collected a big win over its AFC North rival, as quarterback Deshaun Watson led a crucial fourth quarter drive to set up a 33-yard field goal for Andre Szmyt for the win. After the win, the Browns took aim at the Ravens and one of Maryland's signature offerings: crabs.

 

 

 Pittsburgh Steelers 26, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 19 

 Aaron Rodgers threw for 253 passing yards, including two late touchdowns, to help the Steelers rally from a 13-point deficit and force overtime. Steelers wide receiver Germie Bernard caught Rodgers' winning touchdown pass to seal the road victory in overtime.

 And Pittsburgh's social media team had a couple of trolls up its sleeve to rub the win in Tampa Bay's face.

 It first posted a video featuring two alligators dancing on a golf course with two Steelers emblems plastered on them, while a patron in a golf cart watched in disbelief from a distance, a Buccaneers logo on his shirt. The trollers followed up with a snippet from "SpongeBob SquarePants" where a ghost captain asked Patrick to move a pirate ship "behind the rocks." After the ship moved, the bottom was damaged and nearly destroyed. Pittsburgh captioned the post "Don't worry captain..."

 

 

 Houston Texans 34, Jacksonville Jaguars 31 

 Advancing to a two-game win streak, the Houston Texans almost saw their Week 6 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars -- played in London -- go into overtime. However, thanks to a 49-yard field goal by placekicker Ka'imi Fairbairn as time expired, Houston went on to win 34-31. Following the Texans' win, the team unleashed a handful of trolls, beginning with a bubbled "W" in a cup of tea with a Union Jack-styled Texans logo on the tea bag's tag.

 

 Houston continued with a remake of the "Black Clover" and "Assassin's Creed III" posters, adding a spin of Texans branding.

title: Bears' Kyler Gordon returns with vengeance, answers critics
summary: In his season debut, Gordon was a huge factor in Chicago's win Sunday after battling through various injuries.
full_text:
ATLANTA -- The ink was barely dry on the  Chicago Bears ' initial 53-man roster when general manager Ryan Poles cast doubt on whether nickel corner Kyler Gordon would ever play another down of football in Chicago.

 " I don't know ," Poles said on Sept. 1, before adding he still had hope.

 Those three words spoke loudest about a frustrating situation inside Halas Hall. The Bears had planned for Gordon to become a cornerstone in Dennis Allen's defense. But he didn't participate in any team drills during the 2026 offseason because of a right calf injury. He spent all of training camp on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list before being moved to reserve/PUP , which meant he would have to miss at least the first four games. He wasn't even in the building to start the season while rehabbing independently.

 The best way to quell concerns -- at least in the short term -- about dependability was to return to the lineup and dominate, which he wasted little time doing Sunday in Atlanta. Gordon, who was activated Saturday, became the first Bears defensive back with three sacks in a game since Todd Bell in 1983 as Chicago held off the Falcons, 31-23 . Gordon became the third Bears player since sacks became official in 1982 to record three sacks and two forced fumbles in a game.

 

 Gordon had a lot to think about as he stood by himself during the anthem inside Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The highest-paid slot cornerback in the NFL -- $13.3 million per year after signing an extension on April 15, 2025 -- Gordon had played in just five of Chicago's previous 25 games (21%). And while his teammates kept the faith, the injuries created some doubt about his dependability.

 "I mean, it is what it is," Gordon said. "I can't control what someone else says.

 "But at the end of the day, I'm going out there and do my job and do (it to) my best ability and be the best player and the leader at my spot."

 Gordon's talent was never doubted. He was Poles' first draft pick, No. 39 overall in 2022 out of Washington, and Poles rewarded him with the three-year, $40 million extension with $31.25 million guaranteed. His skills were on display Sunday, but Gordon has a bigger hurdle to clear: staying healthy.

 

 No stranger to soft tissue injuries, Gordon has dealt with multiple hamstring, calf and groin ailments. He's also had a concussion and a fracture in his right hand.

 "He was ready to play," Bears coach Ben Johnson said. "I talked with Kyler yesterday morning, and [said], 'Hey, I think we want to activate you. Are you ready to go?' And he said, 'Absolutely,' and he sure enough was. So, huge spark there for us on the defense.

 "We've got to make sure that we keep him on that right track. We've tried to limit his role a little bit, just making sure he was in good football shape. But those snaps that he had were huge ones for us today."

 Trying to find cause of Kyler Gordon's injuries 

 Two stints on injured reserve in 2025 prompted the Bears and Gordon to investigate the root of his health problems. Was it overtraining or undertraining? Was it the type of training he was doing on his own? Was an underlying injury issue to blame for what Poles classified in July as "a delay" in his recovery?

 In the offseason, the team organized a virtual meeting, according to a source with direct knowledge of the call, with the team's decision-makers, trainers, strength and conditioning and other support staff, as well as with people Gordon had hired to work with away from Halas Hall. The purpose was to get all parties on the same page with a plan for Gordon's rehabilitation and offseason training.

 But frustrations continued as Gordon showed up with a calf injury to offseason workouts in late May.

 

 To fully understand the recurring soft-tissue ailments, the Bears then sent him to see a specialist, according to a source familiar with the request.

 Gordon learned during the rehab process that the issue not just his calf, but "something wrong with the way the glute was firing that created a posterior chain issue," according to a source. That caused the calf to strain as well as the hamstring.

 Unlike during the previous offseason, Gordon stayed in the Chicagoland area to rehab and train. He worked with Montel Fleming, known as "Dr. Moe," on body alignment and injury prevention. Fleming also works with other Bears players, from Jaylon Johnson to defensive back Cam Lewis and running back D'Andre Swift .

 The Bears told Gordon's camp during the offseason that he could work with "your guy, come back when you're ready," a source with knowledge of the situation recalled. But those on both sides admit that building consensus on how to attack a delicate injury was, at times, frustrating. One issue for Chicago, per a team source, was that multiple players with severe injuries -- offensive tackle  Ozzy Trapilo (torn patellar tendon), pass rusher Dayo Odeyingbo (torn Achilles) and linebacker Noah Sewell  (torn Achilles) -- returned to the team and the field before Gordon.

 Poles said on Sept. 1 : "any time you have an injury and you're coming back from something there's discomfort that you have to push through and that's what it comes down to. So we haven't been able to get over that hump and we're not progressing as fast as we'd like."

 But Gordon's injury was much more complicated than a calf strain, a source added.

 That Gordon was away from the team -- front offices and coaching staffs typically prefer their players rehab injuries at the team facility -- was an additional layer to consider.

 And the Bears' messaging about Gordon's injury was hard to ignore. In June, while citing Gordon's on-field impact as undeniable, Ben Johnson pointed out that "you can only develop trust (as a player) by being available." That seemingly applied public pressure on Gordon, as did Poles' "I don't know" comment. A source involved believes the team was attempting to "light a fire" under Gordon with those comments.

 Asked Sunday if his team and the Bears' medical staff are on the same page as far as working with Fleming, Gordon said: "Think that'd be a question for Coach."

 Gordon tried to find the positives in what he went through last season, when he played in just three regular-season games and both postseason contests.

 "I've just never been through that before," he said. "So obviously just learning to have that delusional optimism and just use that.

 "So it's been great. Learned a lot and now we're here. So God's great."

 Kyler Gordon didn't say he was vindicated, or needed to be 

 If there was doubt outside the locker room, it wasn't shared by Gordon's teammates.

 "My dog came back after all the talk, all the chatter, worked his ass off, came back and balled," Jaylon Johnson said.

 When asked what it meant to have him back, defensive end Daniel Hardy said: "Everything, man. That guy came out here and put his heart and soul on tape. Phenomenal athlete.

 "He was working his butt off trying to get back to us and y'all could see it out there. He wasn't just chilling at home. He was out there grinding and working and getting his body healthy so he could come back and be the star that he is."

 

 Receiver Rome Odunze played with Gordon at Washington and still gets caught by surprise by his teammate.

 "You think you've seen it all from that guy and then he goes out there and does some stuff like that," Odunze said. "He's one of those players that gets you up out of your seat for sure. The way he moves, his ability to impact the game is incredible.

 "So, super glad to have him back."

 A Bears defense that had allowed 6.2 yards per play (30th in NFL) and ranked 28th in explosive play rate allowed (7.6%) prior to his return Sunday believes Gordon could fix some of the unit's biggest vulnerabilities.

 The Falcons entered the game averaging 361.8 yards per game and were held to 257. Gordon's impact off the nickel blitz was a major factor.

 "Because he's the best in the league at it,"…

title: Judging overreactions to NFL Week 6: Regretting Daniel Jones, A.J. Brown deals?
summary: Did the Colts severely misfire by re-signing Jones? What about the Patriots with the A.J. Brown trade? We're judging overreactions to Sunday's games.
full_text:
We've got your Week 6 overreactions column, fresh out of the oven. Did you think the Texans' season was over? Did you think the Ravens would roll the Browns even without Lamar Jackson ? Did you think the game against the Titans was a get-right spot for the Colts? Did you assume the Rams would take out all their early-season frustrations on the Cardinals?

 You might have been overreacting.

 Sunday started with a wild and important AFC South matchup in London. By the time the 1 p.m. ET window closed, the Panthers were seizing control in the NFC South, J.J. McCarthy had replaced Jameis Winston at quarterback for the Giants , and the AFC North had a combined winning percentage of .652.

 I'm sorry, but we still don't know much about how this season is going to turn out. So, here's our Week 6 overreactions column, where we look at five potential takeaways from all the action and judge them as legitimate stances or irrational stretches. Plus, we hit a few fantasy football overreactions at the bottom.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Patriots will regret trading for Brown? 
 Jones extension worst move of offseason? 
 Thomas next big-name WR on the move? 
 Rams bound to miss the playoffs 
 Bears are NFC North favorites with Williams? 
 Fantasy overreactions 

 
 

 

 The Patriots are going to regret the A.J. Brown trade 
 New England's prized offseason addition got injured in Week 1 and didn't play again until Sunday, when he had three catches for 27 yards on 10 targets and had the home crowd groaning repeatedly with a career-high three drops. To say Brown looked rusty is a massive understatement. Fortunately, the Patriots got enough from the DeMario Douglas / Hunter Henry / Romeo Doubs section of their roster to beat the Jets 26-19 on a day when head coach Mike Vrabel said they were "lucky to win."

 New England saw three more offensive starters -- Doubs and a pair of offensive linemen --  leave the game because of injuries, but that's par for the course for the Patriots this season. But they're still 4-2 and hanging right with the Bills in the AFC East race. It's just that Brown was supposed to elevate the offense, and his rough day coincided with a day on which a lot of what the Patriots did looked difficult.

 

 Verdict: OVERREACTION 

 The 10 targets showed that the Patriots believe Brown to be healthy and were willing to make him a major part of the offense in his first game back. That's a fantastic sign, and so is the fact that they were able to win despite the ball clanging off his massive hands over and over again. They're 4-2 while getting basically nothing at all out of their No. 1 receiver, and that tells you there's room for things to get a lot better.

 

 They play again Thursday night in Chicago , and they're almost guaranteed to be shorthanded because of Sunday's fresh slate of injuries. But Brown is healthy, which means the Patriots are going to keep trying to lean on him. There's nothing in Brown's extensive history as a highly productive NFL wide receiver to indicate that the drops are going to be a problem going forward. Quarterback  Drake Maye was clear after the game that he wasn't worried and even said it was really cool to see Brown in the huddle. This is not going to be the Patriots' biggest problem, I promise.

 

 

 The Daniel Jones extension was the biggest mistake any team made this offseason 
 Jones and the Colts lost to the Titans on Sunday. That's something no other team has done this season. Jones in this game? Well, he was terrible. He was 22-for-42 with a touchdown, two interceptions and a QBR of 20.4. It's the fourth time in six games that his QBR has been under 35 (QBR is on a scale of 1 to 100, remember). It's not even his worst QBR of the season -- he somehow put up a 15.8 in a 30-13 Week 4 victory over the Commanders.

 The Colts were so determined to keep Jones as their quarterback this offseason, even though he was coming off a season-ending Achilles tear , that they used the transition tag to keep him off the free agent market, then handed him a two-year, $88 million contract with nearly $50 million guaranteed. Through six weeks, the Colts are 2-4 and Jones is statistically one of the worst quarterbacks in the league.

 Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION 

 Could it get better? Sure. Lots of things can happen. But how much better can we really expect things to get in Indy? The defense hasn't been very good. Jonathan Taylor isn't having a great season . Alec Pierce , another of their big offseason extensions , is on injured reserve . Star tight end Tyler Warren got hurt in practice late last week and missed Sunday's game .

 It seems as if things are getting worse in Indianapolis instead of better. And if Jones doesn't make an incredible turnaround and get this team into the playoffs, a whole lot of seats are going to start feeling pretty darn hot out there.

 

 

 

 

 Brian Thomas Jr . is going to be the next big-name WR traded ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline 
 Last week saw 2024 No. 4 pick Marvin Harrison Jr . traded from Arizona to Houston after he hired an agent to help him convince the Cardinals to deal him. A lot of eyes now turn to Jacksonville, where the No. 23 pick from that same draft, Thomas, is really struggling in an offense that seems to be leaving him behind. Thomas has fallen to third in the Jaguars' wide receiver pecking order behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers , and by the end of Sunday's loss to the Texans in London you could have argued he was fourth behind Washington, Meyers and CB/WR Travis Hunter .

 Thomas had a pair of drops in the first half and didn't play an offensive snap in the second. He finished with zero catches, and he has a total of nine catches for 105 yards this season. He has played in all six of Jacksonville's games.

 Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION 

 

 The issue Thomas and other Jaguars receivers had with drops last season is one of the reasons Jacksonville felt the need to trade for the sure-handed Meyers and sign him to a long-term extension . The Jaguars talked extension with Washington this offseason and still could do one, though he's setting the price higher with every stellar week.

 Thomas just might not fit in Jacksonville, and while the Jaguars have indicated they don't have interest in trading him, the Cardinals were saying the same thing about Harrison as recently as two weeks ago. There are a lot of people around the league who believe Thomas could have a new home by the trade deadline. It's a situation to monitor.

 

 

 The Rams are going to miss the playoffs 
 It's been a really rough couple of weeks to be a Los Angeles superteam, am I right? While the two-time defending World Series champion Dodgers were getting swept out of the MLB playoffs by the Milwaukee Brewers, the preseason Super Bowl favorite Rams lost Monday night to Buffalo and then dropped an inexplicable division home game Sunday to the Cardinals. The Rams scored 16 points against an Arizona team that allowed an average of 32.4 points per game over the first five weeks this season. The Rams showed little to no life on offense, and while they kept the Cardinals out of the end zone, they did let them march down the field to get into position for six Chad Ryland field goals, including the game winner as time ran out.

 The Rams actually took the lead in the final minute but were flagged for a stupid personal foul penalty after a long Jacoby Brissett completion on the very next drive. That resulted in Arizona being in position to win it with a field goal, and that kick resulted in the Rams having the same 2-4 record as the Cardinals through six weeks. Not exactly the way they drew it up back in the preseason, is it?

 

 Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION

title: Packers use timely turnovers, third-down conversions to beat struggling Cowboys
summary: The Packers used timely third-down conversions and a few big defensive plays to topple a scuffling Cowboys squad.
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- It might be time to starting talking about the Green Bay Packers as one of the hotter teams in the NFL.

 Besides the three remaining undefeated teams, no one has a longer winning streak than the Packers. They won their third straight Sunday night, and the  23-13 win over the Dallas Cowboys improved their record to 4-2 after their 1-2 start to the season. Meanwhile, the Cowboys dropped their second straight to fall to 2-4.

 There was no drama, unlike the 40-40 tie between these two teams last season in Dallas. The Packers jumped out to an early lead and the Cowboys never really threatened.

 Just like last week against the  Chicago Bears , quarterback Jordan Love kept firing deep. And just like the Cowboys have done all season, they struggled to stop it.

 The Packers' biggest problem has been their running game. Despite Dallas having the worst rushing defense in the league, the Packers managed only 57 rushing yards. But that could get better soon with the return of running back Josh Jacobs , who will come off the commissioner exempt list Monday and could play in Week 7 against the  Detroit Lions .

 Here are the most important things to know for both teams:

 

 

 

 Green Bay Packers (4-2) 
 Most surprising performance: Through five games, the Packers were the worst third-down team in the league, converting only 27.6%. All they needed was the Cowboys' shoddy defense to help change that. Dallas came in with the worst third-down defense in the league at 52.6%. On the opening drive, the Packers converted a third-and-5, two third-and-13s and a third-and-6 -- the last one a 9-yard touchdown catch by Matthew Golden . They went on to convert nine of their first 10 third downs to start the game. Their only failed conversion in the first half came on third-and-goal from the Cowboys' 2, forcing the Packers to settle for a field goal. They then failed on their first third down of the second half.

 Trend to watch:  Golden could've had some kind of game if not for drops. Though Golden finished with six catches for 104 yards and a touchdown, he dropped what would have been a 43-yard touchdown in the second quarter when the ball slipped through his hands on a deep shot down the sideline, then dropped another pass in the third quarter. Golden came into the game tied for the league lead with four drops through the first five games, according to ESPN Research, and could've been charged with at least one more drop on a deep shot that was scored as a pass breakup instead. On the same drive in the third quarter that ended with a field goal, Christian Watson dropped a would-be 26-yard touchdown.

 Trend to watch II:   No one has more takeaways in the first half of games this season than the Packers. They ran their total to six thanks to interceptions by Evan Williams and Brandon Cisse . For Williams, it was his second interception of the season, and Cisse -- the Packers' top draft pick this year -- snagged his first career pick after receiver CeeDee Lamb slipped on the Lambeau Field turf. --  Rob Demovsky 

 Next game:  at  Detroit Lions  (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

 
 

 

 Dallas Cowboys (2-4) 
 The easy thing to do following the loss to the Packers would be to blame the Cowboys' defense. It wasn't great and really not even good, especially considering the Packers dropped three potential touchdown passes.

 In their first game since a defensive players-only meeting, the Cowboys were still awful on third down, allowed too many big pass plays and gave up at least 20 points for a franchise-record 13th straight game, but they did record their first interception of the season ( Dee Winters ) and had their first three-sack game of the season.

 But the offense, which wanted to be known as the "Greatest Offense There Is" when the season began, sputtered, to be kind. The Cowboys were blanked in the first half of a game for the first time since 2021. Dak Prescott was intercepted twice in Packers territory. George Pickens was mostly invisible and the run game continued to struggle.

 Now 2-4, the Cowboys might be able to be propped up by a poor NFC East -- and they next face the similarly 2-4 Philadelphia Eagles on "Monday Night Football" -- but they have never made the playoffs in the Super Bowl era with such a record after six games.

 Trend to watch:  Maybe it's too early to call it a trend, but the Cowboys had three sacks. It is the first time this season the Cowboys have recorded at least three sacks in a game and only the second time in their past 11 games. Maybe the mere presence of Micah Parsons on the other sideline inspired the Cowboys? Quinnen Williams had the first sack of Love, his second of the season. Elijah Garcia had the second, and former Packer Kenny Clark , part of the Parsons trade, recorded the third.

 Most surprising performance:  It wasn't the third-down defense for the Cowboys in the first half. The Packers converted their first seven third-down tries against what has been the worst third-down defense in the league. It was that the Cowboys intercepted a pass. Winters picked off a Love throw to Golden in the second quarter, ending a streak of 256 pass attempts dating to Week 15 of last season, when Williams picked off then-Minnesota QB  J.J. McCarthy . The Cowboys have not had a cornerback intercept a pass since Week 8 of 2025.

 Stat to know:  Prescott was intercepted twice in the second half of the Cowboys' Week 5 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . He opened the first half Sunday with two more interceptions. It was the first time Prescott had been intercepted twice in a first half since Week 17 of the 2022 season against the New York Giants . Of Prescott's past four interceptions, three weren't necessarily his fault. The Buccaneers' turnovers came off a teammate's hands and face mask. His second pick Sunday came after Lamb slipped on his cut. --  Todd Archer 

 Next game: at Philadelphia Eagles  (Oct. 26, 8:15 p.m. ET)

title: Who are the winningest NFL coaches of all time?
summary: From Belichick to Reid, there are many iconic coaches in NFL history. Who has the best career record? Check out the stat breakdown now.
full_text:
Only four head coaches in NFL history have won 300 career games across the regular season and postseason. Kansas City Chiefs  coach Andy Reid was the last to cross the 300-win plateau.

 Reid recorded his 300th career victory on Jan. 18, 2025, when his Chiefs defeated the Houston Texans 23-14 in the AFC divisional round.

 Reid, who signed a five-year, $100 million extension with the Chiefs in April 2024, entered the 2026 season looking to add to his career win total and close the gap between him and the NFL's all-time winningest head coach, Hall of Famer Don Shula.

 Let's take a look at which head coaches have the most career victories in NFL history (including both regular-season and postseason play):

 *Active NFL head coach 

 5. Tom Landry, 270 wins 

 Landry was the Dallas Cowboys' head coach for an NFL-record 29 years in a row and the team had 20 consecutive winning seasons, which is also a league record. Landry led Dallas to two Super Bowl wins, defeating the Miami Dolphins in Super Bowl VI and the Denver Broncos in Super Bowl XII. He was named the NFL's Coach of the Year in 1966 and the UPI NFL Coach of the Year in 1975. Landry was an innovator, with the 4-3 defense among his creations. He was named to the NFL's 100th Anniversary All-Time Team.

 *4. Andy Reid, 312 wins 

 Reid is the only head coach in NFL history who has won 100 games with two franchises: the Philadelphia Eagles (coaching the team from 1999 through 2012) and the Chiefs (he has coached Kansas City since 2013). He led the Eagles on multiple deep playoff runs, including a Super Bowl in 2004 and three straight conference finals from 2001 to 2003. However, he wasn't able to hoist the Lombardi Trophy until he arrived in Kansas City. He has turned the Chiefs into a juggernaut, winning three Super Bowls. Reid is an offensive mastermind and quarterback whisperer. He'll likely continue to rack up wins moving forward with Patrick Mahomes , Travis Kelce & Co.

 

 3. George Halas, 324 wins 

 Halas was a co-founder of the NFL and creator of the Bears. For 10 years, he served as player-coach-executive for the Bears (which is how he earned the nickname "Mr. Everything"). In 1930, he retired as a player and focused on ownership, but he would later return to coach the Bears several times. Halas led the Bears to eight NFL championships, tying Belichick's number of titles. Halas coached the team for 40 years and had just six losing seasons. He helped create the T-formation system and used it to set an NFL record for the biggest blowout in league history: a 73-0 win over the Washington team in the 1940 NFL Championship Game. Halas was selected as the AP's NFL Coach of the Year in 1963 and 1965, and he was named to the NFL's 100th Anniversary All-Time Team.

 2. Bill Belichick, 333 wins 

 Belichick is considered by some as the greatest coach in all of professional sports, as he has won an NFL-record eight Super Bowls (six as a head coach with the Patriots and two as an assistant coach with the Giants). He also ranks first among all NFL coaches in playoff wins with 31. Belichick was named the AP's NFL Coach of the Year in 2003, 2007 and 2010. Many franchises have hired away Belichick's assistants and tried to replicate his "Patriot Way," but it hasn't been the same without him. If Belichick returns to NFL coaching, he is just 26 regular-season wins from surpassing Don Shula as the winningest regular-season coach of all time. 

 1. Don Shula, 347 wins 

 After playing in the NFL as a defensive back for seven seasons, Shula decided to retire and become a coach. He got his first head-coaching opportunity in 1963 with the Baltimore Colts, whom he led to the NFL championship in 1968. From 1970 through 1995, Shula had a legendary run as head coach of the Dolphins. Shula led the Dolphins to a pair of Super Bowl victories (in Super Bowl VII and Super Bowl VIII). Miami had a perfect season in 1972, making Shula the only coach in NFL history to go undefeated. He was named the AP's NFL Coach of the Year in 1964, 1967, 1968 and 1972. Whether you're just counting regular-season wins (328) or including playoff wins (347), Shula is the winningest coach in NFL history.

title: Betting buzz: Rams' loss to Cardinals sends shockwaves through survivor pools
summary: The Rams entered the NFL season as the Super Bowl favorites but fell to 2-4 after suffering one of the biggest upsets of the season in the loss to the Cardinals.
full_text:
Everything that happens in sports has additional context when viewed from a sports betting perspective. From season-changing injuries to record-setting moments and so much more, the sports news cycle will constantly and significantly affect the sports betting industry. 

 Our NFL betting buzz file, with contributions from David Purdum, Doug Greenberg and others, aims to provide fans a look at the sports betting stories that are driving the conversation throughout each week of the season.  

 Key links: NFL futures | Awards odds |  Sports betting home  |  DraftKings   

 
 Oct. 18: Cardinals pulls biggest upset of season, add to Rams' struggles 
 By David Purdum 

 The Los Angeles Rams won over the betting public in the offseason and kicked off the regular season as the clear-cut Super Bowl favorites. They haven't lived up to that billing so far, suffering a new low Sunday.

 The Rams lost to the Arizona Cardinals as 13.5-point home favorites in the biggest upset of the season based on point spread. They are only the second double-digit favorite to lose outright in the past two seasons, joining the Green Bay Packers , who lost to the Carolina Panthers in Week 9 last November as 13.5-point favorites.

 

 Arizona's upset shredded survivor pool entries around the nation.

 The Rams were picked by the most contestants in ESPN Survivor contests and in the high-stakes contests Circa Survivor and Circa Grandissimo in Las Vegas. Throw in the  Indianapolis Colts ' loss to the underdog and previously winless Tennessee Titans , and the Circa contests lost greater than 50% of the remaining entries.

 The loss drops the Rams to 2-4 on the season, the same record as the Cardinals. The Rams are the second preseason Super Bowl favorite in the past 20 years to lose four of their first six games, per SportsOddsHistory.com. (The 2015 Seattle Seahawks  started 2-4 and went on to lose in the divisional round of the playoffs.)

 Los Angeles was favored to win the Super Bowl at 5-1 ahead of Week 1. No other team had Super Bowl odds shorter than 10-1. The Rams were +950 to win the Super Bowl on Sunday night at DraftKings, behind four teams.

 More bets were placed and more money was wagered on the Rams to win the Super Bowl than any other team in the offseason at most sportsbooks.

 

 Oct. 11: Who wants to win the NFC East? 
 

 By Doug Greenberg 

 Week 5 was one to forget for the NFC East, to say the least.

 It started Thursday night when the Dallas Cowboys lost outright to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after closing as 8.5-point favorites, tied with four other games as the biggest upset of the season, according to DraftKings odds.

 Not only were the Cowboys heavily backed on the spread and in moneyline parlays at multiple sportsbooks, they were also the most popular pick in both ESPN Survivor (40% of the remaining field) and the $1,000-per-entry Circa Survivor (2,554 entries, 42.8% of the remaining field). It's the third time in the season's first five weeks that ESPN Survivor's most popular pick lost.

 But the misery didn't end there for the division. The Philadelphia Eagles led off the day in London by seemingly notching a winning field goal with eight seconds left against the Jacksonville Jaguars , giving them a 99.5% chance to win the game, per ESPN Analytics.

 Jacksonville returned the ensuing kickoff to the Philadelphia 35-yard line with one second left, allowing the Jags to kick a winning field goal as time expired. It was the first game in the Super Bowl era that featured two go-ahead field goals in the final 10 seconds of the fourth quarter, according to ESPN Research.

 Then, there was the most bizarre result of the week, possibly the season. The New York Giants and Washington Commanders played a mistake-ridden game into an overtime where neither team scored, including in the matchup's final moments when the Commanders somehow ran out the clock while in field goal range.

 "In the closing minutes and overtime, the live moneyline market was in complete chaos," Joey Feazel, Caesars Sportsbook head of football, told ESPN via email. "Every big play looked like it might decide the game and the book's fate, only for the final whistle to leave everyone staring at the screen wondering what had just happened. It was 90-plus minutes of drama, countless swings in perceived win probability, and in the end, nobody got the outcome they were expecting."

 That's right: None of the NFC East teams recorded a win in Week 5 ... despite two of the teams playing each other.

 Going into "Thursday Night Football," the Cowboys had been the +105 favorites to win the division and immediately dropped to +164 following their upset loss, tying them with the Eagles. After Week 5, Philadelphia is now the slight favorite for the division at +170 -- the longest odds for any division favorite in the league. Next comes Dallas at +180, followed by current division leader New York at +320 and Washington at +750. All of the teams in the NFC East show underdog plus-odds to make the playoffs ... even though one of them has to.

 The Eagles had actually been a top-six favorite for the Super Bowl at 17-1 going into the season, but that number has lengthened to 40-1. The Cowboys are now the Super Bowl favorite among NFC East teams at 30-1 after coming into the season at 25-1.

 The whole situation is made all the more disorienting by the fact that bettors had much higher expectations for this division going into the season. At BetMGM, Dallas is the biggest liability for the NFC championship, having attracted a $10,000 wager at 16-1 odds to win $160,000.

 The Giants provoked a $5,000 wager to win the Super Bowl at 66-1 odds, creating a potential payout of $330,000. New York is also the largest liability to win the NFC East at both BetMGM and DraftKings, with both books also reporting some action for the division on Dallas.

 "The Eagles/Commanders right now are the best-case scenario for the book with the Giants/Cowboys being the best-case scenario for the bettors," Feazel said, "but based on today's events we are not sure that any of these teams would like to win the division."

 
 Sept. 28: Betting buzz: 8.5 the magic number for underdogs 
 

 By Doug Greenberg and David Purdum 

 Big underdogs are having a historic start to the 2026 NFL season, and it's all revolving around one number.

 On Sunday, the Washington Commanders upset the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks after coming into the matchup as 8.5-point underdogs. In Week 2, the New Orleans Saints defeated the Baltimore Ravens outright as 8.5-point underdogs and the Cleveland Browns beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as underdogs by the same number. And in Week 1, the Arizona Cardinals pulled off the first big upset of the season when they defeated the Los Angeles Chargers ... again, as 8.5-point underdogs.

 The four straight-up wins by underdogs of eight points or greater is the most through three weeks of a season since 1978 when five teams accomplished the feat, according to ESPN Research.

 Only one 8.5-point favorite has survived so far: the Jacksonville Jaguars , who won and covered against the Browns in Week 1. Additionally, the only two favorites of greater than 8.5 -- the San Francisco 49ers (-12.5) in Week 2 and the Kansas City Chiefs (-10) in Week 3 -- also won and covered, both against the Miami Dolphins .

 Because public bettors generally like to back big favorites -- via straight spread wagers, teasers or money-line parlays -- the underdog wins have been a boon to sportsbooks. title: Jets WR Garrett Wilson holds tongue after 'frustrating' loss to Patriots
summary: New York's star pass catcher only had four catches in the 26-19 loss to New England.
full_text:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. --  Garrett Wilson 's greatest accomplishment Sunday was holding his tongue.

 The  New York Jets ' star wide receiver could've complained about his lack of involvement in the offense (six targets). Or he could've vented about the Jets' penchant for losing to the New England Patriots -- virtually a twice-a-year habit that stretches back, oh, about two-plus decades.

 But, no, Wilson stuck to the company line after the Jets' 26-19 loss at Gillette Stadium. He didn't throw anyone under the bus, but don't believe for a second that he's OK with how it went down. He was absolutely frustrated by his four-catch, 44-yard performance; he was grumbling aloud as he walked through the tunnel and to the locker room.

 "It's just frustrating because we lost, and I want to help the team," he told reporters after a lengthy cooling-off period.

 

 A few days ago, Wilson billed Sunday's matchup as " a big-ass game ," a chance for the Jets to rise up and make a loud statement against their longtime nemesis. How did the Jets respond under such important circumstances?

 Of the 31 plays they ran in New England's territory, the ball ended up in Wilson's hands once -- a 12-yard reception in the fourth quarter. In fact, he was targeted only three times in plus-territory, and only twice overall through the first three quarters.

 "Not every game [is] going to go your way," Wilson said. "I try to reason it in my head because we had [the] fourth quarter, and I know that the game can change at any moment. So just try to keep playing my role, waiting for that moment that they want to call on me."

 If the Jets (2-4) want to make something of this season, if they want to fulfill their potential as an offense, they certainly have to find ways to get Wilson the ball.

 The Frank Reich-led offense is in the bottom 10 after averaging 18.7 points, having scored only four touchdowns in the past three games. Their only score Sunday was  Geno Smith 's 48-yard strike to rookie Omar Cooper Jr ., which cut the Patriots' lead to 17-10 in the third quarter.

 The Jets spent half the game in New England territory, but they were undermined by efficiency on third down (3-for-10) and in the red zone (0-for-3) and fourth-down failures (0-for-2). The defense handed Smith & Co. two short fields because of takeaways, but the Jets generated only six points.

 It was a game of blown opportunities. Wide receiver Tim Patrick called it "a completely frustrating day," adding, "We have to learn to finish."

 "We can't just get in a fight sometimes," Patrick said. "We have to knock somebody out on the first punch."

 

 It would help if the Jets could get Wilson involved. When he's in a groove, the offense performs better.

 He knew this wasn't going to be a breeze, not with cornerback Christian Gonzalez on the other side. Wilson has struggled against him in previous games. This time, he was covered by Gonzalez on 17 of his 30 pass routes, per NFL Next Gen Stats -- generally when he lined up on the outside. It makes you wonder what would have happened if the Jets would have deployed Wilson more often in the slot to potentially continue to create favorable matchups.

 "He's a really good player, and he followed me, and some plays he didn't," Wilson said. "I think it was just -- I don't know, it was just taking advantage of the look, whatever we were getting, whatever Geno was seeing. And that's how it shook out today."

 The upside is that Cooper, a rookie first-round pick in his first full NFL game, enjoyed a breakout -- six catches for 103 yards. Running back Braelon Allen continued to fill in nicely for injured  Breece Hall , rushing for 78 yards on 17 carries for a healthy 4.6 yards per carry average.

 

 Smith said he disagreed with the premise that Wilson's lack of involvement threw the offense out of whack, noting that other players were able to produce.

 "I think Omar did a great job of getting open, [ Kenyon Sadiq ] was open a few times, [ Mason Taylor ] was having a great game," said Smith, whose first interception of the season was a fourth-quarter crusher. "I think our game plan was working the way it should. Again, if we just finish those drives, I think we're talking a lot different."

 Coach Aaron Glenn said "we have all the confidence in the world" that Wilson can beat any cornerback, adding they were able to get the ball to him as the game progressed. Not really, though, not until they were in catch-up mode in the fourth quarter.

 Wilson, in control of his emotions, was measured in his postgame comments, sometimes pausing before choosing his words.

 "I'm going to watch this film and see how I can get more separation or just find a way to get on the right page with [Geno] and find a way to make defenses pay for the looks that we've been getting," Wilson said. "Because [the opportunities] are there."

title: Aaron Rodgers' 2026 NFL season: Tracking records, milestones
summary: The Steelers QB is chasing records in his 22nd NFL season, and ESPN is chronicling his "last rodeo."
full_text:
Entering his 22nd NFL season -- or as Aaron Rodgers says, "his last rodeo" -- the 42-year-old Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is on the cusp of joining several exclusive clubs as he moves up the ranks in the league record books.

 In 2025, he passed former teammate Brett Favre to take sole possession of fourth place in career touchdown passes thrown with his 509th TD pass in the Week 3 win against the New England Patriots . In Week 6 of 2026, he moved into a third-place tie with Peyton Manning with 539.

 "Every now and then I made some special throws that led to touchdowns, but I've been playing a long time, and it's a longevity thing," Rodgers said before passing Favre's mark last season. "I'm proud of it, but not a big deal."

 

 Rodgers supplanted Ben Roethlisberger for fifth in all-time passing yards in a loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Oct. 16, 2025. But now, Rodgers is closing in on his final opportunities to add to that growing list of historic accomplishments.

 Among the milestones for Rodgers are becoming the fourth quarterback in NFL history to appear in 300 games (as of Week 6 he has appeared in 293), joining Tom Brady (383), Favre (326) and Drew Brees (305), and having the second-most regular-season games with multiple touchdown passes. And after Week 6, he needs 2,239 yards to become the fifth player to reach 70,000 passing yards . 

 This season, we're chronicling Rodgers' individual milestones week by week as he rides his last rodeo. Follow along here for the weekly installments.

 

 
 Preseason: 0-for-0, 0 yards, 0 INT, 0 sacks, 0 rushes 
 Despite early hints that Rodgers would take the field during the Steelers' first preseason under McCarthy, the veteran quarterback instead spent two games on the sideline and one on his couch at home. With Rodgers' top two receivers in DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr . sidelined with preseason injuries, McCarthy opted to also keep his quarterback under wraps.

 Rodgers isn't a stranger to sitting out the preseason in recent years. He didn't play in any preseason games for the Steelers in 2025, nor for the New York Jets in 2024 following his season-ending left Achilles tear in Week 1 of the 2023 season.

 
 

 Week 1:  Steelers 20, Falcons 13 
 Rodgers' stat line: 221 yards, 1 TD, 0 INTs, 2 sacks, 3 rushes for -1 yard 
 Rodgers didn't break any records this week, but he pulled within one touchdown pass of Peyton Manning for fourth most in NFL history with his second-quarter throw to tight end Pat Freiermuth  for 6 yards. The touchdown toss was Rodgers' 232nd of the regular season. Rodgers had 26 pass attempts in the first half, his most attempts in the first half of a game since 2020 at Minnesota as a member of the  Green Bay Packers , per ESPN Research.

 After Sunday's game, coach Mike McCarthy said he wanted to find more balance in his offense, which ran the ball just 21 times to Rodgers' 40 pass attempts. Rodgers, though, didn't mind all the throwing.

 "No, keep doing it," Rodgers said, urging his coach to keep calling passes. "Keep doing it."

 And although Rodgers and the Steelers got the win, the quarterback struggled under the pressure from the Falcons' front. He completed 3 of 12 attempts under pressure and was sacked twice. And continuing the trend from last season, Rodgers was also 3-of-12 on throws of 15 or more air yards. Some of those incompletions, though, were the result of drops by his receivers.

 "I liked the plan from Mike," Rodgers said. "I liked the playcalling. We took some shots. I felt like we had really close to having one of those really good games. If we come down with a couple of those, it obviously looks a little different on the scoreboard and stat sheet and stuff, but love my guys, love  DK [Metcalf] .

 

 

 Week 2: Patriots 20, Steelers 3 
 Rodgers' stat line: 187 yards, 0 TD, 1 INT, 4 sacks, 1 rush for 5 yards 
 Rodgers set two personal Steelers milestones in the team's Week 2 loss -- and not in a good way. Rodgers was off target on 26% of his throws (nine attempts) in the loss, his worst as a Steeler. The Patriots frustrated Rodgers with heavy pressures and blitzed on 19 of 44 dropbacks (43%), the second-highest rate he has faced with Pittsburgh. Against the blitz, he was 8-of-17 for 42 yards with two sacks and an interception. And he had his first interception against the blitz as a member of the Steelers.

 "It's frustrating, for sure," Rodgers said of not getting into the end zone at New England on Sunday. "The defense has been playing great. They've been holding [opponents to] 13 points a game in two games, and offensively I think we're averaging like eight points a game. That's not winning football."

 

 

 Week 3: Steelers 30, Bengals 27 
 Rodgers' stat line: 292 yards, 3 TDs, 1 INT, 2 sacks, 3 rushes for 10 yards 
 It turns out Rodgers still has plenty left in the tank. A week after one of his worst performances as a Steeler, Rodgers bounced back with three passing touchdowns to help the offense put up a season-best 30 points and 411 yards in the win against the Cincinnati Bengals . Rodgers aired it out in the first quarter with two touchdown throws and 143 passing yards -- the most he has thrown in the first quarter since Week 6 of 2018 against the 49ers (170). Each of his touchdown passes traveled at least 20 air yards, marking his first time with multiple touchdowns of 20-plus air yards since he joined the Steelers. Entering Sunday's game, Rodgers was 0-of-9 on pass attempts of 20-plus air yards.

 "We definitely needed it because it was just uncharacteristic of us," Steelers wide receiver Ben Skowronek said of the offense's bounce-back performance. "Throughout camp, we felt really confident in what we were doing, moving the ball. And the first two weeks we just weren't us. So credit to the coaching staff, the guys in the building, we locked in this week and we knew we had to have it. We knew we could do it."

 After two weeks without much movement in the record books, Rodgers is starting to make some headway. Sunday's win marked the 165th of his career, tying him with Ben Roethlisberger for fifth most by a starting quarterback since positions were first tracked in 1950. With his first-quarter 38-yard touchdown throw to Roman Wilson , Rodgers also recorded his 233rd career game with at least one passing touchdown, tying Peyton Manning for the fourth most such games in NFL history.

 

 

 Week 4: Browns 27, Steelers 24 
 Rodgers' stat line: 299 yards, 3 TDs, 2 INTs, 5 sacks, 0 rushes 
 Rodgers spent a lot of time on the turf at Huntington Bank Field in what's scheduled to be his final Thursday night game (barring a late-season flex). Rodgers took 10 quarterback hits thanks to Cleveland's aggressive game plan, protection breakdowns and the quarterback's decisions to hold on to the ball as he looked for his pass catchers to get open against man coverage.

 

 All five of the sacks against Rodgers came as he faced man coverage, and on the season, he has been sacked an NFL-worst 12 times when facing man coverage -- seven more than any other quarterback. And while the offense largely stagnated through the second and third quarters, it came alive in the fourth as Rodgers aired it out with 43-, 28- and 22-yard completions to wide receiver DK Metcalf and a 21-yard touchdown throw threaded to Darnell Washington .

 Rodgers even tied the score at 24 with a quarterback sneak for a successful two-point conversion with less than two minutes to go.

 "I felt like there was no chance they'd be expecting that," Rodgers said. "So I just told them in the huddle, if I can this one, I'm going to sneak it.'"

 With the loss, Rodgers still has 13 wins on Thursdays and remains tied with Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott for second most all time.

 
 

 Week 5: Steelers 34, Colts 22 
 Rodgers' stat line: 235 yards, 3 TDs, 1 sack, 1 rush for 6 yards 
 Aaron Rodgers stood to the right of Cameron Heyward as Heyward wrapped up his postgame news conference behind the…

title: Ranking the top 10 rookie performances in Super Bowl history
summary: Which rookies made a name from themselves in the Super Bowl over the years? We listed 10 standout performances, plus honorable mentions.
full_text:
Every NFL player's goal is to win a Super Bowl .

 Some players go their entire career and never get close. Others are lucky enough to make it as rookies. And some rookies even have a major impact on the game, posting records that still stand long after their career ends.

 We ranked 10 of the best performances by a rookie in Super Bowl history, some of whom went on to have good or great careers while others faded away into anonymity.

 Our methodology was largely based on stats, using ESPN Research to identify rookies with extraordinary contributions in the Super Bowl. Because the evaluations were stats-based, the list is heavy with offensive skill-position players. 

 Let's start with a player whose Super Bowl record stands nearly 40 years later.

 COUNTDOWN TO SUPER BOWL LXI: ESPN will televise the Super Bowl for the first time in February. We are counting down to the big game with a Super Bowl Top 10 series , featuring rankings on everything from best catches and performances to biggest upsets, which will run every other Sunday leading up to Super Bowl LXI on Feb. 14, 2027. 

 

 

 1. Washington RB Timmy Smith in Super Bowl XXII 
 When : Jan. 31, 1988 
 Drafted : 1987 fifth-round pick out of Texas Tech
 Smith ran for 204 yards on 22 carries in Washington's 42-10 victory over the Denver Broncos at Jack Murphy Stadium in San Diego. That total still stands as the most rushing yards by a player (not just a rookie) in a Super Bowl.

 

 Smith had more rushing yards in that game than he did in the regular season (126) and nearly as many carries. He had two touchdown runs -- 58 yards in the second quarter and 4 yards in the fourth quarter -- twice as many as he had in the regular season. Smith was thrust into a bigger role in the playoffs because of injuries to starter George Rogers and the ineffective play of Kelvin Bryant, and he ran for 66 yards against the Chicago Bears in the divisional round and 72 yards against the Minnesota Vikings in the NFC Championship Game.

 Smith was unable to recapture his Super Bowl success, playing in only 15 more games in his NFL career.

 
 

 2. Kansas City Chiefs WR Xavier Worthy in Super Bowl LIX 
 When : Feb. 9, 2025 
 Drafted : 2024 28th-overall pick out of Texas
 Worthy set a Super Bowl rookie record with 157 receiving yards in the Chiefs' 40-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles at Caesars Superdome. Former Seahawks WR Chris Matthews previously held the record with 109 yards in Super Bowl XLIX.

 Two of Worthy's eight catches against the Eagles were for touchdowns, but they came with the game already out of hand as the Chiefs' offense, led by Patrick Mahomes , struggled in the campaign for a three-peat. Worthy's first touchdown (a 24-yarder) came with 34 seconds remaining in the third quarter and the Eagles already leading 34-0. He also caught a 50-yard touchdown pass with 1:48 remaining.

 Worthy's performance in this Super Bowl is still his career best in receiving yards. His next-highest receiving total of 85 yards came in the AFC Championship Game that season.

 
 

 3. San Diego Chargers KR Andre Coleman in Super Bowl XXIX 
 When : Jan. 29, 1995 
 Drafted : 1994 third-round pick out of Kansas State
 Coleman dazzled as a rookie special-teamer in the Super Bowl, returning eight kickoffs for 244 yards -- including a 98-yard touchdown -- in the Chargers' 49-26 loss to the San Francisco 49ers at Joe Robbie Stadium in Miami.

 

 In this game, Coleman set the records for the most kickoff returns in a Super Bowl (eight), the most yards gained off a kickoff in a Super Bowl (244) and the longest kickoff return (98 yards; Jacoby Jones now holds this record with 108 in Super Bowl XLVII ).

 Coleman retired from the NFL in 1998 and later became a college and NFL assistant coach.

 
 

 4. Atlanta Falcons WR/KR Tim Dwight in Super Bowl XXXIII 
 When : Jan. 31, 1999 
 Drafted : 1998 fourth-round pick out of Iowa
 Dwight totaled 215 all-purpose yards in the Falcons' 34-19 loss to the Broncos at Pro Player Stadium in Miami. All but five of those yards came on kickoff returns, which included a 94-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter with the Broncos ahead 31-6.

 Dwight, who had one catch on offense for 5 yards, had nearly as many all-purpose yards as Falcons quarterback Chris Chandler had passing yards (219).

 His 10-year NFL career ended in 2007. He still holds the Super Bowl career record for highest average kickoff yardage (42.0).

 
 

 5. Indianapolis Colts RB Joseph Addai in Super Bowl XLI 
 When : Feb. 4, 2007 
 Drafted : 2006 30th-overall pick out of LSU
 Addai put up 143 yards from scrimmage in the Colts' 29-17 victory over the Bears at Dolphins Stadium in Miami. He rushed for 77 yards on 19 carries and caught 10 passes for 66 yards -- touching the ball more than any other offensive player in the game except Colts quarterback Peyton Manning.

 It was a performance a season in the making.

 

 The Colts' starting running back in 2006 was Dominic Rhodes. However, Addai became the first player in NFL history to rush for more than 1,000 yards without starting a regular-season game. He helped the Colts get to the Super Bowl with a go-ahead 3-yard rushing touchdown with 1:00 remaining in the fourth quarter of the AFC Championship Game against the New England Patriots .

 Addai spent his entire six-year NFL career with the Colts. His 10 receptions remain the most catches by a rookie in Super Bowl history.

 
 

 6. St. Louis Rams WR Torry Holt in Super Bowl XXXIV 
 When : Jan. 30, 2000 
 Drafted : 1999 sixth-overall pick out of NC State
 Holt was a major part of the Rams' ''Greatest Show on Turf'' as a rookie, catching 52 passes for 788 yards and six touchdowns in the regular season.

 In the Super Bowl, he caught a game-high seven passes for 109 yards and a touchdown in the Rams' 23-16 victory over the Tennessee Titans at the Georgia Dome in Atlanta. Holt scored the game's first touchdown on a 9-yard pass midway through the third quarter, which put the Rams ahead 16-0.

 Holt would go on to lead the NFL in receiving twice and earn a spot in the NFL's All-2000s team.

 
 

 7. Seattle Seahawks WR Chris Matthews in Super Bowl XLIX 
 When : Feb. 1, 2015 
 Drafted : Undrafted free agent out of Kentucky
 Matthews' first career reception came in the Super Bowl against the Patriots at the University of Phoenix Stadium. He had four catches for 109 yards and a touchdown -- his 11-yard catch with two seconds remaining in the first half tied the score at 14-14. The Patriots won 28-24, however, due to Malcom Butler's interception of Russell Wilson at the goal line.

 

 Matthews signed with the Cleveland Browns in 2011, but he never played a game before heading to the Iowa Barnstormers of the Arena Football League in 2012 and the Winnipeg Blue Bombers of the Canadian Football League in 2013. To start the 2014 season, he was on the Seahawks' practice squad and was promoted to the active roster in December. Matthews played in three games in the regular season, but he didn't record a catch. In the NFC Championship Game, he recovered an onside kick to help beat the Green Bay Packers in overtime.

 After the Super Bowl, Matthews went on to play in 19 more games in his NFL career with the Seahawks and Baltimore Ravens .

 
 

 8. New England Patriots CB Malcolm Butler in Super Bowl XLIX 
 When : Feb. 1, 2015 
 Drafted : Undrafted free agent out of West Alabama (Division II)
 What a great segue. Butler's first career interception with 20 seconds remaining sealed the Patriots' 28-24 victory over the Seahawks at the University of Phoenix Stadium.

 

 Butler played in 11 games (with one start) as a rookie. But the Patriots ran him onto the field when the Seahawks faced a second-and-goal from the New England 1-yard line with 26 seconds remaining. Seahawks QB Russell Wilson tried to hit receiver Ricardo Lockette with a quick pass, but Butler jumped the route and intercepted the pass.

 Butler went on to become a starting cornerback for the…

title: How 49ers QB Brock Purdy mastered the art of layering passes over defenders
summary: Purdy is terrific at layering the football -- fitting it perfectly between the second and third levels of the defense. And it's a big reason why he's playing at an MVP level this season.
full_text:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- For San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy and linebacker Fred Warner , training camp has become an annual battleground. It isn't just about offense versus defense; it's how they can, individually, win the day against each other.

 For Purdy specifically, those chess matches are vital because the middle of the field is fertile but dangerous ground in coach Kyle Shanahan's offense. It requires Purdy to layer the ball to his pass catchers between multiple defenders, the type of precision best achieved through repetition against the best middle linebacker in the game. And he has gotten good enough at it that he can even leave Warner grasping at air.

 Early in the 49ers' 16th training camp practice this August, he completed a pass over Warner's outstretched arms to wideout Mike Evans for a big gain. But later, Warner broke up similar over-the-middle attempts to wide receiver Demarcus Robinson and running back Kaelon Black . Warner turned and boisterously let Purdy hear about it after both.

 As the practice neared its end, Purdy dropped back and saw Warner sink into coverage. Purdy fired it just past Warner's fingertips and into Deebo Samuel Sr .'s waiting hands. Then, Purdy let it fly toward Warner again -- verbally. A loud "F--- you, Fred" echoed across the field. Moments later, Warner and Purdy stood behind the huddle laughing, and they later acknowledged how such intense practice moments push the other to be better.

 

 "The 'Layer King' has some really intensive intensity, and I like that about him," 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris said in August. "When he does those things, it just makes the team go."

 The art of layering isn't just about a deft touch; it's an act of calculated audacity against defensive geometry, requiring Purdy to get the ball over sinking linebackers and in front of hard-charging defensive backs. His mastery of those throws -- and when to deploy them -- helps explain why he has played like a league MVP this season. Through the first five weeks, Purdy led the league in QBR (85.5) and touchdown passes (13).

 To understand how he has reached that level, Purdy recently walked ESPN through film of some of his finest layered throws. Teammates, coaches and a Hall of Fame quarterback offered additional insight into what makes it work.

 "Most people don't understand the degree of difficulty in that offense of those throws," said Kurt Warner, who was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2017. "It's so hard not only to do it once but to be in an offense that asks you to do that over and over and over again. It's one of the things that continually impresses me about Brock is the understanding of when and how to make those throws."

 
 SITTING IN AN office in the bowels of Levi's Stadium in late August, Purdy rewatches some film and talks through his pre-snap checklist: the route concept, protection, timing and defensive coverage.

 "There's a timing to it," Purdy said. "It's not just, 'Hey, drop back and take a couple hitches and if it's there, lob it.' ... This kind of ball is like you're throwing over a guy, but it needs to be just strong enough and just enough touch to get there before the safety hits him."

 Because those layered throws require flawless timing, Purdy must access a mental Rolodex about his likely receiver and the defenders on the field. On each snap, he notes his receiver's speed, height and how he comes out of breaks. He then analyzes the defense, factoring in intricate details like the wingspan of the linebacker sinking into coverage and the short-area speed of the safety lurking over the top.

 

 The goal is to drop the pass over the linebacker but in a spot where the receiver can run after the catch or, at least, avoid a punishing hit from the secondary.

 "I think it's definitely one of the hardest throws on the field," Purdy said. "Those are things that I sort of prided myself on young. ... Now in the NFL, I'm trying to take it to another level."

 In some ways, the layered throw comes naturally to Purdy because he lacks the height and powerful arm of other quarterbacks. It's why he said he spends a lot of time studying Hall of Fame quarterback Drew Brees, who is 6 feet tall.

 Purdy pays attention to how Brees manipulated defenders with his eyes to create throwing lanes, threw balls long before receivers broke and maneuvered in the pocket. To Purdy, Brees' tape is proof of the mental work required to succeed when you aren't the biggest at the position. More often than not, Purdy said he makes those throws without even seeing his intended target when he lets the ball go.

 "I'm not the Josh Allen - or Joe Burrow -type quarterbacks where they're really big and you'd think they could [see the whole field better]," said the 6-foot-1 Purdy. "But I have to take everything into account. ... That's why I'm huge on like, 'This receiver's taking eight steps and he's breaking to daylight on this coverage. I know this hole's going to be there.' And taking those kinds of things into factor because I can't always see."

 That behind-the-scenes work extends beyond the Niners' facility. Whether at home in Nashville, Tennessee, or training in Florida, Purdy spends a little time each day of the offseason working on vision training. Equipped with an iPad and 3D glasses, he watches two squares move in, out and around. His job is to identify how and when those squares converge and diverge with his eyes moving in and out rapidly.

 Purdy also does daily work with saccades, a rapid eye movement exercise in which he must follow arrows that pop up all over a screen and touch the correct one when prompted. According to Purdy, the goal of the two-to-four-minute sessions is to force him to process movement and information as fast as possible while improving his depth perception.

 "All those things help me just work on my eyesight, my eyes moving, being quick with my eyes, making quick decisions," Purdy said. "And then it records my decision-making, how fast, the percentage of getting right and wrong. I do think it helps."

 

 Since taking over as San Francisco's starter in 2022, Purdy ranks among the NFL's elite between the hashmarks. Among quarterbacks with at least 30 starts in that span, he's fourth in the NFL in attempts (224) and completions (163), second in passing yards (2,389) and yards per attempt (10.7) and tied for third in touchdown passes (16).

 On throws between the hashes with a tight window (where the receiver has less than a yard of separation at the time the ball arrives), Purdy is fourth in completions (15), third in passing yards (215) and seventh in attempts (34). He is first in the NFL in passing yards and tied for second in completions on such throws since the start of the 2025 season.

 Purdy credits much of that improvement to Shanahan, quarterbacks coach Mick Lombardi and offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak. The Niners have one route called "skid," where the receiver takes eight steps at a 45-degree angle coming out of his break. For optimal timing, Purdy's objective on that route is to throw the ball 20 yards downfield and 2 yards outside the hashmarks after taking a five-step drop with one hitch.

 "I never would have broken it down like that in high school or college," Purdy said. "But being here with Kyle, there's a detail to it. This is where it should be. It's just rep after rep watching film with Kyle and trusting how he's coaching me."

 That meticulous film study has translated to the field. With 5:38 left in the second quarter of the Niners' wild-card playoff win over the Eagles in January, Shanahan called a play with four players running "skid" routes. Purdy easily recalled the details while walking through the film. He quickly identified Eagles safety Marcus Epps rotating to tight end Jake Tonges . When running back Christian McCaffrey motioned across the formation, linebacker Nakobe Dean followed, leaving safety Reed Blankenship as the lone deep safety on the…
